stories.title: ‘US imperialism’: Anger in Philippines as war with Iran sends oil prices soaring
stories.summary: Protests erupted in the Philippines over soaring oil prices caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the U.S.-Iran conflict. Demonstrators in Manila directed anger primarily at the United States as Washington continues efforts to negotiate the permanent reopening of the strait.

stories.title: Air defense neutralizes 131 out of 154 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 131 of 154 Russian strike drones launched since the evening of May 19. The overnight operation neutralized the majority of the incoming aerial threats.

stories.title: There could be 1,000 or more victims of black-cab rapist John Worboys, says Carrie Johnson
stories.summary: Carrie Johnson, wife of former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson, said there could be up to 1,000 or more victims of convicted black-cab rapist John Worboys. Johnson, who helped bring Worboys to justice after encountering him in 2007, said more women had contacted her about alleged assaults.

stories.title: Israeli authorities transferring 430 Gaza flotilla activists to Israel
stories.summary: Israeli authorities transferred all 430 activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla to Israeli vessels and are bringing them to Israel. The Israel Foreign Ministry said the activists would be able to meet with their consular representatives upon arrival.

stories.title: EU picks tungsten, rare earths, gallium for first critical mineral stockpile
stories.summary: The European Union has shortlisted tungsten, rare earths, and gallium for its first joint strategic stockpile of critical minerals to reduce dependence on China. The EU is in discussions with major ports including Rotterdam in the Netherlands for storage.

stories.title: Somaliland to open first-ever embassy in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Somaliland has announced it will open its first-ever embassy in Jerusalem, Israel. The move follows Israel's recognition of the self-declared breakaway territory, marking a significant diplomatic milestone for Somaliland, which has no other embassies worldwide.

stories.title: Kenya transport strike paused after deadly protests
stories.summary: Transport operators in Kenya suspended a strike over fuel price hikes after deadly protests resulted in several deaths and mass arrests across the country.

stories.title: Xi hails China’s ‘unyielding’ ties with Russia as Putin visits Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed Russian President Vladimir Putin to Beijing on Wednesday for a visit focused on energy security. The meeting followed a recent visit to Beijing by U.S. President Donald Trump, underscoring China's diplomatic balancing between the two powers.

stories.title: 35 families in Hong Kong shoebox flats face eviction since start of new rule
stories.summary: Thirty-five families in Hong Kong's subdivided housing units have faced eviction since the government introduced new regulations to eliminate substandard shoebox homes two and a half months ago. An additional 40 households in Sham Shui Po's Yee Wa Building are still considering their options.

stories.title: Germany urged to stop admiring Beijing and wake up to ‘China Shock 2.0’
stories.summary: The Centre for European Reform think tank warned Germany to stop admiring China's economic success and prepare for a 'China Shock 2.0.' China's trade surplus with Germany doubled from $12 billion to $25 billion between 2024 and 2025, creating a $94 billion trade imbalance that risks deindustrialisation.

stories.title: US, Nigerian forces kill senior ISIS leader in strategic blow to terror group
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu said in a statement on Saturday that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki was killed “along with several of his lieutenants” in a joint strike with the US.

stories.title: ISW: Russia prepares the ground for Baltic aggression as its spy agency threatens Latvian “decision-making centers”
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russia's SVR intelligence agency threatened Latvian "decision-making centers" and military bases over allegations of Ukrainian drone operations that Latvia denies. ISW warned that Moscow may be manufacturing a pretext for aggression against Baltic states.

stories.title: War update: 250 combat engagements on front line, 43 of them in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Russian forces clashed 250 times along the front line over the previous day, with 43 engagements concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector. Russian forces also showed heightened activity in the Huliaipole sector.

stories.title: Xi-Putin summit leaves gas pipeline plan in limbo
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin made little progress on plans for a new gas pipeline between the two countries during their summit in Beijing. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there was still no clear timeline, though a "basic understanding" on the route had been reached.

stories.title: South Korea’s Lee criticizes Israel detentions, says actions ‘way out of line’
stories.summary: In a cabinet meeting, Lee said the South Korean citizens had been detained for reasons not valid under international law, questioning whether such actions could be allowed to pass without protest.

stories.title: Nigeria ex-minister on the run arrested after jail sentence
stories.summary: Nigeria's anti-graft agency arrested former power minister Saleh Mamman one week after he was sentenced in absentia to 75 years in prison on corruption charges. Mamman had been on the run following the court ruling.

stories.title: Comparison of ceremony in China for Putin and Trump visits has no point, Kremlin says
stories.summary: "There is a point in comparing the content," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told state television Kremlin reporter Pavel Zarubin when asked about comparisons with the Trump visit.

stories.title: Modi avoids Norway media: How that led to storm over India’s press freedom
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi avoided taking questions from Norwegian media during a visit, sparking debate over press freedom in India. The country is ranked 157th out of 180 nations in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index.

stories.title: Chinese investment in Europe surges to 7-year high despite rising trade tensions
stories.summary: Chinese investment in Europe reached a seven-year high of €16.8 billion in 2025, driven by increased mergers and acquisitions and record greenfield project completions. However, analysts caution that new project announcements are declining amid trade tensions and Beijing's push to retain domestic industrial capacity.

stories.title: Georgia mayor who fired town’s entire police force resigns, citing family ‘health concerns’
stories.summary: Ron Shinnick, mayor of Cohutta, Georgia, resigned after firing the town's entire police department, a decision the local governing council subsequently reversed. In his resignation letter, Shinnick cited family health concerns but did not mention the police firings, which had gained international media attention.

stories.title: Russian attacks in Sumy region over past 24 hours kill four civilians, wound nine
stories.summary: Russian attacks across Ukraine's Sumy region over a 24-hour period killed four civilians and wounded nine others.

stories.title: 'Crony capitalism and oligarchy': 'Remarkable correlation' between Adani's rise & Modi’s ascendancy
stories.summary: Indian journalist and filmmaker Paranjoy Guha-Thakurta discussed allegations of a nexus between billionaire industrialist Gautam Adani's rise and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political ascendancy. He argued that crony capitalism and oligarchic influence have become deeply embedded in India's state institutions, citing U.S. sanctions investigations.

stories.title: NYT: Israeli-developed plan sought to have Ahmadinejad run Iran after Khamenei killed
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Israel developed a plan to have former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad lead Iran after the anticipated killing of Supreme Leader Khamenei. Israel reportedly used an airstrike to free Ahmadinejad from house arrest, but he ultimately abandoned the arrangement.

stories.title: Russian drone collapses Konotop apartment floors, destroys museum as strikes hit at least six regions
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes hit at least six Ukrainian regions overnight on May 20, collapsing floors of an apartment building in Konotop, Sumy region, and killing two people in Dnipro. A museum in Konotop was also destroyed.

stories.title: Migrant outflow declines in recent years due to visa restrictions: report
stories.summary: The International Organisation for Migration's Pakistan mission chief spoke at the launch of the Pakistan Migration Report 2025 in Lahore. The report highlights declining migrant outflows due to international visa restrictions and emphasizes the need for regular migration pathways.

stories.title: Rachel Reeves to protect ‘critical’ clean energy projects from legal challenges
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves plans to announce planning reforms that would fast-track clean energy and infrastructure projects by limiting judicial review challenges. Parliament would be able to designate critical clean energy projects as of 'critical national importance,' partly in response to the economic impact of the Iran crisis.

stories.title: Pompeii victim revealed to be a doctor fleeing Vesuvius’ eruption over 60 years after discovery
stories.summary: The doctor’s identity followed new analysis of archaeological finds kept in the park’s storage warehouses - including a small case hidden within the cast of one of the victims from the garden.

stories.title: ChaiFlicks – Summertime binge time – your favorite series – now 50% off! - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: ChaiFlicks, a Jewish entertainment streaming service, is offering a 50% discount promotional deal at $48 per year. The platform features Israeli and international television series.

stories.title: Is Russia ‘simulating diplomacy’ because of war losses in Ukraine?
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has discussed a potential truce in the Ukraine conflict, but some analysts argue Moscow may be using diplomatic overtures to buy time while its forces face setbacks on the battlefield.

stories.title: Philippines’ top court rejects Dela Rosa’s bid to block ICC arrest warrant
stories.summary: The Philippine Supreme Court voted 9-5-1 to deny Senator Ronald dela Rosa's bid to block an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him. Dela Rosa, a former national police chief, is wanted by the ICC for his role as the main enforcer of ex-president Rodrigo Duterte's deadly drug war.

stories.title: Russian army loses 920 troops in war against Ukraine over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russian forces lost approximately 920 troops in the preceding 24 hours. Total estimated Russian personnel losses since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022 stand at roughly 1,352,070.

stories.title: ‘Vein of racism’: race discrimination commissioner accuses One Nation and Coalition of scapegoating immigrants
stories.summary: Australia's federal Race Discrimination Commissioner Giridharan Sivaraman accused the One Nation party and the federal Coalition opposition of scapegoating and dehumanising immigrants. Speaking at a Brisbane human rights seminar, he said the rhetoric draws on a deep vein of racism in Australian politics.

stories.title: Race to contain ebola outbreak in war-torn DRC where weak infrastructure hampers response
stories.summary: Health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo are racing to contain an Ebola outbreak in the conflict-affected eastern region. Julie Drouet of Action Against Hunger described a humanitarian system facing both epidemiological challenges and deep structural vulnerabilities including weak infrastructure and ongoing armed conflict.

stories.title: San Diego mosque shooting: Who were the victims?
stories.summary: Authorities identified Amin Abdullah, Mansour Kaziha, and Nader Awad as the three victims killed in a shooting at a San Diego mosque. Officials said all three played a role in responding to the attackers during the incident.

stories.title: Israel, US early war goals sought to reinstate Iran's Ahmadinejad as leader, NYT report says
stories.summary: An associate of Ahmadinejad told the NYT that the Americans viewed Mr. Ahmadinejad as someone who could lead Iran and manage “Iran’s political, social, and military situation.”

stories.title: At least 87 Gaza aid flotilla activists abducted by Israel on hunger strike
stories.summary: At least 87 activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla who were seized by Israeli forces have begun a hunger strike. The protest followed Israel's interception of the last remaining vessel attempting to reach the besieged Gaza Strip.

stories.title: What is the Sharjah–Oman corridor bypassing Hormuz?
stories.summary: The Sharjah-to-Oman corridor has drawn attention as a potential alternative route to the Strait of Hormuz. The corridor's viability has been highlighted amid war-related shipping disruptions in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: French officers raid Nestle’s Perrier water bottling site
stories.summary: French officers conducted raids at two Nestlé sites in Vergeze, France, where the company bottles its Perrier water brand. Nestlé confirmed the raids took place but further details were not immediately provided.

stories.title: China’s Top Numerical Control rides investor fervour for aerospace to 80% IPO gain
stories.summary: Shanghai Top Numerical Control Technology, a Chinese aviation and aerospace parts supplier, surged 80% on its first day of trading in Hong Kong. Shares opened at HK$37, well above the offer price of HK$26.39, reflecting strong investor appetite for the commercial aerospace sector.

stories.title: China and Russia reaffirm close ties amid US visit
stories.summary: President Xi Jinping described China-Russia ties as "unyielding" during talks with President Vladimir Putin in Beijing on Wednesday. The meeting came days after U.S. President Donald Trump visited China, underscoring the geopolitical significance of the summit.

stories.title: Russia is concerned by US, EU rare earth activity in Central Asia, media reports
stories.summary: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin expressed concern to the Izvestia newspaper about US and European Union efforts to secure access to rare earths and critical minerals in Central Asia, signaling growing geopolitical competition over strategic resources in the region.

stories.title: Russia launches unannounced nuclear exercise, including Belarusian launch sites
stories.summary: Russia conducted an unannounced nuclear exercise that included launch sites in Belarus. The exercise combined nuclear saber-rattling with ongoing diplomatic efforts abroad, following a pattern the Kremlin has employed repeatedly.

stories.title: How war-risk marine insurance can set Hong Kong apart
stories.summary: The article discusses how rising conflict in the Middle East has driven up marine insurance costs, creating an opportunity for Hong Kong to establish itself as a center for war-risk marine insurance, risk pricing, and maritime resilience.

stories.title: The Doublespeak of Lebanon’s Other Shiite Leader
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that the Amal Movement's strategic calculations about its own future will significantly influence Hezbollah's fate in Lebanon. The piece examines the political positioning of Lebanon's other major Shiite political faction alongside Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russia attacks Odesa overnight with strike drones, damaging critical infrastructure
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Odesa caused damage to residential areas, warehouses, and critical infrastructure in the southern Ukrainian port city.

stories.title: COMMENT: Trust the signals, but  verify the policy
stories.summary: Indian Army Chief Gen Upendra Dwivedi provoked controversy by suggesting Pakistan must choose between remaining part of "geography or history." The statement came shortly after signals from India's strategic establishment appeared to create space for limited engagement with Islamabad, raising questions about contradictions in New Delhi's Pakistan policy.

stories.title: How Vladimir Putin’s chance encounter with a Chinese boy in Beijing shaped a life’s path
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Chinese engineer Peng Pai in Beijing on Wednesday, reuniting with him more than 25 years after a chance encounter when Peng was 12 years old during Putin's first presidential visit to China. Putin praised Peng's decision to study in Russia.

stories.title: Uganda: Govt Issues New Ebola Guidelines for Public Gatherings, Transport
stories.summary: Uganda's Ministry of Health has issued new Standard Operating Procedures to prevent Ebola transmission during public gatherings, religious services, transport operations, and burial ceremonies. The guidelines come amid heightened regional concern over the Ebola outbreak in neighboring DRC.

stories.title: At White House briefing, US V-P Vance says Iran war won’t be ‘forever’
stories.summary: At a White House briefing, US Vice President J.D. Vance stated that any US military conflict with Iran would not become a prolonged engagement. He also downplayed speculation about a potential presidential bid.

stories.title: UK relaxes strict sanctions on Russian crude as oil costs soar
stories.summary: The UK government issued a trade licence effective Wednesday allowing indefinite imports of jet fuel and diesel refined from Russian crude oil in third countries. The decision responds to fuel supply concerns linked to the de facto blockade of the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: U.S. expert: Ukraine should continue targeting on Russian oil infrastructure
stories.summary: A U.S. expert argued that Ukraine should continue striking Russian oil infrastructure despite Western calls for restraint. The analyst cited Ukraine's existential security concerns as justification for targeting energy facilities.

stories.title: WHO emergency supplies arrive in Bunia as Ebola death toll reaches 136
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has delivered emergency medical supplies to Bunia in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the Ebola outbreak reached 136 deaths and approximately 543 suspected cases. Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba confirmed the figures as WHO scaled up operations.

stories.title: Iran ‘prefers diplomacy’ but if there’s a war, Tehran says it’s ready
stories.summary: Iran stated it prefers diplomacy over military conflict with the United States but is prepared for war if necessary. The exchange followed President Donald Trump's warning of renewed strikes, a day after he said he had paused a major assault in hopes of reaching a peace deal.

stories.title: NATO eastern deterrence strategy takes shape around ‘autonomous zone’
stories.summary: NATO is developing an eastern deterrence strategy centered on an 'autonomous zone' concept informed by lessons from the Ukraine conflict. A Latvian commander noted that in Ukraine's gray zones, any vehicle movement is targeted and destroyed.

stories.title: Putin hails ‘unshakable foundations’ in meeting with China’s Xi
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, where Putin praised the "unshakable foundations" of the bilateral relationship. Xi welcomed Putin to the Chinese capital for the talks.

stories.title: PMD warns of glacial floods in northern regions
stories.summary: The Pakistan Meteorological Department issued a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) alert on Tuesday, warning disaster management authorities to maintain round-the-clock vigilance. A moderate westerly wave is affecting parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan, bringing heavy rain and thunderstorms to mountainous catchments in Pakistan's northern regions.

stories.title: Shock and bafflement at San Diego mosque where three were killed
stories.summary: Three people were killed in a shooting at a mosque in San Diego. The imam of the Islamic Center said the complex had previously been subjected to sporadic acts of Islamophobia. The community expressed shock and disbelief at the attack.

stories.title: Nigeria arrests former minister in hiding after corruption conviction
stories.summary: Nigeria's former power minister Saleh Mamman has been arrested after being convicted of corruption and sentenced in absentia to 75 years in prison. He had been in hiding since the sentencing earlier this month.

stories.title: Indian diplomat found dead inside mission in Bangladesh's Chattogram
stories.summary: Indian diplomat Naren Dhar, an Assistant Protocol Officer at the Indian mission in Chattogram, Bangladesh, was found dead inside the diplomatic compound. His body was discovered early in the morning in front of a bathroom door on the second floor of the old visa centre building.

stories.title: Norwegian journalist's question to Modi sparks controversy in India
stories.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng faced backlash online in India after asking Prime Minister Narendra Modi why he does not take questions from the press during a visit to Norway.

stories.title: Attack on Dnipro kills two, injures six
stories.summary: A nighttime attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed two people and wounded six others.

stories.title: No more politics, only social work: Jahangir Khan Tareen
stories.summary: Former Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party patron-in-chief Jahangir Khan Tareen announced in Lahore that he has permanently left politics. He said he will continue social work in the education sector following his party's defeat in Pakistan's 2024 elections.

stories.title: Moral failure
stories.summary: A commentary in Pakistan questions the meaning of civil honours and public success in a system marked by social and economic injustice. The author reflects on whether accepting state awards is appropriate given pervasive political patronage and selective accountability in the country.

stories.title: Tumps says 'days' left for a deal, Iran promises 'surprises'
stories.summary: Trump has said there were only 'days' left to make a deal. For its part, the Iranian military warned of 'surprises' if the war resumes.

stories.title: ‘Why don’t you take questions, Mr Modi?’
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi faced questions from Norwegian journalists about his practice of not taking press questions during his visit to Oslo for the India-Nordic Summit. A journalist publicly called out Modi as he left a joint briefing with Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in Central Africa could last months, WHO says
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned that the Ebola outbreak in Central Africa could last months. As of May 19, the suspected death toll had exceeded 130 people.

stories.title: US enforces law to crack down on sexual deepfakes
stories.summary: The United States has begun enforcing a new law targeting sexually explicit deepfake content. Critics have raised concerns that the legislation could be used disproportionately against transgender individuals, sex workers, and political speech.

stories.title: CM Maryam inaugurates Punjab Pavilion at Baku forum
stories.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif inaugurated the Punjab Pavilion at the World Urban Forum in Baku, Azerbaijan. She was briefed on progress of the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar housing program by the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency.

stories.title: China turns to Russian oil as Gulf supply drops – but is it too expensive?
stories.summary: China increased crude oil imports from Russia by 11.3% year on year in April to nearly 9 million tonnes, as imports from Gulf nations dropped amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. However, the discount on Russian crude has narrowed, raising cost concerns for Beijing.

stories.title: Final report reveals truth behind deadly Singapore Airlines flight SQ321 turbulence
stories.summary: Investigators have released the final report on Singapore Airlines flight SQ321, which encountered severe turbulence in 2024 while traveling from London to Singapore, killing one passenger and injuring dozens. The flight was diverted to Bangkok for emergency medical treatment.

stories.title: Outbreak of rare Ebola strain sparks race to find vaccines and treatments
stories.summary: An escalating outbreak of a rare Ebola strain in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 130 people, prompting an urgent search for effective vaccines and treatments. WHO Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus expressed deep concern about the scale and speed of the epidemic, noting cases emerging in urban areas.

stories.title: Trump to attend G7 summit in France, Axios reports
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump will attend the G7 leaders' summit in France in June, according to Axios, citing a White House official. He is expected to discuss artificial intelligence, trade, and crime-fighting with other world leaders.

stories.title: NA session adjourned again as quorum crisis persists
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Assembly session in Islamabad was adjourned on Tuesday without conducting any business due to a lack of quorum. PTI-backed independent MNA Iqbal Afridi pointed out the absence of sufficient members shortly after proceedings began. Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah adjourned the sitting until Wednesday after repeated attempts to achieve quorum failed.

stories.title: Chinese supertankers exit Hormuz as Trump, Vance talk up Iran deal
stories.summary: Chinese supertankers have exited the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. President Trump and Vice President Vance publicly discussed prospects for an Iran deal. Oil prices eased on the comments, though experts cautioned prices would remain elevated even if an agreement is reached.

stories.title: US-Saudi civil nuclear pact nears signing without toughest safeguards urged by Democrats
stories.summary: A State Department letter dated May 18 to Democratic Senator Edward Markey says the pact only requires Washington and Riyadh to forge a less onerous "bilateral safeguards agreement."

stories.title: Italy settles on Airbus tanker purchase in swing toward European equipment
stories.summary: Italy has selected an Airbus tanker aircraft purchase, shifting away from Boeing for its air refueling fleet. The Italian Air Force currently operates four Boeing 767-based tanker aircraft that entered service beginning in 2011, making this a notable move toward European-made defense equipment.

stories.title: Attack on Vilniansk injures four people, including two children
stories.summary: An attack on Vilniansk in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia district injured four people, including two children. A private home was destroyed in the strike.

stories.title: Trump says US may strike Iran again but that Tehran wants deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said the US may launch another military strike against Iran but indicated Tehran wants to reach a deal. He warned a new attack could come within days if no agreement is reached.

stories.title: The Navy Needs Precise Mass and Here Is How to Get There
stories.summary: An analysis argues the U.S. Navy must fundamentally change its shipbuilding and combat approach to maintain deterrence in the Indo-Pacific. The ongoing war with Iran is exposing fleet limitations, including the rapid consumption of high-end ships and thinning munitions inventories, with replacement timelines stretching into years.

stories.title: ECC allows NLC to take over shipping corporation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Economic Coordination Committee approved transferring management control and a 30 percent shareholding in Pakistan National Shipping Corporation to the National Logistics Corporation. The decision, chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, aims to integrate freight transport via shipping and road networks. The ECC also approved a 70 percent increase in subsistence allowances for 1989 Kashmiri refugees.

stories.title: Albanese’s department among those blocking 80% of FoI requests, scathing report finds
stories.summary: An Australian audit report found that nearly 80% of freedom of information requests to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's department, Treasury, and the infrastructure department were rejected. The review identified a culture of "resistance and delay," with over 60% of requests exceeding the mandated 30-day response deadline.

stories.title: Japan, South Korea hone diplomatic ‘muscle memory’ amid Taiwan worries
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met on Tuesday for their fourth summit in six months, with energy security as the formal agenda. Analysts say the frequent meetings reflect shared uncertainty among the two U.S. allies amid concerns over Taiwan and regional stability.

stories.title: PPP leaders say ‘premature’ to comment on 28th Amendment
stories.summary: Pakistan Peoples Party leaders, including Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, said it was premature to comment on a reported 28th constitutional amendment that could roll back provincial powers. The PPP stated it had not received any draft of the proposed amendment, echoing remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: US and Iran trade threats but Trump insists Tehran wants deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump warned he could strike Iran again while Tehran's military threatened to open "new fronts" if attacked. The U.S. Senate advanced a war-powers resolution to end the Iran conflict unless Trump obtains congressional authorization. Trump insisted Tehran wants a deal despite ongoing mutual threats.

stories.title: A Russian drone killed their parents. Soldiers found two children in a Dobropillia basement
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on Dobropillia killed two parents, leaving their children stranded in a basement. Ukrainian soldiers discovered the two children despite official records indicating no children remained in the city for evacuation.

stories.title: Bullying crows attack children, parents at Tel Aviv kindergarten
stories.summary:
People say birds swooping down and assaulting them, with some drawing blood; municipality cites annual phenomenon of adults protecting chicks as they learn to fly

stories.title: Ethiopia: EU Lifts Visa Restrictions On Ethiopia Citing Cooperation On Migrant Readmissions
stories.summary: The Council of the European Union lifted restrictive visa measures imposed on Ethiopia in 2024. The decision cited significant improvements in Ethiopia's cooperation on readmission of nationals residing illegally in EU member states.

stories.title: Iran war day 82: Tehran warns of ‘new fronts’ as Trump sets deadline
stories.summary: Iran says it learned from past clashes as Trump gives Tehran 'two to three days' to reach a deal.

stories.title: Machine Overmatch: What Salt Typhoon Reveals About China’s Data-Centric Intelligence Strategy
stories.summary: China's Salt Typhoon cyber-espionage campaign targeted U.S. telecommunications networks and critical infrastructure over multiple years. The operation reflects Beijing's data-centric intelligence strategy, which prioritizes large-scale digital collection, rapid analysis, and operational use alongside traditional espionage methods. The campaign challenges conventional U.S. assumptions about intelligence advantage.

stories.title: UK loosens Russian oil sanctions as fuel prices rise
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has eased sanctions on Russian oil imports by issuing a waiver. The move comes amid rising fuel prices and growing supply concerns linked to an effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Pakistan can buy Russian oil
stories.summary: The United States issued a 30-day general licence through the Treasury Department allowing selected energy-importing nations to purchase Russian oil, easing global crude supply pressures. Diplomatic sources told Dawn that Pakistan may be eligible, though Islamabad's limited technical capacity could prevent it from fully utilizing the concession.

stories.title: Commander of Israeli armoured brigade injured in Hezbollah drone attack
stories.summary:
Commander of Israeli armoured brigade injured in Hezbollah drone attack

stories.title: Rwanda: Relentless Persecution of Rwandan Opposition Leader Victoire Ingabire Continues
stories.summary: Rwandan opposition leader Victoire Ingabire faces a new trial carrying a potential life sentence. Rights observers describe the prosecution as part of ongoing persecution of political dissenters under President Paul Kagame's government.

stories.title: What is the political weight of Diaoyutai guesthouse where Putin is staying?
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for a two-day state visit and stayed at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, a historic venue that has hosted leaders including Richard Nixon and Kim Jong-un. Putin has visited China more than 20 times and met President Xi Jinping over 40 times since 2013.

stories.title: Limit social media ban for under-16s to unsafe apps, Starmer urged
stories.summary: Online safety campaigners including the NSPCC and Molly Rose Foundation urged UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to ban under-16s only from social media apps that fail to meet strict safety standards, rather than imposing a blanket ban. They called for blocking platforms offering "risky" features such as infinite scrolling and disappearing messages to teenagers.

stories.title: Anti-Israel Republican Thomas Massie ousted from Congress as Trump endorsee wins primary
stories.summary: Massie's concession on Tuesday night included a dig at Gallrein’s purported relationship to Israel.

stories.title: Drones attack industrial areas in Russia's Stavropol region, governor says
stories.summary: Drones struck industrial areas near Nevinnomyssk in Russia's southern Stavropol region, according to Governor Vladimir Vladimirov, who reported the attacks on Telegram on May 20.

stories.title: Taiwan’s president says future will not be decided by ‘external forces’
stories.summary: President Lai says Taiwan's future is up to its people as the island faces Chinese and US headwinds.

stories.title: Enemy attack on Dnipro injures five people
stories.summary: Five people were injured and a fire erupted in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro following an enemy attack.

stories.title: In Malaysia, drug-laced vape seizures stoke US-like ‘zombie epidemic’ fears
stories.summary: Malaysian authorities are confronting rising seizures of drug-laced vape liquids, known locally as "piu-piu" or "piao-piao," after viral videos showed young men appearing dazed and disoriented. At least two viral cases triggered arrests, stoking fears of a substance abuse epidemic linked to the country's booming e-cigarette market.

stories.title: South Korean-flagged tanker attempts Hormuz crossing

South Korean-flagged tanker attempts Hormuz crossing

    
    

        
    
                A South Korean-flagged supertanker is attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, according to ship-trackin

stories.title: Rwanda tightens border controls over deadly Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: Rwanda intensified health screenings and tightened border controls with the Democratic Republic of Congo in response to a deadly Ebola outbreak. The outbreak is linked to the rare Bundibugyo strain and continues to spread across the region.

stories.title: US to let DR Congo team in for World Cup despite Ebola restrictions

stories.summary: A Russian court sentenced a Ukrainian woman to 12 years in prison for financing Ukraine's Armed Forces through 78 money transfers. Her Russian accomplice received a 14-year sentence for state treason.

stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense is training demining specialists to use drones and magnetometers for detecting explosive objects. The magnetometers detect changes in the Earth's magnetic field, reducing risks to human life during mine clearance.

stories.summary: "Everything here is rotten and exposed," said the source, who alleged that the response from the military has been insufficient to control the rat manifestation seen daily at the base.

stories.title: Could Putin, Trump visits pave the way for ‘trilateral coordination’ with China?
stories.summary: Back-to-back state visits by Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to Beijing have raised the prospect of emerging "trilateral coordination" between China, Russia, and the United States, according to former Chinese diplomat Cui Hongjian. During talks on Wednesday, President Xi Jinping and Putin discussed energy cooperation, though Cui cautioned the U.S. remains the biggest uncertainty.

stories.title: Dozens could face criminal charges over London’s 2017 Grenfell Tower inferno
stories.summary: British Metropolitan Police announced they would ask prosecutors to consider criminal charges against 57 individuals and 20 organisations in connection with the 2017 Grenfell Tower fire in London, which killed 72 people. Evidence files will be submitted by September, with charging decisions expected by the disaster's 10th anniversary in June 2027.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Rules Out Blanket Ebola Quarantines
stories.summary: Kenya announced it will not impose blanket quarantines on travelers or truck drivers as part of its Ebola preparedness response. Instead, authorities are implementing enhanced risk-based screening and surveillance amid outbreaks in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Nigeria: Army Gives Update On Nigeria-U.S. Operations Against Islamic State, Says 175 Terrorists Killed
stories.summary: Nigeria's Defence Headquarters reported that joint Nigerian-U.S. military operations against Islamic State militants killed 175 fighters. The operations destroyed checkpoints, weapons storage facilities, logistics hubs, and financial structures used by the terrorists.

stories.title: ‘Cockroach Janta Party’: Top Indian judge’s comment sparks satire, protest
stories.summary: Controversial remark by Supreme Court chief justice triggers a political movement, with thousands of Gen Z signing in.

stories.title: US missionary who contracted Ebola is on his way to Germany, CDC says
stories.summary: A U.S. citizen who contracted Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is being transported to Germany for treatment, according to the CDC. The outbreak of a rare Ebola strain in DR Congo has killed over 130 people.

stories.title: Nigeria: How Some People Claimed I Planned to Kill Tinubu to Take Over Power - VP Shettima
stories.summary: Nigerian Vice President Kashim Shettima publicly recounted allegations made against him early in his tenure, claiming unnamed individuals told President Tinubu that Shettima was planning to kill him and seize power.

stories.title: Hong Kong adds 820 extra flights to ease disruption from Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities approved 820 additional flights and fast-tracked 4,100 schedule adjustment applications to address disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict. Transport Secretary Mable Chan said officials are working with airlines to deploy extra cargo capacity to destinations experiencing service shortfalls.

stories.title: Scrap stamp duty and council tax to fix London housing crisis, thinktank says
stories.summary: The Centre for London thinktank proposed scrapping stamp duty and council tax in favour of an annual property wealth tax to address the capital's housing crisis. The report argues the new levy would encourage downsizing, fund social housing, and help renters save for deposits.

stories.title: Children in mental health crisis waiting up to three days in A&E for specialist bed in England
stories.summary: NHS figures reveal that children experiencing mental health crises in England are waiting up to three days in A&E before receiving a specialist bed. The Royal College of Nursing criticised the situation as a "catastrophic system-wide failure," with nurses describing the long waits for distressed under-18s as increasingly common.

stories.title: AI engineer says Google unfairly sacked him after he protested against work for Israel
stories.summary: A Google AI engineer claims he was unfairly dismissed after distributing protest leaflets at Google DeepMind's London offices criticising the company's work for the Israeli government. He has filed an employment tribunal claim, alleging his sacking was retaliation for his protest activities.

stories.title: China teacher slams student’s complaint about lack of benches in smoking area, reignites debate
stories.summary: A student at Xi'an International Studies University in Shaanxi province, China, complained about the lack of benches in a campus smoking area, calling the situation "exhausting." A university teacher responded with a lengthy rejection, reigniting public debate about smoking in public spaces in China.

stories.summary: Lindsay and Craig Foreman, from East Sussex, have each spent several days refusing food, their family says.

stories.summary: Ukraine's State Special Transport Service received 20 Roshel Senator mine-protected armored vehicles through the Demining Capability Coalition. The vehicles are intended to support demining operations across Ukraine.

stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers raised concerns that a proposed nuclear power agreement between the United States and Saudi Arabia lacks strict nonproliferation guardrails, urging the inclusion of voluntary "gold standard" protections.

stories.summary: Somaliland's ambassador to Israel announced plans to open an embassy in Jerusalem. The move follows Israel's recognition of Somaliland last year and reflects deepening diplomatic ties between the two sides.

stories.title: Thailand’s Singha beer dynasty rocked by sexual abuse allegations
stories.summary: Allegations of historic sexual abuse by Sunit Bhirombhakdi, an heir to Thailand's Singha beer dynasty, were made public by his younger brother Siranudh Scott, known as "Psi." stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks in Beijing on Wednesday, with Xi warning against a regression to "jungle law" in international relations. stories.summary: Singapore, Japan, and South Korea have strengthened Ebola screening measures for travellers from affected countries following a WHO alert about a growing outbreak in Central Africa. In Hong Kong, a Lantau Island isolation facility used during Covid-19 is being prepared. Officials say the likelihood of local transmission in Asia remains low.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: WHO Declares Global Emergency As DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Spreads Beyond Borders
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared a global health emergency over the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The death toll has reached 131 with more than 500 suspected cases, and the virus has spread beyond the DRC's borders.

stories.title: Ukraine not considering lowering mobilization age, Presidential Office says
stories.summary: Ukraine's Presidential Office stated the country is not considering lowering the mobilization age or restricting foreign travel for men aged 18 to 24. The clarification addressed public speculation about potential changes to Ukraine's conscription policies.

stories.summary: Norway revoked export licences for Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace's Naval Strike Missile system sold to Malaysia in a deal worth approximately $147 million. Analysts suspect U.S. pressure related to American-made components, including a gyroscope in the missile's guidance system, effectively blocked the arms deal between the two sovereign nations.

stories.summary: NATO's top military commander stated that the alliance is not drawing up plans for a mission in the Strait of Hormuz. Any such operation would require a political decision, despite suggestions from some member states that NATO could play a role there.

stories.summary: The UN Security Council condemned a drone attack near the Barakah nuclear power plant in Abu Dhabi, the Arab world's first nuclear facility. The unclaimed drone struck an electrical generator on May 17, causing a fire but no injuries or radiation leak.

stories.summary: Xi and Putin hold talks just days after US President Donald Trump made an official visit to China.

stories.title: Russia, following Belarus, announces start of nuclear exercises
stories.summary: Russia announced nuclear exercises to run from May 19 to May 21, following a similar announcement by Belarus. The drills focus on the preparation and deployment of nuclear forces under simulated conditions of aggression threats.

stories.title: Russia seeks progress on Power of Siberia 2 pipeline during China talks
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to discuss the proposed Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline during talks in Beijing. The leaders are also set to address economic cooperation, energy security, and geopolitical issues related to the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

stories.title: Vance says US troop deployment to Poland has been delayed
stories.summary: US Vice President J.D. Vance clarified that the deployment of US troops to Poland has been delayed, not withdrawn. He stated that earlier reports characterizing the move as a withdrawal were inaccurate.

stories.title: Vance says US troop deployment to Poland has been delayed
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance stated on Tuesday that a planned US troop deployment to Poland had been delayed. Vance clarified that it would be inaccurate to characterize the delay as a withdrawal of American forces from Europe.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Chinese, South Korean oil tankers pass through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Three oil tankers — two Chinese and one South Korean — crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday as Iran threatened to open "new fronts" if the U.S. resumed strikes. President Trump is expected to attend the G7 summit in France next month amid tensions with allies over the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Trump reveals details of his bunker-like ballroom with drone base, underground hospital
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump revealed details of a new six-storey subterranean complex beneath the White House, including a drone base on the roof and an underground military hospital. Trump gave reporters a tour of the construction project as he sought $1 billion from Congress for security enhancements to the building.

stories.title: Wine accessories take center stage in Israeli homes despite global decline in consumption
stories.summary: Wine accessories are becoming increasingly popular in Israeli homes even as global wine consumption declines. The trend reflects a shift among younger generations toward more moderate and intentional wine drinking.

stories.title: Former Hong Kong top scorer Mung Chiang to lead prestigious Northwestern University
stories.summary: Mung Chiang, a former top scorer in Hong Kong's public examinations and Queen's College alumnus, has been named the 18th president of Northwestern University. He will become the first Asian-American to lead the Illinois-based institution, taking office on July 1.

stories.title: Samsung workers go ahead with 18-day strike as bonus talks collapse
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics' trade union announced that 48,000 workers would begin an 18-day strike on Thursday after bonus payment negotiations collapsed. Union leader Choi Seung-ho said management failed to resolve a remaining sticking point in government-mediated talks, raising concerns about South Korea's economy and global semiconductor supply.

stories.title: Trump reveals new details of bunker-like ballroom with drone base
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump disclosed details about a six-story subterranean bunker-like ballroom he has constructed. Trump said the facility was necessary due to a recent assassination attempt at a Washington hotel, noting it includes a drone base.

stories.title: Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev’s first feature in nearly a decade, ‘Minotaur,’ premieres at Cannes
stories.summary: Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev premiered his new film Minotaur at the 79th Cannes Film Festival. It marks his first feature film in nearly a decade.

stories.title: US Senate advances measure curbing Trump's Iran war powers
stories.summary: The US Senate voted 50 to 47 to advance a procedural measure on a resolution curbing President Trump's war powers regarding Iran. Four Republican senators broke ranks to vote with nearly all Democrats in favor of the measure.

stories.summary: Norway reported Europe's first known case of bird flu in a polar bear after H5N5 avian influenza was detected in a deceased one-year-old male polar bear and a dead walrus.

stories.title: Pentagon says it reduced US troop brigades in Europe from four to three
stories.summary: The Pentagon confirmed it reduced U.S. Brigade Combat Teams in Europe from four to three, returning troop levels to 2021 figures. The drawdown is part of Washington's push for European allies to take greater responsibility for regional defence, and will temporarily delay additional U.S. force deployments to Poland.

stories.title: Two Chinese supertankers leave Strait of Hormuz after months-long delay
stories.summary: Two Chinese supertankers carrying approximately 4 million barrels of crude oil departed the Strait of Hormuz after being delayed in the Gulf for over two months. The vessels' movement followed disruptions and security concerns in the region linked to the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Israel's Negev officially recognized as international wine region
stories.summary: Israel's Negev desert has been officially recognized as an international wine region. The designation places the Negev alongside established wine regions such as Champagne, Chianti, Bordeaux, and Napa Valley.

stories.title: Trump says Iran eager to make deal as conflict continues
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the war involving Iran would end quickly, claiming Tehran was eager to reach a deal. He stated Washington would ensure Iran could not obtain a nuclear weapon and predicted oil prices would fall due to expected global oversupply.

stories.title: Xi-Putin summit live: China’s Xi hails ‘fruitful’ talks, says relations at all-time high
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on Wednesday, with Putin arriving Tuesday evening. Xi hailed the talks as "fruitful" and described bilateral relations as being at an all-time high. The summit followed closely after U.S. President Trump's recent visit to the Chinese capital.

stories.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirms extension of sanctions exemption for Russian oil for another month
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed a one-month extension of a sanctions exemption allowing the sale of Russian oil already loaded onto tankers. The decision provides continued flexibility for shipments of Russian crude already in transit.

stories.title: TikTok bans wave of bloggers, some with millions of followers, over ads for Russian drone assembly college
stories.summary: TikTok banned a wave of accounts that promoted Alabuga Polytech, a college in Tatarstan linked to Russian drone assembly. Some of the banned bloggers had millions of followers, and Russian blogger Alexey Gubanov was among the first to flag the bans.

stories.title: Hong Kong market surge, geopolitics drive ‘fear of missing out’ among French investors
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said French investors are showing renewed interest in Hong Kong, citing strong market performance and improved geopolitical sentiment following U.S. President Trump's visit to Beijing. Chan noted a "marked difference" in perceptions compared to his previous visit to Paris two years ago.

stories.title: Bahrain bars visitors from Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan, Uganda over Ebola risk
stories.summary: Bahrain imposed a 30-day entry ban on visitors from the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan, and Uganda due to Ebola risk. The restriction does not apply to Bahraini nationals.

stories.title: Nigeria says joint US strikes kill 175 ISIL fighters in country’s northeast
stories.summary: Nigerian Army lauds joint US operation as part of ongoing military campaign to 'hunt down and kill terrorists anywhere'.

stories.title: UN cuts global growth forecast amid Iran war and energy shock
stories.summary: The United Nations lowered its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.5 percent from 3 percent, citing rising energy costs and weaker trade linked to the US-Israel war on Iran. The UN report warned that low-income families in developing countries were being hit hardest by surging food and energy prices.

stories.title: Former Tatler Russia editor-in-chief, jailed for extorting Rostec chief, has been released from prison
stories.summary: Arian Romanovsky, the former editor-in-chief of Tatler Russia's edition, has been released from prison. Romanovsky had been convicted of extorting Rostec head Sergei Chemezov.

stories.title: US: Anti-Aipac congressman unseated in most expensive House primary ever
stories.summary: Republican Congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky was defeated in a House primary by Trump-endorsed former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein. The race was reported as the most expensive House primary in US history, with Massie known for his opposition to the pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC.

stories.title: Russia says ready to assist Iran-US negotiations if requested
stories.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said Moscow is prepared to assist in negotiations between Iran and the United States if asked but would not impose its mediation. Speaking to TASS, Ryabkov emphasized Russia's commitment to resolving tensions through political and diplomatic channels.

stories.title: UAE says drone that hit near its nuclear plant was launched from Iraq
stories.summary: The UAE stated that a drone that struck near its Barakah Nuclear Power Plant was launched from Iraq. IAEA chief Raphael Grossi warned that a direct hit on the plant could result in a very high release of radioactivity.

stories.title: Iran talks making ‘good progress’, says US V-P Vance, but Washington ‘locked and loaded’
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance described US-Iran nuclear negotiations as making "good progress," while noting Washington remains "locked and loaded." President Trump gave Tehran a deadline of two to three days to reach an agreement.

stories.title: Sally Rooney to issue novel in Hebrew with Israeli publisher who complies with BDS
stories.summary: Irish author Sally Rooney will publish her latest novel in Hebrew through an Israeli publisher that complies with the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement. The decision prompted backlash in Israel, with bookstore chains reportedly removing some of her earlier works from shelves.

stories.title: NYT: Israeli-developed war plans sought to have Ahmedinejad run Iran after Khamenei killed
stories.summary: According to a New York Times report, Israeli-developed war plans envisioned former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad leading Iran after the killing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. The article appeared alongside reports of the Senate advancing a resolution limiting Trump's war powers against Iran.

stories.title: 20-year Duma veteran among two to quit United Russia’s Smolensk primary in quick succession
stories.summary: Veteran State Duma deputy Sergei Neverov dropped out of the United Russia primary in Smolensk's single-member district after 20 years in parliament. A second candidate, Smolensk City Council deputy and Ukraine war veteran Artem Kornyuchenkov, subsequently also withdrew from the race.

stories.title: EU reaches deal on US trade pact as Trump threatens new tariffs by July 4
stories.summary: EU lawmakers and member states reached a deal early Wednesday to implement the bloc's trade pact with the United States, ending months of internal disagreement. The agreement came as President Trump threatened fresh tariffs unless it was approved by July 4, following late-night negotiations between EU capitals and parliament negotiators.

stories.title: Judge opens probe into politician Philippe over corruption charges, French media reports
stories.summary: A French judge has opened an investigation into centrist politician Édouard Philippe on accusations of misappropriation of public funds, favoritism, conflict of interest, and extortion, according to French media reports on Tuesday.

stories.title: Man who murdered teen TikTok star in Pakistan gets death sentence
stories.summary: A man in Pakistan was sentenced to death for the murder of teen TikTok star Sana Yousaf. Activists noted the case reflects a broader pattern of violence against women in Pakistan.

stories.title: Vance: US ‘locked and loaded’ for military action if Iran talks fail
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that the United States is prepared to take military action against Iran if Tehran does not agree to a nuclear deal. He described the US as "locked and loaded" should diplomatic efforts fail.

stories.title: Rubio to attend NATO talks, pay first visit to India
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department confirmed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio will attend NATO foreign ministers' talks in Helsingborg, Sweden, on May 22, 2026, in preparation for a NATO summit in Turkey in July. He will then pay his first visit to India.

stories.title: Trump critic Thomas Massie defeated in Kentucky Republican House primary
stories.summary: Kentucky voters ousted seven-term Congressman Thomas Massie in a Republican primary, electing Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein, a retired Navy SEAL and farmer. The result demonstrated President Trump's dominance over the Republican Party, following setbacks for other GOP lawmakers who had challenged the president.

stories.title: A China-U.S. summit that drew global attention
stories.summary: A recent China-U.S. summit drew significant global attention amid ongoing international turmoil. The meeting highlighted the growing need for stable bilateral relations between Beijing and Washington.

stories.title: Rwanda says Mozambique has secured funds for it to continue Cabo Delgado mission
stories.summary: Rwanda's foreign minister said on Tuesday that Mozambique has secured funding for Rwandan forces to continue their military deployment in the insurgency-affected, gas-rich Cabo Delgado province.

stories.title: Japan plans island drone deployment to monitor Chinese naval activity
stories.summary: Japan plans to deploy long-range surveillance drones on the remote Pacific islands of Iwo Jima and Chichijima in the Ogasawara chain, as well as Minamitorishima, approximately 1,950 km southeast of Tokyo. The deployment aims to enhance monitoring of Chinese naval activity as Beijing's warships increasingly operate beyond the first island chain.

stories.title: China’s rise will turn Thucydides Trap on its head
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping invoked the Thucydides Trap concept during his Beijing summit with US President Donald Trump, urging both powers to avoid the pattern in which a rising power's challenge to an established one leads to conflict. The theory, popularized by Harvard's Graham Allison, draws on ancient Greek history.

stories.title: Risk of gasoline shortage in Russia due to refinery problems – intelligence
stories.summary: Intelligence reports indicate Russia faces a risk of large-scale gasoline shortages due to ongoing problems at its oil refineries.

stories.title: The European Union unblocks tariff deal with United States after ten months of negotiation
stories.summary: European Union negotiators from the Parliament, Council, and Commission reached a provisional agreement on a tariff pact with the United States after ten months of negotiations. The Cypriot Council presidency confirmed the breakthrough, stating the deal aims to enhance stable and predictable trade relations.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon kill nine, wound dozens
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on the Nabatieh district in southern Lebanon killed nine people, including a woman, and wounded about 12 others, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Additional strikes in the Tyre district on the towns of Hanaway and Maarakeh injured at least 17 more people, including a child.

stories.title: US Senate votes in favour of resolution to limit Trump’s Iran war powers
stories.summary: The US Senate advanced a War Powers Resolution to halt military operations against Iran unless President Trump receives explicit congressional authorization. The vote marked the first time the Senate approved such a measure, though it still requires House approval to take effect.

stories.title: NATO expects US troop cuts from Europe to take years
stories.summary: NATO's top military commander said on Tuesday that the United States will withdraw additional troops from Europe, but the process will take years to allow allied nations time to develop replacement capabilities.

stories.title: IDF intercepts all ships in Gaza-bound flotilla, over 400 activists being transferred to Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military intercepted all ships in a Gaza-bound flotilla and began transferring over 400 activists to Israel. Israel's Foreign Ministry described the Global Sumud Flotilla's attempt to break the Gaza blockade as a "PR stunt at the service of Hamas" and said rubber bullets were fired at the ships.

stories.title: Two polls find growing split among Republicans over support for Israel
stories.summary: Two recent polls revealed a growing divide among Republican voters over US support for Israel. Nearly a third of potential Republican voters said Trump had been "too supportive of Israel," and 22 percent of MAGA voters said Israel has too much influence on US foreign policy.

stories.title: Situation of 'grave concern', IAEA chief says on strike near UAE nuclear plant
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi briefed the UN Security Council on a drone strike near the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant, calling the incident a matter of "grave concern." Grossi said radiation levels remained normal and offsite power had been restored, but warned that attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities were unacceptable.

stories.title: Nigeria says joint US strikes kill 175 Islamic State militants, senior leaders
stories.summary: Nigeria's Defence Headquarters announced on Tuesday that Nigerian forces, operating jointly with the United States, killed 175 Islamic State militants and senior leaders in a series of air and ground strikes in the country's northeast in recent days.

stories.title: Red carpet for Putin: why China-Russia ties outpace Beijing’s engagement with Washington
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for his 25th visit to China, a two-day state visit that follows US President Donald Trump's recent trip to China. It marks the first time Beijing has hosted both the Russian and American leaders in the same month outside a multilateral setting.

stories.title: Chinese man who lost a leg and an arm inspires many by competing in bodybuilding
stories.summary: Liu Xinju, a 32-year-old man with one arm and one leg, competed in the 20th Bodybuilding Competition in Jinan, Shandong province, on May 10. Videos of his performance went viral on Chinese social media, earning him widespread admiration and the nickname "Encouraging Brother."

stories.title: Iran warns of heavier US losses if fighting restarts
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that the US would face heavier losses if military action against Iran resumed. He claimed Iran's forces were the first to shoot down an F-35 fighter jet and cited a US Congressional Research Office report estimating significant American aircraft losses.

stories.title: ‘Anti-Islamic writings’ found in car of California mosque shooting suspects, official says
stories.summary: Authorities in California reported that anti-Islamic writings were found in the car of two teenage suspects in a mosque shooting. The suspects were found dead in their vehicle from apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds.

stories.title: Foreign Ministry denies claims of strikes against Gaza-bound flotilla
stories.summary: Israel's Foreign Ministry denied claims of strikes against a Gaza-bound flotilla, stating that videos showing soldiers firing at boats depicted "non-lethal means." The ministry said no protesters were injured in the incident.

stories.title: US Senate advances resolution to curb Trump’s power to wage war on Iran
stories.summary: The US Senate voted to advance a War Powers Resolution aimed at curbing President Donald Trump's authority to wage war against Iran without congressional approval. The move was seen as a rare bipartisan rebuke of the president amid growing pressure to end US military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Trump tightens grip on Republican Party after Thomas Massie primary defeat
stories.summary: President Donald Trump strengthened his hold on the Republican Party after Kentucky voters ousted Congressman Thomas Massie, one of few conservatives who openly challenged the president. NBC and CNN projected the defeat, which followed setbacks for other Republican dissenters in Indiana and Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy.

stories.title: EU Parliament adopts higher tariffs on foreign steel to battle China’s cheap exports
stories.summary: The European Parliament approved higher tariffs on foreign steel imports aimed at countering cheap exports from China. The measures will take effect from July 1 after receiving final approval from EU member states.

stories.title: Tehran calls US statement on Minab school strike 'appalling lie'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei rejected US claims about a missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in Minab, calling the allegations an "appalling lie." He criticized US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper's assertion that the school was located on an active Iranian cruise missile site.

stories.title: Trump critic Massie defeated in record-breaking US primary
stories.summary: Congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky lost his Republican primary to Ed Gallrein, a former Navy SEAL backed by President Donald Trump and supported by significant outside spending from pro-Israel groups. Massie had drawn Trump's ire by pushing to release Justice Department files related to the late Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: 'No longer fit for purpose': Politicisation of aid endangers millions, medical researchers warn
stories.summary: A report published in The Lancet warned that the politicization of humanitarian aid is endangering millions of lives globally. Medical researchers argued that aid systems guided by political interests rather than need are no longer fit for purpose.

stories.title: Court sentences border guard to 15 years for passing Ukrainian troop locations to Russia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian court sentenced a State Border Guard Service member to 15 years in prison with property confiscation for passing information about Ukrainian troop locations to Russian forces.

stories.title: Iran's UN mission accuses US of spreading 'lies and disinformation'
stories.summary: Iran's UN mission accused the United States of spreading "lies, false accusations, and disinformation" about Tehran's nuclear program during UN Security Council discussions. The mission also alleged that Washington violated international law through maritime blockades and support for Israeli actions in the region.

stories.title: Kazakhstan to deepen financial services cooperation with Hong Kong, consul says
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's consul general in Hong Kong, Bauyrzhan Dosmanbetov, said the Central Asian country aims to deepen financial cooperation with Hong Kong, viewing it as a fundraising hub for accessing renminbi capital through bond issuances. He noted Kazakhstan's community in the city has grown to about 1,000 people, driven by Belt and Road initiatives.

stories.title: Nigeria arrests ex-power minister Mamman after 75-year graft sentence
stories.summary: Nigeria's anti-corruption agency arrested former power minister Saleh Mamman on Tuesday, days after a court sentenced him in absentia to 75 years in prison for laundering 33.8 billion naira (approximately $24.65 million).

stories.title: US troop withdrawals from Europe don’t harm NATO defences, says top commander
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany amid a diplomatic dispute with Germany's chancellor. NATO's top commander stated that the withdrawals do not harm the alliance's overall defense posture.

stories.title: Teenagers behind mass shooting in San Diego rushed at mosque ‘fully armored’
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen, aged 17 and 18, attacked the Islamic Center of San Diego while "fully armored" with handguns and rifles registered to one of their parents. Security guard Amin Abdullah shot one attacker and alerted the school to lock down before being killed. Three people died in the attack.

stories.title: Somaliland says it will open an embassy in Jerusalem, Israel to reciprocate
stories.summary: Somaliland, a self-declared republic and breakaway region of Somalia, announced it will open an embassy in Jerusalem. The move follows Israel's decision to become the first country to formally recognize Somaliland, with Israel planning to reciprocate with its own diplomatic presence.

stories.title: US probe into strike on Iran girls' school near conclusion
stories.summary: A US investigation into a strike on a girls' school in Iran is nearing completion. The strike occurred on February 28, the first day of the conflict, and killed more than 175 children and teachers.

stories.title: New York woman dies after falling into open manhole after exiting car
stories.summary: A 56-year-old woman died after falling into an open maintenance hole on a Midtown Manhattan street near Fifth Avenue and East 52nd Street late Monday. Firefighters recovered her from the hole, but she was pronounced dead. New York authorities are investigating the circumstances.

stories.title: Google announces glasses are back and search is getting an AI makeover
stories.summary: Google announced at its annual I/O developer conference that it will expand its search engine with significant AI capabilities, enabling longer and more complex queries. The company also unveiled new AI-powered smart glasses for consumers, its first major eyewear attempt since Google Glass over a decade ago.

stories.title: ‘Maybe Putin isn’t even being told about this?’ Muscovites in two bombed districts react to Ukraine’s drone strikes.
stories.summary: On May 17, Ukraine launched a massive drone strike on the Moscow area, killing three people and wounding 16. The strikes hit the Kapotnya and Zelenograd districts, damaging an oil refinery area, defense-industry facilities, and residential buildings.

stories.title: Aluminium supply crunch threatens Asia’s clean energy push amid Iran war
stories.summary: The Middle East conflict is disrupting aluminium and nickel production, raising supply-chain risks for Asia's clean energy sector. Countries including Indonesia, Vietnam, and the Philippines face potential cost increases for solar panels, wind turbines, and grid upgrades as the blockade affects key material supplies.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran warns of ‘many more surprises’ if conflict resumes
stories.summary: Iran warned of "many more surprises" if the conflict with the United States resumes. The statement came after President Trump threatened military action and gave Tehran a two-to-three-day deadline to reach a deal.

stories.title: WHO states strike deal to extend talks on pandemic treaty
stories.summary: World Health Organization member states reached an agreement on Tuesday to extend negotiations on a global pandemic treaty. The continued discussions focus on sharing access to pathogens with pandemic potential.

stories.title: Russian missile strike hits Naftogaz facility in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a missile strike on a Naftogaz of Ukraine facility in the Chernihiv region, damaging energy infrastructure equipment.

stories.title: Lebanon says 19 killed in Israeli air strikes
stories.summary: Ten people were killed in a single strike on a house, including three children and three women, Lebanon's health ministry says.

stories.title: Nigeria says joint strikes with US kill 175 IS fighters
stories.summary: Nigeria's military announced that joint airstrikes conducted with the United States killed 175 Islamic State fighters in the country's northeast. Among those killed was Abu Bilal al-Minuki, described as IS's global second-in-command. The region has faced an extremist insurgency since 2009.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza aid flotilla, denies using live ammunition
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted an aid flotilla sailing toward Gaza on Tuesday, with video footage showing soldiers firing shots at least two vessels. Flotilla organizers said live ammunition was used, but Israel denied this and said there were no casualties. The flotilla was attempting to deliver humanitarian aid after earlier missions were intercepted.

stories.title: Court says committee’s vetting of Mossad chief appointment ‘deficient,’ asks for review
stories.summary: Israel's High Court found the committee's vetting of the Mossad chief appointment to be "deficient" and requested a review. The court recommended the appointments panel examine new documents and interview two key figures related to the petitions against Major General Gofman's selection.

stories.title: UAE and France sign new defence cooperation agreement
stories.summary: The UAE and France signed a new defence cooperation agreement during a visit by UAE Minister of State for Defence Mubarak bin Fadhel al-Mazrouei. Both sides emphasized deepening military collaboration and strategic ties.

stories.title: Pop star Harry Styles to ‘Viva Palestina’ concertgoer in Amsterdam: ‘Correct’
stories.summary: Pop star Harry Styles responded "Correct" to a concertgoer referencing "Viva Palestina" during a performance in Amsterdam. It marks his first public comment on the conflict; Styles is reportedly engaged to Jewish actor Zoe Kravitz.

stories.title: Syrskyi: Ukraine fighting Russia across three key fronts
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi stated that Ukrainian forces are engaged with Russia across three key fronts, with both sides competing for advantages in drone warfare, technology, and economic capacity.

stories.title: Vance says Iran talks making ‘good progress’, but US forces remain ‘locked and loaded’
stories.summary: US Vice President J.D. Vance stated that diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran have made "good progress" but warned the US military remains "locked and loaded" to resume operations against Iran if negotiations fail. Vance said the US would not accept any deal permitting Iran to develop nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Death toll rises to 10 after Israeli strike on south Lebanon town
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the town of Deir Qanoun en-Nahr in Lebanon's Tyre district killed 10 people, including three women and three children, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Three others were wounded.

stories.title: France invites European powers to attend July 14 Bastille Day celebrations
stories.summary: France has invited European states participating in Ukraine's "coalition of the willing" to attend its July 14 Bastille Day celebrations in Paris, according to an official invitation seen by Reuters on Tuesday.

stories.title: War update: 189 clashes on frontline, Pokrovsk sector remains hottest area
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 189 combat clashes along the frontline, with the Pokrovsk sector seeing the heaviest fighting. Russian forces launched 40 attacks on Ukrainian positions in that sector alone.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill at least 19 as clashes with Hezbollah continue despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon on Tuesday killed at least 19 people, including four women and three children, according to Lebanon's health ministry. A single strike on Deir Qanoun al Nahr in Tyre province killed 10. The attacks continued despite a US-brokered ceasefire, with Israel saying it targeted more than 25 Hezbollah sites.

stories.title: Firm finds LA county officials did not discriminate in response to Eaton fire
stories.summary: A consulting firm, Citygate Associates, found that Los Angeles County fire officials did not discriminate based on race or socioeconomic status in their evacuation response during the deadly Eaton fire in Altadena. An Altadena community group criticized the report as "pages of deflection" that relied on department insiders rather than residents.

stories.title: UAE says drone that hit near its nuclear plant was launched from Iraq
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates stated that a drone that struck near its nuclear power plant was launched from Iraq. Officials said six drones were launched against UAE territory from Iraq over a 48-hour period.

stories.title: Putin meets Xi: Why Russia and China need each other
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin traveled to Beijing to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping shortly after US President Donald Trump departed the Chinese capital. The summit underscored the strategic relationship between Moscow and Beijing amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Airbus orders spending cuts over fallout from war on Iran
stories.summary: European aerospace company Airbus has ordered staff to cut non-essential expenses by 10 percent due to instability linked to the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: NATO not drawing up plans for Hormuz mission, top commander says
stories.summary: NATO's top commander stated the alliance is not drawing up plans for a naval mission in the Strait of Hormuz. Any such mission would require unanimous approval from all 32 NATO members, and several have already signaled opposition.

stories.title: UK ‘built for climate that no longer exists’ and needs urgent changes to survive global heating, report warns
stories.summary: The UK Climate Change Committee published a landmark report warning that Britain is built for a climate that no longer exists and faces temperatures exceeding 40°C by 2050. The report recommends installing air conditioning in all care homes and hospitals within 10 years and in all schools within 25 years.

stories.title: Britain must think like a hot country – otherwise inequalities will only grow
stories.summary: The UK Climate Change Committee warned that rising temperatures will disproportionately affect vulnerable populations, with heatwaves potentially reaching 45°C.
