stories.title: Three dead in San Diego shooting as police investigate possible hate crime
stories.summary: Police in San Diego, California, are investigating a May 19 shooting at a mosque complex as a possible hate crime. Two teenage gunmen killed three people, including a security guard at the Islamic center whose response reportedly helped prevent further casualties.

stories.title: South Korea’s Lee hails ‘deep friendship’ as he hosts Japan’s Takaichi in hometown
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung hosted Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in his hometown of Andong for their fourth meeting in approximately six months. The leaders emphasized greater bilateral cooperation amid global challenges, including the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Russia-China trade set to lead talks between two leaders
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is heading to Beijing for a two-day visit and talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, with Moscow expressing "high expectations" for the discussions. The visit comes less than a week after US President Donald Trump concluded his own trip to China. Bilateral trade is expected to be a central topic.

stories.title: After Trump’s exit, Putin enters Beijing — with a gas price gap and Ukraine on the table
stories.summary: Russian President Putin visited Beijing days after US President Trump's departure, seeking a natural gas pricing agreement and signals on Ukraine. Moscow is also looking for reassurance that improving US-China relations will not sideline Russian interests.

stories.title: Deadly attack by teen gunmen on a San Diego mosque
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen opened fire at the Islamic Center of San Diego, killing three men before killing themselves nearby. San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl said the shooting is being investigated as a hate crime. Police had been racing to locate one of the teens, an armed runaway, before the attack.

stories.title: Musk vs Altman: What to know about the OpenAI verdict
stories.summary: A court ruled in the legal dispute between Elon Musk and Sam Altman over OpenAI. Musk has announced plans to appeal the verdict, indicating the legal battle will continue.

stories.title: Nato jet shot down reported stray Ukrainian drone over Estonia, defence minister says – Europe live
stories.summary: A NATO jet shot down a reported stray Ukrainian drone over Estonia, according to Estonian Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur. The incident came as Ukraine and Latvia were forced to refute Russian claims that Kyiv was preparing attacks against Russia from Latvian territory.

stories.title: Russia is holding at least 100 people in occupied Crimea with no contact with outside world and no lawyer — and no trials
stories.summary: At least 100 people are being held by Russia in occupied Crimea without access to lawyers, outside contact, or trials. A Ukrainian human rights monitor reports that sentences for the same charges that previously drew 7–10 years now result in 10–20 year terms.

stories.title: Voters in six states head to polls with Kentucky’s Massie facing Trump’s fury – US politics live
stories.summary: Voters headed to the polls in primaries across six US states, with the Kentucky race seen as a test of President Donald Trump's influence over the Republican Party. Trump urged voters to reject Representative Thomas Massie, one of the few senior Republicans who has defied him. Police also investigated a deadly shooting at a San Diego mosque as a hate crime.

stories.title: U.S. Extends Russian Oil Waiver for a Second Time
stories.summary: The United States extended a temporary general license waiving certain sanctions on Russian oil, now effective until June 17. The license had briefly lapsed over the preceding weekend before being renewed for a second time.

stories.title: U.S. to host G20 foreign ministers' meet in Atlanta on October 30-31
stories.summary: The United States will host a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on October 30–31. Spokesperson Tommy Pigott said discussions will focus on international cooperation, global economic challenges, and supporting open markets and resilient supply chains.

stories.title: Workers on New York commuter rail end their strike after wage deal
stories.summary: Workers on a New York commuter rail line ended their strike after reaching a wage deal with management. The workers said they had gone three years without any wage increases prior to the agreement.

stories.title: Russians attack Naftogaz facilities with ballistic missiles in Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: On the evening of May 18, Russian forces struck Naftogaz Group facilities in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region with three ballistic missiles.

stories.title: Two bodies of missing Italians recovered from inside Maldives cave
stories.summary: The bodies of two missing Italian divers were recovered from the deepest chamber of an underwater cave in the Maldives. The pair were among four divers located inside the cave, and specialist divers carried out the recovery operation.

stories.title: 'Cancer of the Jewish community': Amb. Leiter slams J Street's support of arms embargo on Israel
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador to the US Yechiel Leiter called J Street a "cancer of the Jewish community" over its support for an arms embargo on Israel. J Street recently shifted its position to advocate phasing out direct US military aid to Israel, including Iron Dome-related funding.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition vote to impeach President Lai fails
stories.summary: An opposition-led effort to impeach Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te failed in the legislature. Lawmakers from the Kuomintang and Taiwan People's Party had initiated proceedings after President Lai and his premier refused to sign a revenue-sharing bill passed by Parliament.

stories.title: Israel can expect 'tens or hundreds of missiles a day' if Iran war renews, expert warns
stories.summary: A security expert warned that Israel could face tens or hundreds of missiles per day if hostilities with Iran resume. President Trump noted on social media that Gulf state leaders had asked him to delay any military strike on Iran.

stories.title: DeepSeek recruits former Jane Street engineer to catch up on AI agents, revenue race
stories.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, based in Hangzhou, has hired former Jane Street engineer Cui Tianyi to lead its new AI "harness" team. Cui previously co-founded Hong Kong-based quantitative trading firm TSY Capital in 2022. The recruitment signals DeepSeek's push to compete in the agentic AI market.

stories.title: French and Algerian Ministers promote cooperation amid diplomatic thaw
stories.summary: French Justice Minister visited Algeria as diplomatic relations between the two countries begin to thaw. Discussions covered illegally acquired assets and the case of detained French journalist Christophe Gleizes. The visit signals broader Franco-Algerian cooperation after a period of strained ties.

stories.title: Rd Congo sounds alarm over Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo announced plans to open three Ebola treatment centres as the WHO dispatches experts to the country. At least 131 people have died and over 500 have been infected with the rare Bundibugyo strain. The US has begun screening passengers arriving from outbreak-affected areas.

stories.title: Putin trip aims to show China ties unshakeable after Trump pomp
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin traveled to Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, aiming to demonstrate strong bilateral ties days after U.S. President Donald Trump concluded his own visit to China.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 19: Trump frustrated as Iran talks stall, Gulf wary of renewed war
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations have stalled, frustrating President Trump, while Gulf states express concern over the possibility of renewed military conflict. The situation is further complicated by an emboldened Hamas in Gaza and ongoing Fatah central committee elections.

stories.title: San Diego police treating mosque shooting as hate crime
stories.summary: Two teenage shooters killed three people at a mosque in San Diego before taking their own lives several blocks away. San Diego police are investigating the attack as a hate crime. Authorities found evidence the suspects engaged in generalised hate rhetoric, though no specific prior threats against the mosque were identified.

stories.title: Border drill: Belarus district near Ukraine rehearses rocket strike making mass casualties
stories.summary: A Belarusian district near the Ukrainian border conducted a drill simulating a rocket strike causing mass casualties and utility blackouts. The exercise comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has warned of Russian attacks being launched from Belarusian territory.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Better Without Crude Oil, Renowned Environmentalists Insists
stories.summary: Nigerian environmental activist Nnimmo Bassey, executive director of the Health of Mother Earth Foundation, argued that Nigeria was economically and socially better off before crude oil became the country's dominant revenue source.

stories.title: Russia’s fakes stopped reaching Ukraine. So it changed the target
stories.summary: A Ukrainian military intelligence official detailed how Russia's disinformation strategy has shifted from targeting Ukrainian audiences to focusing on domestic Russian consumers.

stories.title: What will Russia and China's leaders discuss over two-day visit?
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit China on May 19–20 for talks with President Xi Jinping, with Moscow seeking to deepen what the Kremlin calls their "privileged partnership." The visit follows US President Trump's recent meeting with Xi in Beijing. Analysts note the asymmetric nature of the Russia-China relationship.

stories.title: Chinese aircraft carrier kicks off drills in western Pacific amid tense Japan ties
stories.summary: China's Liaoning aircraft carrier began training exercises in the western Pacific on Tuesday, including live-fire drills and far-sea tactical flights. State broadcaster CCTV reported the carrier task group's activities, though the Chinese navy did not specify the exact location. The drills come amid heightened tensions between Beijing and Tokyo.

stories.title: Russia’s Defense Ministry announces start of nuclear drills with live launches of ballistic and cruise missiles
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry announced nuclear readiness drills from May 19 to 21, simulating conditions of an imminent threat of aggression, including live launches of ballistic and cruise missiles.

stories.title: Dutch authorities expect more cruise ship outbreaks as hantavirus-hit vessel docks
stories.summary: A cruise ship affected by a deadly hantavirus outbreak docked in Rotterdam, Netherlands, for disinfection. The crew will be placed in quarantine before the vessel departs for Iceland to begin another voyage on May 29. Dutch authorities expect further cruise ship outbreaks.

stories.title: Trump says holding off on strike on Iran at request of Gulf allies
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said on May 18 that he paused a planned military strike against Iran at the request of Gulf allies. Trump described ongoing peace talks with Tehran as "very positive," marking a shift from thinly veiled threats he had issued over the preceding weekend.

stories.title: Irish president 'very worried' about sister detained by Israel
stories.summary: Irish President Catherine Connolly expressed deep concern over the detention of her sister Margaret by Israeli forces. Margaret Connolly was aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla seized near Cyprus, and is one of at least six Irish citizens detained.

stories.title: Russian army shells Sumy region nearly 110 times in one day
stories.summary: The Russian military shelled settlements in Ukraine's Sumy region nearly 110 times between the morning of May 18 and the morning of May 19, causing significant destruction and injuring two people.

stories.title: Rep. Jared Moskowitz becomes latest US Jewish lawmaker to reveal antisemitic threats
stories.summary: US Representative Jared Moskowitz, a Florida Democrat, publicly shared antisemitic threats he has received, including messages calling for violence against Jews. Moskowitz said the United States has crossed a threshold in anti-Jewish hatred.

stories.title: Ebola may be spreading faster than first thought, WHO doctor warns
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned that the Ebola outbreak in central Africa may be spreading faster than initially assessed. Hundreds of cases are suspected, but experts fear the true number could be significantly higher.

stories.title: In 1961, Typhoon Alice claims 4 lives in Hong Kong – SCMP archive
stories.summary: In May 1961, Typhoon Alice struck Hong Kong, killing four people—two women and two children—and injuring around 20 others. The storm set two new records but caused comparatively little damage relative to a severe storm that hit the colony in June 1960.

stories.title: Cuba says it has right to defend itself in case of US attack
stories.summary: Cuban President warned of retaliation in case of a US military attack, asserting Cuba's "legitimate right to defend itself." The statement followed rising tensions after President Trump alluded to taking over the island and imposed additional sanctions on the communist nation.

stories.title: At least 131 dead in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: One US national who contracted Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo was evacuated to Germany for treatment. The Bundibugyo strain continues to circulate in the DRC, prompting travel warnings and entry restrictions for non-US citizens recently in affected regions including Uganda, the DRC, and South Sudan.

stories.title: Musk loses Open AI lawsuit as jury says it was filed too late
stories.summary: A federal jury ruled that Elon Musk filed his lawsuit against OpenAI too late, handing a defeat to the world's richest man. The trial in California featured testimony from prominent Silicon Valley figures. Musk had accused OpenAI's leadership of misleading the public about plans to convert the nonprofit into a for-profit entity.

stories.title: WHO to hold emergency committee meeting as Ebola death toll rises to 131
stories.summary: The WHO is convening an emergency committee meeting to evaluate vaccine options as a new Ebola epidemic has claimed at least 131 lives. The expert panel will assess strategies to contain the outbreak.

stories.title: Elon Musk loses his court battle against Sam Altman's OpenAI, but vows to keep fighting
stories.summary: A California court ruled that Elon Musk waited too long to sue OpenAI over its transition from a nonprofit to a for-profit entity. Separately, Standard Chartered announced plans to cut thousands of jobs while accelerating AI adoption and fired its South Korea CEO over a controversial promotional campaign.

stories.title: Stalled US-Iran talks show "Trump's strategy of pressure" is not paying off
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he called off strikes against Iran following advice from Gulf countries, amid stalled US-Iran negotiations. Neither Washington nor Tehran has shown willingness to compromise on key demands. The Gulf states' strategic interests have influenced the diplomatic dynamics after weeks of conflict.

stories.title: Campaigners warn Italy’s gutted rape bill could help assailants
stories.summary: Italian campaigners have raised concerns that a revised rape bill, stripped of key provisions, could be exploited by assailants. A politician warned the weakened legislation might be used for revenge and called for the bill to be reworded before passage.

stories.title: Iran squad in race against time for World Cup readiness amid US-Israel war
stories.summary: Iran's national football squad faces significant preparation challenges for the upcoming World Cup after the country's domestic league was suspended since March due to the US-Israel war. Most squad members have been inactive for months.

stories.title: Calls grow for US-China energy trade expansion after Trump’s visit – but is it feasible?
stories.summary: The American Chamber of Commerce in China called for expanded US-China energy trade following President Donald Trump's state visit to Beijing. Board member Markel Hubinette emphasized energy as central to the bilateral relationship. Analysts cautioned that uncompetitive pricing could limit Chinese demand for US energy exports.

stories.title: Legacy in ink: how calligraphy links China’s political heritage to academic institutions
stories.summary: Prestigious Chinese universities traditionally display their names in calligraphy inscribed by prominent political leaders on entrance gates. The practice reflects both political heritage and academic prestige. Calligraphy has been a revered art form in China since ancient times, with its aesthetics historically regulated by imperial authority.

stories.title: Lights out for Cuban students as blockade bites
stories.summary: A U.S. fuel blockade on Cuba has deepened the island's energy crisis, leaving residents without electricity for up to 20 hours per day. The prolonged outages are severely disrupting daily life, including students' ability to study.

stories.title: Zelensky, Magyar may meet in coming months — Politico
stories.summary: According to Politico, Ukrainian President Zelensky and Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar may meet in the coming months. Budapest's willingness to discuss Hungarian minority rights in Ukraine signals Hungary may support the launch of formal EU membership negotiations for Kyiv.

stories.title: EU ties part of Ukraine $134 billion aid to unpopular tax measure
stories.summary: The European Union has linked part of a $134 billion aid package for Ukraine to an unpopular tax measure. The requirement applies to the macro-financial portion of the loan, worth €8.4 billion, drawing criticism from Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Middle East Eye: ICC could seek arrest warrant for Israel's Bezalel Smotrich
stories.summary: Middle East Eye reported that the International Criminal Court may seek an arrest warrant for Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich on charges of war crimes, crimes against humanity, and apartheid. Separately, Donald Trump dropped a lawsuit against the IRS in exchange for the creation of a nearly $2 billion fund.

stories.title: Standard Chartered to cut more than 7,000 jobs as it steps up AI use
stories.summary: Standard Chartered announced plans to cut more than 7,000 jobs over the next four years as the London-headquartered bank accelerates its adoption of artificial intelligence. The lender aims to streamline back-office operations and move some workers to new roles to boost profitability.

stories.title: Xi pledged to stop arming Iran—US intelligence warns the weapons still flow
stories.summary: Despite Chinese President Xi Jinping's pledge to halt arms transfers to Iran, U.S. intelligence agencies report that covert Chinese weapons shipments continue to reach Iran through third countries. No formal agreement or monitoring mechanism has been signed.

stories.title: Germany to deploy Patriot battery to Turkey, relieving US forces on NATO’s southeastern flank
stories.summary: Germany has announced it will deploy a Patriot air-defense battery to Turkey to help intercept Iranian missiles, a move Berlin describes as NATO burden-sharing on the alliance's southeastern flank. The deployment is intended to relieve U.S. forces previously tasked with that mission.

stories.title: WHO warns of ‘scale and speed’ of deadly Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo an international health emergency, with an estimated 131 deaths reported. WHO chief expressed concern about the outbreak's "scale and speed." No vaccine or treatment exists for the Bundibugyo strain responsible for the current surge.

stories.title: Settlers said to torch Palestinian fields, block fire trucks from reaching scene
stories.summary: Israeli settlers reportedly set fire to Palestinian agricultural fields in the West Bank and blocked fire trucks from reaching the blaze. Palestinian news agencies claim Israeli soldiers also prevented emergency services from responding to the fires.

stories.title: Iran says its new proposal demands reparations, US troop withdrawal, end to Lebanon war
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran's latest negotiating proposal demands reparations, US troop withdrawal from the region, and an end to the war in Lebanon. The offer also reportedly stipulates the release of frozen Iranian funds and the end of a US blockade.

stories.title: The US, Israel and the normalisation of scandal
stories.summary: The article discusses how recurring scandals involving Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump have become normalized in political discourse, characterizing the phenomenon as a permanent state of overlapping controversies.

stories.title: Bodies of 2 Italian divers recovered from ‘well inside’ underwater cave in Maldives
stories.summary: Finnish divers recovered the bodies of two of four remaining Italian divers who died inside an underwater cave in a Maldives atoll. A local military diver had previously died during rescue efforts, prompting a temporary suspension of search operations. One of the five missing Italian divers' bodies had been recovered earlier.

stories.title: US claims ‘emergency refugee situation’ as it admits 10,000 more white South Africans
stories.summary: The US government announced it will increase admissions of white South African refugees from approximately 7,500 to 17,500 this year, citing an "emergency refugee situation." President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed white Afrikaners face genocide, assertions South Africa's government has firmly denied.

stories.title: Palestinian president’s son vows to put ‘Gaza first’
stories.summary: Yasser Abbas, son of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, has pledged to prioritize Gaza and return it to what he called "the fold of Palestinian legitimacy." His statement signals an effort to reassert Palestinian Authority influence over the territory.

stories.title: Khartoum’s slow recovery amid cautious return
stories.summary: Khartoum, Sudan, is experiencing an uneven recovery following extensive war damage. Residents are cautiously returning to the city but face fragile public services and a struggling economy.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Kharkiv and Kharkiv region leave two killed, 12 injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck Kharkiv and 13 settlements across the Kharkiv region over the past day, killing two people and injuring 12 others, including a child.

stories.title: Donald Trump says held off on new Iran attack, upbeat for agreement
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he paused a planned military strike on Iran after what he called a "very positive development" in negotiations. Trump stated that Arab allies indicated a deal was near that would leave Iran without nuclear weapons, a goal Tehran denies pursuing.

stories.title: Xi told Trump Putin could come to regret the Ukraine war, FT reportes
stories.summary: According to the Financial Times, Chinese President Xi Jinping told U.S. President Donald Trump that Russian President Vladimir Putin could come to regret the war in Ukraine. Sources say this is the first time Xi has offered such an assessment to a U.S. president.

stories.title: China’s rapid chipmaking expansion threatens AI memory chip boom, Samsung adviser warns
stories.summary: A Samsung Electronics executive adviser warned that the AI-driven memory chip "super cycle" may lose momentum by 2028 due to aggressive production expansion by Chinese chipmakers and reduced global tech spending. Adviser Kyung Kye-hyun urged caution for 2027 at a forum hosted by South Korea's National Academy of Engineering.

stories.title: Why the Philippines wants Japan’s old Type 88 missiles
stories.summary: The Philippines has expressed interest in acquiring Japan's retiring Type 88 surface-to-ship missile system. Manila's interest coincided with joint drills between Japanese, American, and Philippine forces demonstrating the missile. The potential transfer has sparked debate extending beyond the aging weapon's technical specifications.

stories.title: Irish president's sister on Gaza flotilla 'kidnapped' by Israel
stories.summary: Irish President Catherine Connolly's sister Margaret released a pre-recorded video saying she would have been "kidnapped" by Israeli forces if the footage was being viewed. She was aboard a Gaza-bound flotilla that was intercepted by the Israeli military.

stories.title: Starbucks Korea CEO fired over promotion that evoked military crackdown
stories.summary: Starbucks Korea's CEO was dismissed after a promotional campaign dubbed "Tank Day" drew public backlash. Critics said the marketing evoked the violent suppression of the 1980 Gwangju pro-democracy uprising in South Korea.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 180 of 209 Russian drones since yesterday evening
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 180 of 209 drones launched by Russia against Ukraine starting on the evening of May 18.

stories.title: S.Sudan inaugurates first Air Traffic Management Control System
stories.summary: South Sudan inaugurated its first national Air Traffic Management Control System, built by China. Officials described the launch as a step toward the country gaining full control of its airspace.

stories.title: American tests positive for Ebola in Congo outbreak, CDC says US risk remains low
stories.summary: An American individual in the Democratic Republic of the Congo tested positive for Ebola after developing symptoms over the weekend. The CDC stated that the risk to the U.S. public remains low despite the confirmed case.

stories.title: Polish officials vent worries over scrapped US troop deployment
stories.summary: Polish officials have expressed concern over the cancellation of a planned U.S. troop deployment to Poland. Defense Minister highlighted that Poland has committed over fifty billion dollars in military purchases from the United States, underscoring the country's expectations for reciprocal security cooperation.

stories.title: At least two dead, four others injured in southern Spain shooting
stories.summary: At least two people were killed and four others injured in a shooting in southern Spain. A Civil Guard spokesperson said the deceased were related to the suspected shooter, without providing further details.

stories.title: China’s military drills are region’s greatest source of instability, Taiwan premier says
stories.summary: Taiwan's premier described China's military drills around the island as the region's greatest source of instability. China's armed forces operate near Taiwan almost daily, conducting live-fire exercises and other training operations.

stories.title: ‘Aid workers are targeted’: Russian drones strike UN convoy in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian drones struck a UN humanitarian convoy delivering aid to civilians in Ukraine's southern Kherson region on May 14. Russian military bloggers initially published footage of the attack before deleting it. The incident highlighted the targeting of aid workers in the conflict zone.

stories.title: ‘China holds the cards’: Why Putin’s visit to Beijing after Trump matters
stories.summary: Russian President Putin visited Beijing shortly after US President Trump, amid limited progress in US-China trade talks. Analysts say the back-to-back visits serve as a diplomatic signal from China, while Putin seeks reassurance that warming US-China ties will not marginalize Moscow.

stories.title: Croatia's president refuses to approve new Israeli ambassador
stories.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanovic refused to approve Israel's proposed new ambassador to Zagreb. Milanovic, a vocal critic of Israel's military operations in Gaza, stated the nominee would not receive his approval.

stories.title: Child survivor of San Diego mosque shooting describes ordeal
stories.summary: A child survivor of a shooting at a mosque in San Diego described witnessing the attack, which killed three people. The boy recounted seeing disturbing scenes during the incident.

stories.title: Terrorists 'will be brought to justice,' San Diego mayor warns after deadly mosque shooting
stories.summary: San Diego Mayor warned that those responsible for a deadly shooting at the city's largest mosque would be brought to justice. Police Chief Scott Wahl confirmed that local law enforcement and the FBI are investigating the attack as a hate crime.

stories.title: Nazi salutes in class: Report details growing antisemitic abuse in British schools
stories.summary: A report documents rising antisemitic abuse in British schools, including students performing Nazi salutes in classrooms. Parents described incidents ranging from Holocaust-related harassment to threats of violence against Jewish students.

stories.title: Pentagon’s internal watchdog to probe US attacks on boats in the Caribbean
stories.summary: The Pentagon's internal watchdog has launched an investigation into U.S. attacks on boats in the Caribbean. As of last week, up to 58 attacks on vessels have been reported in the region.

stories.title: WHO head ‘deeply concerned’ by Ebola outbreak as cases and deaths rise in DRC
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus expressed deep concern about the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, reporting at least 500 suspected cases and 130 suspected deaths. Thirty cases were confirmed in DRC's northeastern Ituri province. An emergency committee meeting was convened to address the crisis.

stories.title: Teachers protest abduction of Gwadar University VC, others
stories.summary: Academic staff associations at Balochistan University protested the abduction of Gwadar University Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Abdul Razzaq Sabir, the pro-VC, and other officials who were kidnapped in Mastung district while traveling to Quetta five days earlier.

stories.title: Why Elon Musk’s post spotlighting Chinese infrastructure has reignited a debate
stories.summary: SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk reposted a video of Chongqing East Railway Station in southwestern China on his social media platform X, drawing millions of views. The post reignited debate about Chinese infrastructure development. It was unclear whether Musk was personally visiting Chongqing at the time.

stories.title: War update: 236 clashes in past day, Ukrainian forces repel 40 attacks in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 236 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front lines on May 18, including 40 repelled attacks in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: What Is Bundibugyo? The rare ebola strain with no vaccine
stories.summary: A rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists, has been identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province and has spread across the border into Uganda. This marks only the third recorded outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain.

stories.title: Is Ukraine about to repeat Hitler´s mistake with the London Blitz?
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Ukraine risks making a strategic error if it shifts to striking Russian civilian infrastructure, drawing a comparison to historically counterproductive bombing campaigns. The piece also contends that Western support for Ukraine remains insufficient.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda Bans Handshakes As Ebola Response Measures Tighten
stories.summary: Uganda's Ministry of Health temporarily banned handshakes and other physical greetings after two confirmed Ebola cases crossed into the country from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Uganda: U.S. Embassy in Kampala Suspends Visa Services Over Ebola Outbreak
stories.summary: The U.S. Embassy in Kampala temporarily suspended all visa operations in Uganda, citing concerns related to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the region.

stories.title: Elon Musk loses blockbuster OpenAI suit as jury says too late
stories.summary: A jury ruled against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI, finding that his claims were filed too late. The verdict came after a three-week trial in which several prominent technology executives testified.

stories.title: Sweden orders 4 frigates from French company Naval Group
stories.summary: Sweden ordered four new frigates from French shipbuilder Naval Group in a deal worth billions, with delivery beginning in 2030. The vessels will be the largest surface warships in Sweden's navy as the newest NATO member accelerates its military buildup.

stories.title: At least 10 dead as huge floods sweep southern and central China
stories.summary: Severe flooding across southern and central China has killed at least 10 people. Chinese meteorologists report the affected area extends more than 1,000 kilometers.

stories.title: Indonesian authorities used fake news to brand critics as ‘foreign agents’: Amnesty
stories.summary: Amnesty International reported that Indonesian authorities, including the military, used online disinformation campaigns to label activists and journalists as "foreign agents" to suppress dissent. The report raised concerns about democratic backsliding under President Prabowo Subianto, a former special forces commander who has expanded the military's role in governance.

stories.title: Israeli attack kills one in Lebanon's Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: An Israeli drone struck a motorcycle in Froun, near Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon, killing one person. The Israeli military also carried out an airstrike on the same town, while the nearby town of Beit Yahoun was subjected to artillery shelling.

stories.title: Warehouse damaged in Odesa region after overnight Russian drone attack
stories.summary: A warehouse in the Izmail district of Odesa region was damaged during an overnight Russian drone strike on May 19.

stories.title: Hong Kong lifts flat resale curbs for Tai Po fire survivors under buy-back plan
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government announced it will lift resale restrictions on replacement subsidised housing for flat owners displaced by the Tai Po fire. Affected owners will receive two-year vouchers to purchase second-hand subsidised homes under a special buy-back scheme, granting them greater flexibility to sell on the secondary market.

stories.title: Uproar after Channel 14 anchor talks about Iran strategy without censor approval
stories.summary: Israeli Channel 14 anchor Shimon Riklin sparked controversy by discussing Iran-related military strategy on air without obtaining prior approval from Israel's military censor. Lawmakers called for an urgent Knesset defense committee meeting on the matter.

stories.title: 'Your only friend right now is Mr. Xi: Normal practice for Putin to go to China every year'
stories.summary: Analyst Aleksei Chigadaev described the Russia-China relationship as marked by asymmetry and strategic necessity rather than an equal anti-Western alliance. He argued that President Putin increasingly seeks legitimacy through encounters with Xi Jinping, while China approaches Moscow with calculated pragmatism. Putin travels to China annually for talks.

stories.title: In closed-door talks, US demands a major role in Greenland
stories.summary: The United States has been pressing for a major role in Greenland during closed-door negotiations. U.S. officials have pushed discussions beyond military matters into broader areas of influence over the territory.

stories.title: The World Keeps Asking Iran the Wrong Question
stories.summary: The article examines longstanding questions about Iran's geopolitical ambitions, arguing that the international community has consistently misframed the issue. It suggests that Iran's core strategic objectives have remained consistent since before the establishment of the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: The World Keeps Asking Iran the Wrong Question
stories.summary: The article examines Iran's longstanding geopolitical aspirations, arguing that the country's core objectives predate the Islamic Republic. It suggests that international discourse often frames the wrong questions when analyzing Iran's strategic motivations and regional ambitions.

stories.title: US passenger on hantavirus-hit cruise blocked from leaving federal quarantine
stories.summary: A U.S. passenger aboard a cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak has been blocked from leaving federal quarantine. Health officials warned they would contact law enforcement if the individual attempted to depart the quarantine facility.

stories.title: Israel allocates NIS 2b. to counter Hezbollah’s lethal fiber-optic drone threat
stories.summary: Israel has allocated approximately NIS 2 billion to develop countermeasures against Hezbollah's fiber-optic-guided drone capabilities. The funding comes from a NIS 4 billion reserve within the Ministry of Defense budget designated for prime ministerial priorities.

stories.title: Quantum IPO wave is a milestone. It should also come with a warning
stories.summary: A surge in stock offerings by quantum computing firms suggests 2026 could be a breakout year for the sector, though commercial viability remains uncertain. China's development of the world's first dual-core quantum computer has sustained investor optimism. Analysts caution that timelines for quantum computing breakthroughs remain unpredictable.

stories.title: Palestine on BRICS agenda
stories.summary: BRICS foreign ministers meeting in New Delhi declared support for an independent Palestinian state through a two-state solution. The unanimous agreement came despite differing positions among member nations on the broader conflict.

stories.title: Ebola: DR Congo death toll rises sharply to at least 131, WHO to host emergency meeting
stories.summary: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo rose sharply to at least 131, with 513 suspected cases reported. DRC Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba provided the updated figures. The WHO convened an emergency committee meeting on Tuesday to address the crisis.

stories.title: Silk Road Virtual Museum opens first Israel exhibit, displays ancient textiles found in Arava
stories.summary: The Silk Road Virtual Museum opened its first exhibit in Israel, displaying ancient textiles from India, Central Asia, and China discovered in the Arava region. The exhibit was curated by academics from the University of Haifa.

stories.title: Man injured in Russian drone attack in Kherson
stories.summary: A man sustained injuries in a Russian drone attack targeting the Korabelnyi district of Kherson.

stories.title: Pocock urges CGT changes as Albanese laughs off AI meme campaign
stories.summary: Australian independent Senator David Pocock warned that proposed capital gains tax changes in the federal budget could drive tech investment offshore. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dismissed an AI-generated meme campaign by startup founders opposing the tax reforms, thanking them for "very flattering" images.

stories.title: Iran will not 'surrender,' Pezeshkian says after Trump claims Iran-US dialogue progress
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian declared that Iran would not surrender, responding to Trump's claim that diplomatic progress was being made after Tehran reportedly sent a peace proposal to Washington.

stories.title: Energy bills will rise by £209 in July to £1,850 a year, forecast says
stories.summary: Energy bills for households in Great Britain are forecast to rise by £209 to £1,850 per year from July, according to consultancy Cornwall Insight. The projected 13% increase in the Ofgem price cap is attributed to rising gas costs linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Ex-HSBC banker acquitted of assaulting wife amid divorce battle
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court acquitted former HSBC banker Kenneth Tung Hoi-yi of assaulting his wife at their Redhill Peninsula home. The Eastern Court suggested the wife may have attempted to frame him to gain advantage in divorce proceedings. Tung was awarded legal costs following the verdict.

stories.title: Ugandan government sets up border controls amid DRC Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Uganda's health authorities established border screening measures near Bundibugyo in western Uganda in response to the Ebola outbreak in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. Workers are checking temperatures and facilitating hand-washing at border points.

stories.title: San Diego mosque shooting: What we know about the victims and the attackers
stories.summary: Authorities are investigating the shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, which killed three people, as a possible hate crime. Details about the victims and the suspected attackers are emerging as the investigation continues.

stories.title: China will open its market to AI chips from US, Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang says
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced that China will open its market to AI chips from the United States. Huang was a last-minute addition to the delegation of U.S. business leaders attending the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing.

stories.title: Sindh Assembly passes bill for legal cover to household workers
stories.summary: The Sindh Assembly passed the Domestic Workers Welfare Bill 2025, establishing formal protections for household workers including rest breaks, medical care, and minimum meal provisions. The bill requires the governor's assent to become law.

stories.title: When humanity meets the sea: Surfing as a source of solace from trauma
stories.summary: Surf therapy programs in Israel are being used as a tool for coping with trauma and mental health challenges. Practitioners say the experience gained in Israel can provide innovative therapeutic approaches internationally.

stories.title: Russian army loses 1,140 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces lost an estimated 1,140 personnel over the past 24 hours in Ukraine, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, to approximately 1,351,150.

stories.title: Israeli envoy to US calls J Street a ‘cancer within the Jewish community’
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the United States, Yechiel Leiter, described the liberal Zionist lobby group J Street as a "cancer within the Jewish community" and called it "duplicitous." J Street's leadership responded that Israel should engage with the organization rather than resorting to insults.

stories.title: Water win
stories.summary: The Permanent Court of Arbitration issued a supplemental award on Pakistan's challenge to the design of two Indian hydropower projects on rivers allocated to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty, reaffirming the treaty's binding nature on both parties.

stories.title: Gunmen abduct 39 students, 7 teachers in attacks on Nigeria schools
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a secondary school and two primary schools in Nigeria, abducting 39 students and seven teachers. The kidnapped children ranged in age from two to 16 years old.

stories.title: Air-con repairman dies after falling from 11th floor of Kowloon City building
stories.summary: A 38-year-old air-conditioner repairman died after falling from the 11th floor of Billionnaire Avant, a residential building in Kowloon City, Hong Kong. The man had climbed out of a bathroom window without protective gear to repair an air conditioning unit. Police received the report at 12:15 p.m. on Tuesday.

stories.title: Apple readies AI writing help, app shortcuts and wallpapers for iOS 27
stories.summary: Apple is preparing new artificial intelligence writing assistance features, app shortcuts, and wallpapers for iOS 27. The software update is expected to be released to the public in September.

stories.title: Israel's Netanyahu praises naval forces for raiding Gaza-bound flotilla
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised naval forces for intercepting a Gaza-bound flotilla on Monday. The Global Sumud Flotilla said Israeli naval forces raided and seized several of its vessels near Cyprus in international waters.

stories.title: China will ‘actively’ help to resolve international conflicts, ex-diplomat says
stories.summary: Former Chinese diplomat Han Zhiqiang said at the Global Prosperity Summit in Hong Kong that China will actively participate in settling international conflicts. He highlighted Hong Kong's potential role as a bridge for exchanges and noted that a recently established mediation body in the city could bolster international rule of law.

stories.title: SC lays down rules for uniformity in civil pleadings
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court issued guidelines to promote uniformity in civil pleadings at the trial court level. The court directed trial courts to scrutinize plaints at the initial stage and asked bar councils to consider standard formats.

stories.title: India will be ‘relegated to history’ if it attempts misadventure against Pakistan: Khawaja Asif
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif warned that India would be "relegated to history" if it attempted any military misadventure against Pakistan, referencing last year's military confrontation that ended with a ceasefire on May 10.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Kryvyi Rih, woman injured
stories.summary: Russian drones struck Kryvyi Rih overnight, injuring a woman and damaging several residential buildings in the city.

stories.title: Lebanon and Syria reshape ties amid Israeli attacks and regional shifts
stories.summary: Lebanon and Syria are recalibrating their bilateral relationship amid ongoing Israeli military operations and broader regional shifts. The two governments are focusing on sovereignty and cooperation, departing from decades of Syrian dominance over Lebanese affairs.

stories.title: Los Angeles World Cup stadium workers threaten strike over ICE deployment
stories.summary: Workers at a Los Angeles stadium slated for the 2026 FIFA World Cup are threatening to strike over planned ICE deployment during the tournament. Their union says the immigration enforcement presence would create a climate of fear.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Jerusalem Day, Nakba mark week of surging attacks
stories.summary: Jerusalem Day and Nakba commemorations marked a week of escalating violence in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Far-right marchers chanted anti-Arab slogans in Jerusalem's Old City, while Israel killed a senior Hamas military commander in Gaza.

stories.title: China’s Moonshot AI moves to unwind offshore structure in IPO pursuit: sources
stories.summary: Beijing-based AI startup Moonshot AI, creator of the Kimi chatbot, is planning to dismantle its offshore Cayman Islands variable interest entity structure to pursue an initial public offering, likely in Hong Kong. The company has informed shareholders and sought investor feedback on the restructuring plan.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump claims Iran attack ‘on hold’ due to request from Gulf allies
stories.summary: President Trump said he postponed a planned military attack on Iran at the request of Gulf allies to allow peace talks to continue. Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran's proposal to the U.S. calls for lifting sanctions, releasing frozen funds, ending a marine blockade, and stopping hostilities on all fronts including Israel's operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A regional roundup noted that Israeli forces intercepted additional Gaza-bound aid boats, prompting protests and diplomatic criticism. Iran accused the U.S. of undermining diplomacy, while military activity continued in Lebanon and a majority of U.S. voters opposed escalation with Tehran.

stories.title: Nigeria: Typhoid Fever - Drink Clean Water, Wash Hands Regularly, Eat Safe Food
stories.summary: Nigerian health authorities are urging the public to drink clean water, wash hands regularly, and eat safe food to prevent typhoid fever, which spreads through contaminated food and water in areas with poor sanitation.

stories.title: Nigeria: AfDB Unveils $200m Support Package for Nigeria's Industrial Sector
stories.summary: The African Development Bank Group approved a $200 million financing facility for Nigeria's Bank of Industry to boost industrial growth and strengthen private sector productivity across key economic sectors.

stories.title: When Refusal Doesn’t Matter: Operation Epic Fury and the Erosion of Host Nation Consent
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the U.S. military's Operation Epic Fury against Iran in February 2026 proceeded despite allies refusing to grant base access, undermining the principle of host nation consent. The article argues that inward flows of U.S. military assets to allied territories during crises may prove more consequential than outward redeployments.

stories.title: Russian strike damages Ukraine Danube port as Moscow intercepts drones
stories.summary: A Russian strike damaged a Ukrainian port on the Danube River, while Moscow intercepted incoming drones. Russia also announced planned military exercises as President Putin prepared for a visit to Beijing.

stories.title: Iran war day 81: Trump delays attack; Tehran says won’t ‘surrender’
stories.summary: On day 81 of the Iran conflict, President Trump confirmed he postponed a scheduled attack on Iran following pressure from Gulf state allies. Tehran responded by declaring it would not surrender, even as renewed diplomatic talks gain momentum.

stories.title: Russian drone attack damages port infrastructure in Izmail
stories.summary: Russian drones targeted the city of Izmail overnight, damaging port infrastructure facilities. Authorities reported the consequences of the strike have been addressed.

stories.title: Ukraine announces its first “Equalizer” for asymmetric warfare: 250 kg warhead, no donor restrictions, third of US JDAM-ER cost
stories.summary: Ukraine announced its first domestically produced precision glide bomb, called the Equalizer, featuring a 250-kilogram warhead at roughly one-third the cost of a U.S. JDAM-ER. The weapon has no donor restrictions and reduces Ukraine's reliance on scarce Western munitions.

stories.title: Two dead in Spain shooting, with babies reportedly among injured
stories.summary: A 25-year-old man is suspected of fatally shooting his parents and injuring four others, reportedly including babies, in southern Spain. Police responded to the incident and identified the suspect.

stories.title: 5 dead, including 2 teen suspects, after shooting at San Diego's largest mosque
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen opened fire at the Islamic Center of San Diego, killing a security guard and two other men before being found dead from apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds. San Diego police and the FBI are investigating the attack as a hate crime. All children at a day school in the mosque complex were accounted for and safe.

stories.title: Shock and horror after California mosque attack
stories.summary: A shooting attack targeted a mosque affiliated with the Islamic Center in the San Diego area of California, killing three men including a security guard. Authorities credited the guard with preventing greater casualties.

stories.title: India-Nordic summit: Why is Modi wooing Northern Europe?
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended a summit with Nordic leaders, with discussions focusing on technology cooperation, green energy transition, Arctic regional engagement, and broader geopolitical alignment between India and Northern European nations.

stories.title: The Recognition Question: Somaliland, Israeli Security Geometry, and the Red Sea Power Struggle
stories.summary: Israel became the first country to officially recognize Somaliland as an independent state in December 2025, when Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced full diplomatic relations. The article examines the implications of this recognition for Red Sea security dynamics and Somaliland's long-standing quest for international legitimacy since declaring independence from Somalia in 1991.

stories.title: US to screen for Ebola at airports, Trump says he’s concerned
stories.summary: President Trump announced that U.S. airports will begin screening travelers for Ebola. Non-U.S. citizens who have been in Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, or South Sudan within the past 21 days are banned from entry.

stories.title: Govt eyes tokenisation of bonds via blockchain
stories.summary: Pakistan is considering linking its Naya Pakistan Certificates and sovereign bonds to a regulated blockchain through Digitally Native Notes to enable faster settlement for retail investors. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired a meeting with the State Bank of Pakistan and the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority to discuss tokenisation pathways.

stories.title: No feelgood factor for Reeves as Iran war snuffs out economic upturn
stories.summary: UK unemployment unexpectedly rose to 5% in the three months to March, with pay growth slowing, in what analysts describe as fallout from the Iran war's economic impact. The data undermines Chancellor Rachel Reeves's hopes for an economic recovery in 2026, as rising energy costs pressure British businesses and households.

stories.title: Vance: Iran talks held in 'good faith', strikes are 'option B'
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance said Iran negotiations were conducted in good faith but described military strikes as an alternative option. This came despite President Trump's earlier suggestion that he was planning a major new attack on Iran.

stories.title: Trump says attack on Iran 'on hold' as negotiations ongoing
stories.summary: President Trump said he had planned a major new military strike against Iran but put it on hold at the urging of Gulf Arab allies. He indicated that diplomatic negotiations with Tehran are ongoing.

stories.title: Putin hails ‘unprecedented’ ties ahead of China visit hot on Trump’s heels
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared that Russia-China relations had reached an "unprecedented level" ahead of a two-day visit to Beijing. Putin pledged mutual support on sovereignty and national unity with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The trip follows closely after U.S. President Trump's recent departure from Beijing.

stories.title: PTI warns of ‘moral collapse’ over treatment of political detainees
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf lawmakers warned of a "moral collapse" if the state failed to uphold constitutional protections for political detainees, demanding transparency over the treatment of former PM Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi.

stories.title: Iran says US behaviour undermining diplomatic efforts
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi that contradictory and excessive U.S. behavior remains a serious obstacle to diplomatic efforts. Araghchi cited deep mistrust stemming from what Tehran describes as repeated broken promises by Washington.

stories.title: Kyiv police bust interregional cocaine trafficking ring, seize drugs worth UAH 8M
stories.summary: Kyiv's National Police dismantled an interregional cocaine trafficking network, issuing notices of suspicion to four individuals and seizing drugs valued at nearly 8 million Ukrainian hryvnias.

stories.title: At least 15m Britons not saving enough to retire, Pensions Commission says
stories.summary: A UK Pensions Commission report found that at least 15 million Britons are not saving enough for retirement, a figure that could rise to 19 million without action. Only 4% of self-employed workers are contributing to pensions, with the commission warning of a severe financial "cliff edge" facing large groups across the country.

stories.title: Your academic future starts in Jerusalem - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem is promoting enrollment through a digital open day scheduled for May 31. The university highlights its academic programs, student experience, and support services.

stories.title: Your academic future starts in Jerusalem - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem promoted its academic programs and invited prospective students to a Digital Open Day scheduled for May 31.

stories.title: Federal Shariat Court strikes down 2022 legislation decriminalising suicide attempt
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Shariat Court struck down 2022 legislation that had decriminalised suicide attempts, ruling it repugnant to Islamic injunctions. A three-member bench reversed amendments to the Pakistan Penal Code that had removed attempted suicide as a criminal offense.

stories.title: UK unemployment unexpectedly rises to 5% as firms squeezed by Iran war
stories.summary: UK unemployment rose unexpectedly to 5% in the three months to March 2025, up from 4.9%, while wage growth eased to 3.4%. The Office for National Statistics data represents the first labor market snapshot reflecting the economic impact of the Iran war, as businesses face pressure from soaring energy costs.

stories.title: SBU detains Russian agent who directed strikes on Nikopol
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) detained a Russian FSB agent in the Dnipropetrovsk region who had been directing strikes on Nikopol using rocket systems, artillery, and FPV drones.

stories.title: Jewish US lawmakers warn antisemitic threats have surged since October 7
stories.summary: Jewish members of the U.S. Congress warned that antisemitic threats have surged significantly since the October 7 attacks. Representative Moskowitz said such threats have become a daily occurrence.

stories.title: Malaysia’s Anwar eyes snap poll before fuel subsidy crunch truly bites
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is reportedly considering calling a snap election well before the 2028 deadline, as a growing fuel subsidy crisis threatens to force unpopular spending cuts. His Pakatan Harapan coalition is showing signs of strain, with partner Barisan Nasional planning to contest the upcoming Johor state election independently.

stories.title: Master your career with Reichman University’s Graduate Programs. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Reichman University in Israel advertised its graduate programs through its Raphael Recanati International School, highlighting its international academic environment.

stories.title: Drone hits Yaroslavl refinery for third time in two weeks as Russia’s fourth-largest oil plant burns again
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery in Russia on May 19 for the third time in two weeks, causing a fire at Russia's fourth-largest oil plant. The Yaroslavl governor confirmed the strike; six Russian airports were temporarily closed.

stories.title: Knesset panel fast-tracks West Bank antiquities bill seen as de facto annexation
stories.summary: An Israeli Knesset committee fast-tracked legislation to create a new civilian body overseeing antiquities management in the West Bank beyond the Green Line. Critics view the bill as a step toward de facto annexation of occupied territory.

stories.title: Australian lawmaker denounces Israel's 'kidnapping in international waters'
stories.summary: Australian Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi condemned Israel's interception of a humanitarian flotilla bound for Gaza, describing the operation as piracy and kidnapping in international waters. She criticized the Australian government for continuing to regard Israel as a friend.

stories.title: Russia to conduct three-day nuclear drills on May 19-21
stories.summary: Russia's defense ministry announced three-day nuclear force exercises from May 19 to 21, involving more than 65,000 troops and 7,800 types of equipment and weapons.

stories.title: At least 25 buildings damaged, casualties reported in Russian attack on Kharkiv
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district damaged at least 25 buildings and caused civilian injuries.

stories.title: What do we know about the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus?
stories.summary: The Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus has caused over 100 suspected deaths and nearly 400 suspected infections in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of May 18. The strain, first identified in Uganda in 2007, is among the less-studied Ebola variants.

stories.title: “One person may still be under the rubble”: Kharkiv struck by back-to-back drone raids, 25+ homes damaged
stories.summary: Russian drones struck the city of Kharkiv twice overnight on May 19, damaging more than 25 homes and injuring at least three people. The attacks were part of a broader 209-drone assault across Ukraine, with one person possibly still trapped under rubble.

stories.title: Protesters rally in Athens after Israeli interception of Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside Greece's foreign ministry in Athens on Monday to protest Israel's interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla near Cyprus. The Gaza-bound aid convoy had sailed from Turkey the previous week before Israeli forces seized it on May 18.

stories.title: Ancient China elites used water fans, ice to cool down in summer; folks had bamboo pillows
stories.summary: A historical account describes how elites in ancient China used ice sculptures, water-powered fans, and other methods to cope with extreme summer heat before modern cooling technology existed. During the Qing dynasty under Emperor Qianlong, a severe heatwave caused devastating casualties across northern China.

stories.title: India raises fuel prices again amid Strait of Hormuz disruptions
stories.summary: India raised petrol and diesel prices for the second time in a week due to ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz affecting global fuel supplies. Petrol rose to 98.64 rupees per litre and diesel to 91.58 rupees per litre.

stories.title: Ukraine just built its own glide bomb—with five times its drones’ warhead
stories.summary: Ukraine completed development of its own precision glide bomb after more than a year of work. The weapon carries a warhead five times larger than those on Ukraine's standard combat drones and is now ready for deployment.

stories.title: Israel's education system is failing its kids - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial highlighted failures in Israel's education system, noting that only 3 percent of ninth-grade students met high standards on the national science exam. More than half scored at low or medium-low levels.

stories.title: Vodka, bullet train and boat rides: how Xi and Putin built up a personal rapport
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin have cultivated a notably personal relationship over the years through shared rituals involving food, birthday celebrations, sports, and boat rides. Xi has publicly called Putin his "best and most intimate friend," an unusual personal disclosure for the Chinese leader.

stories.title: Fears of new China shock as EU industry’s reliance on imports grows
stories.summary: Trade analysts warn that Europe faces a new "China shock" as rising imports of Chinese components threaten to undermine local manufacturing and jobs. Concerns center on a plunging exchange rate and Chinese government support for struggling firms, drawing comparisons to the disruption caused by China's entry into the World Trade Organization roughly 25 years ago.

stories.title: Army probes new Apache transmission problem as service rushes to ditch older helicopters
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is investigating a newly discovered transmission problem in its AH-64 Apache helicopter fleet. Pilots have raised safety concerns that the transmission issues, combined with recent reductions in flight hours, create dangerous conditions. The Army is simultaneously accelerating efforts to retire older Apache models from service.

stories.title: Canberra urges humane treatment for Australians held after Gaza flotilla raid
stories.summary: Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said it was urgently seeking information on Australians believed detained after Israeli forces intercepted Gaza-bound flotilla vessels in international waters. Canberra called for detainees to be treated humanely under international norms.

stories.title: San Diego mosque shooting to be investigated as hate crime
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen fatally shot three men at the Islamic Center of San Diego before killing themselves. Investigators are treating the incident as a hate crime.

stories.title: Israel intercepts more Gaza-bound aid boats with 'fully equipped naval fleet'
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted dozens of boats attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza on Monday, according to flotilla organizers. Activists reported Israel deployed a fully equipped naval fleet, with armed troops boarding vessels in international waters off Cyprus and detaining hundreds of participants.

stories.title: Over 90 deaths in latest DR Congo Ebola crisis: this is what we know
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo an international health emergency after more than 90 suspected deaths and hundreds of possible infections were reported.

stories.title: Australian taxpayers to pay $11bn to extend lifespan of ageing Collins-class submarines amid Aukus delay
stories.summary: The Australian government will spend an additional A$11 billion to extend the operational lifespan of its six Collins-class submarines by approximately a decade. The extension bridges a capability gap before the first AUKUS nuclear-powered submarines are expected to arrive around 2032. HMAS Farncomb, originally due for retirement this year, will now operate until about 2036.

stories.title: New bill aims to make it harder to indict senior officials, including PM, ministers
stories.summary: A new Israeli bill proposed by MK Rothman would require permission from a judge and a special committee before investigating senior officials, including the prime minister and ministers. The legislation is part of broader efforts to split the attorney general's role and limit checks on executive power.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Judgment Raises Concerns About Civic Freedoms in Nigeria
stories.summary: A recent court judgment in Nigeria has raised concerns among rights observers about the state of civic freedoms, with Human Rights Watch calling on the judiciary to uphold the rule of law and protect civic space.

stories.title: How Israel's war on Gaza has made Hajj an unreachable dream
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza have been unable to undertake the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca due to the ongoing Israeli military operations, blocking access to a deeply significant religious journey at a time of widespread suffering.

stories.title: Ride-hailing licence cap ‘must strike a balance’ in Hong Kong, John Lee says
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu said the number of ride-hailing vehicle licences must balance the city's unique conditions with passenger experience. Lee announced that a monitoring mechanism for market data and dynamic quota reviews would be established, and that proposed subsidiary legislation would be submitted on schedule.

stories.title: Record number of Russians unhappy with Kremlin's foreign policy – poll
stories.summary: A recent poll shows Russian public dissatisfaction with the Kremlin's foreign policy has reached a 20-year high. Discontent is driven by the ongoing war in Ukraine, internet restrictions, and worsening economic conditions.

stories.title: Record number of Russians unhappy with Kremlin's foreign policy – poll
stories.summary: A poll indicates that Russian public dissatisfaction with the Kremlin's foreign policy has reached a 20-year high, driven by the ongoing war in Ukraine, internet restrictions, and worsening economic conditions.

stories.title: Australian senator condemns government response to Gaza flotilla seizure
stories.summary: Australian Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi condemned Canberra's response to Israel's seizure of a Gaza-bound humanitarian flotilla, accusing Israeli forces of piracy and kidnapping in international waters. She questioned Australia's continued diplomatic relationship with Israel.

stories.title: Kenya: Four Killed, 348 Arrested in Nationwide Protests Over High Fuel Costs, Murkomen Says
stories.summary: Four people were killed and 348 arrested during nationwide protests in Kenya over rising fuel costs, according to Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Urged to Get New Buyers As UAE Exit Threatens Oil Market Stability
stories.summary: PETAN Chairman Wole Ogunsanya urged NNPC and Nigerian oil producers to develop new crude oil markets outside the OPEC quota system following the UAE's exit, which threatens oil market stability.

stories.title: Five dead, including two teen suspects, after shooting at San Diego mosque
stories.summary: Five people died in a shooting at San Diego's largest mosque, the Islamic Center of San Diego, including three victims and two teenage suspects aged 17 and 19. The suspects died of self-inflicted gunshot wounds, and the FBI is investigating it as a hate crime.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola Strain Spreading in Congo and Uganda Has No Approved Vaccine
stories.summary: The Ebola strain spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda has no approved vaccine. The U.S. CDC announced it is transferring a small number of Americans who were exposed to the virus in Congo.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak - 'Nobody Has a Grip On the Numbers,' Top Expert Warns
stories.summary: Congolese scientist Jean-Jacques Muyembe, co-discoverer of the Ebola virus, warned that health authorities may have detected the DR Congo outbreak too late and still lack clarity on its full spread.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: M23 Tax Drive in DR Congo Puts Squeeze On Aid Groups
stories.summary: The M23 rebel group is imposing taxes in areas it controls in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, placing financial pressure on humanitarian aid organizations operating in the region.

stories.title: U.S. to screen for Ebola at airports, one American in Democratic Republic of Congo infected
stories.summary: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced Ebola screening measures at airports after an American was infected in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The World Health Organisation has declared the DRC Ebola outbreak an international health emergency.

stories.title: Mali: Mali's Military Leader Is Consolidating Power. Why This Is Dangerous
stories.summary: Mali's military junta leader General Assimi Goïta assumed the role of defense minister following the killing of General Sadio Camara. Officials announced the move on May 4, 2026, consolidating Goïta's grip on power.

stories.title: Putin seeks to reinforce China ties after Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, aiming to project strong bilateral ties. The visit comes just days after U.S. President Donald Trump's high-profile trip to Beijing, where he sought to stabilize U.S.-China relations.

stories.title: Dfat officials ‘urgently seeking’ status of 11 Australian Gaza flotilla activists detained by Israel
stories.summary: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs officials are urgently seeking information on 11 Australians detained by Israeli forces after their flotilla was intercepted in international waters off Cyprus. The Global Sumud Flotilla, comprising 38 ships and 319 activists attempting to deliver aid to Gaza, was reportedly about 250 nautical miles from Gaza's coast when intercepted by the Israel Defense Forces.

stories.title: Belarus begins exercises involving combat use of nuclear weapons
stories.summary: Belarus launched military exercises on Monday involving the combat use of nuclear weapons and nuclear support units. No further details about the scope or duration of the drills were immediately provided.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s climate; Singaporeans and a work ethic stereotype: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: A roundup from the South China Morning Post highlights seven major stories from across Asia, including warnings about a potential "Godzilla El Niño" threatening Southeast Asia with drought, flash floods, crop losses, and haze. The compilation also covers topics such as Singaporean work culture stereotypes.

stories.title: Trump says he paused attack on Iran as negotiations continue
stories.summary: President Trump said he paused a previously undisclosed planned attack on Iran as negotiations continue. Gulf leaders had requested the delay, expressing confidence that a deal would be reached.

stories.title: Russian nuclear head: situation at Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant reaching 'point of no return'
stories.summary: Rosatom chief warned that the situation at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine is nearing a 'point of no return' due to increased Ukrainian attacks in the area. The plant is Europe's largest nuclear facility.

stories.title: Marcos says Philippines, because of proximity to Taiwan, likely involved in any conflict
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told Japanese media that the Philippines would likely be drawn into any conflict over Taiwan due to geographic proximity and nearly 200,000 Filipino workers on the island. Marcos said Manila does not want involvement in a Taiwan war but acknowledged it would be unavoidable given the country's location.

stories.title: Two suspects in shooting at San Diego mosque dead, police source says
stories.summary: Two suspects in a shooting at an Islamic center approximately 9 miles north of downtown San Diego were found dead. Authorities believe multiple people were shot during the incident.

stories.title: US targets Cuban political, military leaders with new sanctions
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on nine Cuban officials, including the communications minister, several military leaders, and Cuba's directorate of intelligence. The measures were announced on Monday.

stories.title: The Myth of Zero Enrichment
stories.summary: The article discusses the ongoing dispute over Iran's uranium enrichment program and the U.S. demand for zero enrichment. It notes that Tehran views this demand as equivalent to unconditional surrender, while suggesting potential diplomatic pathways may still exist.

stories.title: The Myth of Zero Enrichment
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Iran views Washington's demand for zero uranium enrichment as tantamount to unconditional surrender, but suggests potential pathways for compromise in nuclear negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Will Chinese become the king language for commanding AI on engineering tasks?
stories.summary: A Tsinghua University study published in China's top aviation journal examined whether the language used to prompt AI models affects performance on engineering tasks such as aircraft design. The research found mixed results, suggesting Chinese may hold an intrinsic advantage in certain contexts, raising questions for the global technology competition.

stories.title: ‘Huge milestone’ as Libyan militia commander accused of torture to appear at ICC
stories.summary: Former Libyan militia commander Khaled Mohamed Ali El Hishri is set to appear at the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder, rape, enslavement, and torture in Libyan detention centres. The prosecution is considered a landmark step toward justice for abuses against refugees attempting to reach Europe from Africa.

stories.title: ‘Come in for one minute’: exhibition showing horrors of 7 October attacks opens in London
stories.summary: An exhibition in east London documenting the October 7 attack on the Nova music festival in Israel opened under heavy security. The commemoration highlights the 378 people killed at the festival and aims to confront those who deny the gravity of the atrocity.

stories.title: US Jewish groups say Islamic Center shooting proves need for federal security funding
stories.summary: U.S. Jewish organizations cited a shooting at an Islamic center in California and a recent ramming attack on a Michigan synagogue as evidence of the need for continued federal security funding for religious institutions.

stories.title: Washington Post: Iran wants war to end before nuclear agreement is announced
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported, citing a Pakistani official, that Iran wants the war to end before any nuclear agreement is publicly announced. Tehran reportedly favors a phased diplomatic approach, while Washington prefers simultaneous announcement of all agreements.

stories.title: Minnesota officials charge ICE agent in shooting of Venezuelan immigrant
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Minnesota charged a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent with assault over the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant in Minneapolis in January. The incident occurred during President Trump's immigration enforcement crackdown in the city.

stories.title: Bolivia protests against President Paz widen with violent clashes, looting in La Paz
stories.summary: Violent protests demanding Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz's resignation intensified in La Paz on Monday amid a deepening economic crisis. Riot police clashed with demonstrators, and government offices were looted as anger over the country's economic situation escalated.

stories.title: Majority of US voters oppose war on Iran, survey finds
stories.summary: A New York Times–Siena College poll of 1,507 registered U.S. voters found that 64 percent opposed the U.S. war on Iran, with only 30 percent in support. The survey also showed 57 percent opposed providing U.S. military aid to Israel.

stories.title: New York Times reports Iran moving missiles into mountain facilities
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Iran is moving ballistic missiles into mountain facilities and revising military tactics during the ceasefire period. U.S. military officials said Tehran reopened dozens of previously bombed missile sites and stored weapons inside caves.

stories.title: Australia secures jet fuel shipments amid Iran war concerns
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the government secured three jet fuel shipments totaling over 600,000 barrels to bolster national fuel reserves. The move responds to global energy supply concerns linked to the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Trump’s repeated ultimatums betray his lack of leverage over Iran
stories.summary: Analyst Foad Izadi argued that President Trump's repeated ultimatums and threats of renewed full-scale war against Iran reflect a lack of leverage rather than strength in the ongoing standoff.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says 'very good chance' of reaching a deal with Iran
