stories.summary: The article addresses the impact of cuts in foreign aid on global health care systems and argues that affected countries have an opportunity to develop their own plans to address the resulting gaps in health services.

stories.title: There Is a Solution to the Global Health Care Crisis
stories.summary: The article discusses the impact of cuts to foreign aid on global health care systems. It argues that affected countries have a limited window to develop their own plans to address the resulting health care crisis.

stories.title: West Bank Palestinians see Nakba repeating under Israeli raids
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank say escalating Israeli military raids on refugee camps are reviving memories of the Nakba. Residents warn of renewed displacement as incursions intensify across the territory.

stories.title: Revolt against UK’s Starmer revives bitter debate over undoing Brexit
stories.summary: A political debate over reversing Brexit is resurfacing within the UK Labour Party amid a leadership crisis for Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Two potential challengers have emerged, including former Health Secretary Wes Streeting, who recently resigned from Starmer's government.

stories.title: Britain faces weeks of leadership limbo in slow-motion coup against Starmer
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a growing internal challenge to his leadership, with critics calling him a "lame-duck" leader. The political turmoil could leave Britain in a prolonged period of leadership uncertainty.

stories.title: US senator says US should ‘hurt’ Iran, destroy infrastructure
stories.summary: Republican Senator Lindsey Graham urged President Trump to intensify pressure on Iran by targeting its energy infrastructure until Tehran accepts U.S. terms in nuclear negotiations. Speaking to NBC, Graham said Iran's energy sector was its "soft underbelly."

stories.title: Rising secondary home prices in China’s major cities in April stoke hopes of stability
stories.summary: Secondary home prices in China's major first-tier cities rose in April, with Shanghai up 0.7%, Beijing up 0.4%, and Shenzhen up 0.3% month-on-month, according to National Bureau of Statistics data. Analysts said the increases offer signs that China's struggling property sector may be stabilizing.

stories.title: Pianist Jayson Gillham says he never considered apologising for Gaza comments, trial hears
stories.summary: Australian pianist Jayson Gillham testified in a federal court case that he never considered apologizing for comments about Israeli forces killing Palestinian journalists. Gillham is suing the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, alleging it unlawfully discriminated against him by cancelling a concert over his views.

stories.title: Anti-Israel Croatian president refusing to sign off on new Israeli envoy — report
stories.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanović is reportedly refusing to approve a new Israeli envoy to Croatia. Milanović, who has previously accused Israel of "terrorism," is feuding with his right-wing government over the appointment.

stories.title: Growing bread queues in Gaza as Israel restricts fuel, flour imports
stories.summary: Bread shortages are worsening across Gaza as Israel restricts fuel and flour imports into the territory. Bakeries are struggling to operate amid fuel scarcity, leading to growing queues for bread among the population.

stories.title: Russia just hit commercial vessel of its closest war ally in Ukrainian waters with Shahed drone
stories.summary: A Russian Shahed drone struck a commercial vessel belonging to China, described as Russia's closest strategic partner, in Ukrainian waters. Russia has repeatedly hit civilian ships across the Black Sea in recent months.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa leaves two people injured, homes damaged
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Odesa injured two people and damaged residential buildings, a school, and a kindergarten.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwandan Genocide Suspect Felicien Kabuga Dies in Custody
stories.summary: Félicien Kabuga, a fugitive accused of financing and encouraging the 1994 Rwandan genocide, has died in custody. He was once among the world's most-wanted suspects.

stories.title: Former Trump ally threatens ‘political revolution’ against US troop deployment to Iran
stories.summary: Former U.S. congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene warned that deploying American troops to Iran would trigger a "political revolution" in the United States. Writing on X, the former Trump ally said she would rally opposition, declaring "no more foreign wars."

stories.title: Hong Kong court confiscates HK$674,860 from 3 defendants in terrorism trial
stories.summary: A Hong Kong High Court ordered the confiscation of more than HK$674,000 from three defendants in a terrorism trial related to the 2019 anti-government protests. The funds were raised by a group called the "Dragon Slaying Brigade" to support a plot to kill police. It is the first such order under the UN Anti-Terrorism Measures Ordinance since 2002.

stories.title: Nir Oz marks birthday of Johnny Siman Tov, killed on October 7
stories.summary: Members of Kibbutz Nir Oz gathered in Karmei Gat to celebrate the birthday of Johnny Siman Tov, who was killed during the October 7 attack. Friends, neighbors, and family members marked the occasion together.

stories.title: Russian missiles hit Dnipro, nine reported injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a missile strike on the city of Dnipro during an air raid alert, with at least nine people reported injured.

stories.title: Report: US ammunition flights arriving in Tel Aviv for resumption of Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli broadcaster Channel 13 reported that dozens of U.S. cargo aircraft carrying ammunition from bases in Germany landed in Tel Aviv over the past 24 hours. The deliveries are reportedly part of preparations by Israel and the United States for a possible resumption of military operations against Iran.

stories.title: IDF reservists forced to cross Lebanon border despite being ineligible for benefits
stories.summary: IDF reservists reported being ordered to cross into Lebanon despite being classified at "Tier B" eligibility, a lower designation than the "Tier A" status given to soldiers in particularly dangerous positions including cross-border operations.

stories.title: India has 1.42 billion people – but some Modi allies want bigger families
stories.summary: Allies of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi are advocating for larger families to counter India's declining fertility rate, despite the country's population of 1.42 billion and challenges like high youth unemployment. The UN projects India's population will continue rising for about four decades, peaking near 1.7 billion.

stories.title: Video: Berlin police storm Nakba Day march and pepper spray demonstrators
stories.summary: Berlin police used pepper spray and charged into crowds at a Nakba Day remembrance march in the German capital. Footage showed officers aggressively pushing through demonstrators during the event, which organizers described as peaceful.

stories.title: Hong Kong urged to trigger travel alert to DR Congo, Uganda amid Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: A Hong Kong infectious disease expert urged authorities to issue a travel alert for the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda amid a worsening Ebola outbreak. The WHO declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, prompting Hong Kong to strengthen health screenings of incoming passengers.

stories.title: CNN: Iran eyeing control over key internet cable routes
stories.summary: CNN reported that Iran is seeking influence over submarine internet cables carrying communications and financial data between Europe, Asia, and Gulf countries. Iranian authorities said major technology companies including Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon would need to pay fees and comply with Iranian laws for cables passing through the region.

stories.title: ‘Occupational bug’: China surgeon goes viral for weighing 150kg due to work stress, bad diet
stories.summary: A Shanghai chest surgeon named Xiang Ruilong went viral online after it was reported he weighs 150 kilograms, which he attributes to work stress and poor diet. He said he weighed about 110 kg when he started his medical career over a decade ago.

stories.title: National Conversation project launches as Britain risks ‘being torn apart by differences’
stories.summary: A National Conversation project launched in Britain, co-chaired by former Conservative chancellor Sajid Javid and former Labour policy chief Jon Cruddas. The Independent Commission on Community and Cohesion is asking the public to share their vision of community and national identity to help rebuild social cohesion.

stories.title: Nigeria: List of Kidnapped Children Emerges, As Parents Detail Horror of Borno Attack
stories.summary: A verified register obtained from a local councillor in Borno State, Nigeria, identified 40 missing children by name, age, and family background following an attack and mass kidnapping.

stories.title: Louder than noise: Noam Bettan let music, not politics, define his performance - editorial
stories.summary: Israeli Eurovision contestant Noam Bettan delivered a notable performance, which an editorial praised for professionalism and restraint amid political controversy surrounding Israel's participation.

stories.title: France's justice minister to visit Algeria amid diplomatic thaw
stories.summary: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin is visiting Algeria on Monday amid improving diplomatic relations. Discussions will focus on judicial cooperation, including the case of detained French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, arrested in 2024 for allegedly glorifying terrorism.

stories.title: Nigeria: What We Know About How Islamic State Leader Mainok Was Killed in Nigeria
stories.summary: Nigerian security operatives tracked and killed Islamic State leader Mainok after monitoring his movements across multiple locations in northern Nigeria, including Abuja and Maiduguri.

stories.title: Israeli media reports military preparing for possible Iran strikes
stories.summary: Israeli media reported that Israel's military is preparing for possible renewed strikes on Iran, with broadcaster Kan citing a security official saying Israel would join any new U.S. operations targeting Iranian energy infrastructure. The reports followed a phone call between President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak kills 88 in DR Congo as WHO declares global emergency
stories.summary: An Ebola outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 80 people and spread to the major city of Goma, prompting the World Health Organization to declare a public health emergency of international concern.

stories.title: Why Sudan disappeared from global headlines - until the Iran war
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that recent geopolitical framing of Sudan's three-year civil conflict has distorted the true picture of the crisis. The article suggests the war in Sudan largely disappeared from global headlines until it was reframed in the context of the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Israel to financially 'incentivize' countries to move embassies to Jerusalem
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved a proposal to offer financial incentives to countries that relocate their embassies to Jerusalem.

stories.title: Israel approves new defense complex at former UNRWA East Jerusalem headquarters
stories.summary: Israel approved construction of a new defense complex at the former UNRWA headquarters site in East Jerusalem. The complex will include an IDF museum, an enlistment office, and an office for the defense minister. Defense Minister Katz called the decision symbolic.

stories.title: Kenya: Oburu Warns ODM Rebels Over Party Discipline in Heated Nyanza Delegates Meeting
stories.summary: ODM party leader Oburu Oginga warned members linked to the Linda Mwananchi faction against undermining party leadership during a delegates meeting in Kisumu, insisting on internal discipline.

stories.title: Kenya: Schools Closed As Transport Strike Threatens Movement
stories.summary: Private schools across Kenya were put on alert as a nationwide transport strike threatened to disrupt learner movement and school operations on Monday.

stories.title: Kenya: NPS Assures Public of Security As Nationwide Psv Strike Begins Over Fuel Prices
stories.summary: Kenya's National Police Service assured public safety as a nationwide public service vehicle strike began Monday, with major PSV operators withdrawing fleets to protest soaring fuel prices.

stories.title: Kenya: 'Walking City' As Transport Strike Strands Thousands Across Nairobi Amid Fuel Price Fury
stories.summary: Thousands of commuters were stranded across Nairobi on Monday as a nationwide transport strike shut down matatu and bus services, turning the capital into a "walking city" amid demands to lower fuel prices.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Is Sending in the Military to Guard Mines and Critical Minerals. Will It Be Enough?
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo plans to create a new paramilitary unit to protect mining sites and critical mineral transport routes, with funding and support from the United States and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Cuba accuses US of fabrication after Axios report alleging drone threat
stories.summary: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez accused the United States of fabricating a "fraudulent case" involving an alleged drone threat from Cuba. Rodriguez said the claims were designed to justify economic sanctions and potential military intervention against the island.

stories.title: Why China rare earth breakthrough in icy northeast could cement global dominance
stories.summary: Chinese scientists discovered a new type of rare earth formation in the northeastern provinces of Heilongjiang and Jilin, consisting of loose sand and gravel created by freeze-thaw cycles. Unlike southern China's clay-based deposits requiring chemical leaching, the northern formations could enable more efficient and less costly extraction.

stories.title: ‘When your signal goes down, something’s going on’: life next to a US air base in the UK
stories.summary: Residents near RAF Lakenheath, a U.S. air base in the UK, describe disruptions including internet and phone signal drops, sonic booms, and low-flying heavy bombers interrupting school assemblies. Community access to the base became more restricted after the September 11 attacks.

stories.title: Two-thirds of NHS nurses believe lack of staff is putting patients at risk, survey finds
stories.summary: A Royal College of Nursing survey found that almost two-thirds of NHS nurses believe staffing levels are too low to keep patients safe. The union plans to urge ministers to introduce mandatory minimum staffing levels, with 64% of respondents expecting service cuts this year.

stories.title: UK’s next ambassador to Japan may be called to give evidence in Mandelson inquiry
stories.summary: UK Members of Parliament may call Corin Robertson, the next British ambassador to Japan, to give evidence in an inquiry into Peter Mandelson's security clearance. Robertson was the Foreign Office's chief operating officer when she was involved in the decision to grant Mandelson clearance against vetting officials' advice in January 2025.

stories.title: Israel preparing to intercept Gaza-bound aid flotilla, local media says
stories.summary: Israel is preparing to intercept a 54-ship aid flotilla, called the Global Sumud Flotilla, approaching Gaza's waters to challenge the Israeli blockade. Prime Minister Netanyahu held security consultations ahead of the convoy's expected arrival within two days. Activists aboard reported spotting a military vessel near the flotilla.

stories.title: Former IRGC commander calls US naval blockade ‘act of war’
stories.summary: Former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Mohsen Rezaei warned the United States to end its naval blockade of Iranian ports, calling it an "act of war." Speaking on Iranian state television, Rezaei said Iran's military remained prepared for confrontation and urged the U.S. to withdraw from the Sea of Oman.

stories.title: Thailand reels from deadly Bangkok train crash, its latest avoidable tragedy
stories.summary: Eight people were killed in Bangkok when a goods train struck a city bus at the Asok-Dindaeng level crossing on Saturday. The train driver tested positive for drugs and lacked a valid operator's licence from the Department of Rail Transport.

stories.title: US air force base investigating aircraft collision in Idaho
stories.summary: Two EA-18G Growler jets crashed near Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show. The base was placed on lockdown as an investigation was launched into the collision.

stories.title: Trump’s China trip assessed, South Korea’s AI problem: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: A roundup covers five weekend stories from across Asia, including assessments of President Trump's visit to China, U.S. CEOs seeking Chinese business, Hong Kong airport's Terminal 2 opening, South Korea's AI challenges, and other regional developments.

stories.title: Taxi driver, 65, arrested after crash kills pedestrian in Hong Kong
stories.summary: A 65-year-old taxi driver was arrested in Hong Kong's Tung Chung after his vehicle struck and killed an 87-year-old pedestrian crossing under a footbridge on Monday. It was the second fatal crash involving an elderly taxi driver in Hong Kong in less than a week.

stories.title: Moldovan leaders decry Russian move on citizenship for separatist region
stories.summary: Moldovan leaders denounced Russian President Vladimir Putin's decree offering simplified Russian citizenship to residents of Moldova's pro-Russian breakaway region of Transnistria. Officials in Chisinau are considering countermeasures against the move, which they view as a threat.

stories.title: Introducing Stateside with Kai and Carter: Stacey Abrams on why gutting US Voting Rights Act is ‘evil’ – podcast
stories.summary: A new podcast features voting rights activist Stacey Abrams discussing the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which struck down consideration of race in redistricting under the Voting Rights Act. Southern states have since moved to eliminate majority-Black districts ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Trump warns 'clock is ticking' for Iran as peace progress stalls
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran that the "clock is ticking" for a peace agreement. Iranian media reported that Washington has not offered concrete concessions in response to Tehran's latest negotiating proposals, suggesting diplomatic progress has stalled.

stories.title: 4 crew members eject safely after two US Navy jets collide during air show in Idaho
stories.summary: Two U.S. Navy EA-18G Growler jets collided mid-air during an air show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho. All four crew members ejected safely. Authorities are investigating the cause of the collision.

stories.title: Xi Jinping prepares to welcome Vladimir Putin to China, four days after hosting Donald Trump
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is preparing to host Russian President Vladimir Putin in Beijing this week, just four days after U.S. President Donald Trump's departure from China. Xi and Putin exchanged congratulatory letters marking the 30th anniversary of their countries' strategic partnership.

stories.title: Israeli strike in eastern Lebanon kills Islamic Jihad leader, daughter
stories.summary: An Israeli missile strike near Baalbek in eastern Lebanon killed a Palestinian Islamic Jihad leader and his daughter, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strike targeted an apartment housing a Palestinian family, despite a ceasefire agreement announced on April 17 and extended for another 45 days.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman taunts Trump with movie clip
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei posted a clip from the biographical film "The Apprentice" on X, featuring a scene about "rules for winning." The post was part of broader Iranian messaging criticizing President Trump's handling of the conflict.

stories.title: Former US defence chief says he rejected Netanyahu’s Iran assessment
stories.summary: Former U.S. Defense Secretary and CIA Director Robert Gates recalled a 2009 conversation in which Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu argued Iran would quickly collapse if attacked. Gates said he told Netanyahu he was "dead wrong" and underestimated Iranian resilience.

stories.title: North Korea to turn southern border into ‘impregnable fortress’ against ‘arch enemy’
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un instructed top military officials to strengthen front-line units and turn the southern border into an "impregnable fortress." Kim made the remarks at a meeting on Sunday, calling for a "great change" to deter war, according to state media outlet KCNA.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda public health emergency of international concern
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern.

stories.title: Tributes flow after Australian shark attack victim named as father-of-two
stories.summary: Steven Mattaboni, a 38-year-old father of two, died on Saturday after a shark attack while spearfishing at Rottnest Island off Western Australia.

stories.title: French star Patrick Bruel denies multiple sexual assault allegations
stories.summary: French singer and actor Patrick Bruel denied multiple sexual assault allegations on Sunday. The Paris prosecutor's office confirmed at least four complaints of sexual assault against Bruel in France, with investigations in both France and Belgium to be consolidated.

stories.title: 'Staggering' Iran toll drives up global executions: Amnesty
stories.summary: Amnesty International reported that Iran carried out over 2,150 executions last year, contributing to the highest global execution total recorded since 1981.

stories.title: Taiwan will not provoke conflict nor give up sovereignty, says president
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te stated that Taiwan will neither provoke conflict nor relinquish its sovereignty, responding to discussions between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping regarding Taiwan's independence.

stories.title: Report: Netanyahu revealed secret UAE visit to avoid being upstaged by election rival Bennett
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu reportedly revealed a secret wartime visit to the UAE after learning that political rival Naftali Bennett was planning his own trip to Abu Dhabi. The disclosure allegedly angered Emirati officials, who denied the visit took place.

stories.title: China unveils world’s first titanium-copper medical implant designed to cut infection risk
stories.summary: China has developed and approved the world's first copper-blended titanium implant for orthopaedic surgery after more than a decade of research. The material retains titanium alloy's strength while significantly reducing post-operative infection risk. The first bone pin using the material was approved by China's National Medical Products authority on April 21.

stories.title: Suspected Ukrainian military drone found crashed in Lithuania, authorities say
stories.summary: A suspected Ukrainian military drone was found crashed in Lithuania on Sunday. Authorities said the drone was not detected when it entered Lithuanian airspace and was not armed with explosives, amid growing Baltic NATO concerns over stray drones from the Ukraine war.

stories.title: Ulyanov suggests Iran appoint special representative to Russia
stories.summary: Russian envoy Mikhail Ulyanov publicly suggested that Iran appoint a special representative to Russia, similar to Tehran's recent appointment of Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as special envoy to China.

stories.title: Singapore softens approach to first-time drug abusers as they get ‘younger and younger’
stories.summary: Singapore announced that first-time drug abusers who surrender to authorities will no longer face detention at rehabilitation centers. Instead, they will be placed on community-based drug supervision with mandatory case management, a policy change effective Saturday aimed at encouraging more abusers to seek help.

stories.title: Trump warns ‘won’t be anything left’ of Iran unless it agrees to deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran on his Truth Social platform that "the Clock is Ticking" and urged Tehran to agree to a deal quickly. He stated there "won't be anything left" of Iran unless it moves fast on negotiations.

stories.title: US says China to buy billions in agricultural goods after Trump-Xi talks
stories.summary: Following talks between President Trump and President Xi Jinping, the White House announced that China will purchase at least $17 billion worth of U.S. agricultural goods annually.

stories.title: Houthis reaffirm support for Hamas after commander’s killing
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement reaffirmed its support for Hamas and allied Palestinian armed groups following the reported killing of senior Hamas commander Izz al-Din al-Haddad. Houthi military leader Yusuf Hassan al-Madani pledged continued joint efforts with Palestinian factions.

stories.title: U.S. weighs drone threat from Cuba: report
stories.summary: A report indicates that the United States is evaluating a potential drone threat originating from Cuba. The assessment comes amid rising tensions between Washington and Havana, with speculation that the U.S. may be building a case for military action against the island.

stories.title: French opposition leader attacks ‘European complicity’ in Iran conflict
stories.summary: French opposition leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon of La France Insoumise condemned what he called European complicity in the US and Israeli strikes on Iran, accusing European nations of enabling the regional conflict.

stories.title: Latest militant attacks on schools in Nigeria leave more than 80 children missing, officials say
stories.summary: Militants attacked a primary school in Borno state in northeastern Nigeria, leaving more than 80 children missing. The assault is the latest in a series of attacks on schools in the conflict-affected region.

stories.title: Australia news live: judge warns about ‘controversy’ as pianist sues orchestra; NSW landlords fined over no-fault evictions
stories.summary: In Australia, a judge warned that a pianist's lawsuit against the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra would not become a broad inquiry into the Middle East conflict. Separately, New South Wales landlords were fined for carrying out no-fault evictions.

stories.title: China to buy at least $21 billion in US agricultural products annually, White House says
stories.summary: China has agreed to purchase at least $21 billion in U.S. agricultural products annually, according to the White House. The commitment follows a steep decline of 65.7% in bilateral agricultural trade after escalating tit-for-tat tariffs in 2025.

stories.title: Trump's Greenland envoy Landry arrives in Nuuk
stories.summary: U.S. special envoy Jeff Landry, appointed by President Trump to pursue American control of Greenland, arrived in Nuuk on Sunday. Local media reported his arrival in the Greenlandic capital as part of ongoing U.S. diplomatic efforts regarding the territory.

stories.title: Moment of collision between two Navy jets at Idaho air show
stories.summary: Two US Navy jets collided during an air show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho.

stories.title: Israel PM says close to killing all architects of October 7 attack
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel is close to killing all the architects of the October 7 attack. His remarks followed the Israeli military's announcement that Hamas armed wing commander Ezzedine Al-Haddad was killed in a Gaza airstrike on May 15.

stories.title: Israel launches strikes on southern Lebanon despite extending ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israel carried out strikes in southern Lebanon near Tyre despite an extended ceasefire, according to Al Jazeera reporting from the region.

stories.title: How ISWAP and Boko Haram are reshaping the Lake Chad Basin
stories.summary: The Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and Boko Haram continue to drive rising violence across the Lake Chad Basin, compounding economic hardship and weak governance affecting local communities.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Drone strikes on UAE and Saudi Arabia fuel escalation fears
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire at a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates on Sunday, while Saudi Arabia reported intercepting three drones. U.S. President Donald Trump urged Iran to act quickly amid stalled efforts to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, heightening regional escalation fears.

stories.title: Ukrainian TV announcer Oleksandr Safonov dies at 82
stories.summary: Oleksandr Safonov, a renowned Ukrainian television announcer and People's Artist of Ukraine, died at the age of 82 following a serious illness. Safonov was a prominent figure in Ukrainian broadcasting.

stories.title: ‘My way or the highway’ is no way to make informed policy for Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government plans to launch a consultation on its first five-year development plan next month, with the final plan expected before year's end. Observers have noted the complexity of the undertaking.

stories.title: Soccer- Azmoun left out of preliminary Iran World Cup squad
stories.summary: Iranian forward Sardar Azmoun was excluded from Iran's preliminary World Cup squad, with reports citing injury amid ongoing controversy over his international future.

stories.title: Settler activists illegally cross into Syria; IDF returns them, hands them to police
stories.summary: Israeli settler activists illegally crossed into Syria and were returned by the IDF and handed over to police. Separately, Lebanese state media reported an Israeli strike in Baalbek that killed an Islamic Jihad commander.

stories.title: Head of village council, deputy, shot in Arab village Jadeidi-Makr
stories.summary: The head of a village council and a deputy were shot in the Arab village of Jadeidi-Makr in Israel's Western Galilee region. Police forces arrived at the scene and launched a manhunt for the suspects.

stories.title: California jury to deliberate on Musk's blockbuster lawsuit against OpenAI
stories.summary: A California jury began deliberations Monday in Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman. Musk alleges that OpenAI's transformation into an $850 billion company violated its original nonprofit mission and misused his $38 million donation. The case is considered Silicon Valley's first major AI trial.

stories.title: Iran discusses Strait of Hormuz with French and South Korean ministers
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held separate talks with French and South Korean officials on Gulf tensions and developments related to the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Charity workers killed in Israeli strike on community kitchen in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip killed at least five Palestinians on Sunday, including three charity workers at a community kitchen in Deir el-Balah. Additional fatalities were reported in Khan Younis and Beit Lahiya.

stories.title: US weighs drone threat from Cuba, report says
stories.summary: Cuba has reportedly begun discussing plans to deploy recently acquired military drones against the U.S. naval base at Guantanamo Bay, prompting U.S. officials to assess the potential threat.

stories.title: Hong Kong records 10 tremor reports after magnitude 5.2 quake hits Guangxi
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory received more than 10 reports of a locally felt tremor following a magnitude 5.2 earthquake that struck Guangxi, China, approximately 550 kilometers west-northwest of Hong Kong, with a focal depth of about 10 kilometers.

stories.title: French bulldog in China known for collecting plastic bottles faces threats from animal abusers
stories.summary: A French bulldog in southern China known for collecting plastic bottles and popular on social media was reportedly targeted by a suspected poisoner. The dog's owner called police, and a suspect was apprehended.

stories.title: Araghchi and Fidan hold talks on regional tensions
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan discussed stalled US-Iran negotiations and broader regional tensions. Turkey has been engaged in behind-the-scenes diplomacy while strengthening security along its border with Iran over displacement concerns.

stories.title: Palestinian ministry condemns Israeli property seizure plan near Al-Aqsa
stories.summary: The Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned an Israeli plan to seize up to 20 properties near Al-Aqsa Mosque in the Bab as-Silsila area of occupied East Jerusalem, calling it ethnic cleansing and part of a broader displacement strategy.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activist reports military vessel near convoy
stories.summary: A Spanish activist aboard a flotilla of vessels sailing toward the Gaza Strip reported that a suspected military vessel approached the convoy. Organisers activated security protocols. Israel has previously intercepted similar aid missions attempting to break its blockade.

stories.title: German intelligence service flags watermelon symbol in new pro-Palestinian extremism guide
stories.summary: Germany's domestic intelligence agency, the BfV, published a guide on pro-Palestinian extremism that flags the watermelon symbol among other codes it says can be used to spread antisemitism while evading detection.

stories.title: The Falklands turn into a small South Atlantic economic power as the ghosts of 1982 return
stories.summary: The Falkland Islands are observing their annual commemoration season marking the 1982 war, culminating in Liberation Day on June 14. The ceremonies come as the archipelago experiences growing economic prosperity while facing renewed diplomatic tensions involving the United States and Argentina.

stories.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship MV Hondius arrives in Rotterdam for disinfection
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius, affected by a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people, arrived in Rotterdam on Monday for disinfection. Dutch authorities prepared quarantine arrangements for remaining crew and medical staff as the multi-country outbreak triggered global health monitoring.

stories.title: Russia, Belarus turning children into obedient mobilization resources – intelligence
stories.summary: An intelligence report indicates that Russia and Belarus are investing billions to indoctrinate children and transform them into obedient mobilization resources. The programs are designed to prepare youth for potential military service.

stories.title: What’s behind the rise in firings linked to disability discrimination in Hong Kong?
stories.summary: Complaints to Hong Kong's Equal Opportunities Commission about firings linked to disability discrimination have more than doubled over five years, reaching 490 employment-related complaints last year. Concern groups attribute the increase to corporate restructuring and layoffs during the economic downturn.

stories.title: How does the Strait of Hormuz stand-off look in the wake of the Trump-Xi summit?
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz standoff was a key topic at the Trump-Xi summit. Iran is moving to formalize control over the strait with a new transit mechanism that would collect fees for shipping services, as the broader impasse continues.

stories.title: Around 10 ‘new’ victims come forward in France’s Epstein probe, prosecutor says
stories.summary: French magistrates are investigating possible offences linked to Jeffrey Epstein that may have been committed in France. Around ten new suspected victims have come forward as part of the ongoing probe into the late sex offender's network.

stories.title: Drone strike hits Abu Dhabi nuclear plant; UAE, Saudi Arabia and UN watchdog condemn
stories.summary: A drone strike hit a nuclear power plant in Abu Dhabi, setting a generator on fire but causing no injuries or radiological release. The UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the UN nuclear watchdog condemned the attack. No group claimed responsibility, though the UAE appeared to attribute it to Iran or its proxies.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran that 'there won't be anything left of them' without peace deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump warned Iran on Sunday to reach a peace deal quickly or face destruction. The statement came as the ongoing US war with Tehran and its allies continues to stall negotiations, increase energy prices, and fuel broader Middle East instability.

stories.title: 'Staggering' Iran toll drives up global executions to 40-year high, Amnesty says
stories.summary: Amnesty International reported Monday that global executions in 2025 reached their highest level since 1981, with at least 2,707 people executed worldwide. Iran accounted for 2,159 of those executions, representing a sharp increase that the UK-based rights organization described as staggering.

stories.title: Republican Representative Massie, critic of Trump, calls president's attacks 'desperate' ahead of primary
stories.summary: U.S. Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky dismissed President Donald Trump's repeated attacks against him as a desperate effort to boost Massie's opponent ahead of Tuesday's Republican primary. Massie, a longtime intraparty critic of Trump, made the remarks on Sunday.

stories.title: UAE ditches oil for AI to build Global South tech ‘bridge’
stories.summary: The UAE is accelerating its pivot from oil to artificial intelligence, aiming to become a tech bridge to the Global South with the delivery of advanced US-designed chips. However, Iran's IRGC has repeatedly targeted major Emirati data centers amid the ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump threatens Tehran; Saudi, UAE report drone attacks
stories.summary: Peace talks between the US and Iran remain deadlocked as drone attacks struck targets in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. President Trump issued threats against Tehran amid the ongoing escalation.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz credits 'political-military partnership' for Pakistan's recognition as US-Iran mediator, changed image
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif credited the country's "political-military partnership" for Pakistan's emergence as a recognized mediator between the United States and Iran. Islamabad continues to engage in de-escalation efforts between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Two injured, car damaged in Russian strike in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: A Russian strike in the Zaporizhzhia district of Ukraine on May 17 injured two people and damaged a vehicle. The attack targeted an area in the Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Julianne Moore says true gender equality still distant at Cannes
stories.summary: At a Women in Motion event during the Cannes Film Festival on Sunday, Oscar-winning actor Julianne Moore stated that true gender equality remains far off both globally and within the film industry. She accepted an award recognizing her advocacy for women in cinema.

stories.title: Iran warns UAE over Israel ties, says patience has limits
stories.summary: Iran issued a sharp warning to the United Arab Emirates over its ties with Israel. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Tehran's Expediency Council and former IRGC commander, said Iran has shown restraint but indicated its patience has limits.

stories.title: Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes, gunfire kill five
stories.summary: Gaza health officials reported that five Palestinians were killed by Israeli strikes and gunfire despite a fragile ceasefire across the territory.

stories.title: War update: 195 clashes on front lines, Ukrainian forces neutralize over 70 occupiers on Pokrovsk axis
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 195 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front lines as of the evening of May 17. The Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors saw the most intense fighting, with Ukrainian forces neutralizing over 70 Russian soldiers on the Pokrovsk axis.

stories.title: Pakistan interior minister holds talks with Iranian president in Tehran
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran for diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Israel strikes kill at least 7 in Lebanon as Hezbollah denounces US-brokered talks
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed seven people in Lebanon on Sunday, including an Islamic Jihad commander and two children, despite a fragile ceasefire. Hezbollah denounced US-brokered talks between Israel and Lebanon as a dead end. Eleven people were wounded across strikes in Tayr Felsay and Tayr Debba.

stories.title: Ukraine condemns drone attack near UAE nuclear plant as 'utterly unacceptable' – Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned a drone attack near the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the United Arab Emirates, calling any strike endangering nuclear facilities "utterly unacceptable."

stories.title: Mid-air collision between two US jets at airshow ends without fatalities in Idaho
stories.summary: Two US Navy EA-18G Growler jets collided mid-air during the Gunfighter Skies airshow at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho on Sunday. All four crew members ejected safely and were evaluated by medical personnel. No injuries were reported among crew, base personnel, or spectators.

stories.title: Israel expands death penalty regime in the occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israel has expanded its death penalty regime in the occupied West Bank, mandating capital punishment in military courts for Palestinian defendants. The law excludes Israeli settlers from prosecution under the same military court system. Protests against the legislation took place in Ramallah.

stories.title: Trade, energy, discussions on global conflicts to top agenda for Modi’s Nordic visit
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to make the first bilateral visit by an Indian PM to the Nordic region in 43 years, beginning in Oslo. The agenda includes trade, energy cooperation, and discussions on global conflicts at the first Nordic summit since 2022.

stories.title: Section 144 imposed throughout Balochistan for one month
stories.summary: The Balochistan provincial government imposed Section 144 across the entire province for one month, banning gatherings of five or more people. The restrictions also prohibit face coverings in public, the display of weapons, pillion riding, and the use of unregistered vehicles.

stories.title: 'This may be the last time you hear my voice': Political executions surge in Iran since start of war
stories.summary: The United Nations has verified the execution of at least 32 political prisoners in Iran since the US and Israeli attack on the country on 28 February.

stories.title: Inside the 'kill-zone' on Ukraine's front line, where new weapons have transformed war
stories.summary: A report from Ukraine's front lines describes how drones and other new weapons are transforming combat in what troops call the "kill-zone." While machines increasingly replace humans in frontline roles, soldiers remain essential for holding territory.

stories.title: UK firms halt investments and hiring as Iran war pushes up costs, bosses warn
stories.summary: A survey of UK employers indicates that businesses are halting investment and hiring plans due to rising costs linked to the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. April job vacancies fell 7.7% as companies shifted focus to cost management amid global uncertainty and economic instability.

stories.title: US citizens in DR Congo potentially exposed to Ebola in outbreak, report says
stories.summary: Several US citizens in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are believed to have been exposed to suspected Ebola cases, with some deemed high-risk exposures, according to STAT News. At least one individual may have developed symptoms. The Ebola outbreak in the DRC and Uganda has been declared a public health emergency of international concern.

stories.title: U.S., China, and the search for stability
stories.summary: An analysis examines U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to China amid the ongoing Iran conflict, exploring key issues discussed with President Xi Jinping including trade and security. The piece assesses outcomes and implications for the bilateral U.S.-China relationship.

stories.title: Pakistan hails PCA's decision in IWT proceedings, says it affirms limits on India’s water-control capability
stories.summary: Pakistan expressed satisfaction over a supplemental award by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in Indus Waters Treaty proceedings. Islamabad said the ruling affirmed limits on India's water-control capability regarding the Ratle and Kishenganga hydroelectric projects on the western rivers of the Indus system in occupied Kashmir.

stories.title: Rwandan genocide suspect Kabuga dies in custody in The Hague at age 91
stories.summary: Félicien Kabuga, a 91-year-old suspect in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, died in custody in The Hague. Kabuga had been accused of encouraging and financially supporting the mass killing of Rwanda's Tutsi minority.

stories.title: Security forces kill five terrorists in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed five suspected terrorists in operations conducted in the Bannu district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Saturday, May 16. The restive northwest region has seen ongoing counterterrorism operations.

stories.title: Ukraine demands Russia open Soviet-era archives on NKVD crimes
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs demanded that Russia open Soviet-era archives related to crimes committed by the NKVD secret police. Kyiv also called on the international community to condemn the crimes of the Soviet regime.

stories.title: Noted Sri Lankan journalist D.B.S. Jeyaraj dies in Canada
stories.summary: D.B.S. Jeyaraj, a prominent Sri Lankan journalist, died in Canada. He had written extensively for over four decades on Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict and political developments, including as The Hindu's Sri Lanka correspondent.

stories.title: All four crewmembers safe after two US fighter jets collide mid-air at Idaho Air Show
stories.summary: Two U.S. fighter jets collided mid-air during the Gunfighters Air Show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho. All four crewmembers were reported safe, and the base was placed on lockdown following the incident.

stories.title: Cuba weighing attacks on US soil, Caribbean assets with drones from Russia, Iran - report
stories.summary: A report indicates that Cuba may be considering attacks on U.S. soil and Caribbean assets using drone technology obtained from Russia and Iran. U.S. officials expressed concern about advanced military technologies being deployed so close to American territory.

stories.title: Russian propaganda spreads fake claims about NABU, SAPO 'investigation' into Ukraine's first lady
stories.summary: Russian propagandists have been spreading false claims on social media about an alleged investigation by Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies NABU and SAPO into First Lady Olena Zelenska. Ukrainian authorities identified the reports as disinformation.

stories.title: Iran chief negotiator Ghalibaf appointed to oversee ties with China: media
stories.summary: Iran's chief nuclear negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf was appointed to oversee relations with China. The appointment was proposed by President Masoud Pezeshkian and approved by Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency.

stories.title: Police investigating after West Bank settler filmed running over sheep with ATV
stories.summary: Israeli police are investigating an incident in the occupied West Bank in which a settler was filmed running over sheep with an ATV and allegedly beating a Palestinian man. The event, captured on video, followed a separate incident the previous day in which a settler was filmed beating a dog in a Palestinian village.

stories.title: Mainland China’s Wu Yongping on what the Xi-Trump summit means for Taiwan
stories.summary: Wu Yongping, dean of the Institute for Taiwan Studies at Tsinghua University in Beijing, discussed the implications of the Xi Jinping–Donald Trump summit for Taiwan. Wu analyzed the signals on the Taiwan question and the prospects for peaceful reunification between mainland China and Taiwan.

stories.title: PM Netanyahu says Israel is close to killing all architects of Oct 7 attacks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that Israel is close to killing all architects of the October 7 attacks. He reiterated that Israeli forces currently control 60 percent of Gaza's territory.

stories.title: Turkish flotilla to reach Israel in 48 hours, Netanyahu to meet with defense officials
stories.summary: A Turkish flotilla is reportedly within 48 hours of reaching Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a preliminary security consultation with defense officials on Sunday regarding the approaching vessels.

stories.title: What do we know about the Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda?
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern on Sunday, May 17.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill 7 as Hezbollah condemns talks
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed seven people in southern Lebanon, including an Islamic Jihad commander, as tensions escalated despite a fragile ceasefire. Hezbollah condemned ongoing US-brokered diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill 5 as Hezbollah condemns talks
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed five people, including two children, in southern Lebanon amid escalating tensions. The attacks occurred despite a fragile ceasefire and stalled diplomatic efforts between the parties. Hezbollah condemned the ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Iran media says ‘no tangible concessions’ in U.S. response to Iran proposal
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported that Washington's response to Tehran's nuclear proposal included a five-point list demanding Iran limit operations to one nuclear site and transfer its highly enriched uranium stockpile to the United States. The agency characterized the U.S. response as offering no tangible concessions.

stories.title: Israel extends death penalty law to Palestinians in West Bank
stories.summary: Israel's Central Command chief, Major General Avi Bluth, signed an order extending Israel's death penalty law to Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. The law targets individuals accused of acts aimed at denying the existence of the State of Israel. Legal and security officials had previously warned against applying civilian Knesset legislation in occupied territory.

stories.title: London Nova Festival exhibit's sign removed over fears of antisemitic crimes
stories.summary: A sign marking the location of a London exhibit commemorating the Nova Festival was removed over concerns about potential antisemitic crimes. Police reportedly requested the sign's swift removal to minimize public awareness of the exhibit's exact location.

stories.title: Woman injured in Russian attack on Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: A 76-year-old woman was injured in a Russian attack on the Sursko-Lytovske community in the Dnipro district of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region on Sunday, May 17.

stories.title: UAE reports drone strike at nuclear power plant as Iran war deadlock endures
stories.summary: Officials in Abu Dhabi reported that a drone strike caused a fire at a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates. The incident occurred amid stalled negotiations to end the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and restore shipping in the Gulf.

stories.title: Military jets’ crew members safely ejected after Idaho air show collision, Navy says
stories.summary: Four crew members safely ejected after two U.S. Navy E/A-18G Growler jets collided mid-air during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show near Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho on Sunday. The collision occurred approximately two miles from the base during an aerial demonstration.

stories.title: Crime increasingly a ‘serious barrier’ to UK growth, say business leaders
stories.summary: A British Chambers of Commerce survey found that two-fifths of UK companies experienced crime in the past year, including rising theft, fraud, and cyber-attacks. Business leaders warned that crime is becoming a serious barrier to economic growth and called on the government to increase support for affected firms.

stories.title: Why set a limit for Hong Kong’s ride-hailing services?
stories.summary: Hong Kong is debating whether to cap the number of vehicles licensed for ride-hailing services. Critics argue that no limit should be imposed, particularly on electric vehicles that meet regulatory standards, and that market forces should determine supply.

stories.title: Zelensky announces intensive week of talks with European Leaders and US
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced an intensive week of diplomatic talks with European leaders and the United States. The engagements include leadership-level meetings with European partners and further communication with Washington.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts three drones entering from Iraq
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed three drones that entered its airspace from Iraq on Sunday. The Saudi Ministry of Defence stated that the kingdom reserves the right to respond and will take operational measures against sovereignty violations.

stories.title: Minnesota deploys national guard to help fight wildfires in northern region
stories.summary: Minnesota Governor Tim Walz activated the state's National Guard to help battle wildfires in the northern part of the state. Walz issued an executive order declaring a peacetime emergency, describing the blazes as unpredictable and fast-moving amid dry, windy conditions.

stories.title: Zilhaj moon sighted, Eidul Azha to fall on May 27
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ruet-i-Hilal Committee announced the sighting of the Zilhaj moon, setting Eidul Azha for May 27. The committee met in Karachi, with zonal meetings held in Islamabad, Lahore, Quetta, and Peshawar.

stories.title: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni meets victims of Modena car incident
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni visited victims in Modena after a 31-year-old Italian man of Moroccan heritage drove into pedestrians in the northern city. The driver had a history of mental health issues. Hundreds gathered at a rally organized by Modena's mayor to counter far-right attempts to link the incident to immigration.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in Congo, Uganda an emergency of international concern
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern after approximately 80 suspected deaths were reported.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz thanks Qatari PM for 'strong endorsement, support' of Pakistan-led peace efforts
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al Thani. Sharif thanked Qatar for endorsing Pakistan-led peace efforts, and the leaders discussed the regional and international situation.

stories.title: The controversy over mixed-gender IDF units still ruffles Israeli society - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece addressed the ongoing controversy over mixed-gender units in the Israel Defense Forces. The debate centers on tensions between principles of gender equality and adherence to Jewish religious law within Israeli society.

stories.title: We notice shift in balance of actions on front line this year – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that a shift in the balance of military actions along the front line has become noticeable in 2026. He noted that Ukrainian Defense Forces' active operations exceeded those of Russian forces over the course of the day.

stories.title: UAE reports strike near Abu Dhabi nuclear power plant
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates reported a strike near the Barakah nuclear power plant in the Abu Dhabi area. Authorities are investigating the source of the attack, which UAE officials described as a "dangerous escalation."

stories.title: Embassies in Jerusalem: Gov't approves proposal allocating budget for relocations to capital
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved a proposal to allocate budgets for incentive packages aimed at encouraging foreign embassies to relocate to Jerusalem. The plan also includes promoting official meetings and delegations in the city and expanding cooperation in various fields.

stories.title: Drone strike sparks a fire on the edge of UAE nuclear facility
stories.summary: A drone strike sparked a fire near the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant on Sunday. Abu Dhabi condemned the attack as a threat to regional security. The incident underscored the risk of renewed conflict amid a fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine's long-range capabilities change situation and overall perception of Russia's war – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine's long-range strike capabilities are changing both the battlefield situation and global perceptions of Russia's war. He emphasized the strategic importance of these weapons in shaping international understanding of the conflict.

stories.title: Iranian media says ‘no tangible concessions’ in US response to Iran proposal
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that the US response to Iran's diplomatic proposal contained "no tangible concessions." The United States had reportedly conditioned a cessation of hostilities on all fronts on the commencement of formal negotiations.

stories.title: Russian air-defense crews are now the hunted as Ukraine bolts rocket pods to its long-range drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone forces struck a protected Russian air-defense position near Myrnyi in occupied Crimea, releasing thermal video of the attack. Ukraine has been equipping its long-range drones with rocket pods to target Russian air-defense crews.

stories.title: Death penalty law for Palestinian terrorists comes into effect in West Bank
stories.summary: A new Israeli law authorizing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of terrorism offenses has taken effect in the West Bank. Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that convicted attackers would "pay the heaviest price."

stories.title: Cuba acquires 300 attack drones from Russia and Iran and discusses potential attacks on US – Axios
stories.summary: A classified U.S. assessment reported by Axios indicates Cuba has acquired more than 300 military strike drones from Russia and Iran. Cuban officials have reportedly discussed potential attacks on U.S. targets, including Guantanamo Bay Naval Base, U.S. warships, and an airbase in Key West.

stories.title: Trump issues dire warning to Iran to accept peace deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned Iran that time is running out to reach a peace deal, stating there would be "nothing left" if an agreement is not reached. U.S.-Iran tensions and regional conflict continue to escalate.

stories.title: Israel to establish defence offices in former UNRWA compound
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to establish defense offices in a compound formerly used by UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees. Defense Minister Israel Katz described the decision as one of "sovereignty, Zionism, and security."

stories.title: Suspected Ukrainian military drone discovered after crashing in Lithuania
stories.summary: A suspected Ukrainian military drone crashed in Lithuania, raising concerns among Baltic NATO members about stray drones crossing into their airspace from the war in neighboring Ukraine. Officials confirmed the drone was discovered on Sunday.

stories.title: ‘Won’t be anything left’: Trump issues threat to Iran amid stalled talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened Iran, warning that there would be "nothing left" if Tehran does not agree to U.S. demands, which include dismantling its nuclear program and missile stockpiles. Negotiations between the two countries remain stalled.

stories.title: Israel kills at least five in Lebanon after ‘ceasefire’ extended
stories.summary: Israeli air attacks struck multiple locations in southern and eastern Lebanon, killing at least five people. The strikes occurred despite an extended ceasefire arrangement between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Hiker killed in attack by herd of cows in Austrian Alps
stories.summary: A 67-year-old woman was killed and her 65-year-old husband seriously injured after being attacked by a large herd of cows on a pasture in the Lienz district of East Tyrol, Austria. Authorities said the cause of the animals' aggressive behavior remains unclear.

stories.title: DRC struggling to contain Ebola outbreak as cases spread
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain a new Ebola outbreak as cases continue to spread. The country has experienced repeated Ebola outbreaks over the years.

stories.title: Islamist attack on Nigerian military school kills 17 police trainees
stories.summary: Suspected Islamist militants attacked a specialized military school in Yobe state in northeastern Nigeria, killing at least 17 police trainees. Nigeria's national police spokesman confirmed the assault on the facility, which trains both military and police personnel.

stories.title: Air force base in Idaho locked down after air show incident, officials say
stories.summary: Emergency crews responded to an incident involving two aircraft during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in western Idaho. The base was locked down and an investigation was initiated.

stories.title: Drone strike starts fire outside UAE nuclear plant
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire outside the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant. Authorities reported no injuries and said radiation levels were unaffected by the incident.

stories.title: Taiwan won't be sacrificed, U.S. arms sales a commitment: President responds to Trump
stories.summary: Taiwanese President Lai responded to the recent Trump-Xi summit in Beijing by asserting that Taiwan will not be sacrificed and that U.S. arms sales represent a commitment to the island's defense.

stories.title: Will the latest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda spread further?
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the latest Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a global health emergency, raising concerns about further spread of the virus across the region.

stories.title: China will buy at least US$17 billion of US farm goods annually, White House says
stories.summary: The White House announced that China has agreed to purchase at least $17 billion in U.S. agricultural products annually through 2028. The commitment resulted from a summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping, supplementing earlier soybean purchase agreements from October 2025.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia condemns UAE drone strike, backs security measures
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia condemned a drone strike that ignited a fire near a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates, calling the attack a threat to regional security and stability. Riyadh expressed solidarity with the UAE and endorsed measures to protect its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.title: Fire breaks out near nuclear power plant in United Arab Emirates following drone attack
stories.summary: A drone strike near Abu Dhabi's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant on May 17 ignited a fire in the vicinity of the facility. The incident prompted regional condemnation and raised concerns about security threats to critical infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Mass DC prayer event with top White House officials seeks to reclaim US Christian roots
stories.summary: Senior White House officials including Pete Hegseth, Marco Rubio, and Mike Johnson are scheduled to speak at "Reclaim 250," a large-scale prayer event in Washington, D.C. Critics have characterized the gathering as promoting Christian nationalism.

stories.title: UAE blames Iran or its proxies for drone strike fire near nuclear plant
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran or its proxies for a drone strike that caused a fire near the Barakah nuclear power plant, calling it a "dangerous escalation." The incident caused no injuries or radiation alerts but occurred during a fragile ceasefire in the sixth week of the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in south Lebanon kill five, wound several
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit several towns in southern Lebanon, killing at least five people and wounding multiple others. Strikes on Tairfalsiya killed three, including a child, and wounded eight. In Tirdaba, two people were killed, including a child, and three others were injured.

stories.title: “There was no way back”: Captured Russian soldiers say commanders welded pipeline shut behind them
stories.summary: Captured Russian soldiers reported that commanders sent them through a gas pipeline behind Ukrainian lines and welded the entry shut, preventing retreat. Ukrainian forces had anticipated the maneuver and positioned drones at the pipeline exit.

stories.title: Russians carry out nearly 40 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving two killed, five others injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 40 attacks on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region using drones and artillery, striking four districts. The attacks killed two people and injured five others.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least five people in Gaza, according to medics. One Palestinian was killed near a police post and another at a tent encampment in Khan Younis.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four people in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed four people in Gaza, according to Palestinian medics. The Israeli military stated it had killed a militant who posed an immediate threat to its forces in the territory.

stories.title: Mexican officials announce 10 dead in early-morning shooting in Tehuitzingo
stories.summary: Mexican officials reported that 10 people were killed in an early-morning shooting in Tehuitzingo. Authorities attributed the attack to unidentified armed individuals but provided no further details about the attackers or their motives.

stories.title: Putin’s new Transnistria citizenship decree is about finding more soldiers for war against Ukraine — Moldova’s president
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on May 15 fast-tracking Russian citizenship for residents of Moldova's breakaway Transnistria region. Moldovan President Maia Sandu characterized the move as an effort to recruit more soldiers for Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran, Pakistan discuss stalled US talks as Ghalibaf criticises US role
stories.summary: Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf met Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi to discuss stalled negotiations between Tehran and Washington. Ghalibaf criticized the U.S. role in the region, arguing that American presence creates insecurity rather than stability.

stories.title: Government approves dedicated unit to assist new immigrants serving in IDF
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved a dedicated unit to assist new immigrants serving in the IDF. The unit will specialize in guiding and supporting olim throughout their military service, following a significant rise in immigration since October 7.

stories.title: Israel kills three Palestinians in strike on an aid kitchen in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a kitchen providing meals to displaced people in Gaza, killing three Palestinians and injuring others. The kitchen had been serving as an aid distribution point for civilians.

stories.title: Palestinian leader's son wins role in Abbas' party, official says
stories.summary: Tareq Abbas, the millionaire businessman son of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, has secured a steering role within the Fatah party, according to a party official in Ramallah. The development comes amid a growing succession struggle for control of the Palestinian Authority.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Patriots are running out. Can a recycled Soviet missile replace them?
stories.summary: As the Iran conflict depletes global Patriot missile stockpiles, Ukraine is exploring alternatives for long-range air defense. A recycled Soviet-era missile system called Freya is being considered as a potential replacement.

stories.title: IDF faces looming manpower gap as ultra-Orthodox draft fight stalls service extension
stories.summary: The Israeli military faces a growing manpower shortage as ultra-Orthodox draft legislation stalls in the Knesset. The issue has gained urgency amid a coalition crisis that could lead to the dissolution of the Knesset.

stories.title: Prime Minister Netanyahu, US President Trump speak on Iran updates, China visit
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump spoke about developments regarding Iran and Trump's recent visit to China. Netanyahu said Israel was prepared for any scenario.

stories.title: Bowlers, opener Joy put Bangladesh in command of second Test against Pakistan
stories.summary: In the second Test in Sylhet, Bangladesh's bowlers dominated Pakistan before opener Mahmudul Hasan Joy scored 52 off 64 balls. Bangladesh closed day two at 110-3 in their second innings, leading by 156 runs with a 1-0 series lead.

stories.title: Pakistan 'critical counter-terrorism partner' in US fight against IS-K: Centcom
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command Commander Admiral Bradford Cooper described Pakistan as a "critical counter-terrorism partner" central to the fight against Islamic State-Khorasan in South Asia. The remarks came during testimony before the Senate Armed Services Committee on the progress of Operation Epic Fury against Iran.

stories.title: PM Modi lands in Sweden; to hold talks on bilateral trade, technology, defence | LIVE
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Modi arrived in Sweden for a two-day visit to hold talks with Swedish Prime Minister Kristersson. Discussions are expected to focus on bilateral trade, technology, and defense cooperation.

stories.title: Washington lets the Russian oil loophole expire, ending months of seaborne sanctions relief
stories.summary: The U.S. administration allowed a sanctions relief carve-out for Russian seaborne oil exports to expire. Senators from both parties had pushed to end the loophole, which critics argued funneled billions of dollars into Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire a dangerous fiction in the war against Hezbollah - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examined the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, noting that Hezbollah has used the agreement to adapt and regroup. The piece argued that negotiations disconnected from battlefield realities create space for armed groups to reorganize.

stories.title: Ukrainian-made weapons used to strike targets in Moscow region — General Staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff announced that domestically developed weapons were used to strike targets in Russia's Moscow region. No further details about the specific weapons or targets were provided.

stories.title: Iraqi farmer killed to hide evidence of two Israeli bases in country: Report
stories.summary: A New York Times investigation reported that an Iraqi shepherd was killed after discovering two secret Israeli military bases in western Iraq. The Wall Street Journal had previously revealed that Israel established a covert outpost in Iraq's desert to support air operations during its conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Andy Burnham faces perilous race to win Makerfield byelection, allies say
stories.summary: Andy Burnham is expected to be confirmed as Labour's candidate for the Makerfield byelection in north-west England. Allies warn he faces a difficult contest against Reform UK, which captured more than 50% of the vote in recent local elections. Reform is expected to campaign heavily on immigration and Brexit.

stories.title: Axios: Cuba has acquired over 300 Russian and Iranian military drones
stories.summary: A classified U.S. intelligence assessment shared with Axios indicates Cuba has acquired over 300 military drones from Russia and Iran since 2023. The assessment reportedly states that Cuba's military has begun weighing potential strikes on U.S. targets.

stories.title: Israel to ban cell phones in middle schools, Education Ministry confirms
stories.summary: Israel's Education Ministry confirmed it will ban cell phones in middle schools. A similar prohibition was introduced in elementary schools in February.

stories.title: World-famous illusionist David Blaine visits Ukraine
stories.summary: World-famous illusionist David Blaine visited Ukraine, traveling via Ukrzaliznytsia rail to Lviv, Kyiv, and Kharkiv.

stories.title: Indian worker among those killed in Moscow drone strikes, Embassy says
stories.summary: An Indian worker was among those killed in drone strikes in the Moscow region of Russia, according to India's embassy. Embassy officials visited the site, met injured workers in the hospital, and coordinated with Russian authorities to provide assistance.

stories.title: Iran chief negotiator Ghalibaf appointed to oversee ties with China: Media
stories.summary: Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf, who served as chief nuclear negotiator, has been appointed to oversee relations with China. The appointment was made at the proposal of the Iranian president.

stories.title: The miracle that shaped Israel Prize winner Avi Rivkind’s life and career - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece profiled Israel Prize winner Avi Rivkind, a trauma surgeon whose career was shaped by a split-second medical decision that saved a young soldier's life.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran ‘clock is ticking’ threatening severe consequences
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a warning to Iran on Truth Social, stating that Tehran must act quickly or face severe consequences. Trump wrote that "the Clock is Ticking" and urged Iran to move fast on negotiations.

stories.title: Israel’s PM says close to killing all architects of October 7 attack
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel is close to eliminating all architects of the October 7 attack. His remarks followed the IDF's announcement that Ezzedine al-Haddad, commander of Hamas's armed wing, was killed in an air strike in Gaza on Friday.

stories.title: PM: IDF combating drones for six years, unlimited budget team formed for Hezbollah's FPV threat
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told the cabinet that the IDF has been combating drone threats for six years and announced the formation of a team with an unlimited budget to counter Hezbollah's first-person-view drone threat.

stories.title: Cutting US aid to Israel would be a strategic disaster for America - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that cutting US aid to Israel would be a strategic mistake for America. The author contended that American assistance gives US diplomats significant leverage over Israeli decisions in the West Bank and Gaza.

stories.title: Ministry of Digital Transformation shares details about use of digital technologies on battlefield
stories.summary: Acting Ukrainian Digital Transformation Minister Oleksandr Bornyakov said Ukrainian forces are effectively deploying digital technologies on the battlefield against Russia. He noted this is occurring despite Russia's advantages in manpower, tanks, and ammunition.

stories.title: Coalition seeks to fast-track 2 key bills through committee, bypassing legal review
stories.summary: Israel's governing coalition moved to fast-track two bills through Knesset committee sessions, bypassing standard legal review. The legislation would split the Attorney General's role and overhaul media regulation ahead of an expected Knesset dissolution and early elections, despite opposition from the legal adviser.

stories.title: Kundi calls on PM to 'take interest' in KP's issues, says told CM Afridi to focus on governance not Adiala
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to take greater interest in the province's issues after meeting KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi in Peshawar. Kundi also said he told Afridi to focus on provincial governance rather than PTI's campaign for party founder Imran Khan's release from Adiala jail in Rawalpindi.

stories.title: A one-meter gas pipe, a scooter, and a surrender: how a Russian assault group became POWs
stories.summary: A Russian assault group was captured in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Oblast after entering positions through a one-meter gas pipe that commanders sealed behind them. Three additional Russian soldiers surrendered near Vovchansk in the Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Russia killed 52 people in Ukraine this week — firing mostly ballistic missiles, hardest for air defense to stop
stories.summary: Russian forces killed 52 people in Ukraine over the past week, primarily using ballistic missiles, which are the hardest type for air defense systems to intercept. Russia also launched 3,170 drones at Ukrainian targets during the seven-day period.

stories.title: IDF warns of severe personnel shortages, last window to solve crisis with legislation
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces warned of severe personnel shortages, stating it is still missing 12,000 troops with the gap expected to widen. Military officials said the government's current draft bill would not provide an adequate solution and called the present moment the last window for legislative action.

stories.title: London police: 20 right-wing, 12 anti-Israel protesters arrested in dueling rallies
stories.summary: London police arrested 20 right-wing and 12 anti-Israel protesters during competing rallies in the city. Nine arrests at a large rally organized by anti-Islam figure Tommy Robinson involved hate crime charges, while two arrests were made among participants of an opposing Nakba Day march.

stories.title: Air raid alerts declared in several regions due to threat of drones
stories.summary: Air raid alerts were declared across multiple regions of Ukraine due to the threat of incoming drones.

stories.title: Sudanese army advances in Blue Nile state deepen displacement crisis
