stories.summary: President Trump defended the Iran war as worth the economic costs it has imposed. Rural voters in communities like Wiggins, Colorado, expressed agreement despite rising gasoline prices.

stories.title: Francesca Albanese on Israeli sexual violence suffered by Palestinians
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese discussed allegations of sexual violence committed by Israeli forces against Palestinians in an interview with journalist Redi Tlhabi.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defence Forces strike Russian command posts, warehouses in occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defence Forces conducted overnight strikes on Russian command posts, warehouses, and other military facilities in occupied areas of the Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions on the night of May 16.

stories.title: UK police brace for far-right rally and counter-demonstration
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in London on Saturday for a far-right march organized by Tommy Robinson and a counter-demonstration linked to pro-Palestinian Nakba Day protests. The Metropolitan Police deployed approximately 4,000 officers along with horses, dogs, drones, and helicopters in one of its largest operations in recent years.

stories.title: DRC health minister warns ‘very high’ Ebola lethality rate as toll hits 80
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's health minister has warned of a very high lethality rate as the Ebola death toll reached 80. The Africa CDC expressed concern that the Bundibugyo strain outbreak could spread rapidly due to intense population movement in the region.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Gaza City kills two, wounds three
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck a vehicle near al-Wahda Tower in western Gaza City on Saturday evening, killing two people and wounding three others. The overall death toll in Gaza has reached at least 72,757 killed and 172,645 wounded since October 7, 2023.

stories.title: North America’s largest commuter rail system shuts down as workers strike
stories.summary: North America's largest commuter rail system shut down operations after unionized workers went on strike, disrupting service for passengers.

stories.title: Ending war along front line can be major victory for Ukraine – Czech analyst
stories.summary: A Czech analyst assessed that ending the Russia-Ukraine war roughly along the current front line would constitute a major victory for Ukraine.

stories.title: Tommy Robinson tells tens of thousands at London rally to prepare for ‘battle of Britain’
stories.summary: Far-right activist Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, held a rally in central London on Saturday drawing tens of thousands of supporters. Islamophobic and ethnonationalist hate speech and flyers were distributed at the event, which Robinson called preparation for the "battle of Britain."

stories.title: Republican Senator Cassidy loses re-election to Trump retribution campaign
stories.summary: Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana became the first elected US senator to lose re-nomination since 2012, falling in the Republican primary as part of a Trump-backed retribution campaign against those who voted to convict the former president.

stories.title: Republican Cassidy faces Trump retribution effort in Louisiana Senate primary
stories.summary: Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana faced a primary election on Saturday against two rivals, including a Trump-backed challenger, after being targeted for retribution by President Donald Trump. A loss would make him the first sitting Senate incumbent to lose renomination in over a decade.

stories.title: Rising diesel costs from Iran war strain U.S. school budgets
stories.summary: Rising diesel fuel costs linked to the conflict with Iran are straining U.S. school district budgets, forcing administrators to use emergency funds, reduce spending, and restructure transportation plans.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in south Lebanon kill couple, hit multiple towns
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit the town of Haboush in southern Lebanon, destroying a home and killing Muhammad Hassan Jammoul and his wife Sakina Muhammad Abbas Makki. The strikes occurred despite Israel and Lebanon agreeing to extend their ceasefire by 45 days on Friday. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported 2,969 killed and 9,112 wounded since March 2.

stories.title: 8 injured as man rams car into crowd in Italy’s Modena
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man drove a car into a crowd in Modena, northern Italy, injuring at least eight people, four seriously. The driver, of North African origin, attempted to flee and attacked a bystander with a knife before being subdued by pedestrians.

stories.title: Ukrainian border guards capture three Russian soldiers near Vovchansk
stories.summary: Ukrainian border guards from the "Forpost" brigade captured three Russian soldiers near the city of Vovchansk in the Kharkiv region along the southern Slobozhanshchyna front.

stories.title: Karachi courts reserve decision on police pleas for alleged drug queenpin Anmol’s physical remand
stories.summary: Multiple courts in Karachi, Pakistan, reserved decisions on police requests for the physical remand of alleged drug queenpin Anmol, also known as Pinky, in over 15 cases including murder. She was arrested earlier in the week in a joint police and intelligence raid.

stories.title: Over 250,000 join Nakba Day march against Gaza war, far-right
stories.summary: Approximately 250,000 pro-Palestine demonstrators marched in London on Nakba Day to protest the war in Gaza and far-right movements. The march reportedly far outnumbered a separate rally organized by far-right activist Tommy Robinson.

stories.title: Hamas official says military chief has died after Israel says it targeted him
stories.summary: A Hamas official confirmed the death of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the group's military chief, after Israel said it targeted him in Gaza City. Witnesses reported that mosques in Gaza City announced his death.

stories.title: Canada deepens Arctic defense ties with Nordics after Trump threats
stories.summary: Canada is strengthening Arctic defense cooperation with Nordic countries amid heightened concerns over Arctic security and pressure from statements by U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: 'There is little which is Jewish about Israel': Haim Bresheeth on antisemitism and Gaza
stories.summary: A planned Nakba commemoration march in London is expected to draw thousands of participants. British-Israeli author Haim Bresheeth-Zabner, a son of Holocaust survivors, plans to join. A separate far-right march led by Tommy Robinson is also scheduled nearby, raising concerns about potential clashes.

stories.title: China, US agree to reduce tariffs on certain goods
stories.summary: China and the United States agreed to reduce tariffs on certain goods to promote bilateral trade, according to a statement from China's Ministry of Commerce.

stories.title: At least 8 killed, 25 injured in train collision that sparks bus fire in Thailand
stories.summary: At least eight people were killed and 25 injured when a train collided with a bus in Thailand, sparking a fire that engulfed the bus and nearby vehicles. Firefighters and rescue crews responded to the multi-vehicle incident.

stories.title: US sanctions relief for Russian oil shipments appears to end with no renewal issued
stories.summary: U.S. sanctions relief allowing Russian oil shipments appears to have expired with no renewal issued. The waiver had been introduced during global energy disruptions linked to the Iran conflict as a temporary measure to stabilize supply.

stories.title: The existential choice: Next Israeli election must be about policy, not poison - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's 2026 elections should focus on substantive policy rather than divisive politics, warning that growing internal divisions may pose a greater threat than external enemies.

stories.title: Former MK Yousef Jabareen elected leader of Arab-majority party Hadash
stories.summary: Former Knesset member Yousef Jabareen was elected leader of the Arab-majority party Hadash following a leadership shakeup in which two sitting MKs stepped down. Jabareen has signaled plans to revive the Joint List alliance of Arab-majority parties.

stories.title: Timmy the whale confirmed dead by Danish authorities
stories.summary: Danish authorities confirmed that Timmy, a beached humpback whale transported to the North Sea in a rescue attempt, was found dead near the island of Anholt in the Kattegat strait. The rescue operation had been criticized by wildlife experts as "pure animal cruelty."

stories.title: War update: 61 clashes on front line since morning
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported 61 clashes with Russian troops since the morning. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk, Northern Slobozhanshchyna, and Kursk sectors of the front line.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon day after ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on at least five villages in southern Lebanon one day after a ceasefire extension was announced. The strikes occurred despite the renewed truce agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: UK’s ex-health minister Streeting says will run to replace PM Keir Starmer
stories.summary: Former UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting announced he will run to replace Prime Minister Keir Starmer as Labour leader. Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham also launched a bid and is considered the frontrunner in the anticipated leadership contest.

stories.title: Taiwan insists it is independent after Trump warning
stories.summary: Taiwan reasserted its independence following a warning from U.S. President Trump, who cautioned against a formal declaration of independence after his summit in Beijing. The statement highlighted ongoing tensions over Taiwan's status.

stories.title: Whale found dead near Danish island after German rescue operation
stories.summary: A whale that had been the subject of a rescue operation off the German coast was found dead near the Danish island of Anholt. Wildlife experts had previously criticized the rescue effort, warning it would cause the animal additional distress.

stories.title: French judge to probe Jamal Khashoggi killing after complaint against Saudi crown prince
stories.summary: A French investigative magistrate will probe a complaint filed by rights groups against Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over the 2018 killing of journalist Jamal Khashoggi. Khashoggi was strangled and dismembered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey.

stories.title: Trump officials urged UAE to seize Iranian island, report says
stories.summary: Senior Trump administration officials reportedly urged the United Arab Emirates to seize Iran's Lavan Island in the Persian Gulf, according to The Telegraph. The report indicated that the island had already been targeted in covert Emirati strikes in early April.

stories.title: IDF kills two Hamas terrorists who infiltrated Israel during October 7 massacre
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces killed two Hamas militants who had infiltrated Israel during the October 7 massacre. An additional Hamas fighter from the Bureij Battalion was also killed in a separate strike on Wednesday.

stories.title: Another Naftogaz employee Injured in Russian attack on Poltava region on May 5 dies
stories.summary: A Naftogaz employee injured in a Russian attack on Ukraine's Poltava region on May 5 has died in hospital. The attack targeted energy infrastructure in the oblast.

stories.title: Hamas confirms killing of military chief after Israeli strike
stories.summary: Hamas confirmed that its armed wing chief, Ezzedine Al-Haddad, was killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City. The Israeli military and intelligence agency said they carried out the precision strike targeting Haddad as part of their ongoing campaign against Hamas's senior leadership.

stories.title: Parents convicted in UK for arranging child marriages of sons in Pakistan
stories.summary: A couple in Nottingham, UK, were convicted of arranging child marriages for their sons in Pakistan. They received two-month suspended sentences and 100 hours of community service at Nottingham Crown Court.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks Iran understandings to relay to US, sources say
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi traveled to Iran to seek understandings that could be relayed to the United States, according to Pakistani sources cited by Al Arabiya. Some progress was reportedly made on issues related to the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Zelensky congratulates scientists and engineers on their professional holiday
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky congratulated scientists and engineers on their professional holiday. He emphasized that technological development and scientific knowledge provide a critical advantage for Ukraine during wartime.

stories.title: Iran will announce Strait of Hormuz mechanism, collect fees, Iranian MP says
stories.summary: An Iranian member of parliament announced that Iran plans to introduce a new mechanism for the Strait of Hormuz, including the collection of fees from vessels transiting the waterway. Only commercial ships from cooperating parties would benefit from the arrangement.

stories.title: Sudanese army captures key town near Ethiopian border from RSF
stories.summary: Sudan's armed forces announced they recaptured a key town in southeastern Blue Nile state near the Ethiopian border from the Rapid Support Forces. The military said it inflicted heavy losses on the RSF during the operation.

stories.title: Hamas confirms Israel's killing of military leader
stories.summary: Hamas confirmed that Israel killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the Qassam Brigades leader, along with his wife, daughter, and other Palestinian civilians in a strike in Gaza on Friday evening. Hamas described the attack as a breach of the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Mamdani shares 'Nakba Remembrance Day' post featuring Zionist-created art
stories.summary: Academic Mahmood Mamdani shared a 'Nakba Remembrance Day' post featuring a 'Visit Palestine' poster originally created in 1936 by Frank Krausz. Krausz was a Zionist Jew and Holocaust survivor.

stories.title: From Nakba to genocide: A Gaza grandmother’s lifetime of loss and resilience
stories.summary: Fatema Obaid, a 95-year-old Palestinian grandmother and survivor of the 1948 Nakba, has endured Israeli bombardment and the loss of 70 family members in Gaza. She refused Israeli military orders to leave Gaza City during the 2023 conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine forecasts brief rain showers on Sunday, temperatures up to +23°C
stories.summary: Ukraine's weather forecast for Sunday, May 17, predicted brief rain showers and thunderstorms across most regions, with daytime temperatures reaching up to 23°C.

stories.title: Israel kills more than 200 children in Lebanon since March
stories.summary: Children's welfare organizations reported that Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March have killed more than 200 children. Minors in Lebanon are also suffering from displacement, distress, and lack of basic services.

stories.title: Israel confirms Hamas armed wing chief killed in Gaza strike
stories.summary: Israel confirmed it killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, chief of Hamas's armed wing, in a strike on a residential apartment and civilian vehicle in Gaza City on Friday. Two Hamas officials also confirmed his death.

stories.title: PM Modi congratulates new Iraq PM Ali Falih Kadhim al-Zaidi on assuming charge
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Ali Falih Kadhim al-Zaidi on assuming the role of Iraq's new Prime Minister. Al-Zaidi emerged as a consensus candidate after weeks of deliberation among Iraq's Coordination Framework parties.

stories.title: Hamas confirms killing of Qassam Brigades leader in Israeli attack
stories.summary: Hamas confirmed that Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the leader of its Qassam Brigades armed wing in Gaza, was killed in an Israeli strike that also killed seven other people.

stories.title: Clavicular strikes plea deal with prosecutors after alligator shooting
stories.summary: An individual reached a plea deal with prosecutors following a shooting involving an alligator. Under the agreement, the defendant must complete 20 hours of community service and take a firearms safety course.

stories.title: Estonian FM Margus Tsahkna: Russia in fragile state now, more pressure needed
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said Russia is in a fragile state and called for increased pressure on Moscow. He cautioned Europe against entering direct negotiations with Russia, arguing that Ukraine currently holds the upper hand.

stories.title: Abu-Bilal al-Minuki: ISIL’s shadow commander in West Africa
stories.summary: Nigeria and the United States announced that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, described as a key ISIL leader in West Africa, was killed in a joint military operation in Borno state, Nigeria.

stories.title: Putin discusses Iran conflict with UAE leader
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed the US-Israeli conflict with Iran in a call with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, according to the Kremlin. Both leaders emphasized the importance of securing peace.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill six in southern Lebanon hours after extension of ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed at least six people, including three paramedics at a health centre, just hours after Israeli and Lebanese officials agreed to extend a ceasefire. Israel also announced it had killed Hamas military chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad in a targeted strike in Gaza on Friday.

stories.title: Israeli artillery fire kills one person in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli artillery fire near the Sarbin junction in southern Lebanon killed one person and wounded another, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency.

stories.title: As Netanyahu spotlights Israel's ties to UAE, its rulers prefer to be discreet
stories.summary: While Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has publicly highlighted Israel's ties with the UAE, Emirati rulers prefer to keep the relationship discreet. The UAE normalized relations with Israel in 2020 under the Abraham Accords.

stories.title: Man arrested in London after 30-year-old run over by van near flag protest in Birmingham
stories.summary: A man was arrested at London's Euston station in connection with an incident in Birmingham in which a 30-year-old was run over by a van after flags were removed from lamp-posts. The arrest took place near the meeting point of the "Unite the Kingdom" march. A second man was arrested on suspicion of encouraging attacks on a police officer.

stories.title: Rising diesel costs from Iran war strain US school budgets
stories.summary: Rising diesel prices driven by the Iran war are straining US school district budgets from Washington state to Texas and Alaska. Districts are tapping emergency reserves to keep buses running and facilities powered.

stories.title: Zelensky, Macron discuss cooperation in countering Russian ballistic weapons
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky spoke with French President Macron about cooperation in countering Russian ballistic weapons. Zelensky said France expressed readiness to collaborate in developing countermeasures against ballistic missile threats.

stories.title: New York’s Long Island Rail Road strike halts busiest US commuter line
stories.summary: A strike by workers on New York's Long Island Rail Road halted service on the busiest commuter rail line in the United States. The railroad serves nearly 300,000 passengers daily.

stories.title: Iran warns of readiness for war and economic costs as US talks falter
stories.summary: Iranian leaders have escalated warnings of war readiness and highlighted potential economic costs as nuclear and diplomatic talks with the United States appear to stall, directing messaging at both domestic and international audiences.

stories.title: Arrests made as Tommy Robinson's far-right supporters rally in central London
stories.summary: Supporters of far-right activist Tommy Robinson gathered in central London on 16 May 2026 for a 'Unite the Kingdom' march. Police made arrests during the rally. Robinson urged attendees to become active in local political parties.

stories.title: Russia maintains military presence in post-Assad Syria – but Damascus now holds leverage
stories.summary: Satellite imagery shows renewed Russian cargo activity at the Tartus naval facility in Syria. Damascus is renegotiating the terms of Moscow's military presence following the fall of the Assad government.

stories.title: At Samsung, the global AI boom has spurred a looming strike and deep divisions
stories.summary: Over 45,000 Samsung Electronics workers in South Korea are threatening an 18-day strike starting May 21 over disputes about bonus payouts. The action could reduce production of memory chips critical to AI data centres, smartphones, and laptops, raising concerns among investors and the South Korean government.

stories.title: How Thomas Massie came to represent Republican dissent in age of Trump
stories.summary: Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky faces a competitive primary challenge from a fellow Republican backed by President Trump, reflecting intra-party tensions over dissent within the GOP.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill man in West Bank camp: Palestinian Ministry
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a man inside Jenin camp in the occupied West Bank. The Palestinian Red Crescent said its teams received the man with a live bullet wound to the thigh and no signs of life.

stories.title: Gaza: Israel kills Hamas leader as deaths mount despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel's military confirmed it killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the head of Hamas's Qassam Brigades military wing, in an air strike on Gaza on Friday. He was the most senior Hamas official killed since the October US-backed ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Putin to visit China May 19 to 20 after Trump trip
stories.summary: The Kremlin announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit China on May 19–20 for talks with President Xi Jinping. The two leaders are expected to sign a joint declaration at the conclusion of their discussions.

stories.title: NATO summit in Ankara to be critical for future of alliance – Erdogan
stories.summary: Turkish President Erdogan stated that the NATO leaders' summit scheduled for July 7–8 in Ankara will be critical for the alliance's future and international security. He emphasized that NATO must adapt to new global threats.

stories.title: Israeli army kills Palestinian man, raids homes in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a 34-year-old Palestinian man during a raid in Jenin Camp in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry.

stories.title: Are new Knesset proposals pushing Israel toward Hungary-style governance? - opinion
stories.summary: New legislative proposals in the Israeli Knesset have raised concerns about potential shifts in governance. Commentators draw comparisons to Hungary's democratic trajectory under similar reforms.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended by 45 days, but fresh strikes raise concerns
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon extended their ceasefire by 45 days with US backing for a long-term solution. However, fresh Israeli strikes and ongoing tensions with Hezbollah have raised doubts about the durability of the truce.

stories.title: Kash Patel faces scrutiny over snorkeling outing at USS Arizona memorial in Hawaii
stories.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel is facing scrutiny after reports that he took a snorkeling excursion around the USS Arizona memorial in Hawaii last summer. The Associated Press obtained government emails describing it as a "VIP snorkel" at the Pearl Harbor site, which holds the remains of more than 1,000 U.S. Navy sailors and Marines.

stories.title: Iran to unveil new mechanism to manage Strait of Hormuz traffic
stories.summary: Iran announced it will soon unveil a new system to manage maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The mechanism would regulate commercial vessel passage and impose fees for specialized services.

stories.title: Wes Streeting confirms he will stand if Labour leadership race is triggered
stories.summary: Former UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed at a Progress conference on Saturday that he would enter a Labour leadership race if triggered. He outlined a policy platform including pursuit of a "new special relationship" with the European Union, potentially involving rejoining the trade bloc.

stories.title: China and US agree to establish trade and investment councils after Xi-Trump summit
stories.summary: China and the United States agreed to establish trade and investment councils following a summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, committing to reciprocal tariff cuts. Progress was also reported on agricultural trade and aircraft issues.

stories.title: No vaccine for new highly lethal Ebola outbreak, DR Congo warns, as death toll hits 80
stories.summary: A new Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused at least 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths. Health Minister Samuel-Roger Kamba confirmed in Kinshasa that the strain, known as Bundibugyo, currently has no available vaccine and is considered highly lethal.

stories.title: Rescue diver dies during search for bodies of Italians who drowned in Maldives caves
stories.summary: A Maldivian military diver, Staff Sgt Mohamed Mahdhee, died during a search-and-rescue operation to recover the bodies of Italian divers who drowned in underwater caves in the Maldives.

stories.title: US and Nigeria presidents say senior IS leader killed in joint operation
stories.summary: The presidents of the United States and Nigeria announced that a senior Islamic State leader was killed in a joint military operation. Nigeria's president called the strike a significant example of counterterrorism collaboration.

stories.title: Sri Lanka imposes 50% surcharge on car imports to protect currency from further slide
stories.summary: Sri Lanka imposed a 50% surcharge on car imports to protect the rupee, which has depreciated over 3% against the dollar by mid-May. Officials attributed the currency pressure primarily to the Iran war and a surge in fuel import costs.

stories.title: London police brace themselves for big far-right rally, counter-demo
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police deployed approximately 4,000 officers along with horses, dogs, drones, and helicopters in preparation for a large far-right rally and a counter-demonstration in central London.

stories.title: Pakistani interior minister arrives in Tehran
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran for unannounced meetings with his Iranian counterpart and other officials. The visit was not previously publicised and was reported by Iranian media.

stories.title: Russia may try to test NATO’s unity in Black Sea, says Czech analyst
stories.summary: A Czech security analyst warned that Russia may attempt to test NATO's cohesion in the Black Sea region, particularly targeting perceived vulnerabilities in countries such as Bulgaria, rather than solely in the more frequently discussed Baltic area.

stories.title: The UAE cannot invoke international law while violating it
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlights allegations that the UAE operates torture sites in Yemen, transfers arms to Sudan, and supports Israel's military campaign in Gaza. These claims are contrasted with the UAE's public invocations of international law in its diplomatic rhetoric.

stories.title: UN event highlights India-Oman maritime ties through maiden voyage of stitched sail vessel
stories.summary: At a UN event, Indian Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish highlighted centuries-old maritime ties between India and Oman. The occasion marked the maiden voyage of a traditional stitched sail vessel symbolizing the two nations' historic trade and commerce relationship.

stories.title: PM Modi in Netherlands LIVE: Modi addresses Indian diaspora at The Hague, highlights Govt's achievements
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Indian diaspora at The Hague during a visit to the Netherlands. He was scheduled to hold talks with Dutch Prime Minister Jetten and call on King Willem-Alexander and Queen Maxima.

stories.title: US and Nigeria claim killing of Islamic State second-in-command
stories.summary: US and Nigerian forces killed a senior Islamic State leader described as the most active terrorist in the world in a joint operation in Nigeria. Both countries' presidents announced the operation's success.

stories.title: Enemies launch missile strike on Kryvyi Rih’s industrial infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a missile strike on the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, damaging industrial infrastructure in the area.

stories.title: Trump says Islamic State group leader was killed in a joint US-Nigerian mission
stories.summary: A joint US-Nigerian military mission killed a senior Islamic State group leader in Nigeria. The operation targeted the group's second-in-command, who had been described as one of the organization's most active operatives globally.

stories.title: At least eight people killed in Bangkok rail crossing collision
stories.summary: At least eight people were killed and 32 injured when a freight train struck a bus at a rail crossing near Makkasan station in Bangkok, Thailand. The collision sparked a fire that engulfed the bus and nearby vehicles. Firefighters and rescue crews were dispatched to the scene.

stories.title: After Trump trip, Putin to visit China on May 19
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit China on May 19–20 for discussions with President Xi Jinping on deepening their strategic partnership. The visit follows closely after U.S. President Donald Trump's recent trip to Beijing.

stories.title: BRICS is evolving with new members; differences will take time to resolve: Brazil FM Mauro Vieira
stories.summary: At a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting, Brazil's Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira acknowledged that differences among the expanding bloc will take time to resolve. Tensions between the UAE and Iran over the ongoing war reportedly hindered consensus, potentially complicating the BRICS Summit planned for September.

stories.title: How will Beijing judge Trump’s take on Taiwan? Look for 1 critical factor
stories.summary: Following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, analysts said China's assessment of Trump's handling of US-China relations will largely depend on future US arms sales to Taiwan. Trump indicated he discussed Taiwan arms sales with Xi and would make a determination soon.

stories.title: IDF confirms Hamas Gaza chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad killed in airstrike
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces confirmed that Izz al-Din al-Haddad, Hamas's Gaza chief known as 'the Ghost,' was killed in an airstrike. Hamas sources also confirmed his death. Al-Haddad was considered one of the last surviving architects of the October 7 attack and had reportedly used hostages as human shields.

stories.title: Toddlers among more than 50 schoolchildren kidnapped in Nigeria
stories.summary: More than 50 schoolchildren, including toddlers, were kidnapped in an attack on Mussa town in Borno state, northeastern Nigeria. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

stories.title: Lebanon-Israel diplomacy: Ceasefire on paper, war on the ground
stories.summary: Despite a ceasefire agreement between Lebanon and Israel brokered with U.S. involvement, Israeli military operations have continued on the ground. Washington has reportedly been unable to restrain Israel from conducting strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: One person killed and two wounded in Kherson due to Russian artillery shelling
stories.summary: Russian troops carried out an artillery strike on the central part of the Ukrainian city of Kherson, killing one man and wounding two others.

stories.title: Russia’s Nevinnomyssk Azot chemical plant reported on fire after overnight explosions – at least 6th attack on the site
stories.summary: The Nevinnomyssk Azot chemical plant in Russia was reportedly set on fire following overnight explosions, marking at least the sixth attack on the facility. Regional authorities said air defense systems were active during the incident. The plant is a key node in Russia's chemical production chain.

stories.title: German court allows anti-Israel encampment in Hamburg park where Nazis deported Jews
stories.summary: A German court permitted an anti-Israel encampment in a Hamburg park historically linked to the Nazi deportation of Jews, timed around Nakba Day. Local Jewish community members condemned the decision, calling it a mockery of Holocaust victims. Many activists involved were accused of holding antisemitic positions.

stories.title: Trump warns against Taiwan independence after China visit
stories.summary: Following his visit to China, U.S. President Donald Trump warned against Taiwanese independence. Under U.S. law, Washington is required to provide defensive weapons to Taiwan, though it has maintained strategic ambiguity on direct military intervention.

stories.title: Fatima Sana to lead women’s side as PCB announces squad for T20 World Cup, Ireland tri-series
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board named Fatima Sana as captain of the women's squad for the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026. Pakistan will first compete in a tri-series in Dublin from May 28 to June 4 against Ireland and the West Indies.

stories.title: At Cannes, a juror claims anti-Israel activists face blacklisting
stories.summary: At the Cannes Film Festival, a juror alleged that activists critical of Israel face blacklisting in the film industry. No Israeli films were included in this year's official festival program, though no formal boycott was announced.

stories.title: Maldivian military diver dies in search of bodies of 4 Italian divers
stories.summary: A Maldivian military diver died on Saturday while searching for the bodies of four Italian divers believed to be trapped inside an underwater cave in Vaavu Atoll. The five Italian divers are thought to have perished while exploring the cave at approximately 50 metres depth on Thursday.

stories.title: Red Sea Film Foundation holds annual Women in Cinema gala
stories.summary: The Red Sea Film Foundation held its annual Women in Cinema gala in southern France on Friday. Six women were honored, including filmmakers from Morocco, Nigeria, and Rwanda.

stories.title: New Zealand car crash: how Hongkongers can stay safe when driving abroad
stories.summary: Two Hong Kong tourists were killed in a car crash near Christchurch, New Zealand. The Chinese consulate confirmed details of the accident, which occurred southwest of the city on Friday.

stories.title: Russians use main gas pipeline to transport assault units in south, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesman Voloshyn reported that Russian forces in the southern operational zone are using a main gas pipeline to transport assault units behind Ukrainian lines. Some Russian soldiers have surrendered after emerging from the pipeline.

stories.title: UN condemns Israeli attack on West Bank mosque
stories.summary: UN Deputy Special Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov condemned an arson attack on a mosque and vehicles in a village in the occupied West Bank. He called for an immediate investigation and noted rising violence by Israeli settlers in the territory.

stories.title: US considers taking Palestinian tax money for Trump's Gaza plan
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering redirecting Palestinian tax revenues to support President Trump's plan for Gaza. Israel has withheld as much as $5 billion in tax revenue from the Palestinian Authority.

stories.title: US considers using Palestinian tax money for Trump's Gaza plan
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering using Palestinian tax revenues to fund the Trump administration's plan for Gaza. Israel has withheld up to $5 billion in tax revenue owed to the Palestinian Authority.

stories.title: French judge to probe Khashoggi killing
stories.summary: A judge in Paris will open a formal investigation into the 2018 killing of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi. The probe follows a legal complaint filed by human rights organizations against Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

stories.title: Syria names new central bank governor
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa appointed Abdul Hamid Raslan as the country's new central bank governor. Raslan previously served as head of the Syrian Development Fund.

stories.title: ‘Accomplished our major goal’: Boeing confirms China’s commitment to buy 200 aircraft
stories.summary: Boeing confirmed that China committed to purchasing 200 aircraft, marking the country's first Boeing order since 2017. The agreement was described as accomplishing a major goal during broader U.S.-China diplomatic engagements.

stories.title: Putin to visit China on May 19-20 to further strengthen 'comprehensive partnership'
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit China on May 19–20 for talks with President Xi Jinping, shortly after U.S. President Donald Trump's trip to Beijing. The Kremlin said the leaders will discuss strengthening their comprehensive partnership and sign a joint declaration.

stories.title: Ukraine Drone Attack Kills 1 in Belgorod Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Belgorod region killed one person. No further details were immediately available.

stories.title: Why does Jerusalem belongs to the Jews? Because history says so - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Jerusalem's Jewish historical ties are supported by the historical record, emphasizing the importance of countering misinformation about Israel on campuses and international forums.

stories.title: How well do you know Israel’s capital? Take the Jerusalem Quiz
stories.summary: Middle school students from 33 Jerusalem schools participated in a quiz competition held at the Tower of David Jerusalem Museum, testing their knowledge of the city.

stories.title: Congolese report constant burials as deaths in new Ebola outbreak reach 80
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing a new Ebola outbreak that has killed at least 80 people. Local residents report constant burials as health authorities work to contain the spread of the Bundibugyo strain.

stories.title: This week, Ukrainian weapons strike targets 1,000 kilometers deep inside Russia, says Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky announced that Ukrainian weapons struck targets nearly 1,000 kilometers deep inside Russian territory over the course of the past week.

stories.title: Volkswagen to produce Iron Dome parts in deal with Israeli firm
stories.summary: German automaker Volkswagen is reportedly nearing a deal with Israeli defense firm Rafael to manufacture components linked to the Iron Dome missile defense system at facilities in Germany.

stories.title: Soldier dies after falling from horse at Royal Windsor Horse Show
stories.summary: A member of the King's Troop Royal Horse Artillery died after falling from a horse at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on Friday evening. The soldier fell after exiting the arena following a display and received medical treatment at the scene but did not survive.

stories.title: Lauren Boebert suggests Trump withheld funds to Colorado over prosecution of election denier
stories.summary: US Representative Lauren Boebert suggested that President Trump withheld federal funding for a clean drinking water project in Colorado because of the state's prosecution of election denier Tina Peters. Colorado Governor Jared Polis commuted Peters' nearly nine-year prison sentence on Friday.

stories.title: Fiery Finns, Australian star favourites at boycotted Eurovision final
stories.summary: A Finnish violinist-singer duo and an Australian performer are the leading favourites at the Eurovision grand final. The contest has faced an unprecedented boycott by multiple participants over Israel's inclusion in the event.

stories.title: Soybean counters: scope of China-US farm deal depends on math, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts say China's pledge to purchase "double-digit billions" in U.S. agricultural products, announced after President Trump's state visit to Beijing, represents only a marginal increase over previous commitments. New orders could, however, reduce China's dependence on Brazilian soybeans.

stories.title: French actor, pop idol Patrick Bruel accused of rape by many women
stories.summary: French actor and singer Patrick Bruel has been accused of rape by TV presenter Flavie Flament, who says the alleged assault occurred when she was 16 years old. Bruel has denied the allegations.

stories.title: Kyiv Says Russia Returned 528 Bodies to Ukraine
stories.summary: Kyiv confirmed that Russia returned 528 bodies to Ukraine as part of ongoing repatriation processes.

stories.title: Taiwan says is an ‘independent’ nation, after Trump’s warning
stories.summary: Taiwan's government responded to Trump's warning by affirming it is an independent nation. Taiwan relies heavily on U.S. security support to deter China, which has threatened to annex the island by force.

stories.title: Karachi roads paved with good intentions but potholed with reality
stories.summary: In Karachi's Gulshan Town, local officials opted for paver blocks to improve the deteriorated Hijri Road in Metroville Colony. The UC 6 chairman said the approach has extended road lifespan despite ongoing sewerage overflow problems in the neighborhood.

stories.title: A growing alliance: Panama’s Jewish ambassador wants to bring Israel closer to Latin America
stories.summary: Panama's Ambassador to Israel, Ezra Cohen, expressed interest in strengthening ties between Israel and Latin America. Cohen highlighted the historical role of Jewish communities in Panama's founding.

stories.title: How China and the US felt the weight of history behind Trump and Xi’s meeting in Beijing
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks in Beijing, with both nations framing the meeting as historic. Discussions took place at the Zhongnanhai leadership compound, a venue choice emphasizing the significance both sides attached to the summit.

stories.title: Pakistan eyes PKR 100 billion defence hike in IMF-linked budget
stories.summary: Pakistan is reportedly planning a defense budget increase of approximately PKR 100 billion in its upcoming IMF-linked budget. The IMF projected Pakistan's total federal revenues for fiscal year 2026–27 at PKR 17.144 trillion, a 13.5% increase over the current year.

stories.title: Russia returns bodies of 528 deceased to Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia returned the bodies of 528 deceased individuals to Ukraine through repatriation efforts. The Russian side indicated the remains may be those of Ukrainian servicemembers.

stories.title: China confirms deal to buy US aircraft and engines after Donald Trump’s visit
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce confirmed on Saturday that it reached an agreement with the United States to purchase aircraft, jet engines, and components. President Trump previously stated the deal includes at least 200 Boeing planes and General Electric engines. Beijing's statement did not specify quantities or total value.

stories.title: New York commuter rail system shuts down as workers strike
stories.summary: The Long Island Rail Road, North America's largest commuter rail system serving New York City's eastern suburbs, shut down on Saturday after unionized workers went on strike. Five unions representing about half the workforce walked off the job, halting all operations on the system.

stories.title: “Point of no return”: Special tribunal for Russia’s war targeting leadership moves forward after 37-country agreement
stories.summary: Thirty-seven countries signed an agreement advancing the creation of a special tribunal to prosecute Russian leadership for the decision to launch the war against Ukraine. The agreement lays the legal groundwork for future prosecutions.

stories.title: Israel launches air raid on town in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched air strikes on the town of Chehabiyeh in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon. Additional strikes were reported between the towns of Arnoun and Yahmar al-Shaqif, also in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Leader of Hamas's armed wing killed in strike on Gaza, says Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced on Saturday that it killed Ezzedine Al-Haddad, head of Hamas's military wing, in an air strike conducted the previous day in Gaza. A Hamas source confirmed that Haddad's wife and daughter were also killed in the strike.

stories.title: Moment of deadly train crash in Bangkok
stories.summary: At least eight people were killed in Bangkok, Thailand, when a freight train collided with a public bus, sparking a fire that also engulfed nearby cars and motorcycles.

stories.title: Bangkok train-bus crash kills 8, Thai PM orders investigation
stories.summary: A collision between a goods train and a bus in downtown Bangkok on Saturday killed at least eight people and injured 35, according to police. Thai Prime Minister ordered an investigation into the crash. Bangkok police chief Urumporn Koondejsumrit confirmed the casualty figures as rescuers cordoned off the busy intersection.

stories.title: Teenager and seven adults injured in Kherson due to morning attacks by Russian forces
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Kherson with drones and artillery early in the morning, injuring eight civilians, including a 15-year-old boy.

stories.title: Agency says over 40 per cent of Sudanese face acute food insecurity
stories.summary: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification reported that approximately 19.5 million people in Sudan—over 40% of the population—face acute food insecurity amid the ongoing civil war.

stories.title: Arrest of Iraqi terror suspect with alleged links to Iran’s Quds Force is astonishing but not surprising
stories.summary: US authorities arrested Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, an Iraqi national allegedly commanding an Iranian-backed militia group, according to a complaint unsealed in federal court in Manhattan. He is accused of organizing 18 terrorist attacks in the UK, Europe, and Canada since the start of the Iran war, with alleged links to Iran's Quds Force.

stories.title: Naqvi discusses cooperation in counter-terrorism, cybercrime with delegation from Egypt
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met an Egyptian delegation led by Major General Magdy Helal in Islamabad. Both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation on counter-terrorism, narcotics enforcement, cybercrime, and safe city initiatives between their interior ministries.

stories.title: UK student dies after meningitis cases at college, two treated
stories.summary: A student at Henley College in the United Kingdom died following confirmed cases of meningitis at the institution. Two other individuals received treatment in connection with the outbreak.

stories.title: UK student dies after meningitis cases at college, two treated
stories.summary: A student at Henley College in the UK died following a meningitis case, and two other individuals were treated. A local general practitioner's office confirmed the death was linked to the college.

stories.title: Congo Ebola outbreak: constant burials as death toll reaches 80
stories.summary: At least 80 people have died in a new Ebola outbreak in the eastern Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 246 suspected cases reported. Health workers in the provincial capital Bunia are intensifying screening and contact tracing. Officials first announced the outbreak on Friday with 65 confirmed deaths.

stories.title: Trump, Nigeria claim killing of ISIS senior leader Abu-Bilal al-Minuki
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Nigerian authorities announced the killing of senior ISIS leader Abu-Bilal al-Minuki. Al-Minuki had been placed under U.S. sanctions in 2023 for his ties to the Islamic State group.

stories.title: Trump says ISIS No. 2 Abu-Bilal al-Minuki killed in Nigeria
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, described as ISIS's second-in-command, was killed in a joint U.S.-Nigerian military operation in Nigeria. Nigeria had previously drawn Trump's attention over allegations of Christian persecution, which the Nigerian government denies.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox conscription dispute pushes Israeli government to brink
stories.summary: Israel's coalition government faces potential collapse over a dispute between coalition parties regarding military draft exemptions for ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) community members.

stories.title: IDF launches strikes targeting Hezbollah for 1st time since Lebanon ceasefire extended
stories.summary: The Israeli military carried out strikes targeting Hezbollah in southern Lebanon for the first time since the Lebanon ceasefire was extended, issuing evacuation orders for nine villages. At least six people were reportedly killed in an overnight strike on a civil defense center, and a drone was launched from Lebanon toward Israel.

stories.title: Amid the fertiliser crisis, Africa has a chemical-free option: Agroecology
stories.summary: Amid a global fertiliser crisis, experts and advocates are urging African governments to invest in agroecology—chemical-free, sustainable farming methods—to boost crop yields and improve food security across the continent.

stories.title: Trump's geopolitical brinkmanship has hit a wall with Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's coercive diplomatic approach, involving public threats and ultimatums, has reportedly stalled in negotiations with Iran. The deadlock over an 11-week-old crisis continues, with Trump showing frustration but little willingness to adjust his stance toward Iranian leaders.

stories.title: Robert Lewandowski to leave Barcelona with his ‘mission complete’
stories.summary: Polish striker Robert Lewandowski is set to depart FC Barcelona after helping the club win three La Liga titles, including the current season's championship, and the 2025 Copa del Rey.

stories.title: Peacock ‘invasion’ of Italian seaside town ruffles feathers
stories.summary: The Italian seaside town of Punta Marina is dealing with a growing population of peacocks that has divided residents. Local authorities have appointed so-called peacock rangers to manage tensions between those who welcome and those who oppose the birds' presence. The peacocks have spread from a disused military barracks in the area.

stories.title: Is China’s new mediation body gaining steam as Western brokers’ influence wanes?
stories.summary: China is promoting a new mediation body aimed at resolving regional conflicts, urging more countries to join. Cui Jianchun, commissioner of China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hong Kong, spoke at a summit highlighting mediation's respect for the autonomy of disputing parties. The push comes amid stalled US-Iran peace talks.

stories.title: Firefighter killed; 11 injured in Maine lumber mill explosion, fire
stories.summary: A firefighter was killed and 11 others were injured in an explosion and fire at a lumber mill in Maine. State and local emergency crews worked for hours to contain the blaze at the facility.

stories.title: Moscow’s threats involving “ultramodern” weapons lose their impact, says former Czech government security adviser
stories.summary: A former Czech government security adviser said Russia's repeated threats involving advanced weapons are losing their impact on Western nations. Moscow's frequent demonstrations of new weapon systems have diminished their deterrent effect.

stories.title: Nigeria: Trump Says U.S. Partners With Nigeria to Kill Islamic State Top Commander
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump announced that U.S. forces partnered with Nigeria to kill a top Islamic State commander. The individual had been designated a "global terrorist" by U.S. authorities in 2023.

stories.title: Nigeria: Just in - Tinubu Confirms Joint Operation With U.S. Killed Isis Commander in Nigeria
stories.summary: Nigerian President Tinubu confirmed that a joint U.S.-Nigerian military operation killed an ISIS commander operating in Nigeria. Tinubu described the operation as a product of successful security cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: UK: Massive security operation in London as counterprotests organised
stories.summary: A large security operation was mounted in London as counterprotests were organized across the city. Details on the specific groups involved and the scale of the operation were not fully disclosed in the initial report.

stories.title: As Iran talks stall, Israel and US prepping to renew war as soon as next week – report
stories.summary: According to a New York Times report, Israel and the United States are preparing for possible military action against Iran as nuclear talks have stalled. U.S. officials indicated commandos could be deployed to extract nuclear material, with a senior Israeli official suggesting fighting could last days to weeks.

stories.title: Divers in Maldives resume search for Italian scuba divers who drowned in cave
stories.summary: Divers in the Maldives resumed efforts to recover the bodies of four Italian scuba divers who drowned while exploring a deep underwater cave at Vaavu Atoll. The divers reportedly died at a depth of approximately 50 metres. Rough weather had temporarily forced authorities to suspend the high-risk recovery operation on Friday.

stories.title: In the shadow of another Iran war, Maccabiah Games in Israel set to go ahead in July
stories.summary: Organizers of the Maccabiah Games plan to hold the international Jewish athletic competition in Israel in July 2026. The event, which draws thousands of athletes worldwide, was canceled the previous year amid regional security concerns related to tensions with Iran.

stories.title: Russian Court Orders Euroclear to Pay Around $250Bln Over Frozen Assets
stories.summary: A Russian court ordered Belgian financial institution Euroclear to pay approximately $250 billion over frozen Russian assets. Euroclear stated it does not recognize the Russian court's jurisdiction, and it remains unclear how Russia would enforce the ruling.

stories.title: Israel kills 8 Palestinians in Gaza, Hamas official assassinated
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it dropped at least 13 bombs on Gaza in an operation targeting Hamas commander Izz al-Din al-Haddad. Eight Palestinians were reported killed in the strikes.

stories.title: Man who stabbed 2 Jews in Golders Green to stand trial next year, London court hears
stories.summary: Essa Suleiman, 45, appeared via video link at a London court charged with the attempted murder of two Jewish men seriously wounded in a stabbing attack in Golders Green on April 29. He is also accused of attacking an acquaintance and is scheduled to stand trial next year.

stories.title: UNRWA secretly rescued Nakba archive from Gaza
stories.summary: UNRWA secretly relocated millions of Nakba-era Palestinian refugee records from Gaza and Jerusalem amid concerns the archive could be destroyed during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Mick Jagger and Eric Clapton win battle to stop 29-storey block being built by Thames
stories.summary: A UK planning inspector upheld a council's rejection of a proposed 29-storey tower near Battersea Bridge on the south bank of the River Thames in London. Celebrities including Mick Jagger and Eric Clapton had campaigned against the development by Rockwell Property for two years. The inspector found the design was not sufficiently distinctive.

stories.title: Israel says it killed Hamas military chief in Gaza
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, described as the head of Hamas's military wing in Gaza, in an air strike on Gaza City on Friday. Hamas has not officially confirmed his death.

stories.title: 46 enemy strikes reported in Chernihiv region; one woman wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 46 strikes on Ukraine's Chernihiv region over 24 hours, wounding one civilian woman. The attacks targeted multiple locations across the northern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Israel, Lebanon say extending ceasefire despite new strikes
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon announced they are extending their ceasefire despite continued Israeli strikes that have killed hundreds in Lebanon since the truce was declared on April 17. The fighting between Israel and Hezbollah has persisted despite the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: US accuses Iraqi man of helping Iran-backed militia's plans for attacks in US, Europe​
stories.summary: An Iraqi national was arrested and brought to the United States to face six terrorism-related charges for alleged involvement in attacks against U.S. interests in Europe. The U.S. Justice Department said the suspect was accused of working with Iranian-backed militia groups to plan attacks in the U.S. and Europe.

stories.title: Israel’s Image Crisis: Becoming Too Big to Spin?
stories.summary: Israel has reportedly increased spending on its national public-relations and propaganda campaigns to record levels as it faces growing international scrutiny over its image.

stories.title: 10 Mexican government, justice officials indicted in US, will surrender
stories.summary: Gerardo Mérida Sánchez, former Secretary of Public Security for Mexico's Sinaloa state, appeared in federal court in Manhattan on Friday after his arrest in Arizona. He and other officials are charged with accepting bribes to help the Sinaloa Cartel smuggle drugs into the United States. He is due back in court on June 1.

stories.title: Indian cricketer Kohli to play 2027 World Cup only if he can add value
stories.summary: Indian cricketer Virat Kohli, 37, said he would only play in the 2027 ODI World Cup if he can still contribute meaningfully. Kohli, now active only in the ODI format, scored 651 runs in 13 ODIs last year and has already hit a century in the current IPL season.

stories.title: Russia fast-tracks citizenship for Moldova’s occupied Transnistria – a familiar playbook returns
stories.summary: Russia has eased citizenship requirements for residents of Transnistria, Moldova's breakaway region. The move mirrors a policy approach Russia has previously employed in other contested territories such as parts of Georgia and Ukraine.

stories.title: Andalucíans to vote in election seen as gauge of Spain’s wider political change
stories.summary: Voters in Andalucía, Spain's most populous region, head to the polls on Sunday in an election widely seen as a barometer of national political trends. The conservative People's Party is expected to secure an absolute majority, while the socialists face a significant defeat in a former stronghold. The vote also tests the trajectory of the far-right Vox party.

stories.title: Republican Louisiana senator in tough primary after Trump backs opponent
stories.summary: Louisiana held primary elections on Saturday, testing the influence of Donald Trump's endorsement against incumbent Republican Senator Bill Cassidy. Trump backed challenger Julia Letlow after Cassidy voted to impeach the president following the January 6 insurrection. Cassidy later sought to mend ties by casting the pivotal vote to confirm Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as health secretary.

stories.title: Three people injured in Kharkiv after Russian drone strike
stories.summary: Three men were injured in Kharkiv, Ukraine, after a Russian Molniya drone struck the city. The attack is part of ongoing Russian aerial assaults on Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: Paved with good intentions but potholed with reality
stories.summary: Residents of Metroville Colony in Karachi's Gulshan Town had paver blocks installed on Hijri Road through the Karachi Development Authority to address longstanding road deterioration. UC 6 chairman Nasir Ashfaq said the pavers have improved the road's lifespan despite recurring sewerage overflow issues in the neighborhood.

stories.title: Trump says ISIS second-in-command Abu-Bilal al-Minuki eliminated
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced the killing of Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, described as ISIS's global second-in-command, in Nigeria. Nigeria had previously drawn Trump's scrutiny over alleged persecution of Christians, which the Nigerian government denies.

stories.title: Damage reported in Vyshhorod district of Kyiv region following Russian drone attack
stories.summary: Russian drone attacks caused damage in the Vyshhorod district of Ukraine's Kyiv region. Authorities reported the strikes but did not immediately detail the full extent of destruction.

stories.title: At least eight killed, 25 injured as train hits bus in Bangkok
stories.summary: A train collided with a public bus near an airport rail link station in Bangkok's city centre, killing at least eight people and injuring 25 others, according to Thai media reports.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon continue despite ‘ceasefire’ extension
stories.summary: Israel continued to carry out air strikes on southern Lebanon despite both sides agreeing to extend their ceasefire deal by an additional 45 days.

stories.title: Israel’s Noam Bettan prepares to take the stage at boycotted Eurovision final
stories.summary: Israeli contestant Noam Bettan is preparing to perform at the Eurovision final, which has faced boycott calls. The Israeli delegation reportedly believes the song 'Michelle' could win the public vote, though Finnish and Australian acts are considered favorites.

stories.title: Scalpers list Swatch-Audemars Piguet watches hours after launch in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hours after the launch of a Swatch-Audemars Piguet collaboration watch in Hong Kong's Causeway Bay, many buyers listed the timepieces for resale at nearly seven times the retail price. At least 70 people were observed queuing in the rain before the store opened.

stories.title: Civilian injured, and 30 cars catch fire due to Russian attacks in Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked three districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times since Friday evening, injuring one civilian. The strikes also caused 30 cars to catch fire.

stories.title: Trump–Xi summit highlights limits of transactional diplomacy
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's two-day visit to Beijing ended without major breakthroughs in talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The summit highlighted the widening strategic gap between Washington and Beijing on issues including Iran, Taiwan, and technology. Analysts had warned beforehand that expectations of a relationship reset were unrealistic.

stories.title: Congo confirms new Ebola outbreak, 80 deaths
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo confirmed a new Ebola outbreak in the eastern Ituri province, with 80 deaths reported as of Friday. The country's health ministry disclosed the outbreak details.

stories.title: Ukraine recovers bodies of 528 fallen servicemembers from Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine recovered the bodies of 528 fallen servicemembers from Russia as part of repatriation efforts. Forensic experts will now begin identification procedures.

stories.title: US aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford to complete longest deployment since Vietnam War
stories.summary: The USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier is set to complete the longest U.S. Navy deployment since the Vietnam War. The carrier has been deployed since June 24, 2025.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 269 of 294 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 269 of 294 Russian drones launched against the country since the evening of May 15. The large-scale drone assault targeted multiple regions across Ukraine.

stories.title: How Taiwan’s Apec attendance could test Beijing’s cross-strait pragmatism
stories.summary: Taiwan plans to send its top trade negotiator to the APEC ministerial meeting in Suzhou, China, on May 22–23, a rare occurrence since official cross-strait communication was cut in 2016. Analysts say the move suggests both sides seek to preserve a workable status quo within the forum.

stories.title: At least five people pardoned by Trump for Capitol attack accused of new crimes
stories.summary: At least five individuals pardoned by former President Donald Trump for their involvement in the January 6, 2021, U.S. Capitol attack have since been accused of new crimes. The most recent, Ryan Nichols, 35, was charged on May 10 after allegedly brandishing a handgun during an argument in a church parking lot in Harleton, Texas.

stories.title: After China-US reset, Putin heads to Beijing for Sino-Russian strategic refresh
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit Beijing on May 19–20 to reinforce the Sino-Russian strategic partnership, days after a tentative US-China reset. The visit was confirmed by Chinese state news agency Xinhua following an invitation from President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: IMF sets Rs17.1tr federal revenue target for 2026-27
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund has set Pakistan's federal revenue target at 17.145 trillion rupees for fiscal year 2026-27, proposing 430 billion rupees in new budgetary measures and an 18 percent increase in the petroleum levy. The IMF projects 3.5 percent economic growth and 8.4 percent average inflation.

stories.title: Rival pro-Palestine, far-right protests in London as 4,000 police deployed
stories.summary: Two major demonstrations took place in London on Saturday: a pro-Palestine Nakba Day march and a far-right Unite the Kingdom rally organized by Tommy Robinson. The Metropolitan Police deployed more than 4,000 officers in what it described as an unprecedented operation.

stories.title: Militia commander tied to Iran plotted attacks on Jewish sites, prosecutors say
stories.summary: Prosecutors accused a militia commander with ties to Iran of plotting at least 20 attacks against US and Israeli interests in Europe and Canada. The alleged targets included Jewish sites.

stories.title: Russians kill civilian in Donetsk region; four others wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces killed one civilian and wounded four others in Ukraine's Donetsk region over the past 24 hours, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Gazan artists paint mural to honour Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal
stories.summary: Artists in Gaza painted a mural honoring 18-year-old Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal. Yamal waved a large Palestinian flag from an open-top bus during Barcelona's La Liga victory parade on Monday.

stories.title: Jewish groups call on UK to bar ‘dangerous’ Hasan Piker amid antisemitic attacks
stories.summary: Several Jewish organizations have urged the United Kingdom to deny entry to American streamer Hasan Piker, who is scheduled to speak at a festival and record a live podcast in London in early June. The groups cite his record of antisemitic statements and October 7 denial.

stories.title: U.S. accuses Iraqi man of helping Iran-backed militia's plans for attacks in U.S., Europe​
stories.summary: U.S. prosecutors charged an Iraqi national, identified as Al-Saadi, with directing and encouraging attacks on American and Israeli targets in the U.S. and Europe on behalf of Iranian-backed militant groups. The allegations include efforts to kill Americans and Jewish civilians as part of a broader campaign.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla sails for a third time despite threats: 500 activists depart
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla departed from southern Turkey on its third attempt to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza. Previous voyages were intercepted by Israel in international waters. Approximately 500 activists are aboard the ships.

stories.title: Fed names Powell chair pro tempore until Warsh sworn in
stories.summary: The US Federal Reserve named Jerome Powell as chair pro tempore until Kevin Warsh is sworn in as his successor. A Fed spokesperson declined to comment on when Warsh's swearing-in would take place.

stories.title: Trump says ISIS second in command Abu Bilal al-Minuki eliminated
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Abu Bilal al-Minuki, described as the global second-in-command of ISIS, was killed in a joint operation by American and Nigerian forces. Trump called al-Minuki "the most active terrorist in the world" and said the mission was conducted at his direction.

stories.title: 'There is little which is Jewish about Israel': Haim Bresheeth on antisemitism and Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli-British author and filmmaker Haim Bresheeth discussed antisemitism and the Gaza conflict at an event in London. Thousands gathered in the British capital to commemorate Nakba Day.

stories.title: Israeli settler blindfolds and detains Palestinian in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: An armed Israeli settler blindfolded and detained a Palestinian man in the occupied West Bank. The incident highlights ongoing tensions between settlers and Palestinians in the territory.

stories.title: Ukrainian plane carrying explosives grounded in Trinidad and Tobago
stories.summary: A Ukrainian-registered plane carrying explosives was grounded at Piarco International Airport in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, on Thursday. The aircraft had arrived from the Bahamas to refuel and was scheduled to continue to Libya via Cape Verde, which raised police suspicions.

stories.title: US-Israel attacks on Iran could resume as early as next week - report
stories.summary: Reports indicate that U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran could resume as early as next week. President Trump stated that Iran can either agree to a deal or face annihilation, claiming Tehran has refused to honor previously agreed terms.

stories.title: Putin to hold taks with Xi in China days after Trump’s trip to Beijing
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin will travel to Beijing next week for a two-day visit that includes talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, the Kremlin announced. The meeting follows closely after U.S. President Donald Trump's state visit to China, which concluded without major breakthroughs on trade, the war in Ukraine, or the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon; 250,000 attend London Nakba protest
stories.summary: Israel continued strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday despite a ceasefire extension with Hezbollah, killing several people. Separately, approximately 250,000 people attended a Nakba protest in London.

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon; Nakba, far-right protests sweep London
stories.summary: Israel continued striking southern Lebanon on Saturday despite an extended ceasefire agreement with Hezbollah, killing several people. Separately, Nakba Day commemorations and far-right protests took place in London.

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon; Nakba, far-right rallies begin in London
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued to strike targets in southern Lebanon on Saturday despite a ceasefire extension with Hezbollah, reportedly killing several people. Separately, Nakba commemoration and far-right rallies were held in London.

stories.title: Israel bombs Lebanon after agreeing to extend 'ceasefire'
stories.summary: At least six people were killed in Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon, including three paramedics, despite the recently extended ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: What do travellers need to know when Hong Kong airport’s Terminal 2 opens?
stories.summary: Hong Kong International Airport's Terminal 2 will reopen on May 27, with regional and low-cost carriers including HK Express and AirAsia group airlines relocating check-in operations from Terminal 1 as part of the airport's three-runway expansion project.

stories.title: FBI offers $200,000 reward for former US Air Force specialist accused of spying for Iran
stories.summary: The FBI is offering a $200,000 reward for Monica Witt, a former U.S. Air Force specialist accused of spying for Iran. The bureau believes Witt defected to Iran in 2013 and may still be assisting Tehran's intelligence activities.

stories.title: Senior IS leader killed by US and Nigerian forces
stories.summary: U.S. and Nigerian forces killed senior Islamic State leader Abu-Bilal al-Minuki in a joint operation. President Trump described him as "the most active terrorist in the world."

stories.title: War update: 263 clashes on front lines; Pokrovsk sector remains most intense
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 263 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front lines on May 15. The Pokrovsk sector in eastern Ukraine remained the most intense area of fighting.

stories.title: LGBTQ campaigners denounce Eurovision 'pinkwashing' ahead of final
stories.summary: LGBTQ campaigners called for a boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest final in Vienna, accusing organizers of "pinkwashing" by allowing Israel's participation amid the ongoing conflict in Gaza.

stories.title: ‘You’re going to get beheaded one by one, you dirty Jews,’ London man threatens
stories.summary: London police are investigating after a video circulated online showing a man threatening Jewish people with violence. The Community Security Trust, a Jewish community security organization, confirmed law enforcement is taking the incident seriously.

stories.title: China, US, Israel compete in fast-growing laser weapons race
stories.summary: China, the United States, and Israel are competing in a fast-growing laser weapons race. Several Gulf states are increasingly adopting laser weapon systems to counter drone threats amid the Iran war.

stories.title: French judge to probe complaint against Saudi’s MBS over journalist Jamal Khashoggi’s killing
stories.summary: A French investigative magistrate will investigate a complaint against Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over the 2018 assassination of journalist Jamal Khashoggi in Istanbul. The probe follows years of legal proceedings over the admissibility of the case in French courts.

stories.title: From the Nakba to Gaza’s ruins: One man’s lifetime of displacement
stories.summary: A Palestinian man who survived the 1948 Nakba recounts decades of displacement, including being forced from his home again during the 2023 conflict in Gaza, while expressing continued attachment to his homeland.

stories.title: Extra 4,000 officers in London as police brace for far-right and pro-Palestine marches – live
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers, armoured vehicles, horses, drones, and helicopters for two major demonstrations. The events included Tommy Robinson's far-right 'Unite the Kingdom' rally and the annual Nakba Day pro-Palestine march in central London.

stories.title: One dead and 23 wounded in Kherson region due to Russian attacks
stories.summary: Russian shelling in Ukraine's Kherson region killed one person and wounded 23 others over a 24-hour period.

stories.title: Bosnia signed. Ukraine still has time not to.
stories.summary: At the Lviv Media Forum 2026, Bosnian journalist Harun Karčić warned Ukrainians about the risks of accepting a flawed peace deal, drawing parallels with Bosnia's 30-year experience under the Dayton Agreement. He noted similarities between Bosnia's deal and the 28-point plan currently proposed for Ukraine.

stories.title: 'No sign' of China's willingness to pressure Iran after Trump's visit
stories.summary: Following U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to China, analysts noted no indication that Beijing is willing to pressure Iran on behalf of Washington. The assessment suggests limits to any diplomatic leverage gained during the Trump-Xi meetings.

stories.title: Ukraine vows retribution after Russian strike on housing block kills 24
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike on a residential apartment building in Kyiv killed 24 people, including three children. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the site, laid roses at the rubble, and vowed retribution against Russia.

stories.title: Houses and port infrastructure damaged in Odesa region following Russian attack; casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a drone attack on the southern Odesa region overnight, damaging residential buildings and port infrastructure. Casualties were reported in the strike.

stories.title: Buyers flock to SHKP project in New Territories as confidence grows in home market outlook
stories.summary: Hundreds of prospective buyers flocked to Sun Hung Kai Properties' Lime Spark development in Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong's New Territories. By early afternoon, more than 80 percent of the 121 flats on offer had been sold, reflecting growing confidence in the city's residential property market.

stories.title: Criminal networks in Negev, Galilee tighten grip on Israel’s economy, infrastructure
stories.summary: The CEO of Shomer HaHadash described extensive criminal networks operating in Israel's Negev and Galilee regions, involving systematic theft of water, electricity, and fuel that affects the country's economy and infrastructure.

stories.title: UK leadership crisis deepens: Starmer faces growing calls to step down
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces intensifying calls from within his party to step down amid a deepening leadership crisis. Political analysts are discussing the implications of the growing internal dissent within the Labour Party.

stories.title: US ramps up pressure on Cuba and plans to indict Raúl Castro
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department is preparing to seek an indictment against former Cuban President Raúl Castro, as President Donald Trump has also raised the possibility of military action against Cuba.

stories.title: Sealed files on Nazi ‘Angel of Death’ Mengele to be opened, Swiss intel agency says
stories.summary: Switzerland's intelligence agency announced it will unseal classified files on Josef Mengele, the Nazi doctor known as the "Angel of Death." Mengele fled to Argentina after World War II and was never prosecuted despite a West German arrest warrant.

stories.title: A new fiscal compact
stories.summary: An editorial discusses Pakistan's upcoming budget, noting the formal economy is overtaxed while investment remains weak and salaried individuals face rising burdens. The piece highlights tensions between the need for tax relief and fiscal constraints imposed by debt servicing costs, slowing growth, and IMF program conditions.

stories.title: Russia’s Putin to visit China following Trump’s trip
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to visit China to meet President Xi Jinping. The Kremlin stated the visit aims to further strengthen the comprehensive partnership between Moscow and Beijing.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Israel targets top Hamas leader in Gaza
