stories.title: China says summit with US 'injected much-needed stability' into the world
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the Beijing summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump produced 'a series of new common understandings.' According to the ministry, both leaders agreed on a vision for a constructive US-China relationship to guide ties for the next three years and beyond.

stories.title: IMF highlights ‘Gulf exposure’ as biggest external risk for Pakistan
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund, after releasing a $1.1 billion tranche for Pakistan, identified economic exposure to Gulf Cooperation Council countries as Islamabad's most significant external risk. The IMF noted that 81% of Pakistan's fuel imports and 55% of its remittances originate from GCC nations.

stories.title: South Korea’s 500,000 Drone Warriors Will Be a Hollow Force
stories.summary: South Korea plans to build a large-scale drone force inspired by Ukraine's battlefield use of expendable drones. North Korea has gained direct experience by rotating thousands of troops through Russia's war in Ukraine, and Ukrainian intelligence reports some are returning home to serve as military instructors.

stories.title: Benched Mbappe says he’s fourth-choice forward at Real Madrid under Arbeloa
stories.summary: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé said he has been reduced to fourth-choice striker under coach Álvaro Arbeloa. Mbappé was jeered by fans when he came off the bench during Madrid's 2-0 La Liga victory over Real Oviedo.

stories.title: ‘Tell good stories of Hong Kong’ amid global turmoil, John Lee urges local media
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee urged local media to "tell good stories of Hong Kong" amid global turbulence as the city develops its first five-year blueprint aligned with national development. He spoke at an annual award ceremony organized by the Newspaper Society of Hong Kong.

stories.title: Former Wang Fuk Court representative and wife held over fraud, money laundering
stories.summary: Jason Kong Cheung-fat, a former residents' representative for the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong, was arrested along with his wife on suspicion of conspiracy to defraud and money laundering. Both are directors of Ace Interior Design & Engineering Company.

stories.title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker, May 2026
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump completed a three-day visit to China, the first by a U.S. leader in nine years, originally postponed due to the Iran war. Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to visit Beijing the following week, with Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also expected.

stories.title: Death toll after Russian strike in Kyiv rises to 21, including three children
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on Kyiv rose to 21, including three children. Emergency rescue operations continued at the site of the attack.

stories.title: Chad: Chad is No Longer a Country
stories.summary: Chad faces acute structural vulnerability under President Mahamat Déby Itno, raising concerns about potential state collapse. Analysts argue the international community has long mistaken Chad's military capacity for internal stability.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teenager in West Bank village near Nablus
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed 16-year-old Fahd Zidan Owais in the village of Al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, according to the Wafa news agency. Local sources reported that Israeli forces withheld the teenager's body and prevented Palestine Red Crescent Society crews from reaching him.

stories.title: Cuba mulls US offer of $100 million in aid but wary of Trump's motives, blockade
stories.summary: Cuba said it would consider a U.S. offer of $100 million in humanitarian aid but expressed skepticism about President Trump's motives, citing an ongoing U.S. oil blockade that has severely disrupted public services on the island.

stories.title: British Gas customers to receive up to £112m over prepayment meter scandal
stories.summary: British Gas will pay up to £112 million in compensation and debt write-offs to customers who had prepayment meters forcibly installed in their homes. UK energy regulator Ofgem found that British Gas forced the devices on households struggling to pay bills during the Russian gas crisis, in one of the regulator's most complex investigations.

stories.title: Greening of UK politics could mean big business for Asian renewable exporters
stories.summary: The Green Party of England and Wales achieved record-breaking gains in the May 7 UK local council elections, capitalizing on voter disillusionment with Labour and the Conservatives. Analysts suggest South and Southeast Asian nations may benefit as clean energy exporters due to the shift in UK politics.

stories.title: Deaths of six migrants in Texas railcar investigated as human smuggling
stories.summary: Six migrants from Mexico and Honduras were found dead inside a sweltering railroad boxcar in Laredo, Texas. Officials are investigating the deaths as a human smuggling case.

stories.title: Russian elite sees no alternative to continuing war against Ukraine – CCD
stories.summary: According to the Centre for Countering Disinformation (CCD), Russia's political elite aims to restore Soviet-era influence in Eastern Europe and divide the European Union, and views continuing the war against Ukraine as the only path to those goals.

stories.title: Mitoma fails to make Japan’s 2026 World Cup squad due to hamstring injury
stories.summary: Brighton winger Kaoru Mitoma was excluded from Japan's 2026 World Cup squad due to a hamstring injury. Monaco forward Takumi Minamino was also omitted for injury reasons, while former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu was included.

stories.title: US scraps deployment of 4,000 troops to Poland
stories.summary: The United States canceled the planned deployment of approximately 4,000 troops to Poland, a decision that came amid growing pressure on NATO allies to increase their defense spending.

stories.title: US scraps deployment of 4,000 troops to Poland
stories.summary: The Pentagon canceled plans to temporarily deploy 4,000 U.S.-based troops to Poland, raising renewed questions about President Trump's expected troop reductions in Europe.

stories.title: How David Ben-Gurion got the Palestinians wrong in 1948
stories.summary: The article examines Israeli founding leader David Ben-Gurion's miscalculations regarding the Palestinians during the 1948 war. It argues that the Palestinian question persisted despite Israel's efforts to suppress it.

stories.title: Former China hawk elected Solomon Islands' leader
stories.summary: The Solomon Islands parliament elected a former China hawk as the nation's new leader, one week after lawmakers ousted the country's previous pro-China prime minister.

stories.title: Canada to pressure Russia to end war – Carney
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada will continue to pressure Russia to force it to end its war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran war day 77: Trump, Xi discuss Hormuz as Tehran rallies BRICS
stories.summary: On day 77 of the Iran conflict, Presidents Trump and Xi discussed the Strait of Hormuz during their Beijing summit. Both leaders agreed the strait should remain open to ensure global supply chains. Tehran simultaneously sought diplomatic support from BRICS nations.

stories.title: Staff-Sgt. Negev Dagan killed by Hezbollah mortar fire near Litani River in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Staff Sergeant Negev Dagan of the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion was killed by Hezbollah mortar fire near the Litani River in southern Lebanon. He was serving in Israel's ongoing military operations in the region.

stories.title: In 2021, China becomes the third country to safely land a rover on Mars – SCMP archive
stories.summary: This is a 2021 archival article recounting China's successful landing of its Zhurong rover on Mars, making it the third country to achieve a safe Mars rover landing after the China National Space Administration completed the mission.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Israel launched a series of attacks on towns across Lebanon, particularly in the south, in violation of a ceasefire agreement reached in mid-April. The strikes occurred despite ongoing peace talks between Israeli and Lebanese officials, which a senior US State Department official described as 'productive and positive.'

stories.title: Soldier killed by Hezbollah mortar shell in south Lebanon; rockets fired at north
stories.summary: Staff Sergeant Negev Dagan of the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion was killed by a Hezbollah mortar shell in southern Lebanon near the Litani River. The IDF also issued evacuation warnings near Tyre and struck Hezbollah targets as a third round of Israel-Lebanon talks began in Washington.

stories.title: Neo-Nazi group National Socialist Network criminalised under hate laws passed after Bondi terror attack
stories.summary: Australia's federal government has listed the neo-Nazi group National Socialist Network, also known as White Australia, as a prohibited hate group. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the ban criminalizes supporting, funding, recruiting for, and joining the organization. The listing was made under hate-group legislation passed after the Bondi terror attacks.

stories.title: 1MDB scandal: Anwar says Malaysia won’t oppose Jho Low’s Trump pardon bid
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia will not oppose fugitive businessman Jho Low's bid to seek a pardon from U.S. President Donald Trump related to the 1MDB corruption scandal, describing the matter as a "non-issue."

stories.title: Syrian Foreign Minister makes first visit to Morocco since Assad’s fall
stories.summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Assaad al-Chaibani visited Rabat for talks with Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita, marking the first visit by a senior Syrian official to Morocco since the fall of Bashar al-Assad's government.

stories.title: Ignoring ‘pay-for-slay’ reform, Ramallah court tells PA to reinstate money for prisoner
stories.summary: A Ramallah court ordered the Palestinian Authority to reinstate stipend payments to a detained security prisoner, potentially undermining PA reforms to its controversial prisoner payment program. The ruling could affect approximately 1,600 other security inmates whose stipends were previously cut amid international criticism that the program incentivizes violence.

stories.title: Muslim Americans accuse Republicans of using congressional hearings to stoke fear
stories.summary: Muslim American groups accused Republican lawmakers of using congressional hearings to stoke fear after the House Judiciary Subcommittee held a hearing titled 'Sharia-Free America.' The hearing questioned the compatibility of political Islam and Sharia law with the US Constitution.

stories.title: Editor's Notes: The Mossad has always been led by outsiders - comment
stories.summary: A commentary discussed the appointment process for Mossad leadership, noting the controversy surrounding Roman Gofman's candidacy. The piece argued that the debate reflects broader questions about who Israel's security establishment is willing to accept into its ranks.

stories.title: China blogger drives 1,300km overnight to help schoolmate see recently deceased mother
stories.summary: A Chinese university blogger drove 1,300 kilometers overnight from Yinchuan in Ningxia to help a fellow North Minzu University student reach her hometown to see her recently deceased mother before the funeral.

stories.title: Europe must remember the reason Eurovision was formed or risk losing it completely - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argued that the Eurovision Song Contest risks collapse unless Europe remembers the competition's founding purpose of unity. Several countries including Spain, Ireland, Slovenia, Iceland, and the Netherlands boycotted the event over Israel's participation.

stories.title: Japan eyes dedicated ship to lead deep-sea rare earths race, cut reliance on China
stories.summary: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party is preparing a proposal for the government to build a dedicated deep-sea mining vessel to extract rare earth minerals from the Pacific Ocean floor, aiming to reduce reliance on Chinese supply chains.

stories.title: Provocative Austrian feminist artist Valie Export dies at 85
stories.summary: Austrian avant-garde feminist artist Valie Export, known for pioneering performance art in postwar Europe, died in Vienna at age 85, her foundation announced Thursday.

stories.title: Judge bars Kars4Kids from advertising, saying it misled donors about Orthodox Jewish mission
stories.summary: A California Superior Court judge barred Kars4Kids from advertising in the state, ruling that the charity violated false advertising and unfair competition laws. The court found that the organization misled donors by failing to disclose how and where it allocated donated funds, including its connection to an Orthodox Jewish mission.

stories.title: Israel issues forced displacement orders for five towns, villages in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military issued forced evacuation orders for residents of five towns and villages in southern Lebanon: Shabriha, Hamideh, Zuqaq al-Mufdi, Mashouk, and El Haouch. Residents were warned to evacuate immediately to open areas at least 1,000 metres from their homes amid Israel's ongoing military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Why India’s RSS is lobbying the West amid attacks on minorities at home
stories.summary: Reports indicate that hate speech targeting religious minorities in India increased over the past year. Experts suggest the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a far-right Hindu nationalist organization, is engaging in outreach to Western audiences as a form of damage control amid criticism of its domestic record.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims targeting of Israeli drones with missiles
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it targeted Israeli aircraft and drones over southern Lebanon with surface-to-air missiles and claimed attacks on Israeli forces in several areas in the south. Sirens were activated in northern Israel following reported rocket fire from Lebanon at dawn.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1540: Ukrainian drone pilots demonstrate their edge during NATO drills on Gotland
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone pilots demonstrated their capabilities during NATO drills on the Swedish island of Gotland on day 1,540 of the Russo-Ukrainian war. Separately, a US House discharge petition bypassed Speaker Johnson to force a vote on nearly $10 billion in new Ukraine assistance, reflecting bipartisan frustration with stalled aid.

stories.title: Ship reported seized off UAE, as Trump discusses Iran with China’s Xi
stories.summary: A ship was reportedly seized off the UAE coast amid rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping discussed Iran during their meeting in Beijing, agreeing on the need to keep the critical shipping lane open.

stories.title: Israeli shelling reported in Lebanon, as army issues expulsion orders to towns
stories.summary: The Israeli army issued evacuation warnings to residents in several towns near the southern Lebanese city of Tyre, including Shabriha, Hamideh, Zuqaq al-Mufdi, Mashouk, and El Haouch. Artillery shelling and gunfire were also reported in the towns of Qalawiya and Wadi al-Hujeir in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel says soldier killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military announced that Staff Sergeant Negev Dagan, 20, was killed in combat in southern Lebanon. His death brings Israel's total military losses to 20 personnel since the war on Lebanon began in early March.

stories.title: U.S. to drop graft charges against Gautam Adani: NY Times
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly preparing to drop bribery charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, according to The New York Times. Adani was alleged in November 2024 to have agreed to pay over $250 million in bribes to Indian officials for solar-energy contracts.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Keeps Somalia Border Closed Over Security Concerns, Ruto Says
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto said renewed instability in Somalia has compelled Nairobi to keep its border with Somalia closed, nearly 15 years after the frontier was first shut.

stories.title: Nigeria: Makinde Declares 2027 Presidential Bid
stories.summary: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde declared his bid for Nigeria's 2027 presidential election at a joint mega rally of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the Allied Peoples' Movement (APM) in Ibadan.

stories.title: Nigeria: Death Toll Hits 191 As Lassa Fever Cases Rise
stories.summary: Nigeria's death toll from Lassa fever has reached 191, with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) warning of an increasing fatality rate as cases continue to rise.

stories.title: South Africa: President Ramaphosa Dismisses Social Development Minister
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa dismissed Minister of Social Development Sisisi Tolashe from her position, invoking section 91(2) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa.

stories.title: Africa: Kagame Criticises Use of Sanctions, Urges Africa Cooperation
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame criticized the use of sanctions in global politics, arguing they are applied unfairly and used as tools of pressure against weaker nations. He called for greater cooperation among African countries.

stories.title: Former head of medical commission sentenced to five years in prison for bribery in disability case
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Khmelnytskyi region, a former head of a regional medical and social expert commission from the Donetsk region was sentenced to five years in prison for demanding a $5,000 bribe in exchange for granting disability status.

stories.title: As Trump wraps up China trip, what will he and Xi take from historic summit?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump concluded a state visit to China on Friday after Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted him at Zhongnanhai in Beijing for small-group talks. The two leaders strolled through the compound's grounds amid ancient trees and roses.

stories.title: Giggle for Girls app discriminated against trans woman Roxanne Tickle, appeal judge rules when doubling damages
stories.summary: An Australian Federal Court appeal panel upheld a 2024 ruling that the women-only social media app Giggle for Girls unlawfully discriminated against transgender woman Roxanne Tickle by denying her access. Justices Perry, Abraham, and Kennett affirmed the gender-identity discrimination finding and doubled damages to $20,000.

stories.title: Trump says China's Xi has become a 'friend'
stories.summary: During his visit to China, US President Donald Trump described Chinese President Xi Jinping as having 'become really a friend' and claimed the two leaders settled numerous issues. Trump also said both leaders share similar views on Iran, opposing its nuclear ambitions and wanting the Strait of Hormuz kept open.

stories.title: Jews protest at New York Times office against column alleging abuse of Palestinians
stories.summary: Jewish protesters gathered outside The New York Times office in Manhattan to demonstrate against a column alleging abuse of Palestinian detainees. Demonstrators chanted 'Stop the libels, stop the hate,' expressing concern that the coverage could incite violence.

stories.title: US House narrowly rejects bid to rein in Trump Iran war powers
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives narrowly rejected a resolution to limit President Trump's war powers regarding Iran. It was the third House vote on an Iran war powers measure this year.

stories.title: Angola: Angola and DR Congo Move Forward With Africa's Largest Electricity Interconnection Project
stories.summary: Congolese Minister of Water Resources and Electricity Molendo Sakombi announced in Luanda that Angola and the Democratic Republic of Congo will build one of Africa's largest electricity transmission lines, a roughly 1,450-kilometer link between Malanje and Fungurume.

stories.title: France squad: Didier Deschamps unveils his selections for the 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: France head coach Didier Deschamps announced his 26-man squad for the 2026 World Cup, selecting 25 capped internationals and one uncapped player, defender Robin Risser. The squad comprises three goalkeepers, nine defenders, five midfielders, and nine forwards for Deschamps' final tournament in charge.

stories.title: Tourist arrivals up 10% year on year in April, driven by Hong Kong Sevens
stories.summary: Hong Kong welcomed 4.21 million tourists in April, a 10% year-on-year increase driven partly by the annual Hong Kong Sevens rugby tournament. Total arrivals in the first four months reached 18.52 million, up 15% from the same period last year.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian following settler attack
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed one Palestinian and wounded another overnight in a town south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, following a settler attack in the same area. Settlers had stormed the area and attempted to attack residents' properties before Israeli forces raided the town, firing live ammunition and sound bombs.

stories.title: Nigeria: Dangote Restates Why He Didn't Buy Arsenal, Remains Passionate Fan
stories.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote reiterated that his $20 billion refinery project in Lagos prevented him from pursuing an ownership stake in English Premier League club Arsenal, while affirming he remains a passionate fan.

stories.title: Drone attacks kill one, injure three in Russia's Belgorod border region
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks killed one person and injured three in Russia's Belgorod border region on Thursday. Belgorod has been a frequent target of Ukrainian strikes.

stories.title: South Africa: Judge Condemns Zuma's 'Stalingrad Defence' As Arms Deal Trial Date Is Finally Set
stories.summary: A South African judge, Nkosinathi Chili, set a trial date for former President Jacob Zuma's long-running 1999 arms deal case, condemning repeated legal challenges as a "Stalingrad defence" tactic that has stalled justice for years.

stories.title: ‘I got really scared’: how the Philippine Senate shoot-out unfolded
stories.summary: Tensions in the Philippine Senate escalated into a shoot-out after lawmakers ousted the Senate leader and former police chief Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court, appeared at the building after six months in hiding.

stories.title: IDF prosecutors file indictment against terrorist who killed Yehuda Sherman in ramming attack
stories.summary: Israeli military prosecutors filed an indictment against a suspect accused of killing Yehuda Sherman in a vehicular ramming attack. Prosecutors requested the suspect, identified as Hasson, remain detained until the conclusion of legal proceedings, and the court ordered his continued detention.

stories.title: Israel to sue New York Times over article detailing rape of Palestinians detainees
stories.summary: Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced it is preparing legal action against The New York Times over an article describing rapes of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli custody. The decision was announced on social media after the newspaper publicly defended the report by columnist Nicholas Kristof.

stories.title: Trump hails ‘fantastic’ China trade deals, signalling Boeing, oil sales
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared he had secured "fantastic trade deals" during his state visit to Beijing, speaking alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Zhongnanhai leadership compound. The talks also covered Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Trump characterized the visit as beneficial for both countries.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 15: Art on trial from Venice to Jerusalem
stories.summary: The Times of Israel's culture editor Jessica Steinberg discussed anti-Israel protests at the Venice Biennale, a new theater production about the Adolf Eichmann trial, and artist Yaacov Agam receiving the Israel Prize. The briefing covered cultural developments spanning Venice and Jerusalem.

stories.title: Report: Israel and US weighing options for renewed attacks on Iran
stories.summary: Israeli and US military officials held meetings over the past week to discuss plans for potential renewed military action against Iran, according to Israeli public broadcaster Kan. Discussions included scenarios involving US strikes to pressure Tehran into negotiations and tightening a maritime blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UN: Russia kills 566 civilians in Ukraine in three months
stories.summary: A United Nations report found that 566 civilians were killed and 2,731 were injured in Russian attacks on Ukraine during the first quarter of this year, representing a 20% increase compared to the same period last year.

stories.title: China calls for peace in the Middle East, urges reopening of shipping lanes
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry called for an urgent ceasefire in the Middle East and the early reopening of shipping lanes. Beijing stressed that a 'comprehensive and lasting ceasefire' should be reached to restore peace and stability in the Middle East and Gulf region.

stories.title: From drab partitions to haute couture host: how a Sydney civic masterpiece was rescued
stories.summary: The former Department of Lands building on Sydney's Bridge Street has been recognized with a National Trust heritage award following its redevelopment. The sandstone building, once used for soldier settlement lottery draws, had been subdivided with partitions before being restored to its original grandeur.

stories.title: Russia’s Putin is heading to China next week, days after historic Xi-Trump summit
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to make a one-day visit to Beijing on approximately May 20, shortly after the Xi Jinping–Donald Trump summit concludes. Sources described the trip as part of routine Moscow-Beijing diplomatic engagement, with no elaborate ceremonies expected. It marks the first time China has hosted both leaders in such close succession.

stories.title: Sudan: RSF Claims Drone Downed in South Darfur As Attacks Continue
stories.summary: The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) claimed to have shot down a military drone over Nyala in South Darfur as the city endured renewed bombardment for a fourth consecutive day. Attacks were also reported in Mellit, Ed Damazin, and Mogja.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudanese Authorities Carry Out Deportations and Abuse of South Sudanese
stories.summary: Sudanese authorities have carried out deportations and abuses against South Sudanese nationals, according to reporting from Wunthou in South Sudan. Deportees described being told they had to return to their country.

stories.title: Settlers set ablaze vehicles, spray racist slogans in Ramallah
stories.summary: Israeli settlers infiltrated the outskirts of Jibya village near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank early Friday, setting fire to multiple vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on walls and properties. The incident is part of a wave of escalating settler violence in the area.

stories.title: Top US admiral: Strikes severely degraded Iran’s military, defence
stories.summary: Admiral Brad Cooper testified before US lawmakers on Capitol Hill, defending the outcomes of joint US-Israeli military operations against Iran. He argued that the strikes had severely degraded Iran's military and defense capabilities, though some legislators raised questions about the campaign's effectiveness.

stories.title: China hosts Trump at Temple of Heaven; Hong Kong sushi parasite video: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post highlighted seven stories of the week, including China's decision to host U.S. President Trump at Beijing's Temple of Heaven. The venue choice was noted for its diplomatic symbolism, as China frequently uses historic sites to convey messages about bilateral relationships and shared history.

stories.title: CIA director meets with top officials in Havana, Cuban government says
stories.summary: A U.S. delegation led by CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with counterparts at Cuba's Interior Ministry in Havana on Thursday. The meeting occurred amid worsening tensions over a U.S. fuel blockade that has severely limited Cuba's power generation.

stories.title: What Makes Trump’s New Counterterrorism Strategy So Alarming
stories.summary: A newly released U.S. counterterrorism strategy document has drawn scrutiny for the terrorist threats it omits. Analysts have flagged concerns about gaps in the strategy's coverage of specific threat categories.

stories.title: Iran's foreign minister calls on Brics members to condemn US and Israel
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister urged Brics member nations to condemn what he described as violations of international law by the United States and Israel, including what he called 'illegal aggression against Iran.' The appeal was made during a Brics meeting on Thursday.

stories.title: China wants Hormuz Strait open without restrictions, US official says
stories.summary: A US Trade Representative said Chinese officials made clear during the US-China summit that they want the Strait of Hormuz reopened without restrictions or tolls. Jamieson Greer told Bloomberg that China is being 'pragmatic' in its involvement with Tehran regarding the issue.

stories.title: Falklands, artists film on local talent and works
stories.summary: A new short film explores the arts and culture scene in the Falkland Islands, featuring local artists discussing their work and creative inspirations. The film was released alongside a new exhibition by ceramicist and islander Graham Bound.

stories.title: Trump says he will not be 'much more patient' with Iran, calls for a deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump warned Iran during a Fox News interview that he is running out of patience, stating he will not be 'much more patient.' Trump urged Iran to reach a deal, adding that the country could either negotiate or face severe consequences.

stories.title: Russians attack UN humanitarian mission cars in Kherson with drone
stories.summary: Russian forces struck vehicles belonging to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs with a drone in the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson, targeting a humanitarian mission.

stories.title: Egypt unveils two restored New Kingdom tombs in Luxor
stories.summary: Egyptian authorities unveiled two restored ancient tombs on the West Bank of Luxor dating to the New Kingdom period. The tombs contain scenes depicting daily life and funerary rituals.

stories.title: From Confucius to Tsinghua: Trump invokes history to anchor China-US future
stories.summary: At a state banquet in Beijing's Great Hall of the People, U.S. President Trump referenced centuries of shared history—including Confucius and Tsinghua University—to frame the future of China-U.S. relations. The speech was crafted to appeal to Chinese hosts, including President Xi Jinping, and characterized the bilateral relationship as one of the most consequential in history.

stories.title: After Trump’s pledge to ‘open up’ China, low expectations for trade deal
stories.summary: Following President Trump's pledge to 'open up' trade with China, analysts express low expectations for a significant breakthrough between the world's two largest economies. Observers anticipate only modest progress in US-China trade negotiations.

stories.title: What happens to those who say no to fighting wars?
stories.summary: Al Jazeera's Ava Warriner examined the status of conscientious objectors—individuals who refuse to participate in military combat. The report explored the legal and social consequences faced by those who decline to fight in contemporary conflicts.

stories.title: Middle East live: Trump says he won’t 'be much more patient’ with Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned he would not be much more patient with Iran and urged Tehran to reach a deal with Washington. The remarks came during his state visit to China and were part of broader diplomatic discussions on Middle East issues.

stories.title: The New York Times missed the mark on Israel and Eurovision
stories.summary: A commentary argued that claims of Israeli manipulation of Eurovision voting overlook the dynamics of the contest. The piece contended that in a politicized competition, a concentrated bloc of supporters can outweigh dispersed opposition.

stories.title: Terrorists hurl rocks at vehicles in West Bank, prompting search for attackers, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces reported that attackers hurled rocks at vehicles in the West Bank, prompting a search operation. Troops from the 636th Combat Intelligence Collection Battalion killed one suspect and injured another during the response.

stories.title: US House narrowly rejects bid to rein in Trump Iran war powers
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives voted 212–212 on a war powers resolution intended to limit President Trump's authority regarding military operations against Iran. The measure failed because it required a majority to pass, despite some Republican support.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon talks held in Washington as expiration of ceasefire nears
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese delegations held talks in Washington, D.C., as the expiration of their ceasefire agreement approaches. Al Jazeera's Manuel Rapalo reported from Washington, where the first of two scheduled days of negotiations concluded.

stories.title: OSCE to launch Moscow Mechanism to investigate Russia’s militarization of Ukrainian children
stories.summary: More than 40 member states of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe invoked the Moscow Mechanism to launch an investigation into Russia's alleged indoctrination and militarization of Ukrainian children.

stories.title: Russian adventurer pushing homemade cart ‘to Brazil’ reportedly killed in Ukrainian drone strike
stories.summary: Alexander, a Russian traveler from Stavropol Krai known online as "Sasha Kon," was reportedly killed on May 13 in Russia's Bryansk region by a Ukrainian drone strike while pushing a homemade cart on a journey he said was headed to Brazil.

stories.title: Bolsonaro reversal on ties to jailed banker leaves allies reeling
stories.summary: Allies of Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro sought to distance him from a jailed banker amid a growing political scandal in Brasilia. The controversy threatens Bolsonaro's prospects in the closely contested October presidential election.

stories.title: Ceasefire nation: Caught between war and peace, can Israelis move forward?
stories.summary: Psychologists say that while most Israelis are not living in active wartime conditions, shaky truces on three fronts and the persistent threat of renewed conflict prevent psychological healing. The report examines whether Israeli society can move forward amid ongoing uncertainty between war and peace.

stories.title: Trump China visit live: Rubio hoping for ‘positive response’ to appeal for release of Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai
stories.summary: During the second day of Trump-Xi talks in Beijing, Secretary of State Rubio raised the case of imprisoned Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai. Xi Jinping warned Trump that Taiwan could lead to clashes or conflict between the two nations. Trump also reportedly downplayed the urgency of securing Iran's enriched uranium.

stories.title: Third round of Israel-Lebanon peace talks 'productive, positive' so far, US official says
stories.summary: A U.S. official described the third round of Israel-Lebanon peace talks as productive and positive. An Israeli official said the negotiations in Washington aimed to discuss a framework for a broader agreement in greater depth.

stories.title: Nigeria rights body demands probe into civilian deaths in airstrikes
stories.summary: Nigeria's national human rights commission called on the military to conduct a thorough and prompt investigation into recurring civilian casualties caused by military airstrikes. The demand follows continued reports of civilian deaths from aerial operations.

stories.title: Trump says ‘decimation’ of Iran’s army ‘to be continued’ after he and China’s Xi discuss Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump stated that military action against Iran's army would continue after speaking with Chinese President Xi Jinping about the Strait of Hormuz. Xi reportedly pledged China would not supply military equipment to Iran. The U.S. House narrowly rejected an effort to limit Trump's war powers.

stories.title: Angus Taylor accused of ‘dog-whistling’ and marginalising immigrants over plan to cut benefits to non-citizens
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese accused opposition leader Angus Taylor of imitating One Nation policies and marginalizing immigrants after Taylor announced plans to cut social benefits and government programs for non-citizen permanent residents in his budget reply speech.

stories.title: Is Trump behind Japan’s push for radical military spending hike?
stories.summary: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party is considering raising defense spending to as much as 5% of GDP, driven by pressure from U.S. President Trump and worsening Indo-Pacific security conditions. This would represent a major shift from Japan's longstanding policy of keeping defense outlays near 1% of GDP.

stories.title: Elderly woman dies in fire sparked by faulty air-conditioner in Hong Kong flat
stories.summary: A 70-year-old woman died in a fire at Yu Tung Court's Hei Tung House in Hong Kong's Tung Chung district, suspected to have been caused by a malfunctioning air conditioner. Around 300 residents were evacuated from the building.

stories.title: Sri Lanka’s Fisheries Minister urges CM Vijay to ban bottom trawling
stories.summary: Sri Lanka's Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay to ban bottom trawling, citing its impact on marine resources. Chandrasekar said he hopes to travel to Tamil Nadu to meet the chief minister directly.

stories.title: Singapore doctor jailed over woman’s death during beauty treatment
stories.summary: A Singapore doctor, Chan Bingyi, was sentenced to 18 months in jail for causing the death of 31-year-old Lau Li Ting during an aesthetic treatment. He administered EDTA too quickly and at too high a concentration, leading to cardiac arrest. He later concealed the use of EDTA from her family and medical personnel.

stories.title: IMF says constructive US-China dialogue, reduced tensions good for world economy
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund said that constructive dialogue between the United States and China and reduced bilateral tensions would benefit the global economy. The statement came as the Trump-Xi summit took place amid pressures from the Middle East war and Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Hamas linked network behind Red Ribbon campaign for Palestinian 'hostages' - exclusive
stories.summary: A Red Ribbons campaign advocating for Palestinian detainees, launched in mid-November, has been linked to a Hamas-associated network. British activist Adnan Hmidan, who claimed the campaign, reportedly has extensive ties to organizations connected to Hamas and the Muslim Brotherhood.

stories.title: Does China’s Jiuzhang 4.0 computer herald the age of quantum supremacy?
stories.summary: Chinese researchers unveiled Jiuzhang 4.0, a photonic quantum computer developed at the University of Science and Technology of China. The team claims it vastly outperforms the world's fastest classical supercomputer, with results published in the journal Nature on May 13.

stories.title: Chinese man earns US$7,400 monthly selling fried rice at night market while dressed in a suit
stories.summary: A 19-year-old man surnamed Lu has gone viral in China for selling fried rice while wearing a suit at a night market in Yantai, Shandong province. He reportedly earns around 50,000 yuan (US$7,400) per month and has been running the stall since age 17.

stories.title: Romanian metal, Australian star Delta Goodrem qualify for Eurovision grand final
stories.summary: Romania's metal act, Danish club anthem performer, and Australian singer Delta Goodrem advanced to the Eurovision Song Contest 2026 grand final after the second semi-final in Vienna. Albania, Bulgaria, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Malta, Norway, and Ukraine also qualified for Saturday's final at the Wiener Stadthalle.

stories.title: UN denies early release of Bosnian Serb general Mladic
stories.summary: A UN tribunal denied a request for the early release of convicted Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladić. Mladić is serving a life sentence for genocide and crimes against humanity committed during the 1992–95 Bosnian War.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit live: Trump says Xi wants to assist US on Iran
stories.summary: During the second day of the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, President Xi Jinping warned Trump of potential clashes and conflicts over Taiwan. Trump reportedly told Xi he wants China's help on Iran, while Secretary of State Rubio appealed for the release of imprisoned Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai.

stories.title: P. Kumaran takes charge as India’s High Commissioner in London
stories.summary: P. Kumaran assumed charge as India's High Commissioner to the United Kingdom in London. Upon arrival, he paid tributes at the statues of Mahatma Gandhi and at Ambedkar House.

stories.title: Cuba's electrical grid suffers partial collapse as protests flare
stories.summary: Cuba's electrical grid suffered a partial collapse early on May 14, cutting power across eastern Cuba. The outage intensified public frustration as Cubans contend with chronic blackouts exacerbated by a U.S. fuel blockade, with protests reported.

stories.title: Eurovision braces for new protests over Israel’s participation
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest is approaching its grand final, with organisers preparing for renewed protests against Israel's participation in the event.

stories.title: Over 113,000 civilians remain in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities
stories.summary: Approximately 113,500 civilians remain in the Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities of Ukraine's Donetsk region, areas that face daily shelling from Russian forces.

stories.title: US says talks between Israeli, Lebanese ambassadors were ‘productive’
stories.summary: The United States described talks between Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors as productive. Separately, the U.S. House rejected a resolution to constrain President Trump's Iran war powers by a single vote, and the IDF conducted a readiness drill on Israel's eastern border.

stories.title: Brutal raid on woman's birthday party highlights rise of Russian vigilante group
stories.summary: The Russian vigilante group Russkaya Obshina carried out a violent raid on a woman's birthday party. The group conducts such raids targeting activities it considers contrary to what it calls traditional Russian values.

stories.title: With proposed FTA, Asean set to be ‘central’ in Canada’s trade diversification
stories.summary: Canada has proposed a free-trade agreement with ASEAN, aiming to diversify trade away from dependence on the United States. Analysts say the deal could benefit ASEAN sectors including mining and manufacturing while supporting Ottawa's broader economic diversification goals.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump’s visit to China shadowed by conflict with Tehran
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister stated that Iranians will not yield to pressure, asserting there is no military solution to the ongoing conflict between Iran and the United States during President Trump's visit to China.

stories.title: War update: 202 clashes on frontline as Ukrainian forces repel 30 Russian assaults in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: More than 200 combat engagements occurred along the Ukrainian frontline on Thursday, with Ukrainian forces repelling 30 Russian assaults in the Pokrovsk sector. Russian forces lost nearly 100 troops in failed breakthrough attempts.

stories.title: Haredi extremists demonstrate outside Military Police chief’s home, 2 weeks after breaking into it
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) demonstrators protested outside the home of Israel's Military Police chief, opposing the arrest of Haredi men who evaded military conscription. The IDF condemned the protest. One demonstrator was briefly detained and then released.

stories.title: Moscow court orders arrest of former deputy natural resources minister in absentia. His lawyer says he ‘temporarily’ left Russia and is not evading investigators.
stories.summary: A Moscow court ordered the arrest in absentia of Denis Butsayev, a former Russian deputy minister of natural resources, on charges of large-scale fraud. His lawyer said Butsayev had "temporarily" left Russia and was not evading investigators.

stories.title: Haiti gang clashes kill at least 78 in Port-au-Prince suburbs, UN says
stories.summary: Gang clashes in suburbs of Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital, have killed at least 78 people and wounded 66 since Saturday, according to the United Nations office in Haiti. The death toll included 10 civilians amid worsening insecurity in the Caribbean nation.

stories.title: Russian drones strike energy facility in Odesa region, cause power outages
stories.summary: Russian drones struck energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region on Thursday evening, causing power outages across the area.

stories.title: US admiral says Iran’s ability to threaten neighbours dramatically degraded
stories.summary: The head of US Central Command stated that Iran's defense industry has been set back by 90%, saying Tehran's ability to threaten its neighbors has been dramatically degraded.

stories.title: UN aid convoy hit by drone strikes in Ukraine’s Kherson
stories.summary: A United Nations humanitarian convoy delivering aid to the city of Kherson in southern Ukraine was struck twice by drones, hitting the UN vehicles.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla sets sail again after Israeli interceptions
stories.summary: Ships from the Global Sumud Flotilla departed from Marmaris, Turkey, on May 14 for a third attempt to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, after previous voyages were intercepted by Israel in international waters.

stories.title: Gazprom's Astrakhan plant halts fuel output after drone attack – Reuters
stories.summary: Gazprom's gas processing plant in Russia's southern Astrakhan region halted motor fuel production after a drone attack on May 13 caused a fire. Reuters reported the disruption to output at the facility.

stories.title: More Israeli strikes hit towns across southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel carried out air strikes on the southern Lebanese towns of Majdal Selem and Haris and shelled Deir al-Zahrani and al-Nabitieh al-Fawqa, violating the existing ceasefire agreement according to Al Jazeera reporters. The strikes occurred despite U.S. officials describing Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington as positive.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox protesters attempt to invade military police chief's home
stories.summary: Groups of ultra-Orthodox men in Israel attempted to storm the home of the military police chief amid escalating tensions over a Haredi draft bill being debated in the Knesset.

stories.title: Italy’s embassy says it continues to accept visa applications from Russians through intermediaries. Russia’s tour operators association had said the practice was banned.
stories.summary: Italy's embassy in Russia confirmed it continues to accept visa applications from Russian citizens through intermediaries, contradicting claims by Russia's tour operators association that the practice had been banned.

stories.title: China fires verbal warning shot at US over Taiwan
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping warned U.S. President Donald Trump that any misstep over Taiwan could push the two countries toward direct military confrontation, delivering the message during their summit in Beijing.

stories.title: Only Russia believes fake claim that King Carl XVI did not shake hands with Zelensky – Swedish expert
stories.summary: A Swedish expert said only Russian audiences believed a propaganda claim that Sweden's King Carl XVI refused to shake hands with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky during a royal visit to Ukraine. The expert dismissed the narrative as absurd disinformation.

stories.title: Why did Hongkongers queue round the clock for a new watch?
stories.summary: Shoppers in Hong Kong's Causeway Bay queued for days to purchase "Royal Pop" pocket watches, a collaboration between luxury watchmaker Audemars Piguet and Swatch, with lines stretching across several city blocks.

stories.title: Russian anti-war actress Olga Vasilieva calls ‘letter of repentance’ attributed to her a fake
stories.summary: Russian actress Olga Vasilieva, known for her anti-war stance, denied authoring a "letter of repentance" reportedly petitioning Russia's State Duma for permission for her and her husband, Dmitry Nazarov, to return to Russia. She called the document a fake.

stories.title: Lawmakers push for domestic shipbuilding fixes as US Navy explores overseas options
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers are pressing for improvements to domestic shipbuilding capacity as the Navy's fiscal 2027 plan, released Monday, outlines the possibility of manufacturing warships at foreign shipyards.

stories.title: First day of Lebanon-Israel ceasefire talks ‘positive’, US official says
stories.summary: The United States described the first day of ceasefire talks between Israel and Lebanon in Washington as positive. The existing truce is set to expire on Sunday, and violence continued even as negotiations proceeded. Israel has been striking Lebanon in response to Hezbollah fire.

stories.title: Netanyahu said seeking to dissuade Haredi parties from backing September elections date
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is reportedly trying to persuade ultra-Orthodox Haredi parties not to support scheduling elections for September, citing the need to focus on the war with Iran. Reports indicate the government is also planning a five-year support program for the ultra-Orthodox community.

stories.title: Italy's defence minister urges decision on EU SAFE loans before deadline
stories.summary: Italy's defense minister wrote twice to the Treasury urging a decision on whether to access the European Union's SAFE arms-buying fund. Rome must confirm its participation by the end of May.

stories.title: Talking (and Not Talking) Taiwan
stories.summary: The article examines contrasting U.S. and Chinese official readouts regarding discussions on Taiwan during the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, highlighting divergent messaging from both sides.

stories.title: US official says first day of Lebanon-Israel talks ‘positive’
stories.summary: A senior U.S. State Department official characterized the first day of Lebanon-Israel negotiations in Washington on Thursday as productive and positive. The official indicated that talks would continue the following day.

stories.title: Death toll from Russian attack on Kyiv rises to 13
stories.summary: The death toll from Russia's May 14 missile strike on Kyiv rose to 13, with rescue and recovery operations continuing at the attack site.

stories.title: One dead and two more ill after meningitis outbreak in Berkshire
stories.summary: A young person died and two others are being treated following a meningitis outbreak in Reading, Berkshire. UK health officials are offering antibiotics to close contacts as a precaution.

stories.title: Fight for Second Intifada victims reopens with $655 million judgment against PA - interview
stories.summary: A U.S. federal appeals court reinstated a $655.5 million judgment against the Palestinian Authority and the PLO. The case was brought by American families over attacks during the Second Intifada more than two decades ago.

stories.title: Cuba’s Diaz-Canel open to US aid amid worsening fuel crisis, blackouts
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel signaled openness to U.S. assistance as Cuba faces a deepening fuel crisis and widespread blackouts. A U.S. delegation led by CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with Cuban officials in Havana on Thursday to discuss bilateral relations.

stories.title: Israel to sue New York Times over article on rape of Palestinian detainees, Netanyahu says
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to sue The New York Times and one of its journalists for defamation over an article alleging widespread sexual violence by Israeli soldiers, prison guards, and settlers against Palestinian prisoners.

stories.title: Sweden began rebuilding its total defense system after Russia's annexation of Crimea – expert
stories.summary: Following Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea and the onset of aggression in eastern Ukraine, Sweden began rebuilding its total defense system starting in 2015, according to a defense expert.

stories.title: King Charles visits Jewish area of London hit by anti-Semitic attacks
stories.summary: King Charles visited Golders Green, a neighborhood in London home to a sizeable Jewish population, following a series of anti-Semitic attacks in the area.

stories.title: Spain PM defends Barcelona footballer against Israeli criticism
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez publicly defended Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal after Israeli Defense Minister accused the footballer of inciting hatred for waving a Palestinian flag at a victory rally. Sánchez said he was proud of Yamal's show of solidarity with Palestine.

stories.title: CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims
stories.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Cuban officials in Havana on Thursday amid significantly deteriorated U.S.-Cuba relations. Washington imposed a fuel blockade on the island in January, and the meeting aimed to improve bilateral dialogue.

stories.title: Senior Emirati scholar says ‘war criminal’ Netanyahu never visited UAE
stories.summary: Emirati scholar Abdulkhaleq Abdulla called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" and said he is unwelcome in the UAE. The UAE foreign ministry denied Netanyahu had visited the country, contradicting a statement from Netanyahu's office claiming a secret trip in March.

stories.title: Outcry in Italy over plans to expand Rome's famed Borghese Gallery
stories.summary: Italian heritage groups announced opposition to proposed construction of a new structure near Rome's Borghese Gallery, arguing the project would damage one of the world's most famous museums to accommodate mass tourism.

stories.title: New fires erupt in Chornobyl Exclusion Zone after downing of Russian drones
stories.summary: New fires broke out in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone on May 14 after Russian drones were downed over the area. The fires erupted in difficult-to-access terrain within the zone surrounding the former nuclear power plant.

stories.title: Trump says Beijing opposes Iranian toll in Hormuz, as Chinese vessels exit waterway
stories.summary: The White House said Chinese President Xi Jinping opposes Iran's toll on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and is considering purchasing more U.S. oil to replace lost Gulf supplies. The announcement followed a meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi during a state dinner in China.

stories.title: Iran and India discuss ‘regional developments’ in Brics talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister met India's national security advisor on the sidelines of the BRICS meeting in New Delhi on Thursday to discuss bilateral ties and regional developments. The meeting followed India's condemnation of an Iranian attack on an Indian-flagged vessel off Oman's coast.

stories.title: No hugs, ancient Greece and KFC: Five highlights from Trump-Xi talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Beijing for high-stakes talks covering the Iran conflict, the Ukraine war, and economic cooperation. The summit featured elaborate ceremony at the Great Hall of the People, with Trump publicly praising Xi.

stories.title: The US-China trade war is entering a worrying new phase: a legal arms race
stories.summary: President Trump's visit to China coincides with the U.S.-Iran war disrupting global energy supplies and straining Washington-Beijing ties. An analysis explores the intensifying legal arms race between the U.S. and China as a new dimension of their trade conflict.

stories.title: Cuba calls on US to lift blockade rather than offer aid
stories.summary: Cuban President Díaz-Canel urged the U.S. to lift its blockade rather than offer aid as the island endures worsening power cuts. CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Cuban officials in Havana on Thursday to advance political dialogue between the two nations.

stories.title: Tape shows Bolsonaro son asking jailed banker for $26.8m to fund film on father
stories.summary: Leaked audio published by Intercept Brasil shows Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a leading rightwing presidential hopeful, asking a banker accused of corruption for $26.8 million to fund a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

stories.title: Yemen government, Houthis to release more than 1,600 prisoners in conflict's  largest swap
stories.summary: The internationally recognized Yemeni government and the Iran-aligned Houthi group agreed to exchange more than 1,600 prisoners, according to the UN special envoy's office. It marks the largest prisoner swap since the Yemen war began.

stories.title: Amnesty calls for 'war crimes' probe into Israeli destruction of south Syria homes
stories.summary: Amnesty International called for a war crimes investigation into Israel's destruction of homes in southern Syria. Israel has launched hundreds of strikes on Syria and conducts regular incursions into the country's south, where it demands a demilitarized zone.

stories.title: Netanyahu's coalition moves to fast-track controversial laws ahead of upcoming Knesset dissolution
stories.summary: Netanyahu's coalition is moving to fast-track controversial legislation before an upcoming Knesset dissolution. The push follows a crisis within the coalition involving ultra-Orthodox parties over a disputed conscription law.

stories.title: Senior Emirati scholar says ‘war criminal’ Netanyahu never visited UAE
stories.summary: A senior Emirati scholar stated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu never visited the UAE, contradicting claims from Netanyahu's office that a trip took place in March. The scholar referred to Netanyahu as a "war criminal."

stories.title: Zelensky on meeting with US delegation: Ukraine cooperates with US at all levels
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated after meeting a U.S. delegation that Ukraine is cooperating with the United States at all levels. He cited engagement with the White House, Congress, the political community, the American corporate sector, and civil society.

stories.title: Haifa Port opens new cruise terminal as Israel’s tourism sector eyes recovery
stories.summary: Haifa Port inaugurated a new cruise terminal built with an investment of over 16 million NIS, set to begin operations with the opening of the cruise season on May 14 as Israel's tourism sector seeks recovery.

stories.title: Eurovision 2026: Delta Goodrem sends Australia to the grand final with note-perfect performance
stories.summary: Australian singer Delta Goodrem advanced to the Eurovision 2026 grand final with a performance described as note-perfect, becoming the first Australian act to qualify on the contest's 70th anniversary.

stories.title: Pakistan-UAE ties unaffected by external engagements, says FO
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office stated that Pakistan-UAE relations remain strong and unaffected by any external engagements by the Gulf state. The spokesperson cited bilateral trade of nearly $8 billion and a Pakistani diaspora of 2.2 million in the UAE as foundations of the relationship.

stories.title: Israel to sue NYT over ‘distorted’ report on sex abuse of Palestinian inmates
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to sue The New York Times over a report it described as "distorted" concerning the sexual abuse of Palestinian inmates. The report included accounts from fourteen individuals who said they had been sexually assaulted by Israeli settlers or security forces members.

stories.title: Trump says Beijing opposes Iranian toll in Hormuz, as Chinese vessels exit waterway
stories.summary: President Trump announced that Beijing opposes Iran's toll imposed on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, as Chinese vessels exited the waterway. The White House said China agreed to purchase more US oil to reduce its dependence on Gulf supplies.

stories.title: Israeli defence minister accuses Barcelona footballer of ‘inciting hate’ for waving Palestine flag
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz accused FC Barcelona footballer Lamine Yamal of "inciting hatred" against Israel after the 18-year-old waved a Palestinian flag during a victory parade in Barcelona. Katz called on FC Barcelona to distance itself from the player's actions.

stories.title: Ukraine’s kamikaze drones can now attack and return
stories.summary: Ukraine's Fire Point FP-1/2 kamikaze drone has been upgraded with the ability to attack targets and return for reuse, joining a growing trend of converting single-use Ukrainian drones into reusable platforms.

stories.title: Zelensky says Kh-101 missile produced in violation of sanctions likely used in Kyiv apartment building strike
stories.summary: President Zelensky said a Kh-101 cruise missile that struck a Kyiv apartment building during a massive Russian attack was manufactured in the second quarter of 2025, indicating Russia continues to bypass international sanctions. He called for decisive international action against sanctions-evasion schemes.

stories.title: Former Rosnano chief Anatoly Chubais denounces prosecution of ex-managers as ‘repressions’
stories.summary: Former Rosnano chief Anatoly Chubais publicly denounced the criminal prosecution of the Russian state nanotechnology corporation's former top managers, calling the cases "repressions" and "a mockery of the law."

stories.title: Russia starved Pokrovsk into submission. Kostiantynivka’s robots are blocking the encore.
stories.summary: After Russian forces starved Pokrovsk into submission in the Donetsk region, Ukraine is deploying resupply robots to help defend the nearby city of Kostiantynivka. However, human soldiers remain essential to the defense effort.

stories.title: Photo of US-China delegation criticized over absence of women: ‘masculine, militarized and exclusionary’
stories.summary: A photo of the U.S.-China delegation meeting in Beijing's Great Hall of the People drew criticism for the complete absence of women from either side. Observers called the image a signal that women's voices are excluded from shaping the global order.

stories.title: Israeli army fires at towns in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli artillery struck the southern Lebanese towns of Nabatieh al-Fouqa, Kfar Tebnit, Jebchit, and Mefdoun on Thursday, violating the ceasefire agreement. The strikes occurred as Lebanon and Israel held a new round of direct talks in Washington. Nearly 3,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since fighting resumed on March 2.

stories.title: Role of Gulf states in Iran conflict said to change over one week - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the role of Gulf states in the Iran conflict shifted over the course of a week. Iran's narrative highlighted that some Gulf states hosted US forces, while the UAE and Bahrain had signed the Abraham Accords with Israel.

stories.title: Trump hails ‘fantastic trade deals’ with Xi, China issues warning on Taiwan
stories.summary: President Trump claimed "fantastic trade deals" were reached during his final talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. However, Xi delivered a blunt warning that U.S. missteps on Taiwan could push the two nations toward conflict, according to Chinese state media reports.

stories.title: Russia’s State Duma appoints new human rights commissioner. Meduza sources say filmmaker Nikita Mikhalkov backed her appointment.
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma appointed Yana Lantratova as the country's new human rights commissioner. Sources indicated that prominent Russian filmmaker Nikita Mikhalkov backed her appointment.

stories.title: Pakistan raises $250m equivalent in inaugural Panda bond issuance
stories.summary: Pakistan raised $250 million equivalent through its inaugural Panda bond issuance in China's onshore capital market at a 2.5% interest rate with a three-year maturity. Finance advisor Khurram Schehzad called it Pakistan's first entry into the world's second-largest capital market.

stories.title: Chants of ‘death to Arabs’ at Jerusalem Day march as Ben Gvir flies Israeli flag on Temple Mount
stories.summary: During the annual Jerusalem Day march in Jerusalem's Old City, extremist youth groups chanted anti-Arab slogans and harassed journalists. National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir flew an Israeli flag on the Temple Mount. Police arrested 13 people and dispersed a left-wing group that came to protect Palestinians.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi 'doesn't want to appear too much in cooperation with Israel', analyst says
stories.summary: Analyst Federico Donelli said Abu Dhabi does not want to appear closely aligned with Israel given its actions in the region. The UAE denied Netanyahu's claimed secret visit, and a ship was seized off the UAE coast amid Strait of Hormuz tensions.

stories.title: Last residents evacuated from frontline village in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Armed Forces personnel evacuated the last two remaining residents from the frontline village of Dolynka in the Zaporizhzhia region. The evacuation removed all civilians from the village near the front lines.

stories.title: Australia news live: Delta Goodrem hits the stage in Eurovision semi; Angus Taylor accused of ‘dog whistle’ budget reply
stories.summary: Australian singer Delta Goodrem performed her song "Eclipse" in Eurovision's second semi-final ahead of Sunday's grand final. The competition has drawn controversy after Israel's Noam Bettan, who was booed during his performance, advanced from the first semi-final.

stories.title: ‘China is gaining from what the US is doing in Iran’
stories.summary: Geopolitical analyst Steve Okun argued that China is benefiting from the ongoing U.S. confrontation with Iran, gaining strategic and economic advantages as Washington focuses on the conflict.

stories.title: Watch: Congress ends suspense: V. D. Satheesan to be next Kerala CM | Above the Fold | 14.05.2026
stories.summary: India's Congress party named V.D. Satheesan as the next Chief Minister of Kerala after weeks of internal deliberations. Separately, India hosted a BRICS Foreign Ministers' meeting in New Delhi, where External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed global diplomatic priorities.

stories.title: BBC on the ground during march through Jerusalem's Old City
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Israeli marchers paraded through Jerusalem's Old City, in the area captured during the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. The BBC reported from the scene during the annual march.

stories.title: Diaspora Jews aren't ‘traitors’ for not making aliyah, Diaspora Affairs Minister Chikli says
stories.summary: Israeli Diaspora Affairs Minister Amichai Chikli stated that Jews living outside Israel should not be called "traitors" for not immigrating to Israel, saying such attacks on Diaspora Jewry do not serve Israeli interests.

stories.title: New Iraq PM pledges monopoly on arms
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament voted in Ali al-Zaidi as the new prime minister on Thursday. Zaidi pledged to establish a state monopoly on weapons and reform the security apparatus amid US pressure on Baghdad to dismantle Tehran-backed armed groups.

stories.title: Iraq sought financial assistance from IMF as result of Iran war, source close to IMF says
stories.summary: Iraqi officials have approached the International Monetary Fund in Washington seeking financial assistance due to the ongoing conflict with Iran in the Middle East, according to a source close to the IMF.

stories.title: China restores US beef trade amid Trump-Xi summit, alarming Brazilian exporters
stories.summary: China renewed US beef import licences during the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, alarming Brazilian exporters who depend on the Chinese market. A senior Brazilian government official expressed concern that the move could reshape competition and affect domestic cattle prices in Brazil.

stories.title: Top California Democratic strategist pleads guilty to $225,000 fraud charges
stories.summary: Dana Williamson, a prominent California Democratic political strategist with ties to Governor Gavin Newsom, pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges. Authorities said Williamson conspired to steal $225,000 from a dormant campaign account belonging to gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra.

stories.title: Cuba runs out of fuel, diesel amid US blockade
stories.summary: Cuba has exhausted its fuel and diesel supplies as the US blockade deepens the island's energy crisis. The Cuban government is considering a renewed US aid offer from the Trump administration, though the assistance would come with conditions.

stories.title: Almost 20 million people in Sudan still face acute hunger, monitors say
stories.summary: A global hunger monitor reported that approximately 19.5 million people in Sudan — over 40 percent of the population — face acute hunger. The ongoing war in Sudan has created what monitors describe as the world's worst hunger crisis.

stories.title: Day 1 of Beijing Summit Produces No Big Wins for Trump
stories.summary: The first day of the US-China summit in Beijing concluded without major breakthroughs for President Trump. Discussions covered the Iran war and trade issues, but no significant concessions were secured from President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Trump, Xi Hold High-Stakes Summit in Beijing
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a high-stakes summit in Beijing. Discussions covered topics ranging from the Iran conflict to trade relations. Trump reportedly failed to secure major concessions from Xi during the meeting.

stories.title: FC Barcelona apologizes to Israeli fans after player goes viral waving Palestinian flag
stories.summary: FC Barcelona issued an apology written in Hebrew specifically addressed to its Israeli fans after player Lamine Yamal went viral for waving a Palestinian flag.

stories.title: The Pentagon wants 10,000 small cruise missiles. Here’s who is making them.
stories.summary: The Pentagon is pursuing a major procurement effort to acquire 10,000 small cruise missiles. The initiative represents a significant push to expand U.S. munitions stockpiles, with multiple defense contractors competing for production contracts.

stories.title: Israel marks 59th Jerusalem Day with Old City flag march, nationwide celebrations
stories.summary: Israel celebrated its 59th Jerusalem Day on May 14 with the traditional flag march through Jerusalem's Old City and nationwide festivities. The date also coincided with the anniversary of Israel's Declaration of Independence.

stories.title: Vessel seized off UAE's Fujairah and heading toward Iranian waters, UKMTO says
stories.summary: A vessel anchored northeast of the UAE port of Fujairah was boarded by unauthorized personnel and began heading toward Iranian territorial waters, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations. The incident occurred as Iran asserted that ships entering the Strait of Hormuz must cooperate with the Iranian navy.

stories.title: Cautious optimism in Lebanon as direct talks with Israel progress
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli officials held two days of ambassador-level negotiations in the United States aimed at reaching a new ceasefire agreement. Lebanese officials expressed cautious optimism about the outcome of the direct talks.

stories.title: To deliver for the warfighter, acquisition reform must provide a level playing field
stories.summary: A sponsored commentary argues that defense acquisition reform should ensure all companies compete under uniform rules. Proponents contend that a level playing field in procurement fosters innovation and strengthens the U.S. defense industrial base to better serve warfighters.

stories.title: Iran’s FM urges BRICS states to condemn US-Israeli aggression
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi addressed a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi on Thursday, calling on member states to condemn what he described as US-Israeli aggression.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone commander proposes “Standard-10” for every strike crew in country
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone commander proposed a "Standard-10" benchmark for every strike crew in the country. His own unit in the 414th Brigade averages 30.6 confirmed kills per month, compared to a national average of three.

stories.title: Massive Russian attack on Kyiv: Death toll climbs to 12, including two children
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on Kyiv's Darnytskyi district on May 14 rose to 12, including two children. The attack was part of a massive Russian bombardment targeting the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Nobel winner Mukwege warns of predatory US deal for DR Congo
stories.summary: Congolese Nobel Peace Prize laureate Denis Mukwege criticized a US-brokered peace deal for eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, calling it predatory. Separately, China and Turkey are overtaking France as leading investors in Senegal's economy.

stories.title: Vessel seized off UAE’s Fujairah and heading toward Iranian waters, UKMTO says
stories.summary: A Honduras-flagged vessel, believed to be the Hui Chuan fishery research vessel, was seized off the UAE's Fujairah coast and was heading toward Iranian waters, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations and two maritime security sources.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli troops in northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it launched a drone attack targeting Israeli soldiers in northern Israel, injuring several Israeli civilians near the Israel-Lebanon border. The attack occurred as Lebanese and Israeli representatives met for direct talks in Washington.

stories.title: Israeli arrested in Netherlands on suspicion of drug trafficking, being in int'l smuggling ring
stories.summary: An Israeli national was arrested in the Netherlands on suspicion of drug trafficking and involvement in an international smuggling ring. Dutch police said the investigation is ongoing, with additional arrests expected in Israel and other European countries.

stories.title: FO says voices in India calling for dialogue with Pakistan a 'positive development'
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi described Indian voices calling for dialogue with Pakistan as a "positive development." He expressed hope that "warmongering" and "belligerence" in India would diminish over time.

stories.title: Macron ‘slap’ was sparked by texts with Iranian actress, book claims
stories.summary: A new book by a French journalist claims that text messages between President Emmanuel Macron and Iranian-French actress Golshifteh Farahani prompted a reported "slap" from First Lady Brigitte Macron. An AI-generated fake tabloid cover falsely depicted the pair together, amplifying the story.

stories.title: Skyeton makes Raybird reconnaissance drone Ukraine has used since 2018. Russia just destroyed its Kyiv office
stories.summary: Russia destroyed the Kyiv office of Skyeton, the Ukrainian manufacturer of the Raybird reconnaissance drone, which Ukraine's military has operated since 2018. The company stated it had anticipated eventually becoming a target.

stories.title: IMF warns of 'worst-case scenario' economic impact from Iran war
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that continued disruptions from the Middle East conflict risk a "worst-case scenario" for the global economy. IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack cited concerns about low growth and high inflation if the war persists.

stories.title: Beja swords remain 'cherished tradition' in Sudan market
stories.summary: At the Daim Arab Market in Port Sudan, Beja merchants continue to sell kaskara swords—straight, double-edged blades traditionally carried at weddings and on journeys. The swords remain a symbol of eastern Sudanese identity among the Beja people.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses strengthening Ukraine’s air defense with German delegation
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed strengthening Ukraine's air defense capabilities with senior German officials, including Thorsten Frei, Head of the Federal Chancellery, and Martin Jäger, President of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service.

stories.title: Iran military threat is diminished but not eliminated, CENTCOM chief says
stories.summary: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper stated that U.S. operations have severely degraded Iran's military capacity. He noted that roughly 90% of Iran's naval mine inventory has been eliminated. Cooper emphasized that while the threat is diminished, it has not been fully neutralized.

stories.title: A hero's sacrifice: The railway worker who embraced death to save lives
stories.summary: A 44-year-old Pakistani railway worker, Muhammad Liaqat Ali, was killed after confronting a suicide bomber wearing an explosive vest near the Mankoor check post in Attock's Jand-Kohat railway section, close to the Khushal Garh Bridge.

stories.title: Four killed in Israeli strikes on northern Gaza
stories.summary: At least four Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on northern Gaza, according to hospital sources. Several others, including children, were wounded. Separately, a Palestinian child was injured by Israeli settlers in the Silwan neighborhood of occupied East Jerusalem.

stories.title: IDF reveals it supplies Lebanese army with anti-explosive drone barbed wire
stories.summary: The Israeli military disclosed that it has been supplying the Lebanese army with anti-explosive drone barbed wire. Approximately 158,000 square meters of the material have been provided so far, covering an area equivalent to roughly 20 football fields.

stories.title: CENTCOM head: War massively reduced Iran’s capabilities, but it’s still able to strike
stories.summary: CENTCOM commander testified before Congress that the war has reduced Iran's defense industry capabilities by approximately 90%. However, he stated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps remains a major force and Iran retains the ability to carry out strikes.

stories.title: Israel’s Lebanon Strategy Is Self-Defeating
