stories.title: Neuty the nutria, viral pet rodent whose family fought a state to keep him, dies of cancer
stories.summary: Neuty, a domesticated nutria in Louisiana who gained viral fame and appeared on cable news, has died of cancer. Owners Denny and Myra Lacoste, who previously fought state wildlife authorities for the right to keep the semi-aquatic rodent as a pet, announced his death on Instagram to over 37,000 followers.

stories.title: China emperors drank from mountain springs, melted snow; commoners used murky well water
stories.summary: An article explores the historical significance of drinking water in ancient China, where water quality was linked to social rank, health beliefs, and ritual practice. Imperial figures consumed mountain spring water while commoners relied on murky well water.

stories.title: Nigerian film star Alex Ekubo dies aged 40
stories.summary: Nigerian actor Alex Ekubo has died at the age of 40. He was widely recognized for his contributions to the entertainment industry and his humanitarian work.

stories.title: SBP says it has received $1.3bn tranche from IMF
stories.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan confirmed receipt of approximately $1.3 billion from the International Monetary Fund after the IMF Executive Board completed the third review under the Extended Fund Facility and approved disbursements totaling SDR 914 million, including funds from the Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

stories.title: At least eight killed in Israeli drone strikes on highway south of Beirut
stories.summary: Israeli drone strikes hit three cars on a highway near Jiyeh, south of Beirut, killing at least eight people, including two children. The strikes targeted vehicles on the Saida-South coastal highway.

stories.title: Russian foreign minister says ‘nothing is happening’ in US talks on Ukraine and peace process is stuck – Europe live
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said "nothing is happening" in US-mediated talks on Ukraine, describing the peace process as stuck. His remarks came before leaders of the Bucharest Nine group met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Meanwhile, Ukraine's military intelligence reported Russia launched a combined airstrike on critical facilities using drones, missiles, and ballistic weapons.

stories.title: Hong Kong labour chief rejects review of non-local graduate visas despite job slump
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun rejected calls to review immigration schemes for non-local graduates despite declining entry-level job opportunities. He argued the city's workforce is shrinking and local degree holders cannot meet labor demand.

stories.title: UK housebuilder Vistry warns of ‘significantly’ lower profits amid Iran war uncertainty
stories.summary: UK housebuilder Vistry, owner of Bovis Homes, warned that first-half profits would be "significantly" lower due to uncertainty caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The company's shares fell 10.5% to their lowest level in nearly 15 years after it disclosed it had been forced to cut prices as buyers became cautious.

stories.title: Trump set to meet with Xi in Beijing as war and inflation weigh on his presidency
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for a summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping amid global concerns over war, trade, and artificial intelligence. The visit comes at a difficult moment for Trump's presidency, with his domestic popularity affected by the US-Israel war with Iran and rising inflation.

stories.title: France intensifies hantavirus surveillance as 22 contact cases identified
stories.summary: France has identified 22 contact cases linked to the hantavirus outbreak that originated on a cruise ship, bringing total reported cases to 11, with 9 confirmed. A French woman infected during the outbreak is critically ill in a Paris hospital. Authorities say there is currently no widespread transmission of the virus in the country.

stories.title: Drones strike “industrial facility” in Yaroslavl, Russia
stories.summary: Russian local authorities in Yaroslavl confirmed that Ukrainian drones damaged an industrial facility in the city. No further details on casualties or the specific nature of the facility were immediately provided.

stories.title: Macron's interview with FRANCE 24: French president recaps his work in Africa over 2 terms
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron gave an interview to France 24, RFI, and Le Monde at the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, Kenya. He used the opportunity to review his Africa policy over the course of his two presidential terms, beginning in 2017.

stories.title: How Keir Starmer could be replaced as UK PM after discontent rises in his own party
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces growing calls to step down from within his own Labour Party after heavy local election losses. Potential leadership contenders include Health Secretary Wes Streeting, former Deputy PM Angela Rayner, and Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham.

stories.title: Series of tremors near Tehran renews concerns over major quake risk
stories.summary: A series of tremors struck near Tehran close to the Mosha fault, one of Iran's most active seismic zones. The activity has renewed concerns about the risk of a major earthquake in the densely populated area surrounding the Iranian capital.

stories.title: NIS 200,000  allocated for laptops, school equipment for low-income children in northern Israel
stories.summary: Israel allocated NIS 200,000 for laptops and school equipment for low-income children in northern Israel. The one-time allocation from the Ida Abush public endowment includes safeguards to ensure the fund can continue operating in the future.

stories.title: Bring Me the Horizon and Eric Clapton struck by objects thrown by audience members
stories.summary: Bring Me the Horizon frontman Oli Sykes suffered a concussion after being struck by a phone thrown by an audience member during a concert in St. Louis on Monday. Separately, Eric Clapton was also struck by an object thrown while performing. Both incidents are part of a growing trend of musicians being hit by items at live shows.

stories.title: Russian ship that sank after strange explosions reportedly carying nuclear reactors to North Korea
stories.summary: A Russian ship that sank following unexplained explosions was reportedly carrying nuclear reactors destined for North Korea. US military surveillance aircraft, known as "nuke sniffers," have been recorded surveying the wreckage site twice, in August 2025 and February 2026.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 111 of 139 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces shot down 111 of 139 Russian drones launched against Ukraine since the evening of May 12. Twenty-eight drones were not intercepted.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Govt Introduces Drug Integrity Tests for Secondary, University Students
stories.summary: The Nigerian government announced a new policy requiring students seeking admission to secondary and tertiary institutions to undergo drug integrity tests.

stories.title: Israeli defense-tech company secures $10.7 million contract with US to supply AI-powered system
stories.summary: Israeli defense-technology company Smart Shooter secured a $10.7 million contract with the United States to supply its AI-powered SMASH targeting systems. Deliveries are expected in the third quarter of 2026.

stories.title: US intelligence says Iran retains 70% of missile arsenal
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence assessments indicate Iran has retained approximately 70 percent of its missile arsenal. According to The New York Times, Iran has restored operational control over 30 of its 33 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz, with only three remaining inaccessible.

stories.title: China’s new rules give the West a new headache
stories.summary: China has introduced new regulations granting Beijing expanded authority to penalize companies that relocate manufacturing operations out of the country. The rules add to compliance challenges for multinationals navigating trade tensions among the US, EU, and China.

stories.title: ‘Like whale bones’: South Korea’s war memorial sparks conflict over symbolism
stories.summary: A newly unveiled Korean War memorial of 23 stone monuments in Seoul's Gwanghwamun Square has sparked a dispute. Critics question whether the massive installation belongs in the historic public plaza long associated with civic gatherings and pro-democracy protests.

stories.title: Helper molested 10-year-old girl while waking her up, Hong Kong court hears
stories.summary: A 10-year-old girl testified via video conference in Hong Kong's Kowloon City Court that domestic helper Lady Jay Santos Flores inappropriately touched her while waking her up. Flores is standing trial on four counts of indecent assault involving two daughters of her former employer.

stories.title: Trump arrives in China for talks; Israel kills 12 in Lebanon
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Separately, Israeli strikes killed 12 people in Lebanon. Beijing had previously urged Pakistan to intensify mediation efforts toward a deal with Iran.

stories.title: Trump arrives in China as Iran sets truce conditions
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly a decade. The visit follows Beijing's encouragement of Pakistan to intensify mediation efforts for a deal with Iran.

stories.title: Trump travels to China as Iran sets truce conditions
stories.summary: President Trump is set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing after China urged Pakistan to intensify mediation efforts to broker a deal with Iran. The visit comes as Iran has outlined conditions for a truce.

stories.title: Leaving so soon? US, China hold briefest trade talks yet before leaders’ summit
stories.summary: Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent concluded their seventh round of trade talks in Seoul in under four hours on Wednesday, making it the shortest session since negotiations began. The meeting ended without any media statements, just hours before President Trump's scheduled arrival in Beijing.

stories.title: Austrian jets intercept unauthorized US military planes two days in a row
stories.summary: Austrian military jets intercepted unauthorized US military aircraft over the Totes Gebirge mountain range in Upper Austria on May 10, more than 60 kilometers from the German border. The intercepts occurred on two consecutive days.

stories.title: War update: 210 combat clashes on front line over past day, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors remain hottest
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces recorded 210 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line on May 12. The Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors saw the heaviest fighting.

stories.title: Taiwan stages live-fire drill on island facing mainland China as Trump heads to Beijing
stories.summary: Taiwan conducted a large-scale live-fire military exercise on Kinmen Island, located near mainland China, on Wednesday simulating a People's Liberation Army amphibious assault. The drill took place hours before US President Donald Trump was due to arrive in Beijing for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, amid Taiwanese concerns about becoming a bargaining chip in US-China negotiations.

stories.title: Trump flies to Beijing, Nvidia’s Huang joins trip at last minute
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump departed for Beijing and called on Chinese leader Xi Jinping to open China to American business. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined the presidential delegation after a last-minute invitation, boarding Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska on Wednesday.

stories.title: Japan crisp packs to go colourless due to Iran war crunch
stories.summary: Japanese snack manufacturer Calbee announced it would switch its potato chip packaging from colorful designs to two-color printing due to supply instabilities linked to the Iran war, affecting 14 product lines starting in late May or June.

stories.title: NYT pushes back on Israeli criticism of column alleging rape of Palestinian inmates
stories.summary: The New York Times defended a column alleging rape of Palestinian inmates in Israeli custody after criticism from Israeli officials and Jewish groups. Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert said the column misrepresented his words. Jewish organizations announced a protest outside the newspaper's Manhattan offices.

stories.title: Jason Collins, first openly gay active NBA player, dies after cancer battle
stories.summary: Jason Collins, who in 2013 became the first openly gay active player in the NBA, has died after battling a brain tumour. The 213cm centre played 13 seasons in the league.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region kill eight civilians, injure 11
stories.summary: Russian attacks across Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed eight civilians and injured 11 others.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopian Marathon Star Yebrgual Melese Dies During Training
stories.summary: Ethiopian marathon runner Yebrgual Melese died at the age of 36 after falling ill during a routine training session. She was a prominent figure in Ethiopian long-distance running.

stories.title: How Silicon Valley giants are turning into war contractors
stories.summary: Major Silicon Valley companies including Palantir, Anduril, and Google are increasingly entering the defence sector. The firms are developing and selling AI-powered, computer-guided weapons systems to military clients.

stories.title: Burkina Faso's military rulers intensify crackdown on civil society groups
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military government announced the suspension of an additional 247 civil society associations, bringing the total number closed or dissolved since the previous month to more than 900.

stories.title: Rubio, with new Chinese name, heads to Beijing despite sanctions
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who authored key congressional legislation imposing broad sanctions on China, is traveling to Beijing. He has adopted a new Chinese name ahead of the visit despite remaining under Chinese sanctions.

stories.title: ‘New historical juncture’: Beijing frames Trump visit as ‘milestone’ for stable ties
stories.summary: Ahead of President Trump's state visit to Beijing, Chinese state media characterized the summit with President Xi Jinping as a milestone opportunity to stabilize bilateral relations. China's ambassador to the US, Xie Feng, expressed hope in a Newsweek interview that the meetings would help manage differences and broaden cooperation.

stories.title: Florida plans to close 'Alligator Alcatraz' migrant detention center - report
stories.summary: Florida plans to close a migrant detention center nicknamed "Alligator Alcatraz," according to reports. The US Department of Homeland Security said it continues to evaluate detention needs and requirements to meet operational demands.

stories.title: Russia seizes 900 Mariupol apartments from owners it forced to flee
stories.summary: Russian authorities are redistributing nearly 900 apartments in occupied Mariupol, Ukraine, that belonged to residents who fled the city during bombardment. The apartments are being reassigned to Russian officials.

stories.title: War overshadows BRICS forum bringing together Iran and UAE in India
stories.summary: The ongoing regional war overshadowed a BRICS forum in India where Iran and the UAE were both present. Tehran urged host India to build consensus condemning US-Israeli strikes, while reports of Saudi and Gulf military actions against Iran heightened tensions at the gathering.

stories.title: Starmer holds 16-minute meeting with Streeting amid leadership crisis
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting met with Prime Minister Keir Starmer at Downing Street for approximately 16 minutes on Wednesday amid Labour's leadership crisis. An ally of Streeting renewed calls for Starmer to resign, saying his authority had "irretrievably ebbed away" following the party's heavy losses in local elections.

stories.title: Why the world needs China to save more, not less
stories.summary: A G7 economists' memo and an IMF report both recommended that China reduce its current account surplus by boosting domestic consumption. The article argues this diagnosis is misguided, contending that China's high national saving benefits the global economy, particularly emerging markets, by exporting surplus capital abroad as net investment.

stories.title: WHO praises Spain's handling of repatriation: 'Further Hantavirus spread can be stopped effectively'
stories.summary: The World Health Organization praised Spain's handling of hantavirus patient repatriation, saying further spread of the virus can be stopped effectively. Virologist Muhammad Munir of Lancaster University described the repatriation effort as a critical juncture where scientific preparedness and political coordination must converge.

stories.title: Iran sets five conditions for US talks amid ceasefire tensions
stories.summary: Iran announced five preconditions for restarting negotiations with the United States. The conditions include lifting sanctions, ending regional wars, and recognizing Tehran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russian drones target industrial infrastructure in Odesa region
stories.summary: Russian strike drones carried out a mass attack on industrial infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region overnight on May 13.

stories.title: Australian military plane to join efforts to reopen strait of Hormuz as Marles considers ‘how else we can contribute’
stories.summary: Australia announced it will deploy an E-7A Wedgetail surveillance aircraft to join a UK and France-led international mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran conflict. Defence Minister Richard Marles participated in a meeting with defense ministers from over 40 countries and did not rule out sending additional assets to the Middle East.

stories.title: Islamabad lawyers unhappy as JCP decision dims elevation prospects
stories.summary: The Judicial Commission of Pakistan decided against making fresh appointments to the Islamabad High Court after transferring three of its judges to other provinces. Islamabad's legal community expressed concern over diminished local representation and is considering legal challenges.

stories.title: Hantavirus vs. Covid: Low transmission efficiency means far less risk of another widespread outbreak
stories.summary: Canadian virologist Bryce Warner of the University of Saskatchewan assessed the hantavirus outbreak, noting that the Andes virus has far lower transmission efficiency than COVID-19. Despite concerns raised by suspected human-to-human transmission on a cruise ship, Warner said the scientific reality differs profoundly from the early days of the coronavirus pandemic.

stories.title: Four authors named as finalists for Sami Rohr Prize
stories.summary: Four authors have been named finalists for the Sami Rohr Prize for Jewish literature. The awards ceremony, held in association with Israel's National Library, is scheduled to take place in Jerusalem in July.

stories.title: Earthquake shakes Tehran, a city with already frayed nerves
stories.summary: An earthquake struck Tehran, Iran, rattling residents in the capital. There were no immediate reports of damage or casualties. The tremor added to existing anxieties in a city already on edge.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,130 troops, three air defense systems in Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russia lost approximately 1,130 troops in Ukraine over the past day, along with three air defense systems. Total Russian combat losses since the February 2022 full-scale invasion have reached approximately 1,344,180 personnel.

stories.title: Woman dies, another unconscious as taxi driven by man in 70s crashes into planter
stories.summary: A taxi driven by a man in his seventies mounted a pavement on Choi Ha Road in Ngau Tau Kok, Hong Kong, on Wednesday afternoon, killing one woman and leaving another unconscious. The vehicle struck two women in their thirties before crashing into a concrete planter. The driver and his two passengers were also injured.

stories.title: Man who averted suicide attack nominated for ‘highest civil award’
stories.summary: Muhammad Liaqat Ali, a railway employee in Attock district's Jand tehsil near the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border, was killed while intercepting a suspected suicide attacker targeting a police checkpost. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz nominated him for Pakistan's highest civil award.

stories.title: In Gaza, e-wallets have become lifeline amid growing cash crises
stories.summary: E-wallet applications have become a critical financial lifeline in Gaza amid severe cash shortages. The digital payment tools have spread rapidly through markets, grocery stores, transportation networks, and displacement camps across the territory.

stories.title: Easy as ABC: voters in England tend to pick names nearer top of ballot, data suggests
stories.summary: A Guardian analysis of English local election results found that where parties fielded multiple candidates in a ward, those listed nearer the top of the ballot paper—with surnames earlier in the alphabet—tended to receive more votes. The data was compiled from results gathered by the website Democracy Club.

stories.title: President Macron faces backlash after summit outburst
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron faced criticism after interrupting a panel at the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, Kenya, to demand silence from the audience. The incident drew widespread backlash.

stories.title: Israel orders evacuations in six south Lebanon towns
stories.summary: The Israeli military ordered evacuations in six southern Lebanese towns and villages—Meiss El Jabal, Yanouh, Borj El Chmali, Houla, Debl, and Aabbasiyyeh—warning of imminent forceful action. Residents were told to move at least 1,000 metres away. Separately, Israel reported Hezbollah rocket fire targeting its soldiers.

stories.title: The power of trust
stories.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan released its annual report documenting a severe contraction of civic space, erosion of judicial independence, and deepening insecurity in 2025, including 273 new cases of enforced disappearances registered by the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances.

stories.title: Russian agent sentenced to 15 years for plotting to blow up gas pipeline in eastern Ukraine
stories.summary: A Russian military intelligence agent was sentenced to 15 years in prison with property confiscation for plotting to blow up a major gas pipeline in eastern Ukraine and spying on Ukraine's Defense Forces.

stories.title: China’s Xi expected to press Trump on Taiwan, tariffs during summit
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to press U.S. President Donald Trump on Taiwan-related arms sales and tariffs during an upcoming summit. Analysts say Xi will likely seek concessions on U.S. weapons deliveries to Taiwan.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says stopping Iran's nuclear program outweighs Americans' economic pain
stories.summary: Iran's chief negotiator stated that Washington must accept Tehran's latest peace plan or face failure. US President Trump said stopping Iran's nuclear program outweighed the economic costs to Americans.

stories.title: Iran war day 75: Trump-Xi talks loom in Beijing as tensions rise in Gulf
stories.summary: President Trump is travelling to Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping as the Iran conflict enters its 75th day. Escalating tensions in the Gulf are expected to feature prominently alongside broader bilateral issues.

stories.title: Kabbalah of information: Rethinking death through physics and faith - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Dr. Eduard Shyfrin, a Doctor of Chemistry, has published a book titled The Relativity of Death. The work presents a theory synthesizing Kabbalistic thought and modern physics to explore questions of existence and death.

stories.title: Trump expects ‘big, fat hug’ from Xi amid tense agenda
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with Taiwan, tariffs, rare earths, and the US-Israel war on Iran among key agenda items. Trump said he expected a warm reception despite the contentious issues on the table.

stories.title: Trump's proposed ‘Golden Dome’ estimated to cost $1.2 trillion, far more than he initially said
stories.summary: The US Congressional Budget Office estimated the proposed Golden Dome missile defense system would cost $1.2 trillion, significantly more than initial projections. The system would include ground- and space-based capabilities to detect and intercept missiles at all stages of attack.

stories.title: In Latvia, military robots roll across a new communication challenge: woodlands
stories.summary: During military exercises in Latvia, operators of unmanned ground vehicles reported significant communication challenges in densely forested areas of the Baltic nation. Many of the UGVs relied on Starlink for connectivity, which proved problematic under heavy woodland canopy.

stories.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang joins Trump as tech dominates China trip
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined President Trump's delegation to Beijing after a reported last-minute invitation, alongside executives including Elon Musk, Tim Cook, and Goldman Sachs's David Solomon. The group is accompanying Trump on a 36-hour visit for meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, underscoring US AI and technology ambitions.

stories.title: Video: Israel passes law to execute Palestinians linked to 7 October attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed legislation on Tuesday with 93 votes in favour and none opposed to establish public trials and impose the death penalty on Palestinian detainees accused of involvement in the 7 October attacks. The bill drew support from across the political spectrum.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Diplomatic activity around the Iran conflict is intensifying as US President Donald Trump travels to Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. China is also pressing Pakistan to continue mediating between Washington and Tehran. Lebanon continues to face Israeli strikes while concerns over Strait of Hormuz shipping security persist.

stories.title: Geopolitical shift in ME
stories.summary: An editorial analyzes US President Donald Trump's conflicting statements on the Iran conflict, including his rejection of Tehran's peace proposal and claims of having achieved war objectives, while suggesting the Middle East is undergoing a significant geopolitical shift.

stories.title: US might restart striking Iran, Trump and Hegseth warn
stories.summary: President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the United States might resume military strikes against Iran. The ongoing conflict has cost an estimated US$29 billion so far.

stories.title: Mexico rejects CNN report on deadly CIA operations against cartels
stories.summary: Mexico's government rejected a CNN report alleging deadly CIA operations targeting drug cartels on Mexican soil. The reported presence of CIA operatives in Mexico has recently strained bilateral relations between the two countries.

stories.title: State bodies, NGOs up in arms over oil company’s plan to move into fiber optics
stories.summary: Israeli state bodies and NGOs are opposing the Europe Asia Pipeline Company's plan to expand into fiber optics. Opponents argue the law limits EAPC to crude oil transportation and storage, while the company says the project would make Israel a regional communications hub.

stories.title: The Missing Navies: The Hormuz Crisis and the Limits of America’s Indo-Pacific Partnerships
stories.summary: After a South Korean vessel came under fire in the Strait of Hormuz on May 4, 2026, President Trump urged Seoul to join US-led operations to secure the waterway. The article examines a broader paradox: the Hormuz crisis disproportionately affects Asian economies, yet Asian nations have been largely absent from efforts to resolve the maritime disruption.

stories.title: Police uncover interregional network helping soldiers desert military service
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Police uncovered an interregional criminal network that illegally transported servicemen out of military units to help them desert from the country's Security and Defense Forces.

stories.title: Iran war costs soar past $29bn as truce teeters
stories.summary: The Pentagon disclosed that the US conflict with Iran has cost Washington more than $29 billion since hostilities began, as peace prospects dimmed due to rigid stances from both sides. Separately, Pakistan's mediation efforts earned praise from President Trump.

stories.title: 'Serious disease': Hantavirus less infectious than COVID, yet has significant fatality rate - 1 in 3
stories.summary: Professor Matt McKee of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine described hantavirus as a serious disease with a fatality rate of roughly one in three. However, he emphasized it does not spread at rates comparable to COVID-19, drawing clear distinctions between the two diseases.

stories.title: King Charles to lay out government agenda as Starmer battles to keep PM job
stories.summary: King Charles III delivered the government's legislative programme in the traditional King's Speech on Wednesday, as Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced mounting pressure over his leadership following Labour's heavy local election defeats. The speech outlined the government's agenda amid deepening divisions within the ruling party.

stories.title: British-German startup just flew hypersonic missile at 7,400 km/h — months after UK said such weapons could boost Ukraine’s firepower
stories.summary: British-German startup Hypersonica, part of the company Nightfall, successfully tested a hypersonic missile that reached speeds exceeding 7,400 km/h. The launch took place at Andøya Spaceport in Norway, months after the UK suggested such weapons could enhance Ukraine's military capability.

stories.title: PM orders uninterrupted supply of fertiliser to safeguard food security
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed authorities to ensure uninterrupted fertiliser supply to farmers and ordered continuous monitoring of reserves to protect food security. He also instructed ministries to explore alternative fertiliser imports from Central Asia.

stories.title: South Korea adds ‘extreme heat emergency’ to first major alert update in 18 years
stories.summary: South Korea's Korea Meteorological Administration announced a major overhaul of its national weather warning system on Wednesday, the first such restructuring in nearly two decades. The update introduces a top-tier "extreme heat emergency" alert category in response to intensifying climate change effects on the country's seasonal patterns.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit: Trade, Taiwan and Iran on the table at high-stakes Beijing meeting
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump's visit to Beijing on Wednesday for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping is expected to cover trade, Taiwan, and Iran. Trump said he would have a "long talk" about Iran with Xi and also discuss US arms sales to Taiwan during the high-stakes summit.

stories.title: Pakistan’s New Logic of Limited War May Not Keep War Limited
stories.summary: During the May 2025 India-Pakistan crisis, Indian BrahMos missiles struck Pakistani air bases, but Pakistan deliberately withheld its dual-capable Babur cruise missile to avoid signaling nuclear escalation. The four-day confrontation was intense but contained, illustrating a new logic of limited war in South Asia defined by deliberate restraint.

stories.title: Fuel levy yields lowest fiscal deficit in nearly three decades
stories.summary: Pakistan recorded its lowest fiscal deficit in at least 27 years at 0.7 percent of GDP during July-March of the current fiscal year. The improvement was driven by higher provincial surpluses, strong petroleum development levy collections, and lower interest payments, despite declines in revenue ratios.

stories.title: US intelligence shows Iran retains substantial missile capabilities
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence assessments indicate that Iran retains significant missile capabilities despite the ongoing conflict. Approximately 70 percent of Iran's mobile missile launchers remain operational and deployed across the country.

stories.title: Trump and Xi to meet in Beijing: The key issues shaping the China summit
stories.summary: President Trump and President Xi Jinping are meeting in Beijing for a high-stakes summit. Trade disputes, the status of Taiwan, and the ongoing Iran war are the dominant issues on the agenda.

stories.title: Kremlin using criminal networks and mercenaries to destabilize EU countries – CCD
stories.summary: Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation reported that the Kremlin is using criminal networks, mercenaries, and marginalized recruits as low-cost tools for terror and destabilization in European Union countries.

stories.title: 3 arrested after HK$11.3 million in suspected illicit proceeds and cigarettes seized
stories.summary: Hong Kong customs arrested three members of a local syndicate suspected of selling illicit cigarettes and money laundering on Tuesday. Officers raided five residential flats, seizing approximately 2.2 million untaxed cigarettes and alleged criminal proceeds of HK$11.3 million. Two men aged 31 and 37 and a 35-year-old woman were detained.

stories.title: US and China in ‘unprecedented’ cooperation against scam centres in Dubai
stories.summary: The FBI and Chinese police participated in a joint operation with Dubai Police targeting scam networks in the United Arab Emirates. The operation, dubbed Tri-Force Sentinel, dismantled at least nine scam hubs and led to the arrest of 276 suspects, most from Southeast Asia. The rare cooperation came ahead of President Trump's visit to China.

stories.title: Peru presidential candidate Sanchez accused of financial crimes after advancing to runoff
stories.summary: A Peruvian prosecutor accused leftist presidential candidate Roberto Sanchez of financial crimes, according to local outlet RPP. The accusations came hours after electoral authorities confirmed Sanchez was on track to advance to the country's presidential runoff vote.

stories.title: US social media legislation gains momentum as key Republican senator pledges support
stories.summary: A key Republican senator has pledged support for U.S. social media legislation, giving the effort new momentum. The proposed measures target harms to minors including eating disorders, depression, and sexual harassment.

stories.title: Iran executes man accused of spying on behalf of Israel’s Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed 32-year-old Ehsan Afrashteh, who was accused of spying for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. Iranian judiciary officials said he confessed to being paid to carry out tasks for Mossad, while a human rights group said the confession was fabricated.

stories.title: Video: Turkey’s Fidan says Israel’s policies becoming ‘global security problem’
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated on Tuesday that Israel's actions are evolving into a "global security problem" beyond the region. He accused Israel of escalating regional tensions through violence and expansionism.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Troops Intercept 400 Starlink Devices Allegedly Used By Terrorists - Official
stories.summary: Nigerian military forces intercepted approximately 400 Starlink satellite terminals allegedly used by terrorist groups. The devices were seized during operations across Sambisa Forest, the Timbuktu Triangle, and other enclaves in northeastern Nigeria.

stories.title: US-China head-to-head: Explained in 11 maps and charts
stories.summary: Ahead of President Trump's visit to Beijing, Al Jazeera published an analysis comparing the United States and China across economics, military capability, and resources using 11 maps and charts.

stories.title: SBU detains Russian spotter guiding strikes on Sloviansk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a Russian agent in the Donetsk region who had been directing Russian strikes on the town of Sloviansk.

stories.title: Singapore’s Lawrence Wong urges global push for upholding international sea laws
stories.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong warned that weakened international maritime law would directly threaten Singapore's status as a global trade hub. He called on like-minded nations to cooperate in upholding the law of the sea to keep vital waterways open.

stories.title: South Korea signals ‘phased’ support for US-led Hormuz mission after ship attack
stories.summary: South Korean Defence Minister Ahn Gyu-back said Seoul is reviewing a phased contribution to efforts ensuring safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, signaling support short of direct military participation. He conveyed this position to US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth during talks in Washington.

stories.title: Haiti residents protest after Cite Soleil clashes displace hundreds
stories.summary: Residents of the Cite Soleil neighborhood in Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince protested on Tuesday, demanding government protection after armed clashes over the weekend displaced hundreds of people from their homes.

stories.title: Israeli drone strike hits town in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike hit a town in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military reported that Hezbollah fired several rockets at Israeli forces operating in southern Lebanon, which landed near troops without causing injuries. Warning sirens also sounded in Avivim in the Upper Galilee.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox parties break with Netanyahu but know they have nowhere else to go
stories.summary: Israel's ultra-Orthodox political parties broke with Prime Minister Netanyahu over the military draft law, but analysts say they have no viable coalition alternative. Despite Rabbi Lando's ultimatum, any alliance with the center-left is considered unrealistic as Haredi factions fear losing their voter base.

stories.title: Philippines’ Asean maritime hub pitch meets ‘big red elephant’ South China Sea realities
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. proposed a new Southeast Asian maritime centre at the ASEAN summit, but analysts raised concerns about Manila's South China Sea dispute with Beijing and potential duplication of existing regional bodies.

stories.title: Democratic lawmakers grill FBI’s Kash Patel over report alleging excessive drinking
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers questioned FBI Director Kash Patel during a hearing about an Atlantic report alleging excessive drinking. Patel denied the allegations, calling the report a "total farce."

stories.title: South Africa: Home Affairs Wins Constitutional Court Case Against Repeat Asylum Applications
stories.summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs won a Constitutional Court case against repeat asylum applications. The ruling in Director-General, Department of Home Affairs v Irankunda addressed abuse of the asylum system.

stories.title: Kharkiv hit by Russian strikes, fire reported at infrastructure site
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Shevchenkivskyi and Kholodnohirskyi districts of Kharkiv, causing a fire at an infrastructure facility.

stories.title: US and China begin trade talks in South Korea ahead of Trump visit
stories.summary: Delegations from the United States and China began economic and trade consultations at Incheon International Airport near Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday. The talks preceded President Donald Trump's scheduled meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on Thursday and Friday.

stories.title: Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr kept waiting for Saudi Pro League title by own goal
stories.summary: Al-Nassr's bid to clinch the Saudi Pro League title was denied after goalkeeper Bento scored a bizarre injury-time own goal against Al Hilal. The error turned what would have been a title-sealing 1-0 home victory into a draw.

stories.title: Bahrain-led UN resolution on Strait of Hormuz gains support of 112 nations
stories.summary: A United Nations resolution led by Bahrain calling for free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iranian attacks on Gulf neighbours has gained the support of 112 nations.

stories.title: Experts believe breakthrough in US fentanyl crisis may have started in China
stories.summary: US overdose deaths linked to fentanyl have dropped significantly, though experts attribute the decline to a supply shock involving Chinese-produced precursor chemicals and caution it may be temporary. The issue remains a major point of contention between Washington and Beijing, with the US accusing China of failing to curb precursor sales at a recent UN meeting.

stories.title: China sends embryos into orbit to find out if humans can have babies in space
stories.summary: China launched artificial embryos to its space station to study whether human reproduction is possible in zero gravity. Project leader Yu Leqian said the experiment aims to understand gravity's impact on early development in preparation for potential human settlement beyond Earth.

stories.title: China farmer suffers stroke while selling 4,000kg of apples; hospital staff clear stock in 19 hours
stories.summary: A farmer named Ji Yaozhong from Yangxian county in Shaanxi province, China, suffered a stroke while selling 4,000 kilograms of apples in Xianfeng county, Hubei province. Hospital staff and locals rallied to purchase his entire stock within 19 hours, prompting both counties to establish reciprocal tourism arrangements.

stories.title: French president’s onstage outburst in Kenya overshadows Africa bid
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron faced backlash after interrupting a panel at the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, Kenya, to rebuke audience members for disrupting speakers. The incident overshadowed the summit's goal of showcasing France's renewed engagement policy for the African continent.

stories.title: Rush hour on Air Force one as Melania director Brett Ratner joins Trump China trip
stories.summary: Filmmaker Brett Ratner joined President Donald Trump aboard Air Force One for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Trump is scheduled to hold talks on economic and geopolitical issues including Iran and Taiwan. Major US tech and finance executives, including Apple's Tim Cook and Tesla's Elon Musk, also accompanied the delegation.

stories.title: Wednesday briefing: How much longer can Keir Starmer cling to power?
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a deepening leadership crisis as the Labour party is reportedly split, with speculation mounting over whether he can survive politically. A vote of confidence motion by Health Secretary Wes Streeting provided a temporary lifeline.

stories.title: Iraq denies reports of unknown military sites in Najaf desert
stories.summary: Iraq's Ministry of Defence denied reports of unidentified military installations in the Najaf desert, stating the area remains under full control of Iraqi security forces. The denial followed a field inspection conducted Tuesday after media reports alleged the presence of unknown military bases.

stories.title: Florida plans to close ‘Alligator Alcatraz’ migrant detention centre, New York Times reports
stories.summary: Florida plans to close a migrant detention facility located roughly 60 kilometers west of Miami in a wetland area, according to the New York Times. The site, informally dubbed "Alligator Alcatraz," is situated near habitat home to various reptiles.

stories.title: Florida plans to close 'Alligator Alcatraz' migrant detention center, New York Times reports
stories.summary: Florida plans to close a controversial federal migrant detention center known as "Alligator Alcatraz," according to a New York Times report citing a federal official and three people familiar with the facility's operations.

stories.title: Guy Bradley takes helm as Cathay chairman, Patrick Healy retires after 3 decades
stories.summary: Guy Bradley has succeeded Patrick Healy as chairman of Cathay Pacific Airways and Swire Coca-Cola. Healy is retiring after more than 30 years with the Swire group. Bradley, who also chairs Swire Pacific and Swire Properties, was appointed to the airline and bottling roles in December.

stories.title: Starmer vows to carry on governing ahead of grand parliamentary ceremony
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue governing despite dozens of Labour lawmakers calling for his resignation. Starmer warned that ousting him would lead to chaos and instability ahead of a major parliamentary ceremony.

stories.title: Uganda: No More Time to Sleep - Museveni Sets Tone for Seventh Term After Swearing-in
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni was sworn in for a seventh term and urged citizens to embrace wealth creation and hard work, warning that the country can no longer afford complacency.

stories.title: One Nation senator Malcolm Roberts again fails to rule out Bondi beach terror attack being ‘false flag’
stories.summary: Australian One Nation senator Malcolm Roberts faced criticism after declining to definitively rule out the Bondi beach antisemitic terror attack being a "false flag" during a YouTube interview, though he later called the proposition "absurd" while maintaining he lacked sufficient data.

stories.title: Iranian Vice President Sheena Ansari says Kharg oil spill caused by foreign tanker
stories.summary: Iranian Vice President Sheena Ansari, who heads the Environmental Protection Organisation, said a suspected oil spill near Kharg Island in the Gulf was most likely caused by a non-Iranian tanker discharging contaminated sewage. Ansari stated that monitoring showed no evidence of leaks from Iranian pipelines or oil facilities.

stories.title: Sikorski says only recognition of failed war aims will force Putin to negotiate
stories.summary: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski stated that Russia no longer has the capacity for large-scale escalation or confrontation with NATO. He argued that only Vladimir Putin's recognition that his war objectives against Ukraine have failed will push Russia toward genuine negotiations.

stories.title: Colombia sees worst civilian impact from conflict in a decade, says Red Cross
stories.summary: The International Red Cross Committee reported that the humanitarian impact of Colombia's armed conflict on civilians reached its worst level in a decade in 2025. Increased hostilities and armed groups' disregard for humanitarian law drove the deterioration.

stories.title: Ghana: President Mahama Approves Evacuation of 300 Ghanaians From South Africa
stories.summary: Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama approved the immediate evacuation of 300 Ghanaian nationals from South Africa following renewed xenophobic attacks targeting foreign citizens in the country.

stories.title: Trump says he doesn’t need China’s help to end Iran war, Tehran tightens grip on Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump stated he does not need China's assistance to end the US-Iran war. Meanwhile, Iran has strengthened its control over the Strait of Hormuz and secured deals with Iraq and Pakistan to ship oil and liquefied natural gas from the region.

stories.title: Headwinds ahead for India’s travel sector after Modi calls for foreign holiday restraint
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal to citizens to avoid unnecessary foreign travel is expected to dampen outbound tourism bookings during the peak April-to-June season. The travel industry reports that inflationary pressures had already reduced summer overseas inquiries by up to 15 percent.

stories.title: Trump’s China state visit raises hopes for steadier U.S.-China ties
stories.summary: Business leaders, academics, and international officials expressed hopes that US President Donald Trump's upcoming state visit to China will help stabilize US-China relations. The visit aims to expand cooperation between the world's two largest economies amid growing global uncertainty.

stories.title: China urges Pakistan to intensify Iran-US mediation efforts
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged Pakistan to intensify mediation efforts between the United States and Iran to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz. During a phone call, Pakistani Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar briefed Wang on Islamabad's recent mediation work. Wang praised Pakistan's role in facilitating talks and extending a temporary ceasefire.

stories.title: Nigeria: Over 100 Killed in Zamfara Market Airstrike
stories.summary: A military airstrike hit Tumfa market in Zurmi Local Government Area, Zamfara State, Nigeria, reportedly killing at least 117 people and injuring several others. Residents said the casualties included both bandits and civilians.

stories.title: Two paramedics and soldier among 15 killed in Israeli strikes in Lebanon
stories.summary: Fifteen people, including two paramedics and a Lebanese soldier, were killed and 13 others wounded in 59 Israeli attacks across Lebanon on Tuesday, according to Anadolu Agency. The strikes included air raids and artillery shelling despite a ceasefire declared on 17 April, with 23 raids targeting areas in the Tyre district.

stories.title: Fighting in Sudan’s Blue Nile State displaces thousands
stories.summary: Fighting in Sudan's Blue Nile State has displaced thousands of people. Al Jazeera reported from Al Karama camp in Al-Damazin, where displaced populations have gathered in southeastern Sudan.

stories.title: Chad: Chad's Refugee Crisis Overwhelms Maternity Care in East, UN Agency Warns
stories.summary: The UN reproductive health agency UNFPA warned that a worsening humanitarian crisis in eastern Chad is overwhelming maternity care. Women in refugee areas are giving birth in overcrowded clinics with limited medicine, minimal equipment, and severe anesthesia shortages.

stories.title: US offers $15m reward over information on Iran-linked oil transfers
stories.summary: The US State Department announced a reward of up to $15 million through its Rewards for Justice Program for information on oil shipments connected to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Washington is seeking details on IRGC-linked oil deliveries, the tankers and entities involved, and individuals connected to the transfers.

stories.title: Mexico, CIA reject report of US assassination campaign against cartels
stories.summary: Both the Mexican government and the CIA denied a US media report alleging that the CIA directly participated in lethal operations targeting drug cartels in Mexico.

stories.title: Marine survey spots rare bird and thriving dolphins
stories.summary: The Israel Nature and Parks Authority conducted a two-day marine survey along the Mediterranean coast, the first since 2022. The survey identified a rare bird species and observed thriving dolphin populations.

stories.title: Chelsea flower show garden designers clash over use of AI
stories.summary: Award-winning garden designer Matt Keightley sparked debate at the Chelsea Flower Show by using artificial intelligence to design his exhibit. Fellow horticulturalists expressed alarm over AI's role in automating garden design at the prestigious London event.

stories.title: Canvas reaches deal with hackers to return data, including Hong Kong users
stories.summary: Education platform Canvas, owned by Instructure, reached an agreement with hackers to return data compromised in a global breach affecting approximately 9,000 institutions worldwide, including 72,571 users in Hong Kong. The company announced a webinar to discuss system-hardening measures.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Golden Dome’ missile shield could cost $1.5 trillion over 20 years: Budget office
stories.summary: The Congressional Budget Office, a nonpartisan U.S. body, estimated that President Trump's proposed "Golden Dome" missile defense shield could cost up to $1.5 trillion over 20 years.

stories.title: Argentine city tries to shrug off hantavirus ship ‘patient zero’ suspicions
stories.summary: The Argentine port city of Ushuaia is pushing back against suspicions that it was the source of a hantavirus outbreak that killed three passengers aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, which departed the Patagonian port on April 1.

stories.title: Oil prices fall as markets watch Iran ceasefire and China talks
stories.summary: Oil prices fell on Wednesday after three consecutive days of gains as investors monitored the fragile ceasefire involving Iran, the US, and Israel alongside President Trump's visit to China. Brent crude dropped 0.76 percent to $106.95 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate fell 0.65 percent to $101.52.

stories.title: Ethiopia: French Companies Expand Presence in Ethiopia, Despite Security Concerns
stories.summary: French companies are expanding operations in Ethiopia, drawn by a market of over 120 million people, despite ongoing security concerns. The trend was highlighted at the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, reflecting France's efforts to reposition itself on the African continent.

stories.title: Putin hails Russia’s test launch of ‘most powerful missile in the world’
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the test launch of the Sarmat intercontinental ballistic missile, describing it as the most powerful missile in the world. Putin said the nuclear-capable weapon is expected to enter combat service by the end of the year.

stories.title: Canada signs Convention establishing International Claims Commission for Ukraine
stories.summary: Canada became the first country outside Europe to sign the Convention establishing an International Claims Commission for Ukraine. The commission is intended to address claims arising from the conflict in Ukraine.

stories.title: At Abraham Foxman’s funeral, an elegy for the last generation with direct ties to the Holocaust
stories.summary: Abraham Foxman, who led the Anti-Defamation League for nearly 30 years and served in its leadership for two decades prior, was eulogized at his funeral. Speakers reflected on him as part of the last generation with direct personal ties to the Holocaust.

stories.title: ‘Heavy’ hearts as residents of Wang Fuk Court’s only spared block return again
stories.summary: Residents of the sole surviving block of Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong's Tai Po district returned to collect belongings following a November 26 fire that destroyed seven of eight blocks, killed 168 people, and displaced nearly all occupants. Homeowners expressed uncertainty about the government's voluntary buy-back scheme.

stories.title: NSW police to drop charges against Isaac Herzog protesters laid using unlawful public assembly restrictions
stories.summary: New South Wales police confirmed they would drop charges against protesters who demonstrated against Israeli President Isaac Herzog at Sydney Town Hall, after the public assembly restrictions used to lay the charges were found to be unlawful. Approximately 30 people had been charged.

stories.title: Kuwait accuses Iran of trying to infiltrate its territory
stories.summary: Kuwait accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of attempting to infiltrate its territory, reporting that Iranian personnel exchanged fire with Kuwaiti soldiers on Bubiyan Island.

stories.title: India’s Role in a Disordered World
stories.summary: An analysis highlights India's diplomatic role amid increasing global instability. The piece argues that high-quality diplomacy from New Delhi is more critical than ever as the international order faces growing disorder.

stories.title: Chinese company that tracked US bombers over Iran wears sanctions with pride
stories.summary: Chinese satellite imagery firm MizarVision, which gained prominence for tracking US military movements during the US-Israel war on Iran, was added to the US sanctions list. The Hangzhou-based company is treating the designation as a badge of honor in its recruitment efforts.

stories.title: ‘It’s a failed nation’: Trump pressures Cuba as fuel crisis deepens
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump called Cuba a "failed nation" as his administration intensified its pressure campaign against the island amid a deepening fuel crisis.

stories.title: Hong Kong halves tunnel tolls for commercial vehicles amid surging fuel prices
stories.summary: Hong Kong announced a two-month, 50 percent toll discount for commercial vehicles using public tunnels starting Sunday, aiming to ease business costs amid surging fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict. Private cars and motorcycles are excluded from the measure.

stories.title: Cannes-winning writer claims actors ‘blacklisted’ for opposing Israel amid Gaza war
stories.summary: Cannes-winning screenwriter Paul Laverty alleged that Hollywood actors including Susan Sarandon, Javier Bardem, and Mark Ruffalo have been blacklisted by studios for opposing Israel's actions during the Gaza war.

stories.title: Cosmic order, political authority: the messaging in temple setting for Trump’s China visit
stories.summary: As President Trump prepares for his visit to Beijing — the first by a US president in nearly nine years — attention has focused on the symbolic significance of the historic venues China has chosen for the reception, continuing a tradition of carefully staged diplomatic settings in US-China summits.

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon as 380 reported killed since April 17 ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel intensified strikes on southern Lebanon on Tuesday, with Beirut reporting 380 people killed since an April 17 ceasefire took effect. Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem vowed to turn the battlefield into "hell" for Israeli forces and rejected US calls for the group's disarmament ahead of Washington-hosted talks.

stories.title: China-US trade talks kick off in Seoul ahead of high-profile leaders’ summit
stories.summary: Senior Chinese and US trade officials, led by Vice-Premier He Lifeng and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, began a seventh round of trade negotiations in Seoul, South Korea, ahead of President Trump's arrival in Beijing. Both officials met South Korean President Lee Jae Myung beforehand.

stories.title: Islamic State claims deadly attack on Syrian government forces
stories.summary: Syria's state news agency SANA reported that two Syrian army soldiers were killed and others wounded in an attack on a bus in the Hasakah countryside. The Islamic State claimed responsibility for the assault on government forces.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi sanctions 21 people and groups over Hezbollah links, state media reports
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates designated 16 Lebanese nationals and five Lebanon-based entities as terrorists over alleged links to Hezbollah. UAE authorities ordered regulatory bodies to identify connected individuals and companies and freeze related assets within 24 hours.

stories.title: UK pledges warship and fighter jets for Hormuz mission
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced it would deploy military assets to a multinational mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz, including the warship HMS Dragon, Eurofighter Typhoon jets, drones, and an autonomous mine-hunting system. Britain also allocated £115 million in new funding for mine-hunting drones and counter-drone systems.

stories.title: Iran’s Guards hold military drills in capital as ceasefire teeters
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps conducted military drills in Tehran as the ceasefire with the United States appeared increasingly fragile. The exercises aimed to boost combat readiness after President Trump warned the truce was on the brink of collapse.

stories.title: Australia backs UK-France led mission in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles announced that Australia will join a UK- and France-led multinational naval mission to protect freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Australia will contribute a Boeing E-7 Wedgetail surveillance aircraft. The announcement followed talks with defence officials from more than 40 countries.

stories.title: The Trump-Xi summit in Beijing turns on five fronts: Iran, Taiwan, tariffs, rare earths, and AI
stories.summary: The Trump-Xi summit in Beijing is focused on five key issues: the US war with Iran, Taiwan, bilateral tariffs, Chinese rare earth exports, and an initial framework for managing AI risks. It marks the first visit by a US president to China's capital in nearly nine years.

stories.title: UN resolution on Hormuz gains backing from 112 countries
stories.summary: A draft UN resolution calling for the protection of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz has gained support from 112 member states, nearly two-thirds of the 193-member body. Backers reportedly include India, Japan, South Korea, most European countries, and Gulf states.

stories.title: Vietnam asks US to allow ‘extremely important’ oil tanker to slip past Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Vietnam's state oil company urged the United States to allow a supertanker carrying 1.99 million barrels of Iraqi crude to pass through a US naval blockade near the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel, Agios Fanourios I, performed a U-turn at the blockade line after clearing the strait.

stories.title: What Hong Kong’s planned ride-hailing regime could mean for your next Uber trip
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities have begun detailing regulations for ride-hailing platforms including Uber, Tada, and Didi Chuxing, following passage of the city's first legal framework for the sector in October. Enforcement powers, penalties, and licensing arrangements have been outlined, though vehicle caps remain unresolved.

stories.title: China and US agree on opposing Hormuz tolls, State Department says
stories.summary: Senior U.S. and Chinese officials agreed that no country should be permitted to exact shipping tolls in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the State Department. The shared stance signals an effort to find common ground on pressuring Iran to relinquish control of the vital waterway.

stories.title: Belgium refuses to renew passport of Israeli citizen living in Jerusalem area beyond Green Line
stories.summary: Belgium's consulate refused to renew the passport of Annabelle Herciger-Tenzer, a Belgian-Israeli citizen who has lived in Pisgat Zeev, a Jerusalem neighborhood beyond the Green Line, since immigrating to Israel in 1980.

stories.title: Forest fire raging for more than week localized in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: A large-scale forest fire that started on May 5 in the Koriukivka forestry district of Ukraine's Chernihiv region has been localized after burning for more than a week.

stories.title: France says 11 more countries back limiting vetoes at UN Security Council
stories.summary: France announced that 11 additional countries have backed a proposal to limit the use of vetoes at the UN Security Council. The council has been largely paralyzed by vetoes, particularly from Russia and the United States.

stories.title: Trump says he doesn’t need Xi’s help on Iran
stories.summary: President Trump said he plans to discuss the war in Iran extensively with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his upcoming trip to China. However, Trump stated he does not believe he needs Xi's assistance on the matter.

stories.title: South Korea weighs phased role in Hormuz mission after US talks, defense minister says
stories.summary: South Korean Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back said Seoul is considering a phased role in the multinational Strait of Hormuz mission. Ahn conveyed South Korea's position during a meeting with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on Monday.

stories.title: Qatar and Saudi Arabia discuss Iran-US ceasefire efforts
stories.summary: Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud held a phone call to discuss US-Iran ceasefire efforts and regional stability. Qatar's Foreign Ministry said the talks focused on reducing tensions in the region.

stories.title: Iran says conflict will define ‘good and evil’ for future generations
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei issued a statement characterizing the conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran as a generational struggle over "good and evil." He accused Israel and the US of fabricating justifications for violence while portraying Iran as defending its sovereignty.

stories.title: US prepared to handle Iran ‘by any means necessary,’ Trump says
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he expected to discuss Iran and the Strait of Hormuz crisis with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his visit to Beijing. Trump stated the US had the Iran situation "very much under control" and that trade would remain the primary focus of the summit.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia launched covert attacks on Iran as regional war widened, sources say
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia conducted covert attacks against Iran as the regional war expanded, according to unnamed sources. The operations reflect Riyadh's increasingly assertive posture in defending itself against its primary regional rival.

stories.title: Iraq, Pakistan strike energy deals with Iran as Tehran flexes Hormuz control
stories.summary: Iraq and Pakistan have struck energy deals with Iran to ship oil and liquefied natural gas through the Persian Gulf, according to five sources. The agreements demonstrate Tehran's ability to leverage its control over the Strait of Hormuz to manage regional energy flows.

stories.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang joins Trump’s trip to China at last minute
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined US President Donald Trump aboard Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska en route to China. Nvidia confirmed Huang was attending at Trump's invitation to support US administration goals during the summit.

stories.title: Trump embarks on visit to China, focus on trade
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump traveled to China for talks with President Xi Jinping, with trade as the primary focus. Trump sought to downplay differences over Iran and the conflict's impact on global oil markets.

stories.title: How ByteDance plans to turn OpenClaw craze into a profitable AI business
stories.summary: ByteDance's cloud unit Volcano Engine is developing AI business applications through its ArkClaw tool, built on the open-source OpenClaw platform. The company is betting on cheaper tokens, higher inference efficiency, and longer context windows as the next phase of AI development.

stories.title: Russia tests long-range missile after US nuclear treaty expires
stories.summary: Russia conducted a test of a long-range missile following the expiration of a nuclear arms treaty with the United States in February. The lapsed agreement had placed limits on the atomic arsenals of both countries.

stories.title: Iran retains access to majority of missile launch sites, US intelligence shows - report
stories.summary: US intelligence assessments indicate Iran retains access to a majority of its missile launch sites. According to The New York Times, Iran can also utilize stockpiles from non-operational sites by transferring them via mobile launchers.

stories.title: Brazil’s Lula launches anti-organised crime plan amid rising security pressure before elections
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched a new anti-organized crime plan aimed at ending criminal territorial control, five months before elections. Lula said security cooperation was also discussed during his recent meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: In the Łódź Ghetto, Jews defied Nazis through art. Now it is exhibited in Jerusalem
stories.summary: A new exhibition at Yad Vashem in Jerusalem displays artwork created by Jewish residents of the Łódź Ghetto in Poland during World War II. The ghetto held approximately 164,000 Jews who were subjected to forced labor under the Nazi regime.

stories.title: FBI Director Kash Patel fires back at drinking allegations
stories.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel and Senator Chris Van Hollen clashed during a Senate budget hearing, with the exchange centering on allegations about Patel's drinking habits.

stories.title: Partisans report Russia moving military warehouses deep into rear areas
stories.summary: The Atesh partisan movement reported that Russian forces are relocating warehouses storing FPV drones and ammunition further from the front lines. The shift indicates a significant change in Russian logistics strategy in response to battlefield conditions.

stories.title: US budget watchdog estimates Golden Dome will cost $1.2 trillion, dwarfing Pentagon estimate
stories.summary: The US Congressional Budget Office estimated that President Trump's proposed Golden Dome missile defense system would cost approximately $1.2 trillion, far exceeding Pentagon estimates. Acquisition costs alone were projected at over $1 trillion, including a space-based interceptor layer and a constellation of 7,800 satellites.

stories.title: UK to send drones, jets and warship to join defensive mission securing Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Britain announced it will deploy autonomous mine-hunting equipment, Typhoon fighter jets, and the warship HMS Dragon to a multinational mission aimed at protecting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Baltimore ship crash: U.S. slaps criminal cases against Singapore, Chennai firms and Indian national
stories.summary: U.S. federal authorities filed criminal charges against Singapore- and Chennai-based firms and an Indian national in connection with the Baltimore ship crash. Charges include conspiracy, obstruction, failure to report a hazardous condition to the U.S. Coast Guard, and making false statements.

stories.title: Singaporeans refute lack of hunger stereotype, warn of ‘self-fulfilling bias’ over jobs
stories.summary: Singaporean workers are pushing back against stereotypes about local employees lacking drive, warning that such perceptions create a self-fulfilling bias in the job market. Some professionals report difficulty finding permanent roles as companies increasingly rely on contract workers and overseas hires.

stories.title: US’ scientific self-harm will only help China
stories.summary: The article argues that cuts to US scientific research and institutions will undermine American competitiveness and ultimately benefit China's scientific advancement. It traces the history of US government-funded science from the Lewis and Clark expedition onward.

stories.title: Former Anti-Corruption Foundation director denies ex-deputy prime minister’s allegations, defends Navalny’s return to Russia
stories.summary: Vladimir Ashurkov, former executive director of Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, gave a three-hour interview to journalist Yury Dud. Ashurkov addressed scandals surrounding the foundation, including allegations about oligarch funding, and defended Navalny's decision to return to Russia.

stories.title: Less than two years after landslide, unloved Starmer battles to save his job
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is facing a serious challenge to his leadership less than two years after Labour's landslide election victory. Critics say his pragmatic but ideologically vague approach has eroded political support and left him fighting for survival.

stories.title: Senate Democrats seek seventh vote to curb Trump's war powers
stories.summary: US Senator Chuck Schumer urged Republicans to support a War Powers Resolution to end President Trump's military campaign against Iran, arguing the conflict was pushing US petrol prices above $4.50 a gallon. This marks Democrats' seventh attempt to pass the resolution to curb presidential war powers.

stories.title: Yemen says Iran using cross-border militias for blackmail, exporting chaos
stories.summary: Yemen condemned Iran for what it described as hostile acts on Kuwait's Bubiyan Island carried out by an armed group affiliated with Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps. Yemeni officials accused Iran of exporting chaos and using cross-border militias to threaten regional security.

stories.title: Russia’s happiness index falls to 15-year low in April, state pollster reports
stories.summary: Russia's happiness index, measured by the state pollster VTsIOM, dropped to 52 points in April 2026, its lowest level in 15 years.

stories.title: How Australia’s mining giants are helping China to globalise the yuan
stories.summary: Major Australian mining companies are increasingly using the Chinese yuan for financing and trade settlements, aiding China's efforts to internationalize its currency. China has leveraged its dominance as the world's largest iron ore buyer to encourage the shift away from US dollar transactions.

stories.title: China actor who stopped growing at 9 faces mockery over wedding photos called ‘mother and son’
stories.summary: Chinese actor Hou Xiang, 40, whose growth stopped around age nine due to a childhood condition linked to premature birth, has faced public mockery over wedding photos. Despite the ridicule, he has earned recognition for his acting performances.

stories.title: Iran said to retain access to 30 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Reports indicate Iran retains access to approximately 30 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Australia announced it would join a naval mission in the strait led by France and the UK, and Lebanon reported 13 people killed by Israeli strikes in its south on Tuesday.

stories.title: ‘I’m afraid if she gets out’: US author’s sons say they want mother to stay in jail
stories.summary: The three sons of Utah author Kouri Richins said they would feel unsafe if their mother were released from prison. Richins, 35, was convicted in March on five felony counts including aggravated murder for killing their father and faces several decades to life at her sentencing hearing.

stories.title: Norway and Iran discuss latest round of negotiations in Tehran
stories.summary: Norway's Deputy Foreign Minister Andreas Mutzfelt Kravik met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran to discuss the latest round of negotiations related to the US-Israeli conflict. Iran criticized what it called the provocative rhetoric and lack of goodwill from the American side.

stories.title: Kremlin intensifying work with Russians abroad to conduct hybrid operations – CCD
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry announced plans to intensify engagement with Russian nationals living abroad. Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation warned the Kremlin is using these "compatriot" networks to conduct hybrid operations against Western countries.

stories.title: Hezbollah planning to occupy Beirut as pressure on Naim Qassem builds
stories.summary: Hezbollah is reportedly planning to occupy Beirut amid growing internal pressure on its leader Naim Qassem. Israeli security sources say Hezbollah believes Israel is plotting to divide Lebanon, potentially causing the Lebanese state to lose large areas of territory.

stories.title: Hong Kong teens dive deep to safeguard global shipping lanes
stories.summary: A team of Grade 8 students from the Canadian International School of Hong Kong won multiple awards at the Conrad Challenge Global Innovation Summit in Houston, including the Power Pitch Award. Their project addressed the safeguarding of global shipping lanes.

stories.title: Starmer at risk because he pushed Labour to be ‘new Conservative Party’
stories.summary: Author Oliver Eagleton argues that British Prime Minister Keir Starmer's political position is under threat because he steered the Labour Party toward policies resembling those of the Conservative Party.

stories.title: Hong Kong to launch public consultation on 5-year blueprint ‘by early June’
stories.summary: Hong Kong is expected to launch a public consultation by early June on its first five-year development plan aligned with the national blueprint. Chief Executive John Lee will present a preliminary framework and gather feedback from various industries.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia and UAE coordinate on regional security efforts
stories.summary: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan held a phone call to discuss regional developments and security cooperation. The conversation took place amid heightened regional tensions and ongoing conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Trump says US will ‘finish the job’ against Iran, ‘peacefully or otherwise’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared the US would "finish the job" against Iran "peacefully or otherwise" as he departed for China. Iran's government remained defiant, insisting the US must accept its demands.

stories.title: Middle East live: Trump says stopping Iran's nuclear program outweighs Americans' economic pain
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon is his top priority and outweighs concerns about Americans' financial struggles. He made the remarks as the U.S. continues efforts to negotiate an end to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it repelled Israeli advance near Wadi al-Ain
stories.summary: Hezbollah reported carrying out 25 strikes against Israeli forces and military equipment across southern Lebanon on Tuesday. The group claimed it repelled an advancing Israeli column near Wadi al-Ain and al-Bayyadah using guided missiles and heavy artillery.

stories.title: US EIA concedes Middle East supply disruptions are far worse than prior estimates
stories.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration significantly revised its forecasts to reflect larger and longer-lasting disruptions to global oil supplies from the Iran war than previously estimated. The revision highlights the uncertainty that has affected energy markets since the conflict began three months ago.

stories.title: Southeast Asia warned of ‘Godzilla El Nino’ whiplash threatening drought, floods, haze
stories.summary: Experts warned that Southeast Asia faces a potentially severe El Niño event that could bring drought, flash floods, crop losses, and haze across the region. The climate threat compounds existing economic pressures from geopolitical tensions and rising energy costs.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump travels to China as conflict with Tehran looms large
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli attacks on Lebanon have killed 2,883 people and injured 8,787 since March 2. The developments come amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Louisiana police to pay $4.85m to daughter of Black motorist who died at officers’ hands in 2019
stories.summary: Louisiana State Police and a local sheriff's office agreed to pay $4.85 million to the daughter of Ronald Greene, a Black motorist who died during a 2019 arrest after being shocked, punched, and dragged.
