stories.summary: A decomposed body found near an abandoned vehicle roughly 50 km from Lake Cargelligo in New South Wales is believed to be Julian Ingram, 37. He was the subject of a large-scale manhunt since January after allegedly shooting and killing his pregnant former partner Sophie Quinn, her boyfriend, and her aunt.

stories.title: The Global Sumud Flotilla is sailing on, here is why
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla announced it would continue its maritime mission after part of the flotilla was attacked by Israeli forces. Organizers said the incident reinforced their determination to proceed.

stories.title: PM Starmer’s dreadful Monday: will a speech overcome the greatest challenge to his political future
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced the greatest threat to his premiership on Monday, delivering a speech promising bolder action on major challenges. He sought to persuade Labour MPs not to replace him as party leader following poor election results.

stories.title: War update: 180 combat engagements over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military recorded 180 combat engagements with Russian forces along the frontline on May 10. The clashes occurred across multiple sectors as fighting continues throughout eastern and southern Ukraine.

stories.title: Malaysia’s fuel subsidy headache leaves Anwar ‘scrambling for solution’
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim faces a politically difficult decision on how to reform fuel subsidies by defining income thresholds for eligibility. The Middle East energy shock has strained government finances, forcing authorities to balance fiscal discipline against the risk of angering middle-class voters.

stories.title: Trump says Iran truce on 'life support', rejects peace proposal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump called Tehran's peace proposal 'totally unacceptable' while Israel intensified its bombing campaign in Lebanon despite a ceasefire. Trump characterized the truce between the U.S. and Iran as being on 'life support.'

stories.title: US-Iran talks stall after Trump, Tehran trade rejections
stories.summary: US-Iran peace negotiations stalled after President Trump rejected Tehran's proposal as "totally unacceptable." Meanwhile, Israel intensified its bombing campaign in Lebanon despite an existing truce.

stories.title: Returns on multipolarity
stories.summary: An analysis argues that global politics is shifting toward multipolarity, with the US experiencing declining ability and willingness to project power, as evidenced by challenges in Eastern Europe and the Persian Gulf, driven by internal structural pressures.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s property recovery could be more robust than many think
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings reported that Hong Kong's property market may experience a stronger-than-expected recovery, citing competitive bids at recent residential land auctions. S&P noted Hong Kong has become the first major city in China whose property market has bottomed, potentially attracting mainland developers.

stories.title: Is the UN irrelevant?
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues the UN is both relevant and irrelevant: it has failed to address the Middle East crisis triggered by the US-Israeli attack on Iran, yet continues to play vital roles in humanitarian assistance, including aid to Palestinians in Gaza.

stories.title: Israel faces Hezbollah’s attrition trap on the Lebanese border - opinion
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem stated that the organization is returning to guerrilla warfare tactics against the Israeli Defense Forces along the Lebanese border. An opinion piece argues that Israel faces an attrition trap set by Hezbollah in the area.

stories.title: In Malaysia, ex-Proton CEO’s self-reliance sermon spurs backlash: ‘spare us’
stories.summary: Former Proton CEO Syed Zainal Abidin Syed Tahir faced online backlash after calling on Malays to abandon a "mentality of waiting for aid" at a dialogue founded by Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Social media users pointed to Proton's own long history of government support.

stories.title: Britain, France to host multinational meeting on mission to escort ships through Hormuz
stories.summary: Britain and France will host a multinational meeting to discuss a naval escort mission for commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Organizers indicated the mission would only commence once a sustained ceasefire or peace deal in the region is reached.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda Faces Critical Shortage of Specialist Doctors - Aceng
stories.summary: Ugandan Health Minister Jane Ruth Aceng warned of a critical shortage of specialist doctors in the country, saying the gap is straining Uganda's capacity to deliver advanced and specialized healthcare services.

stories.title: Art looted from Jewish collector hanging in home of Dutch SS leader’s family, sleuth says
stories.summary: A researcher discovered that a painting looted from a Jewish collector during World War II, "Portrait of a Young Girl" by Toon Kelder, has been displayed in the home of a Dutch SS leader's descendants. The theft has passed the statute of limitations.

stories.title: One dead, three injured in Ramle shooting, police rule incident as criminal
stories.summary: One person was killed and three others were injured in a shooting incident in Ramle, Israel. Israeli police classified the incident as criminal in nature, reporting that the shooter opened fire near a local market after the victim attempted to flee from the shooter's home.

stories.title: Russia loses 920 troops, 76 artillery systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military estimated that Russia lost 920 troops and 76 artillery systems in the past 24 hours. Total estimated Russian combat losses since the February 2022 full-scale invasion have reached approximately 1,342,030 personnel as of May 11, 2026.

stories.title: Weather tracker: US and Mexico brace for heatwave as deadly floods hit South Africa
stories.summary: A severe heatwave is expected across western parts of the United States and Mexico, with temperatures forecast 10–15°C above average in some areas. The U.S. National Weather Service issued heat advisories for California and Arizona, while deadly floods struck South Africa's Western and Northern Cape.

stories.title: Iran war day 73: Trump and Tehran clash over latest peace proposals
stories.summary: On day 73 of the US-Iran war, negotiations remained deadlocked as President Trump rejected Tehran's latest peace proposal as "totally unacceptable." Brent crude prices rose amid the continuing impasse.

stories.title: Situationer: Punjab set to launch land-lease scheme amid concerns
stories.summary: Punjab's Board of Revenue is preparing to launch the Apna Khet, Apna Rozgar (AKAR) land-leasing scheme, initially covering 124,363 acres of state land. The initiative uses GIS-based mapping to allocate unused land to landless farmers for cultivation.

stories.title: Trump rejects Iran peace offer, raising fears of escalation
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, delivered via Pakistani mediators, calling it "totally unacceptable" in a social media post. The rejection raised fears of further escalation in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Six people found dead in boxcar in Laredo, Texas, police say
stories.summary: Police in Laredo, Texas, reported that six bodies were discovered inside a train boxcar on Sunday, May 10. Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the deaths.

stories.title: Ex-Israeli PM: Hezbollah is the enemy of Lebanon and must be disarmed
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert called for the disarmament of Hezbollah, describing the group as an enemy of Lebanon. He spoke about the 2006 war, Lebanon's situation, and the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Spain’s Nico Williams sustains hamstring injury before World Cup
stories.summary: Spain's Nico Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Athletic Bilbao's 1-0 loss to Valencia, leaving the pitch before half-time. The injury raises concerns about his availability for the upcoming World Cup.

stories.title: Imran says ‘army is mine, country is mine’: PTI
stories.summary: Pakistan's PTI party marked the first anniversary of what it calls the 'Marka-i-Haq' military response to Indian aggression, claiming that jailed founder Imran Khan sent a message from Adiala jail stating 'the army is mine, and the country is mine.'

stories.title: Tankers reportedly disable trackers to avoid attacks in Hormuz
stories.summary: Three oil tankers carrying crude passed through the Strait of Hormuz with tracking systems disabled to avoid potential Iranian attacks, according to Reuters citing Kpler and LSEG shipping data. Two very large crude carriers, the Agios Fanourios I and Kiara M, each carried about 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude.

stories.title: Netanyahu wants to wean Israel off US military support, he tells CBS news network
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told CBS News that he wants to reduce Israel's dependence on US military support. Israel currently receives approximately S$4.8 billion in US military aid annually.

stories.title: Ukrainian officer: Russian frontline assaults now rare as 60-70% of infiltrators die before reaching Ukrainian lines
stories.summary: A Ukrainian senior lieutenant reported on Telegram that Russian frontline assault operations have become rare, with 60–70% of infiltrators dying before reaching Ukrainian positions. Small-group infiltration has become Russia's main remaining tactic.

stories.title: US Senate expected to confirm Kevin Warsh as next Federal Reserve chair
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate is expected to confirm Kevin Warsh as the next chair of the Federal Reserve, succeeding Jerome Powell. The confirmation comes as President Donald Trump continues efforts to influence the central bank during a turbulent economic period.

stories.title: Why China’s new duty-free access is a lifeline for South African exporters
stories.summary: China began granting zero-tariff access to South African exports from May 1, removing the 10% tariff on apples. The first shipments cleared included 24 tonnes of apples through Shenzhen Bay port and 6,000 bottles of wine processed in Hunan province, providing a lifeline for South African exporters seeking market diversification.

stories.title: Plan to make 5G handsets ‘affordable’ hits roadblock
stories.summary: A Pakistani government proposal to make 5G-enabled smartphones available on instalment plans has stalled, with authorities still awaiting responses from industry stakeholders following the country's 5G spectrum auction held in March.

stories.title: Russians strike Zaporizhzhia region 785 times in one day, leaving one killed, two injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 785 strikes on 36 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over one day. One person was killed and two others were injured in attacks on the Zaporizhzhia district.

stories.title: No butts: case dismissed after Woolworths worker claims hurt feelings over plumber’s crack
stories.summary: Australia's Fair Work Commission dismissed a former Woolworths employee's unfair dismissal claim filed after he was told to cover up exposed clothing. Deputy President Alan Colman rejected the case, warning there is no disincentive for speculative claims.

stories.title: Foreign economic assistance inflows rise nearly 20pc
stories.summary: Foreign economic assistance inflows to Pakistan rose nearly 20 percent to $6.594 billion during July-March of the current fiscal year, driven largely by IMF programme support, compared to $5.507 billion in the same period last year.

stories.title: Africa Forward Summit: France seeks fresh start with Africa
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron began a visit to Kenya ahead of the Africa Forward Summit, an event designed to reframe France's relationship with Africa as a partnership of equals rather than one shaped by its colonial past.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Diplomatic prospects between Washington and Tehran have dimmed after President Trump called Iran's latest response to the US peace proposal "totally unacceptable." Meanwhile, Israeli strikes in Lebanon are intensifying, oil prices are rising, and concerns grow over shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US widens drive to revoke citizenship of foreign-born Americans
stories.summary: The Trump administration's Justice Department has expanded denaturalisation proceedings against roughly a dozen naturalised US citizens, including an Indian businessman, over allegations of fraud, terrorism links, and financial crimes. Civil liberties groups have raised concerns.

stories.title: Gaza filmmakers slam BBC after shelved documentary wins Bafta
stories.summary: A documentary about Gaza filmmakers, previously shelved by the BBC, won a BAFTA award. Journalist and presenter Ramita Navai accepted the award and condemned censorship and silencing of the film's creators.

stories.title: If Starmer is serious about stamping out antisemitism, he must end Britain's blind support for Israel
stories.summary: A commentary argues that UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer should reassess Britain's relationship with Israel, contending that Israeli government actions are contributing to risks for Jewish communities in Britain.

stories.title: Taiwan confident in US ties, hopes Trump-Xi summit brings no ‘surprises’
stories.summary: Taiwan expressed confidence in its relationship with the United States ahead of a planned summit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Taipei voiced hope that the meeting would not produce any unexpected developments affecting Taiwan's interests.

stories.title: Temperatures up to +22°C, rain expected across Ukraine on Monday
stories.summary: Forecasters predicted cloudy weather with clear spells across Ukraine on Monday, May 11, with temperatures reaching up to 22°C and rain expected in most regions, along with thunderstorms in some areas.

stories.title: Temperatures up to +22°C, rain expected across Ukraine on Monday
stories.summary: Cloudy weather with intermittent rain and temperatures reaching up to 22°C was forecast across Ukraine on Monday, May 11. Thunderstorms were expected in some areas.

stories.title: Malawi: Cost of Living Crisis Deepens As Household Expenses Jump 8 Percent in One Month
stories.summary: Malawian households saw expenses surge by more than 8 percent in April alone, driven by rising fuel prices and a weakening economy, deepening the country's cost of living crisis.

stories.title: Far-right provocateurs hurl homophobic abuse at gay secularist activist in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: A far-right group led by government-aligned activist Mordechai David targeted gay secularist activist Naor Narkis and his partner in Tel Aviv with homophobic slurs and abuse.

stories.title: Iran executes man accused of spying for CIA and Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed Erfan Shakourzadeh, a man accused of spying for the CIA and Israel's Mossad. According to Iranian state-linked media, Shakourzadeh worked at a scientific organization involved in satellite activities and allegedly transferred classified information to foreign intelligence services.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump rejects Iran’s peace proposal as 'totally unacceptable'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal as "totally unacceptable" after receiving it on May 10. The proposal had raised hopes for a potential breakthrough to end the ongoing Iran-Israel war.

stories.title: Ankara’s Crossroads: Rearmament, Risk, and the Prospect of War with Israel
stories.summary: Speculation about a potential military clash between Israel and Turkey has intensified over the past year, driven by disputes over Syria, the Palestinian territories, and regional security. In December 2025, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu indirectly accused Ankara of seeking to reestablish Ottoman imperial influence over the Levant. Turkish rearmament efforts have added to tensions.

stories.title: Cotton stocks at ‘lowest ebb’ ahead of ginning season
stories.summary: Pakistan's cotton stocks have reportedly dropped below 10,000 bales ahead of the new ginning season, an unprecedented low attributed partly to the closure of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border blocking approximately 500,000 bales. Some textile mills may face partial shutdowns.

stories.title: Philippine parliament start vote on Sara Duterte’s impeachment bid
stories.summary: Philippine lawmakers began voting on the impeachment of Vice President Sara Duterte-Carpio, which could create a major obstacle to her 2028 presidential bid. A House justice committee had previously found probable cause based on accusations of misusing public funds and threatening President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife.

stories.title: Iran says US has not issued World Cup visas for players
stories.summary: The Iran Football Federation said the United States has not yet issued entry visas to Iran's national football team ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Federation president Mehdi Taj said the process was taking an unusually long time and that he planned to seek resolution during a training camp in Türkiye.

stories.title: Kharkiv region hands over batch of pickup trucks to two combat brigades
stories.summary: The Kharkiv regional administration delivered a batch of pickup trucks to soldiers of the 92nd Assault Brigade and the 57th Separate Motorized Infantry Brigade of Ukraine's Armed Forces. The vehicles are intended to support combat operations.

stories.title: IDF reservist killed in Hezbollah explosive drone attack in northern Israel
stories.summary: IDF reservist Alexander Glovanyov, 47, was killed in a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in northern Israel. Three additional troops were lightly injured in a separate drone attack in southern Lebanon. The IDF is also investigating a strike that killed a man and his 12-year-old daughter.

stories.title: Conflict, CASEVAC, and the Golden Hour in the Age of Persistent Surveillance
stories.summary: An analysis challenges Western battlefield casualty evacuation doctrine, which is built on assumptions from the Global War on Terror era. The central premise—that wounded soldiers can be moved to higher levels of medical care within the 'golden hour'—faces serious obstacles in modern conflicts characterized by persistent surveillance and contested airspace.

stories.title: New ‘Nakba’ in Jerusalem: Israel steps up Silwan demolitions near Al-Aqsa
stories.summary: Israel has accelerated home demolitions in the Silwan neighbourhood of occupied East Jerusalem near Al-Aqsa Mosque. Palestinians say at least 50 homes have been demolished since October 2023, with Israel accused of using wartime conditions to expand settler-linked projects and expel residents.

stories.title: UK’s Keir Starmer battles for political survival after election defeat
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer delivered a speech pledging to confront major challenges as he fights for political survival following electoral losses to the Reform and Green parties.

stories.title: ‘It was either this or the pool’: hantavirus ship becomes latest Tenerife tourist attraction
stories.summary: The MV Hondius, the cruise ship struck by a hantavirus outbreak that has killed three people, anchored near Tenerife's Granadillo commercial port after reaching the Canary Islands on Sunday. The ship has become a tourist attraction, drawing locals and visitors who gather on nearby hills to view the vessel.

stories.title: Brent crude climbs above $105 after Trump rejects Iran response
stories.summary: Brent crude futures rose above $105 per barrel after President Trump rejected Iran's response to the US peace proposal. West Texas Intermediate crude also climbed sharply, driven by fears of further conflict disrupting energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: China ranks third in global index for AI competitiveness in life sciences
stories.summary: China ranked third globally in a new AI competitiveness index for life sciences, behind only the United States and the United Kingdom. The index, released by Deep Knowledge Group, measured competitiveness in applying AI to biotechnology, healthcare, drug discovery, and diagnostics.

stories.title: Iran two-tier internet cuts citizens off as elites stay online
stories.summary: Iran has imposed a nationwide internet blackout during its conflict with the US and Israel, leaving millions of ordinary citizens unable to communicate, work, or access information. Reports indicate a two-tier system in which government elites retain online access while the general population is cut off.

stories.title: The Weeknd reveals dates for Hong Kong concerts at Kai Tak Stadium
stories.summary: Canadian singer-songwriter The Weeknd announced two concerts at Hong Kong's Kai Tak Stadium in October as part of the final leg of his "After Hours Til Dawn" world tour. K-pop group Babymonster also revealed a January performance at Hong Kong's AsiaWorld-Arena.

stories.title: Russian strike in Zaporizhzhia region leave one injured, houses damaged
stories.summary: A woman was injured and residential buildings were damaged in a Russian strike on the Zaporizhzhia district in southeastern Ukraine. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure in the region.

stories.title: Calls for 20,500 ride-hailing permits to keep 15,000 cars on Hong Kong roads daily
stories.summary: Hong Kong lawmakers and experts are calling for approximately 20,500 ride-hailing permits to be issued in the first phase of platform regulation, arguing that at least 15,000 active vehicles daily are needed to meet demand and avoid transport shortages.

stories.title: US schools face a crisis as the number of children drops
stories.summary: US schools are facing a growing crisis as declining child enrollment leads to reduced funding. School budgets are tied to student numbers, meaning fewer children directly translates to less financial support for educational institutions.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Moves to Clear Apapa, Tin Can Port Corridors
stories.summary: Nigeria's Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council announced a two-day clean-up and enforcement exercise along the Apapa and Tin Can port corridors in Lagos to improve trade facilitation and seaport efficiency.

stories.title: Nigeria: Sokoto, Sightsavers Step Up Vaccination After Meningitis Kills 33 Children
stories.summary: Sokoto State Government and Sightsavers Nigeria have intensified vaccination and immunisation efforts following a meningitis outbreak that killed 33 children in Sokoto State.

stories.title: Nigeria: ICPC, Artificial Intelligence and the New Frontline in Nigeria's Anti-Corruption War
stories.summary: Nigeria's Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC) is exploring the use of artificial intelligence tools as part of the country's anti-corruption efforts, potentially enhancing transparency and accountability.

stories.title: Nigeria: Xenophobic Attacks: Ramaphosa, Urgently Show Leadership
stories.summary: A Premium Times editorial calls on South African President Cyril Ramaphosa to show leadership in addressing xenophobic attacks, arguing that the insularity being promoted by some South Africans ignores the realities of globalisation.

stories.title: French evacuee from hantavirus-hit ship tests positive, health minister says
stories.summary: A French national evacuated from the hantavirus-affected luxury cruise ship has tested positive for the virus, according to France's health minister. Four other French passengers tested negative but will undergo further testing.

stories.title: Comedy for Koby’s yearly tour benefiting Israel’s bereaved families - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Koby Mandell Foundation is hosting its annual comedy tour across multiple Israeli cities, including Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, Ra'anana, Gush Etzion, and Modi'in. The events are fundraisers benefiting Israel's bereaved families.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali PM Says Government Focused On Security, Democratic Transition
stories.summary: Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre stated in Mogadishu that the federal government is prioritising security, institutional rebuilding, and implementation of an inclusive democratic system as political and economic reforms continue.

stories.title: Africa: Tinubu Arrives Nairobi for a Two-Day Africa Forward Summit
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu arrived in Nairobi on Monday to attend the two-day Africa Forward Summit hosted in the Kenyan capital.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Repel Attack On Military Base, Kill Three Terrorists, Recover AK-47 Rifle
stories.summary: Nigerian troops from Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters on the 120 Task Force Battalion in Gonori, killing three militants and recovering an AK-47 rifle.

stories.title: Nigeria: Many Traders Shutting Down As Transportation Eats Deep Into Profits
stories.summary: Traders across Nigerian markets are increasingly shutting down their shops as rising transportation costs erode profits, replacing once-bustling market activity with growing silence.

stories.title: Nigeria: Oil Firms Export 80 Percent of Crude Output Despite Local Refining Demand
stories.summary: Oil companies in Nigeria exported roughly 80 percent of the country's crude oil production in the first quarter of 2026, despite increasing demand from domestic refineries.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Swoop On Violent Crimes and Illegal Mining Nets 79 in Mazowe
stories.summary: Zimbabwean police arrested 79 suspects in a crackdown on violent crime and illegal mining in the Mazowe area of Mashonaland Central province, with authorities warning of growing lawlessness and environmental destruction.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 Presidency - Jonathan's Declaration Sparks Stir
stories.summary: Former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan is reportedly planning to seek the presidency again in 2027, using the Peoples Democratic Party as his platform for a return to office.

stories.title: Drone operators destroy Russian flag installed in Kostiantynivka
stories.summary: Drone operators from Ukraine's Liut Brigade used a drone to destroy a Russian flag that had been planted in Kostiantynivka in the Donetsk region. The operation was carried out by the Luhansk assault regiment of the brigade.

stories.title: Gaza: Doctors Under Attack wins BAFTA award after BBC rejection
stories.summary: The documentary "Gaza: Doctors Under Attack" won the current affairs BAFTA after being dropped by the BBC and subsequently broadcast by Channel 4. The film investigates attacks on medical workers and healthcare facilities in the Gaza Strip during the war.

stories.title: Timberwolves win, tie Playoff Series after Spurs’ Wembanyama is ejected
stories.summary: Anthony Edwards scored 36 points to lead the Minnesota Timberwolves to a 114-109 victory over the San Antonio Spurs, tying the Western Conference semifinals at 2-2. Spurs star Victor Wembanyama was ejected during the game.

stories.title: South Africa: Public Gets Three More Weeks to Comment On Eskom Nuclear Site - - but Critics Say It's Not Enough
stories.summary: South Africa's deadline for public comment on a 2,700-page draft environmental scoping report related to Eskom's proposed nuclear site has been extended to 25 May, though critics argue the additional three weeks remain insufficient.

stories.title: Somalia: Mogadishu Wakes Up Under Curfew As Security Forces Deploy Ahead of Planned Opposition Protest
stories.summary: Mogadishu residents woke under a de facto curfew on Saturday as Somali federal security forces deployed across several districts ahead of a planned opposition protest in the capital.

stories.title: Netanyahu concedes he bears some responsibility for Oct. 7, but says ‘everyone’ shares it
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told CBS's "60 Minutes" that he bears some responsibility for the October 7 attack but said responsibility is shared broadly. He also stated that the fall of Iran's regime is not guaranteed and acknowledged Israel has struggled in the "propaganda war."

stories.title: Hong Kong leverages ‘unrivalled’ medical hub status amid global hantavirus alarm
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee positioned the city as a global partner in pandemic preparedness at the Asia Summit on Global Health, citing its medical innovation hub status in response to emerging threats including a recent hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship.

stories.title: Occupiers want to 'nationalize' 150 commercial properties in Luhansk – RMA
stories.summary: Russian occupation authorities in Luhansk have selected 150 commercial real estate properties for forced "nationalization," according to the regional military administration. The seizures target businesses in the temporarily occupied city.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya, France Sign 11 Deals As Ruto Pushes 'Looking Forward' Partnership Agenda
stories.summary: Kenya and France signed 11 cooperation agreements covering transport, energy, digital infrastructure, and trade following bilateral talks between President William Ruto and President Emmanuel Macron at State House in Nairobi.

stories.title: Things are not going so well for Russia
stories.summary: Russia is facing multiple challenges, including a stalled military advance in Ukraine, domestic economic difficulties, and growing concerns about instability in its so-called 'near abroad' — countries in its traditional sphere of influence.

stories.title: Body recovered in search for two missing US soldiers in Morocco
stories.summary: The Moroccan army announced it recovered the body of one of two US soldiers who went missing during the African Lion international military training exercise in southern Morocco.

stories.title: Interceptor missiles launched from Kiryat Shmona after drone alert
stories.summary: Israeli Channel 12 reported that two interceptor missiles were launched from Kiryat Shmona toward southern Lebanon after a suspicious aerial target was detected near the border. The Israeli military confirmed it intercepted the target amid ongoing cross-border tensions with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Hezbollah using fibre optic drones to evade Israeli jamming
stories.summary: The Israeli military is struggling to counter Hezbollah's first-person-view drones that use fibre optic tethers to evade electronic jamming, according to The Jerusalem Post. Hezbollah released footage showing an FPV drone striking an Iron Dome battery near Israel's northern border.

stories.title: First Sergeant Alexander Glovanyov killed in combat near Israel-Lebanon border
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced that First Sergeant Alexander Glovanyov was killed in combat near the Israel-Lebanon border. Glovanyov served as a lead vehicle driver in the 6924th Transport Battalion, and his family has been notified.

stories.title: Robots to the rescue? South Korea looks for AI solutions to dwindling army numbers
stories.summary: South Korea's defense ministry is in talks with Hyundai Motor to develop and potentially deploy robotics and AI-powered unmanned systems for frontline military use. The initiative aims to address the country's deepening troop shortage by building what officials describe as a high-tech, science-driven force.

stories.title: The blame for October 7 lies with more than just one camp - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that blame for the October 7 attack extends beyond any single faction in Israeli politics. It suggests that in future elections, Israeli voters will favor leaders who demonstrate that genuine lessons have been learned from the security failure.

stories.title: UK firefighters called to one lithium-ion battery fire every five hours
stories.summary: UK fire brigades responded to 1,760 lithium-ion battery-linked fires in 2025, averaging one every five hours—a 147% increase over three years. Fire chiefs warn that public awareness and government regulation have not kept pace with the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries in devices ranging from phones to e-bikes.

stories.title: UK households bracing for new cost of living crisis, report finds
stories.summary: A PwC survey found that UK consumer confidence has fallen at its fastest rate since June 2022, driven by concerns about the Iran war's impact on the economy and personal finances. British households are bracing for a new cost of living crisis similar to the one triggered by Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: China eatery owner closes shop briefly to donate stem cells to toddler; customers show support
stories.summary: Shao Sanhu, a 33-year-old barbecue stall owner from Anhui province in central China, temporarily closed his business for 13 days to donate stem cells to a three-year-old child. Upon reopening, he was met with long queues of supportive customers.

stories.title: Watch live: Macron meets young entrepreneurs at Africa Forward summit
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron inaugurated the Africa Forward Summit in Kenya, marking the first time the event has been held in an Anglophone country. Macron met with 450 young entrepreneurs from across Africa and France to discuss ideas for the continent's future development.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya, France Sign 11 Deals On Rail, Ports, Energy and Digital Economy
stories.summary: President William Ruto and President Emmanuel Macron witnessed the signing of 11 agreements in Nairobi to strengthen Kenya-France cooperation in transport, energy, digital infrastructure, and trade.

stories.title: Iran demands sovereignty over Hormuz in counterproposal to US
stories.summary: Iran's counterproposal to the United States demands full war-damage compensation, the lifting of all sanctions, the release of frozen assets, and recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal was delivered through Pakistani mediators, and President Trump subsequently rejected it.

stories.title: Monday briefing: Will the international effort to stop the further spread of hantavirus be successful?
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak aboard a luxury cruise ship has prompted international health responses, with passengers evacuated to multiple countries. The situation highlights concerns about how easily deadly pathogens can spread across borders and the fragility of global preparedness systems.

stories.title: Trump and Xi are set to meet. Where do US-China tariffs stand?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to visit China from May 13 to 15, marking the first presidential trip to Beijing in nearly a decade. The visit will test a fragile tariff truce between the two nations amid broader trade tensions.

stories.title: ‘Totally unacceptable’: Trump rejects Iran peace terms as Tehran warns of new attacks
stories.summary: President Trump rejected Iran's peace terms as "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE" on social media. Tehran warned of potential new attacks in response to the breakdown in ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in Hezbollah drone attack near Lebanon border
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was killed in a Hezbollah drone attack near the Manara area along the Israel-Lebanon border. The Israeli military said the death brings the total of soldiers killed since clashes with Hezbollah escalated in early March to 18. Israel responded with airstrikes and artillery shelling on positions in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: No power outages expected on Monday – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's state grid operator Ukrenergo announced that no electricity consumption restrictions were planned for Monday, May 11. The country's power supply was expected to meet demand without scheduled outages.

stories.title: Mali: Malian Filmmaker Captures Disappearing Tuareg Culture and Traditions
stories.summary: Malian filmmaker Intagrist el Ansari's documentary 'Undertows: A Tuareg Tale' documents the disappearing way of life of Tuareg communities, filmed over 10 years in nomadic settlements and refugee camps.

stories.title: Uganda: Inside the Chimpanzee 'Civil War' That Has Locked a Ugandan Forest in Conflict
stories.summary: In western Uganda's forests, a chimpanzee community has split into rival factions engaged in repeated deadly attacks against each other. Researchers say the unusual violence offers insight into how social bonds can fracture even in close-knit primate groups.

stories.title: Australian women accused of slavery in Islamic State territory in Syria face Melbourne court
stories.summary: Kawsar Ahmad, 53, and her daughter Zeinab Ahmad, 31, both Australian women, appeared in a Melbourne court after being charged with slavery offences allegedly committed while living under Islamic State rule in Syria. They were arrested by the Victorian joint counter-terrorism team at Melbourne airport.

stories.title: Paratroopers jump onto Britain’s most remote inhabited island for hantavirus mission
stories.summary: British paratroopers and Royal Air Force personnel landed on Tristan da Cunha, Britain's most remote inhabited overseas territory in the South Atlantic, to deliver medical personnel and oxygen supplies. The deployment responded to a suspected hantavirus case in a British national who had disembarked from the cruise ship MV Hondius.

stories.title: Multinational talks held on restoring navigation through Hormuz
stories.summary: Defence ministers and representatives from over 40 countries held remote talks on military contributions to a European-led mission to escort commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. The discussions addressed growing tensions and concerns over the security of one of the world's most critical shipping routes.

stories.title: New insurance pays Indian workers to stay home when heat turns deadly
stories.summary: A parametric insurance scheme in India is paying informal workers such as door-to-door clothes seller Lata Solanki to stay home when temperatures exceed dangerous thresholds. Payouts are triggered automatically after two consecutive days at 43.72 degrees Celsius, protecting workers' health without sacrificing income.

stories.title: Minority groups brace for surge in racism after Reform UK election gains
stories.summary: Following Reform UK's strong performance in local elections, including emerging as the largest party in Birmingham with 22 councillors, members of minority communities expressed fears of a surge in racist rhetoric. Outgoing Labour council leader John Cotton urged the incoming administration to champion the city's diversity.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran response “totally unacceptable”
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's response to Washington's peace proposal, calling it "totally unacceptable." The development marks a setback in diplomatic efforts to resolve tensions between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Africa Forward Summit: Paris seeks fresh start with Africa
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron began a visit to Kenya ahead of the Africa Forward Summit, aimed at reframing France's relationship with the continent as a partnership of equals rather than a legacy of colonial dominance.

stories.title: Doctor says targeting healthcare workers 'consistent policy' of Israel
stories.summary: Dr. Tahir Mohammed, a surgeon who has worked in Lebanon and Gaza, told Al Jazeera he has seen no evidence supporting Israeli claims that Hezbollah uses ambulances to transport weapons. He described Israel's targeting of healthcare workers as a consistent policy, citing incidents where medical crews were prevented from reaching wounded civilians in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Hong Kong rugby player denies molesting woman at bar, but admits vandalism
stories.summary: Hong Kong-based Samoan rugby prop Faizal Solomona Penesa, 33, pleaded guilty at Eastern Court to vandalizing a door bolt at Central police station while in custody. He pleaded not guilty to a charge of molesting a woman at Bobby's Rabble bar on Wyndham Street on September 28, 2025.

stories.title: EDGE CEO talks company’s role in Iran conflict, plus future partnerships
stories.summary: EDGE Group CEO Hamad Al Marar discussed the UAE-based defense company's role in the ongoing Iran conflict, including its UAV technology capabilities and future partnership plans, in an interview with Breaking Defense.

stories.title: Trump says Polish, Moldovan prisoners released from Belarusian, Russian detention
stories.summary: President Trump announced on social media that three Polish and two Moldovan prisoners had been released from detention in Belarus and Russia.

stories.title: Risks and rewards in France-Kenya partnership
stories.summary: France and Kenya have deepened their bilateral partnership, but the arrangement has drawn criticism from observers in Nairobi who worry that Kenya's national interests may be subordinated to those of Paris.

stories.title: Trump set to ‘apply pressure’ on China’s Xi over Iran
stories.summary: President Trump is expected to pressure Chinese President Xi Jinping over Beijing's oil purchases from Iran and Russia during his upcoming China visit, having raised the issue multiple times in previous calls.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran's response to his peace proposal “totally unacceptable”
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected Iran's response to Washington's latest proposal to end the ongoing conflict between the two countries, calling it "totally unacceptable" in a post on his Truth Social platform on Sunday. The war between the U.S. and Iran has been underway since late February.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine accuse the other of ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine have each accused the other of violating ceasefire terms. Both sides traded allegations of breaches, though specific details of the claimed violations were not immediately elaborated.

stories.title: US investors warm to Ukrainian defense startups—but export laws slow cooperation
stories.summary: US investors are showing growing interest in Ukrainian defense startups, but American export control regulations are slowing cooperation. At least one firm reports that month-long waits for regulatory approval are putting it at a competitive disadvantage in the fast-moving defense technology sector.

stories.title: US disappointed in Taiwan’s smaller defence budget, official says
stories.summary: A U.S. official expressed disappointment with Taiwan's defense budget after Taiwan's Parliament approved US$25 billion in extra defense spending on May 8, suggesting Washington expected a larger commitment.

stories.title: Xi’s leverage ahead of Trump meet, Hong Kong schools: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post compiled a weekend roundup covering several Asia-focused stories, including a Chinese military study on omega-3 supplement risks, consecutive years of net student enrollment growth in Hong Kong schools, and analysis of Xi Jinping's leverage ahead of a summit with U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Ukraine records dozens of hantavirus cases each year – Public Health Center
stories.summary: Ukraine's Public Health Center reported that the country records dozens of hantavirus infection cases annually. The virus is transmitted to humans from rodents.

stories.title: How Philippine prison kingpins ran Japan, South Korea crime rings
stories.summary: Law enforcement officials in South Korea and Japan traced multiple drug deals, home invasions, and robberies to inmates serving sentences in Philippine prisons. The prisoners allegedly ran cross-border criminal operations using smartphones and encrypted messaging apps, exploiting the Philippines' overwhelmed corrections system.

stories.title: Iran makes new offer on uranium in response to US, report says
stories.summary: Iran has submitted a new proposal offering to dilute some of its highly enriched uranium and transfer the remainder to a third country. The offer represents an updated response to U.S. demands in ongoing nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: ‘Never, ever’: Tim Wilson walks back comments on potential One Nation rightwing alliance
stories.summary: Australian Liberal frontbencher and shadow treasurer Tim Wilson reversed earlier comments that appeared open to a coalition with Pauline Hanson's One Nation party. Wilson stated he would "never, ever, ever" support such an arrangement and urged the Liberal Party to focus on defining its own platform.

stories.title: Body of missing US soldier recovered in Morocco
stories.summary: The U.S. Army announced that a search team recovered the body of an American soldier who went missing near a cliff during a training exercise at Cap Draa, Morocco.

stories.title: Greece scrambles to explain how explosive-packed drone landed in its waters
stories.summary: Greek authorities are investigating how an explosive-laden drone ended up in waters off the country's western coast. Military bomb disposal experts detonated the unmanned device at sea, and the drone is suspected to be of Ukrainian origin. Officials have defended Greece's preparedness against such novel threats.

stories.title: A big step forward for optical core of China’s Taiji gravitational wave project
stories.summary: Chinese scientists at the Institute of Mechanics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, have developed the optical core for a space-based gravitational wave detector as part of China's Taiji project. The detector is designed to observe gravitational waves from space, marking a significant hardware milestone for the initiative.

stories.title: Trade, Iran and Taiwan dominate agenda of Trump-Xi summit beginning Wednesday in Beijing
stories.summary: China confirmed that U.S. President Donald Trump will make a state visit to Beijing from May 13 to 15 at the invitation of President Xi Jinping. The visit—the first by a U.S. president to China in nearly a decade—will address trade relations, the U.S. war against Iran, and disputes over Taiwan's sovereignty.

stories.title: Up to 8,000 Latin Americans fight in Ukraine for Russia, many deceived, international report finds
stories.summary: An international report presented in Kyiv estimates that between 1,000 and 8,000 Latin Americans are serving in the Russian army fighting against Ukraine. The report, produced by FIDH, Truth Hounds, and the Kazakhstan International Bureau for Human Rights, describes the recruitment as a global human-trafficking network used to replenish Russia's frontline casualties.

stories.title: UK, France to host defense ministers meeting on Hormuz, amid Iran threats
stories.summary: The United Kingdom and France are hosting a defence ministers' meeting on securing the Strait of Hormuz, with over 40 nations attending. Both Paris and London are dispatching military vessels to the area as Iran asserts that only it can provide security in the waterway.

stories.title: Paraná waterway: Milei's largest privatization advances amid tailored-bid suspicions
stories.summary: Argentina's tender to concession the Paraná-Paraguay waterway for 25 years has entered its final stage, with Belgian firms Jan de Nul and DEME as finalists. The waterway handles roughly 85% of Argentina's foreign trade. Political questions have mounted over the tender's design and the integrity of its technical documentation.

stories.title: Israeli attorney-general opposes appointment of next Mossad chief
stories.summary: Israel's attorney-general has opposed the appointment of the next Mossad chief over allegations that the candidate failed to protect a teenager he had secretly recruited for an intelligence mission after the recruit was caught.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian peace laureate Mohammadi moved to hospital in Tehran
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been transferred to a hospital in Tehran and granted a sentence suspension on heavy bail, according to a family-run foundation.

stories.title: Hegseth rejects senator’s claims US munitions are depleted
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth publicly denied claims by Democratic Senator Mark Kelly that American munitions stockpiles had been significantly depleted by the war involving Iran. Hegseth accused Kelly of disclosing details from a classified Pentagon briefing.

stories.title: Iran’s Araghchi holds talks with Dutch foreign minister
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke by phone with Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen to discuss bilateral relations and regional developments. The call followed a separate conversation Araghchi held with Egypt's foreign minister.

stories.title: Rain and thunderstorms to dominate weather in Ukraine next week
stories.summary: Ukraine's coming week is expected to be dominated by atmospheric fronts bringing rain and occasional thunderstorms across the country.

stories.title: Rain and thunderstorms to dominate weather in Ukraine next week
stories.summary: Ukrainian meteorologists forecast that atmospheric fronts will bring rain and occasional thunderstorms across Ukraine throughout the coming week.

stories.title: Antony Catalano: media mogul accused of assaulting wife excused from attending court due to fears over press scrutiny
stories.summary: Australian media mogul Antony Catalano, 59, co-owner of Australian Community Media, was excused from attending court in person on charges of assault, false imprisonment, and making threats to kill against his wife. His lawyer argued that press scrutiny could be detrimental to his mental health. The charges stem from an incident on March 13.

stories.title: Netanyahu blames social media for declining US support for Israel
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told CBS News's "60 Minutes" that declining U.S. public support for Israel since the Gaza war began was driven by social media disinformation campaigns, despite Israel's efforts to move civilians from combat zones.

stories.title: Teenager charged after assault on Singaporean blogger Amos Yee at anime event
stories.summary: An 18-year-old Chinese national and Singapore permanent resident, Bosco Chun Ho Wang, was charged with voluntarily causing hurt and public nuisance after allegedly punching and kicking blogger Amos Yee, 27, at an anime convention. The incident occurred on Saturday at Suntec City Convention Centre in Singapore.

stories.title: Jewish couples get married in Kyiv for first time since war started thanks to weekend ceasefire
stories.summary: Several Jewish couples were married in Kyiv for the first time since the start of the war in Ukraine, taking advantage of a weekend ceasefire. The ceremony at Beit Menachem Jewish Community Center included couples of all ages, with one pair aged 92.

stories.title: Mass layoffs hit Iran as businesses struggle under wartime pressures
stories.summary: Mass layoffs are spreading across Iran as businesses face mounting wartime economic pressures. Some manufacturers remain nominally open but have effectively frozen operations with little to no output.

stories.title: Iranian official says response based on regional consultations
stories.summary: An Iranian official described Tehran's response to a U.S. proposal as "realistic and positive," focused on ending fighting across the region, particularly in Lebanon. The response included negotiations on the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear programme, and full sanctions relief.

stories.title: Crude prices surge on fears of escalating Iran conflict
stories.summary: Oil prices rose sharply after President Trump rejected Iran's response to Washington's proposal to end the war, stoking fears of further escalation. Brent crude climbed 2.69 percent to $104.01 per barrel, while WTI also gained amid concerns over Strait of Hormuz disruptions.

stories.title: Gaza documentary dropped by the BBC wins BAFTA
stories.summary: The documentary "Gaza: Doctors Under Attack," which examines attacks on Gaza's healthcare system and medical personnel during the war, won the Best Current Affairs award at the BAFTA Television Awards.

stories.title: Rare earths deal between US and China is still in effect, US official says
stories.summary: A U.S. official confirmed that the rare earths trade deal between the United States and China remains in effect but said it was unclear whether the agreement would be extended upon expiration.

stories.title: Nearly 2,250 hectares burned in Ukraine's ecosystems due to fires – SES
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported that nearly 2,250 hectares of land have been burned across the country due to ecosystem fires.

stories.title: Iran responds to U.S. ceasefire proposal but Trump rejects it as ‘unacceptable’
stories.summary: Iran submitted its response to a U.S. ceasefire proposal via Pakistani mediators, seeking to end the war on all fronts including in Lebanon against Hezbollah and to secure shipping routes. President Trump rejected the response as "unacceptable."

stories.title: Netanyahu meets with leaders of Druze, Circassian communities at Dead Sea summit
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu met with leaders of Israel's Druze and Circassian communities at a Dead Sea summit, emphasizing his commitment to ensuring their safety and noting ongoing discussions with President Trump.

stories.title: Middle East conflicts a danger for whales off S.Africa: study
stories.summary: A study warns that Middle East conflicts are increasing dangers for whales off South Africa's coast, as commercial shipping routes shift away from the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz into whale habitats.

stories.title: UK, France to host defence ministers meeting on Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Kingdom and France announced plans to host a multinational defence ministers meeting focused on securing shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, following Iranian warnings against foreign naval deployments in the waterway.

stories.title: Iran war ‘not over,’ enriched uranium must be removed: Israeli PM Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu called for the removal of Iran's enriched uranium, a stance that contrasts with US President Trump's position that Tehran's nuclear programme has already been contained.

stories.title: Macron opens Africa summit in Kenya with push for new France-Africa partnership
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Kenya on Sunday to open the Africa Forward Summit, promoting a new France-Africa relationship based on partnership rather than influence. The summit takes place amid France's military withdrawal from West Africa and ongoing debate about its post-colonial role on the continent.

stories.title: Singaporean killed in Dukono eruption ‘didn’t go for social media’: family
stories.summary: Singaporean hiker Timothy Heng was killed during the eruption of Mount Dukono in Indonesia. His family said he likely stayed behind to help others, describing him as someone who consistently put others before himself.

stories.title: Hong Kong may broaden at-risk elderly support after recent deaths, minister says
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun said authorities may expand support programs to cover younger elderly residents after two recent deaths of at-risk seniors. He described current identification efforts as "just the beginning."

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia accuse each other of breaching US-backed ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia each accused the other of violating a US-backed ceasefire. Russia's military reported shooting down 57 Ukrainian drones over the past day and said it had retaliated with strikes of its own on the battlefield.

stories.title: War with Iran not over, enriched uranium needs to be removed, Netanyahu tells 60 Minutes
stories.summary: Prime Minister Netanyahu told CBS's "60 Minutes" that the war with Iran was not over and that Iran's enriched uranium needed to be physically removed. Asked how, he replied: "You go in, and you take it out."

stories.title: Israeli air strikes hit southern Lebanon as death toll rises
stories.summary: The Israeli military carried out approximately 40 air strikes on villages in southern Lebanon on Sunday, alongside artillery shelling and home demolitions. Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health reported at least 2,846 people killed and 8,693 wounded since the escalation began.

stories.title: Middle East war live: UK and France to host defence talks on Hormuz shipping mission
stories.summary: The United Kingdom and France will host a multinational defence ministers' meeting on Tuesday to discuss military plans to restore trade flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran warned it would deliver a "decisive and immediate response" to any French and British naval deployment in the strait.

stories.title: Trump says call with Netanyahu was ‘very nice’ amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: President Trump described a phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu as "very nice" amid heightened regional tensions. The conversation covered Iran's response to a U.S. proposal regarding the conflict and Tehran's nuclear programme.

stories.title: Iran seeks guarantees against future attacks in US response, Tasnim reports
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported that Tehran's response to a U.S. proposal demanded an immediate end to the war, guarantees against future aggression, sanctions relief, and recognition of Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Tehran says US proposal sought Iran’s surrender
stories.summary: Iranian state television said Tehran rejected the latest American proposal because it amounted to demanding Iran's "surrender." Iran's response sought compensation for wartime losses, including the death of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and senior IRGC commanders, as well as sanctions relief.

stories.title: In Lviv region, conflict between two men ends with shots being fired at car; suspect detained
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Lviv region, a conflict between two men escalated when one fired shots at the other's car. No injuries were reported, and the suspect was detained by police.

stories.title: Hong Kong right to move to extend long arm of the law to claw machines
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities are considering extending regulations to cover claw machine arcades, amid concerns that the games exploit dopamine-driven instant gratification in ways similar to smartphone and social media addiction.

stories.title: Macron says Paris, London preparing mission for Hormuz navigation
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that France and the United Kingdom had prepared a mission involving around 50 countries to help resume maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in coordination with Iran. He stated that military deployment in the waterway was not planned.

stories.title: Israeli PM says more work remains despite gains against Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told CBS News that the war with Iran "is not over yet," stating that enriched uranium still needed to be removed and Iranian enrichment facilities dismantled. He said Israel had inflicted significant damage on Iranian capabilities.

stories.title: Lebanese PM says Bint Jbeil ‘has become a version of Gaza’
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said the southern town of Bint Jbeil "has become a version of Gaza" due to continued Israeli attacks and siege. He stated that 68 Lebanese villages are now under Israeli control and that Lebanon was dragged into the Iran-U.S. confrontation.

stories.title: Iran calls US greatest threat to international peace, says its demands are unreasonable
stories.summary: Iran labeled the United States the greatest threat to international peace and called US demands unreasonable while insisting on an end to the blockade and the unfreezing of its assets. Separately, a woman was killed in Ramle and a boy seriously injured in Lod in separate shootings in Israel.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Iran regime’s fall not guaranteed, acknowledges Hormuz standoff wasn’t foreseen
stories.summary: In a CBS "60 Minutes" interview, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said the fall of Iran's regime was not guaranteed and acknowledged that the Strait of Hormuz standoff had not been foreseen. He also expressed a plan to wean Israel off U.S. aid.

stories.title: China confirms dates for President Donald Trump’s state visit to Beijing
stories.summary: China confirmed that U.S. President Donald Trump will pay a state visit to Beijing from May 13 to 15, the first by a U.S. president in nearly nine years. The visit coincides with the fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire and the Strait of Hormuz blockade affecting global energy costs.

stories.title: Cigarette butts ‘strong evidence’ of smoking ban breach at work sites: Chris Sun
stories.summary: Hong Kong's labour chief Chris Sun said cigarette butts will serve as "strong evidence" of possible breaches under a proposed construction site smoking ban, with maximum fines of HK$400,000. The measure follows an inquiry into the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire.

stories.title: Trump’s China return: what’s changed since his ‘friendly’ 2017 visit
stories.summary: President Trump is scheduled to visit Beijing on May 13–15, nine years after his first trip to China in 2017. The summit will focus on extending the trade truce and addressing ongoing tensions over tariffs, Taiwan, and technology rivalry.

stories.title: China woman fined for applying make-up, dancing while driving; claims assisted driving more reliable
stories.summary: A driver surnamed Lin in Wenzhou, Zhejiang province, eastern China, was fined after posting videos of herself applying make-up and dancing while driving through a tunnel with her hands off the steering wheel. She claimed her vehicle's assisted-driving system was more reliable than her own driving.

stories.title: Latvian defence minister resigns after Ukrainian drones hit oil tanks
stories.summary: Latvian Defence Minister Andris Spruds resigned on Sunday in Riga after two Ukrainian drones transited from Russian airspace and struck oil storage facilities in Latvia on Thursday.

stories.title: Trump, Tehran and a Qatari tanker transit: here’s what happened overnight
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's response to a one-page US peace proposal aimed at ending the ongoing US-Israel war against Iran, now in its tenth week. Trump called the response "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE" on social media. A Qatari tanker transit and stalled peace talks remain key developments.

stories.title: Ailing Iran Nobel laureate given bail and hospital transfer
stories.summary: Iranian authorities granted bail to Nobel Peace Prize laureate and human rights activist Narges Mohammadi, allowing her transfer to a hospital due to deteriorating health while in prison.

stories.title: Partisans disrupt transfer of Russian military cargo toward Sumy sector
stories.summary: Agents of the ATESH partisan movement sabotaged a railway section in Russia's Lipetsk region, disabling a freight locomotive transporting military cargo destined for the Sumy sector of the front line in Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump's visit to China will focus on Iran issue, demand more pressure on Tehran, US officials say
stories.summary: U.S. officials said President Trump's upcoming visit to China will center on the Iran issue, with Washington demanding that Beijing increase pressure on Tehran amid concerns over continued Chinese support for Iran's government.

stories.title: Martin Short opens up about ‘nightmare’ death of his daughter Katherine
stories.summary: Actor and comedian Martin Short spoke publicly for the first time about the death of his 42-year-old daughter, Katherine Short, calling it "a nightmare for the family." Katherine died by suicide in February at her home in the Hollywood Hills, as confirmed by the Los Angeles Medical Examiner's office.

stories.title: Somalis rally against government-ordered evictions in Mogadishu
stories.summary: Demonstrators in Mogadishu rallied against a wave of government-ordered evictions that have displaced families across the Somali capital.

stories.title: Israel’s election may end the Netanyahu era but not the ‘forever wars’
stories.summary: Israel's next election, constitutionally scheduled for October, is shaping up as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security record following the October 7, 2023 attacks and subsequent wars. A crowded field of challengers is forming amid political defections and coalition-building efforts.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump slams Tehran’s reply; Israel kills 2 medics in Lebanon
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump called Tehran's response to a diplomatic proposal "unacceptable," while Iran's military warned it was prepared if hostilities with the U.S. and Israel resumed. Separately, Israeli forces killed two medics in Lebanon.

stories.title: War update: 144 clashes on frontline throughout day
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces recorded 144 combat engagements with Russian troops on May 10, with the most intense fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector of the front line.

stories.title: Jailed Iran Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi transferred to hospital after medical crisis
stories.summary: Nobel Peace laureate Narges Mohammadi was transferred from Zanjan prison to a Tehran hospital after collapsing more than a week earlier. Her foundation said her condition had been described as critical and that she was granted a prison sentence suspension on bail, though the duration remains unclear.

stories.title: In photos: Mourners in Gaza bury their loved ones
stories.summary: Mourners in Gaza buried victims of the ongoing conflict, including two Palestinian police officers reportedly killed in an Israeli airstrike on their vehicle.

stories.title: Trump says US would need two weeks to hit all Iran targets
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the US military would need two more weeks to strike all remaining targets in Iran, claiming 70 percent of identified targets have already been hit.

stories.title: Syria sets first cabinet reshuffle since Assad ouster, state media reports
stories.summary: Syria announced its first cabinet reshuffle since the ouster of former President Bashar al-Assad, coming approximately a year and a half into the five-year transitional period outlined in the country's constitutional declaration.

stories.title: How social media turned Indian film star Vijay into a political force
stories.summary: Indian film star Vijay became a significant political force in Tamil Nadu, with his fan club members acting as digital campaigners who amplified his message on social media despite his limited personal campaigning.

stories.title: Why Eurovision's fallout over Israel may change the competition forever
stories.summary: Eurovision faces its largest boycott in 70 years over Israel's participation, raising questions about the future format and political neutrality of the long-running international music competition.

stories.title: Ukraine submits “list of 1,000” to Russia for prisoner swap
stories.summary: Ukraine submitted a list of 1,000 names to Russia as part of preparations for a prisoner exchange between the two countries.

stories.title: Evacuation flights leave Tenerife after cruise ship hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: Evacuation flights carrying Spanish and French nationals departed Tenerife on Sunday after a deadly hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship. One of five French passengers showed symptoms during the repatriation flight to Paris, and all were placed in strict isolation.

stories.title: Trump calls Iranian proposal to end war 'totally unacceptable'
stories.summary: President Trump called Iran's proposal to end the war 'totally unacceptable.' Tehran's proposal stressed ending hostilities on all fronts and lifting sanctions on Iran, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran's response to US peace proposal 'totally unacceptable'
stories.summary: Iran rejected the latest US peace proposal on Sunday, and President Donald Trump dismissed the response as "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE" on social media. The failed exchange represents another setback in efforts to reduce tensions in the Persian Gulf amid disrupted shipping and rising energy prices.

stories.title: Filmmakers slam BBC after Gaza documentary wins award despite being dropped
stories.summary: A documentary about the war in Gaza won an award after the BBC had dropped it from broadcast. Filmmakers criticized the BBC, accusing the broadcaster of bias and censorship.

stories.title: Deaf artist who lost life’s work in Hong Kong’s Tai Po fire is ‘painting to heal myself’
stories.summary: Hong Kong deaf illustrator Apple Tong Wing-yin lost her life's work — canvases, awards, and archived projects — when a fire struck Wang Fuk Court in the Tai Po housing estate in November. The blaze was one of Hong Kong's deadliest. Tong says she is now painting to recover emotionally.

stories.title: Man detonates grenade in Sumy region, five people injured
stories.summary: A man detonated a grenade in the town of Okhtyrka in Ukraine's Sumy region, injuring five people including himself, three police officers, and one civilian.

stories.title: Militia kill at least 69 in DR Congo: local, security sources
stories.summary: Militia fighters killed at least 69 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province, where the Hema and Lendu ethnic groups have been engaged in a long-running violent conflict in the gold-rich region bordering Uganda and South Sudan.

stories.title: Past top Israeli, US officials reveal new vision for ties rooted in tech partnership
stories.summary: Former U.S. Ambassador Tom Nides and former IDF intelligence chief Amos Yadlin proposed a Technology Alliance between Israel and the United States, envisioning $2 billion in annual joint investment to redefine bilateral ties amid declining U.S. public support for Israel.

stories.title: Chinese 6-seat electric SUVs to stand out amid weak domestic sales, says Morgan Stanley
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley reports that six-seat premium electric SUVs from Chinese automakers are poised to challenge German luxury brands in China's automotive market. More than a dozen locally developed models are expected this year, combining technological advantages and competitive pricing to potentially offset weak domestic sales.

stories.title: Trump rejects Iran peace terms, Tehran warns of new attacks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump dismissed Iran's response to a U.S. peace proposal, warning of a deepening crisis in Middle East war negotiations. Tehran has warned of potential new attacks.

stories.title: NYC anti-Israel activists plan Monday protest against Israel real estate event
stories.summary: Anti-Israel activists in New York City announced a Monday protest targeting an Israeli real estate event. The demonstration follows a similar protest held the previous Tuesday by the group PAL-Awda.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia trade accusations of violating US-backed ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged accusations of violating a three-day ceasefire announced by President Trump. The U.S.-backed pause is part of broader peace efforts that have not ended the more than four-year-old war.

stories.title: Anti-Iranian regime activists hold global protests denouncing months-long internet outage
stories.summary: Anti-Iranian-regime activists held protests in multiple cities worldwide, denouncing a months-long internet outage imposed by Iranian authorities. Some demonstrators displayed banners praising Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Sybiha heading to Brussels for EU, NATO talks and child return summit
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha is traveling to Brussels for EU and NATO-related meetings on May 11. He will also attend a ministerial session of the International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children.

stories.title: Trump rejects Iran response, calls it 'inappropriate'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump rejected Iran's response to a U.S. ceasefire proposal, calling it "inappropriate" in an interview with Axios. Trump also confirmed a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu but stressed that Iran negotiations are his matter alone.

stories.title: Modi urges Indians to reduce petrol, diesel consumption amid Middle East war disruption
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to reduce petrol and diesel consumption amid supply disruptions caused by the Middle East war. India has raised LPG prices following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran and Iran's near-total blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran releases Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi on bail amid health fears
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been released on bail and transferred to Tehran for urgent medical treatment. Supporters had warned she was at risk of dying in prison, where she reportedly suffered two suspected heart attacks. Mohammadi was jailed for campaigning against Iran's clerical system.

stories.title: Australia politics live: Albanese blames Coalition for ‘legitimising’ One Nation; Joyce says his party will ‘go for government’
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese blamed the Coalition for "legitimising" One Nation following the party's emphatic byelection win in the Farrer electorate. One Nation's Barnaby Joyce declared the party would pursue government.

stories.title: Emergency crews containing forest fire in Zhytomyr region
stories.summary: Emergency crews are working to contain a forest fire in the Polissia Nature Reserve in Ukraine's Zhytomyr region. Smoldering debris and forest floor were still being observed as firefighting operations continued.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran ceasefire response 'totally unacceptable'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social rejecting Iran's latest reply to U.S. ceasefire proposals, calling it "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE" in blunt terms.

stories.title: Hezbollah strikes Iron Dome battery with FPV drone
stories.summary: Hezbollah struck an Israeli Iron Dome battery using a first-person-view (FPV) drone. The IDF has reportedly struggled to counter the FPV drone threat, which uses special cables and manual piloting to evade Israel's advanced jamming and tracking technologies.

stories.title: Experts call for UK four-day week as study links long work hours to obesity
stories.summary: Research presented at the European Congress on Obesity in Istanbul found that countries with longer working hours, including the U.S. and Mexico, have higher obesity rates. Experts in the UK called for a four-day work week based on the findings.

stories.title: Taiwan’s Cheng Li-wun on cross-strait peace, meeting Xi Jinping and managing ties with US
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun discussed her vision for cross-strait peace with mainland China, her April meeting with Xi Jinping, and an upcoming U.S. trip, advocating the 1992 consensus as a basis for dialogue.

stories.title: Taiwan’s opposition KMT leader on restoring stable peace with Beijing
stories.summary: KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun outlined her approach to restoring stable relations between Taiwan and mainland China in an interview, discussing her meeting with Communist Party leader Xi Jinping and upcoming visit to the United States.

stories.title: Starmer under pressure: “Swapping leaders won’t fix problems,” says former Labour adviser
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting internal pressure after Labour lost a significant number of council seats in local elections, while Reform UK made strong gains. Backbench MP Catherine West has suggested she could trigger a leadership contest. Starmer is preparing a key speech on Monday aimed at resetting his agenda.

stories.title: Lebanon says 2,846 killed in Israeli attacks since March
stories.summary: Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health reported that Israeli attacks have killed at least 2,846 people and wounded 8,693 since March 2. Of those, 552 deaths and 1,149 injuries occurred after a ceasefire took effect on April 16.

stories.title: Ukraine, Norway agree on joint production of 155 mm artillery shells – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine and Norway have agreed to jointly produce long-range 155 mm artillery shells, bolstering Ukraine's ammunition supply.

stories.title: Jailed Iran peace laureate Mohammadi moved to hospital in Tehran
stories.summary: Imprisoned Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was transferred to a Tehran hospital after suffering a heart attack. She was granted a temporary suspension of her sentence.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran will 'be laughing no longer', condemns behavior of past 47 years
stories.summary: President Trump warned Iran it will 'be laughing no longer' and condemned its behavior over the past 47 years. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was expected to speak with Trump shortly after the statement, according to a source familiar with the details.

stories.title: CNN accuses IDF of detaining Palestinian reporter for a year without probing terror charges
stories.summary: CNN accused the Israeli military of detaining a Palestinian reporter for approximately one year without investigating the terrorism charges against him. The IDF has not publicly responded to the allegations or addressed its broader handling of arrested journalists.

stories.title: Why the UAE’s Opec exit spells the beginning of the end of Gulf unity
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates gave Opec three days' notice of its departure on April 28, driven by longstanding disputes over production quotas. The move reflects shifting Gulf security dynamics following Iranian strikes on UAE infrastructure.

stories.title: Drone incidents in Latvia caused by Russian EW, Ukraine’s FM Sybiha says
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke with Latvian counterpart Baiba Braže about drone incidents in Latvia, attributing them to Russian electronic warfare that may have redirected drones from Russian territory into Latvian airspace.

stories.title: On Marka-i-Haq's first anniversary, PM Shehbaz commemorates Pakistan's 'historic response' to India
stories.summary: Pakistan commemorated the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq at a ceremony at the Pakistan Monument in Islamabad. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, President Zardari, and Field Marshal Asim Munir attended, recalling Pakistan's military response to India following the April 2025 Pahalgam attack.

stories.title: London man charged for assault on three Jewish residents
stories.summary: A man in London was charged with assaulting three Jewish residents — a 53-year-old woman, a 58-year-old man, and a 26-year-old man — all of whom sustained minor injuries that did not require further medical treatment.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran’s response to US peace proposal ‘unacceptable’
